abstract:
Take AU Home With You.

Visit the all-new AU Merch Store for exclusive Autodesk apparel, premium swag, and limited-edition AU collectibles. Celebrate the ideas, innovations, and connections that brought us together and grab a piece of the experience before it's gone.

title: Breakfast
abstract: Grab coffee and a bite to eat to fuel your first day at AU.

title: Stop Sharing Screens – Start Sharing Space: Practical XR for Model Coordination
speakers: Joseph Huang, Principal, Architect, BIM Design Team Lead, Stantec | Raghavendra Bhat, Principal, Sr. BIM Integration Specialist, Stantec
topics: Buildings | Forma Data Management Essentials | Navisworks Manage | Pype | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | XR
abstract: Immersive technologies are often promoted as the future of model coordination, yet most teams remain stuck in screen sharing and pilot demos. This session challenges that pattern, presenting a practical playbook for using shared immersive space as a deliberate coordination tool rather than a novelty. Through real project scenarios, it shows when XR enables faster understanding and better decisions, when desktop review works better, and how to structure immersive meetings so technical and non-technical stakeholders collaborate effectively. Hardware, visualization, and platforms matter – but only when paired with clear intent, facilitation, and decision focused workflows.

title: Multi-AI-Agent BIM Orchestration: Building Autonomous Query. Check. Fix Loops for Revit.
speakers: Phuc Le, Account Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: What if your Revit model could check itself—and fix what it finds—autonomously? This session will introduce a multi-agent system where specialized AI agents collaborate in a loop: a Query agent will read model data via Model Context Protocol (MCP), a QC agent will check it against configurable standards, and a Design agent will propose corrections - each previewed, human-approved, and audited before any write. The cycle will repeat until the model passes. We’ll demo three live scenarios: Naming Convention Fix, Parameter Completeness, and Geometry Checking - built with Revit MCP Server, Forma MCP, Python, LangGraph, and configurable YAML rules. We'll also cover transaction management, convergence control, and the points where human oversight remains essential.

title: From Massing to Metrics: Integrating Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights for Outcome-Based Design
speakers: Jessica Carson, Architect, GHD Design | Isaac McCormack, Architect, GHD Design | Michael from Chile Sturm, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Forma | Insight | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Around 80% of a building’s environmental impact is determined in the first 20% of design, yet this phase often relies on intuition rather than data. This presentation will introduce GHD’s outcome-based workflow that embeds predictive AI and cloud simulation into early design, providing carbon insights when decisions matter. Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) enables real-time evaluation of wind, thermal comfort, and early embodied carbon from simple massing models. As designs progress, Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights (formerly Autodesk Insight) calculates energy-use intensity and examines trade-offs between operational and embodied carbon. The result is an iterative, data-driven approach that integrates carbon performance into design and enables credible sustainability narratives from project inception.

title: Using MCP to Build Self-Improving AEC Data Workflows
speakers: Nabil Sadeg, CTO, Nacorm
topics: Architecture services | Autodesk Platform Services | Revit | AECO | Software Development
abstract: Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) data stays raw because processing it manually does not scale. This session will demonstrate a working pipeline where AI classifies documents, extracts structured information, enriches records, and validates outputs at every stage. Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects AI agents to Revit, Autodesk Platform Services, and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), letting them read and write connected data across tools in a single workflow. A live walk-through of a real pipeline used on AEC projects will show how feedback loops capture user corrections so results improve with every iteration. You will leave with a reusable architecture pattern you can adapt to your own challenges, from tender analysis to intelligent models to construction submittals.

title: The Superb Guide to Easy Revit Rides On!
speakers: Rina Sahay, BIM Lead, Wade Trim
topics: Architecture services | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Docs | Inventor | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: The award-winning Superb Team continues with enhanced insights into the ever-expanding world of Revit software and its friends. Our lively conversation spiced with weird, wild, witty, and wonderful war stories will energize you with the latest and greatest developments in Revit 2027 and Autodesk Forma industry cloud. Discover wild and wonderful things to do with Revit using native tools or third-party software for reality capture, visualization, and AR/XR. Use interoperability with add-ins and other authoring and visualization software. Get a glimpse of the future with innovative use cases using AI. Discover more ways and means to enhance productivity. Join us for wise and fun pointers on how to be a fearlessly productive Revit Warrior.

title: Rendering Reality: The Rise of Gaussian Splats
speakers: Logan Foster, Product Owner, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | 3ds Max 2 | AECO | Media & Entertainment
abstract: Join industry experts from design visualization and VFX as they explore how Gaussian Splats and solutions from Autodesk Interactive Media & Entertainment are transforming digital workflows. Learn what these techniques are, how they enable highly accurate digital twins and immersive world building, and where they fit in real-world production pipelines. Through examples and firsthand insights, speakers will share what excites them about this approach—along with the practical pros, cons, and challenges of adopting it.

title: MCP on Autodesk Platform: Three Production Servers Across the Full Stack
speakers: Jose Baquero, Senior Consultant MGF - AI Solutions, Avant Leap | Enrique Galicia Tovar, Director of Innovations and AI, AvantLeap
topics: Architecture services | Autodesk Platform Services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Software Development
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the layer that lets AI agents access Autodesk tools, data, and APIs through a standardized interface. The firms building this infrastructure today will define the standard—not just use it. This session will go deep on three production MCP servers: revitDeploymentMCP (CI/CD pipeline as four AI-callable tools), a Dynamo MCP server (exposing Dynamo scripts for AI orchestration), and an Autodesk Platform Services Data Pipeline server (chaining the Model Derivative API, the Data Management API, and the Design Automation API without auth failures or silent webhook drops). Each server is examined at the architecture, implementation, and deployment levels. You’ll receive complete implementation patterns for all three.

title: Forma to Energy: AI-Powered Workflows for Carbon Insight
speakers: Tetsuya Hishida, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk | Daniel Stine, Director of Design Technology, Lake Flato | Chris Balbach, Director of R&D, Performance Systems Development of NY, LLC
topics: Architecture services | Forma | Insight | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Energy and carbon analysis often arrives too late—after key decisions have been made. Despite tools like Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Insight software, most teams rely on manual, disconnected workflows that limit iteration. This session will introduce a connected, data-driven approach. By embedding performance data in BIM and using AI to generate simulation logic, teams can automatically produce carbon and energy analyses—earlier, more frequently, and without deep simulation expertise. Through a live demo, you’ll see design data flow from Autodesk Forma through Revit into automated workflows and into Insight for actionable results. Attend this class to learn how to replace one-off analysis with scalable, repeatable carbon workflows.

title: From Revit Stills to Stories: AI Video Workflows for Architectural Communication
speakers: Qian Huang, Design Technology Specialist, HOK
topics: Architecture services | 3ds Max 2 | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Architects increasingly need to communicate design intent through motion before there is time or budget for traditional animation and for audiences who do not read drawings. This session shows how approved design assets from Revit based rendering views, diagrams, sketches, physical model, photos, can become short AI-assisted motion assets for design reviews, competitions, and client presentations. Attendees will learn a repeatable still-to-video workflow, see where AI video supports architectural communication and where it falls short, and apply QA guardrails for review and trust before using outputs in practice. A 5 minute case study assembled from 30 AI-assisted clips will also demonstrate how short generations become a coherent story.

title: From 2D to Digital Twin: Connecting Design to Oper
speakers: Enrico Trovato, Head of AECO Automation & Intelligence, EssilorLuxottica
topics: Desktop Connector | Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract: Retail construction still relies heavily on fragmented 2D documentation, creating a disconnect between design, construction, and operations. This session will explore how EssilorLuxottica is transforming that model by converting 2D assets into structured 3D BIM and building a connected digital lifecycle. By linking design data to Internet of Things (IoT) sensors and maintenance workflows, stores evolve from static deliverables into dynamic, data-driven digital twins. This session will present a scalable approach to connect design to operations, improve asset visibility, and enable predictive maintenance, turning retail environments into fully integrated intelligent assets.

title: Do You Trust Me? Building Trustworthy AI for Design and Engineering Workflows
speakers: Ousama Lakhdar-Ghazal, Director, Trusted AI & Privacy, Autodesk
topics: None | Future Industry Innovations
abstract: As AI becomes embedded in design and engineering tools, the question isn’t just what it can do—it’s whether you can trust it. This session will cover practical ways to make AI more reliable, including handling proprietary versus common design data—and validating outputs. You'll learn practical tactics for increasing the trustworthiness of AI models, with a focus on real-world challenges like distinguishing proprietary intellectual property from common design elements and validating the accuracy of AI-generated outputs. We’ll explore assessing inputs, adding safeguards, and creating feedback loops to improve performance over time—so you can adopt and build AI responsibly without sacrificing quality or compliance.

title: Maximizing Autodesk Platform Services Value: Smarter Usage, Greater Control, AI-Ready Scale
speakers: Dwanill Mehta, Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Autodesk Platform Services continues to evolve to better support how customers build, scale, and optimize applications in an increasingly AI-driven world. APIs and Model Context Protocols (MCPs) are becoming foundational to agentic AI workflows, making it more important than ever to understand and optimize Autodesk Platform Services use. This session will highlight the features Autodesk Platform Services is building to help you make the most of cloud APIs and MCPs, whether developing directly on Autodesk Platform Services or integrating through third-party applications. You’ll also see new capabilities that provide greater visibility and control, including Autodesk Platform Services reporting, cost management tools, and AI-powered usage prediction through Autodesk Assistant. Join us to learn how to scale with confidence and maximize value from Autodesk Platform Services.

title: AI-Connected Workflows: Fusion, Claude, and MCP 101
speakers: Luke Mihelcic, Senior Manager,  Product & Technical Marketing - Design, Autodesk
topics: Product Development
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Fusion, Claude, and MCP (Model Context Protocol) can work together to create smarter, more connected engineering workflows. This introductory session will explore how conversational AI can assist with design, automation, scripting, documentation, and workflow generation inside Fusion environments, while MCP enables secure connections between AI, tools, and data sources. Attendees will learn foundational concepts, practical integration examples, and real-world use cases that demonstrate how AI-driven workflows can improve productivity, collaboration, and decision-making across product development and manufacturing.

title: A.I. Without Chaos: AutoCAD and Revit Plugin Development with Spec-Driven Development
speakers: Fernando Malard, Chief Technology Officer, ofcdesk, LLC
topics: Engineering service providers | AutoCAD | Revit | AECO | Software Development
abstract: AI coding tools are changing how software is developed in architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO). Inconsistent outputs, lack of standards, and tight coupling to platform APIs often lead to fragile and unstable plug-ins. This class will introduce Spec-Driven Development (SDD) as a practical, tool-agnostic approach to bring structure and reliability to AI-assisted development. Instead of prompts and chat history, SDD uses persistent specifications as the source of truth. Using plug-ins in AutoCAD and Revit software, we’ll demonstrate how to separate business logic from platform-specific implementations. You’ll learn how SDD can use modern AI tools such as OpenAI Codex to transform AI from a source of chaos into a controlled software development asset.

title: Building Custom AEC Apps in Minutes: AI-Assisted Development with FORMA and VIKTOR.AI
speakers: Peter Madlener, CEO, VIKTOR | Jordana Rosa, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract:
Design teams increasingly need trusted workflows that connect Autodesk Forma, Autodesk Platform Services (APS), agentic AI, engineering tools, proprietary company knowledge, and cloud automation to solve real project challenges. This session explores how organizations can use open APIs and modern development platforms to build custom applications and intelligent workflows around Forma Site Design and Building Design.

Attendees will learn how to integrate project data, automate engineering and design processes, connect cloud services, and extend Autodesk workflows with company-specific logic. We will also introduce the Autodesk Marketplace and discuss how developers can package and distribute solutions that strengthen the Autodesk ecosystem.

Using VIKTOR.AI as the application, workflow, and agentic automation layer, we will demonstrate how Autodesk technologies can be combined with AI, engineering software, and internal knowledge. We will show how organizations can move beyond isolated AI prompts by creating transparent, controlled, and verifiable workflows in which agents execute tasks, use engineering tools, and present traceable results for expert review.

title: Agentic AI Running Project Workflows in Autodesk Forma with MCP
speakers: Farzad Towhidi, Senior Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk | Luis Salmeron, Senior Digital Systems Engineer, Professional Engineering Consultants (PEC)
topics: Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Software Development
abstract: This session will explore how PEC is implementing agentic AI to run real project workflows within Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). By using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server as a governed orchestration layer, AI agents can securely connect to Autodesk APIs, query live project data, perform QA/QC checks, and execute tasks across project systems. You’ll see how this architecture moves beyond automation into true workflow execution—enabling scalable, consistent, and intelligent project delivery. We’ll share real-world examples, implementation strategies, and lessons learned to help teams begin adopting AI-driven workflows today.

title: Boosting Autodesk Development Using AI with AutoLISP and C# .NET
speakers: Todd Schmoock, Implementation Consultant, Graitec | James Johnson, Application Developer, Synergis Software
topics: Engineering service providers | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Architecture | AutoCAD Electrical | AutoCAD Mechanical | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design
abstract: Learn how to use AI as a practical coding assistant to accelerate AutoCAD development. This 30-minute strategy session will show how AI can generate AutoLISP routines and C# .NET code, assist with debugging, and support code translation—enabling faster iteration and higher-quality results. Attendees will gain strategies to evaluate AI-generated code, integrate it into existing projects, and apply AI-assisted workflows effectively across both legacy and modern Autodesk development.

title: Which Revit Structural Model to Use for Analysis? Analytical or Physical or Both?
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E
topics: Engineering service providers | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: This class will explore whether structural analysis workflows in Revit software should rely on the analytical model, the physical model, or a hybrid of both. Traditionally, structural analysis platforms use only the analytical model to translate geometry and structural properties from Revit. Why limit workflows to just the analytical model? With analytical and physical models now able to act independently, users can choose which representation best fits their needs. This class will compare approaches and evaluate when each method—or a combined strategy—provides the most reliable and efficient structural analysis workflow. We’ll also explore customizing structural analysis tools to accept physical model geometry.

title: AI for Ideation: Telling a good story with Generative AI and Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
speakers: Andrell Laniewicz, East Region RBG Digital Delivery Lead, HDR | Zachary Smith, Autodesk Platform Developer, HDR
topics: Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | Forge | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Imagine this scenario: You’re a developer and a user identifies a problem that, when solved, could save hundreds of hours per project. Moreover, there doesn’t appear to be a solution on the market that solves this problem adequately, so you get to build something. In an industry where users are more likely to buy a story than a product, how do we tell a good story? This discussion will center around our approach to collaboratively translating ideas into prototypes. We’ll use generative AI and Autodesk Platform Services as our low-barrier-to-entry tools for the code, and demonstrate the value of building trust in the solution by building it together.

title: Revit MEP Fundamentals and New Tricks
speakers: Matthew Collier, Technical Product Manager, IMEG Corp. | Sean Fruin, Mechanical Applications Product Owner, IMEG
topics: Engineering service providers | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Many teams still rely on outdated Revit MEP habits that slow coordination and create inconsistent models. This session will cover how to build a strong foundation in spaces, connectors, systems, circuits, and documentation. Then we’ll show how recent Revit improvements support better analysis, clearer panel and circuit workflows, improved analytical visibility for duct and pipe systems, and a smoother path from design to fabrication. We’ll share practical methods that help newer users build confidence and experienced users work faster, model more accurately, and reduce rework.

title: Connecting BIM to Citizen-Scale Digital Twins: Sustainability, Compliance & Connected Infrastructure
speakers: Francesco Cappilli, Head of Digital Engineering, Infrastrutture Milano Cortina 2026 Spa
topics: Engineering service providers | Build | Civil 3D | Revit | Workshop XR | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: SIMICO S.p.A delivered infrastructure to the 2026 Winter Olympics (Livigno, Cortina, Milano, Verona, Bormio) using a full Autodesk pipeline: Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), Autodesk Forma Build, Autodesk Platform Services, Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD, and Navisworks software. Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Build managed cost, schedule, and field workflows. Autodesk Platform Services connected everything bidirectionally. This Autodesk-Azure dual common data environment (CDE) enabled a complex environment where BIM authoring changes synced with Forma cost tracking, Build field logs, and compliance docs. These pipelines preserved data integrity from Autodesk tools to digital XR experiences (VR/AR/pixel streaming), making the twin accessible to all stakeholders. Tailored as such, this system delivered an organic ecosystem, reducing risk and accelerating decisions on complex public infrastructure in Italy.

title: AI Changes the Cost Curve but Connected Data Changes Value Creation
speakers: Knut Ramstad, CTO and Partner, Registered Architect, Nordic Office of Architecture | Marius Jablonskis, Digital Transformation Leader, Norconsult ASA
topics: Engineering service providers | None | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: AI is often discussed in terms of efficiency, but the bigger shift may be how connected data improves the quality, consistency, and usefulness of expert delivery. This session will share Norconsult’s perspective on how AI and connected data are beginning to influence decision support, delivery workflows, and client value across architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO). We’ll explore why the impact goes beyond isolated productivity gains, where connected data makes AI more relevant in practice, and what leaders should consider as technology starts to affect how value is created in engineering and project delivery. The session will focus on practical implications and lessons emerging from real industry needs.

title: Continuous vs. Periodic Clash Detection : Can Model Coordination and Autodesk AI replace Navisworks?
speakers: Anas Poshekar, Associate Sr. BIM Coordinator, Burns & McDonnell India
topics: Engineering service providers | Cloud Worksharing | Forma | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Is the Navisworks silo holding your project back? For 20 years, coordination was a "once a week" event locked on a desktop. No more. This session will explore the leap to continuous, cloud-native coordination in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll dive into how Model Coordination democratizes BIM, using Autodesk AI and Autodesk Assistant to validate clashes against specs in real time. Learn to ditch static PDF reports for a closed-loop workflow that connects designers directly to fixes. We’ll settle the debate: Where does Model Coordination win, and when do you still need the Navisworks "power user" kit? Join us to build a road map for a faster, AI-augmented and integrated future. Stop clashing. Start coordinating.

title: End-to-End Drainage Design with Forma, InfoDrainage and Civil 3D
speakers: Javier Soto, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | Civil 3D | Forma | InfoDrainage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract:
InfoDrainage and Autodesk Forma will soon work together as part of a connected workflow for site drainage design. In this session, you'll work with Civil 3D and InfoDrainage models hosted in Forma, using live references such as surfaces and CAD background data to keep design information connected across applications. 

 Starting from a site design, you'll develop and optimize a drainage network in InfoDrainage, leveraging connected site data to accelerate hydrologic design. 

 The workflow continues with dynamic hydraulic simulation, exceedance assessment, and review of results, followed by compliance-ready reporting. The session concludes by synchronizing the completed drainage design back to Civil 3D, demonstrating a streamlined, connected workflow from site model to validated drainage design.

title: APS GraphQL in Production: AEC & MFG Patterns from Analytics to AI Agents
speakers: Kevin Vandecar, Sr Mgr, Technology Consulting, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | Docs | Forma | Fusion | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Autodesk's Data Model APIs for architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) and manufacturing (MFG) use GraphQL—unlocking richer integrations and AI-powered workflows. But GraphQL differs from REST in ways that quietly break production systems. Our team has shipped analytics dashboards, workflow automation, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, letting AI agents query live design data. We've hit the pitfalls so you don't have to. This session will deliver production-proven patterns: query design for AEC/MFG data models, partial-success error handling, enterprise authentication, mutation patterns, and AI-agent enablement via MCP. We’ll also highlight the underused GraphQL capabilities in the User Profile API. Real examples. Real lessons. Patterns that work from day one.

title: Bridging BIM and Hydraulics: Civil 3D and InfoWorks WS Pro for Smart Pressure Networks
speakers: Nathan Gerdts, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | Civil 3D | InfoWorks WS Pro | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Discover a new integration between Civil 3D and InfoWorks WS Pro software that connects BIM-based pressure pipe network design with detailed hydraulic analysis. See how bidirectional data exchange helps teams create constructable 3D networks using real parts while validating pressure, flow, and performance in InfoWorks WS Pro. Learn how this workflow improves design quality, reduces rework, and supports more-cost-effective outcomes. An industry expert will share real-world workflows, key benefits, lessons learned, and practical recommendations for successful adoption.

title: Agents of Change: Mastering Agentic AI and MCP Workflows for the Multi-Discipline AEC Firm
speakers: Michael Gustafson, SVP of Strategic Growth, QNECT LLC | Andrew Sundal, Structural Engineer/Comp Design Specialist, HGA
topics: Engineering service providers | Docs | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: The AEC industry is undergoing a paradigm shift where the lines between software developers, industry groups, and design firms are blurring. This session explores how AI strategies are being collaboratively shaped to move beyond basic research into high-impact implementation within multi-discipline engineering environments. We will examine the evolution of AI maturity, moving from foundational context engineering to the deployment of agentic services and Model Context Protocols (MCPs) that automate complex engineering tasks. Drawing on real examples, business leaders will gain a clear view of the emerging landscape and a practical way to balance AI’s potential against the demands of modern design practice.

title: Unified Production Environment: How AI and Data Transformed Ramboll’s Engineering
speakers: Marc Sleegers, Sr Principal, Business Consultant, Autodesk | David Thomson, Principle Product Owner Digital Design, Ramboll
topics: Buildings | Civil 3D | Forma | Model Coordination | Revit | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: Ramboll is reinventing itself as a data-centered, AI‑powered engineering firm. Through its Together for Better Outcomes (T4BO) partnership with Autodesk, Ramboll has productized a unified production environment (UPE) to accelerate AI adoption. By embedding the Autodesk AI tool Autodesk Assistant into daily workflows, productivity increases while more-sustainable client value is delivered. This session will show how data-centered design and AI‑assisted engineering are transforming project delivery and ways of working, reinforcing Ramboll’s role as a partner for sustainable change. We’ll share tangible outcomes, such as higher delivery quality, deeper sustainability insights, and increased project capacity without adding headcount.

title: Connecting AECO Workflows End-to-End with the Autodesk Forma Industry Cloud
speakers: Joey Matla, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk | Alejandra Beaujon, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Build | Docs | Forma | Model Coordination | Quantity Takeoff | AECO | Architecture
abstract: See how architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) teams connect planning, design, coordination, and construction workflows in a single AI and data-driven environment using the Autodesk Forma industry cloud. This technical and practical deep dive will walk through real workflows—from site planning in Autodesk Forma to design in Revit software, coordination in Forma Design Collaboration, and execution in Forma Build. Learn how data flows through Autodesk Data Management as a common data environment, preserving decisions across phases with practical examples. Explore practical AI-powered use cases such as rapid design iteration, automated analysis, and model-based coordination. And discover how to reduce manual work, improve collaboration, and implement connected workflows across the AECO lifecycle.

title: From Change to Clarity: Better Multidiscipline Coordination Model in Revit and Autodesk Forma Data Management
speakers: Leslaw Janus, Senior Principal Experience Designer, Autodesk | Mihaela Stan, Sr. Manager, Software Development, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | BIM Collaborate | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Discover how to effectively use Revit software’s Coordination Model Changes to monitor and manage updates across disciplines. In this hands-on session, architects and engineers will learn practical methods to detect, review, and act on element changes directly within their models. The session will cover step-by-step workflows for identifying additions, deletions, and modifications, using visual cues, filters, and structured object data. You’ll also explore how to assess geometry, properties, and transformations of updated elements to support better decision making. By the end, you’ll be able to reduce manual coordination effort, improve accuracy, and confidently integrate change tracking into your daily Revit workflows.

title: Building an AI-Ready BIM Data Backbone with Autodesk APS
speakers: Valeriia Vlasenko, Expert, Drees & Sommer | Moritz Mombour, Head of Digitalization EPCM REI, Drees & Sommer SE
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) organizations struggle to scale automation and AI because BIM data is fragmented, inconsistently governed, and tied to individual projects. This session will show how Drees & Sommer and AnkerDB built a centralized BIM data backbone using Autodesk Platform Services and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to enable reliable automation and consistent data quality at scale. The collaboration started as a rapid proof of concept at DevCon 2025, was validated across multiple projects, and is now scaling at the business-unit level. The session will explain how Autodesk Forma data, Autodesk Platform Services software, and downstream systems were connected to support automated validation, data enrichment, analytics, integrations, and AI-supported workflows for cost management and lifecycle assessment (LCA).

title: From Reality to Simulation: Capturing, Predicting & Replaying the Experience of Design with APS & AI
speakers: Kean Walmsley, Dir., Systems Design/Architecture Engrg, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | AECO | Software Development
abstract: How do you capture or predict the human experience of design and replay it to build empathy and drive better design decisions? This session will present a technical workflow spanning three research projects: real-world experience capture (The Bentway, Toronto), XR-based capture in virtual environments, and agentic simulation of human behavior. Learn how Autodesk Platform Services powers a system where human-experience data—whether captured using sensors, or in VR, or predicted using AI—can be replayed by designers to better appreciate the diversity of the human experience of design. We’ll explore the technology that will power future human-experience-driven workflows, from sensors and VR headsets to knowledge graphs and vision language models.

title: Eaton and Trane: 1-GW Data Center Codesign with BIM and Autodesk Forma
speakers: Justin Carron, Director of Segment Marketing, Eaton | Matt Lemay, Principal Account Executive, Enterprise, Autodesk | Victor Mirasola, General Manager - TRACE, Trane Technologies
topics: Buildings | Docs | Forma | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: This class will showcase how Trane, Eaton, and Autodesk enable collaborative codesign for gigawatt-scale data centers using BIM and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). You will see how data center reference kits become live, cloud-based environments for real-time collaboration between owners, engineers, and contractors. These environments centralize BIM and engineering data into a shared source of truth, enabling coordinated design of mechanical and electrical systems at massive scale. The session will demonstrate how Autodesk Forma Build supports structured codesign workflows, role-based collaboration, and asset-centered data models. This approach enables faster iteration, reduced risk, and scalable delivery for data centers of 1 gigawatt capacity.

title: AI Agents Meet APS: From Forma Building Design to Operational Digital Twin
speakers: Frank Otto, Product Owner - Platform, N+P Informationssysteme GmbH
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Autodesk Viewer | Docs | Forma | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Most digital twin projects stall at the same point: There’s no 3D model. Point cloud scanning takes weeks—too heavy for operational use cases like workplace booking or shop-floor monitoring. But we’ve found a faster path: Design buildings in Autodesk Forma Building Design, process them server-side via the Autodesk Platform Services Automation API for Revit, then use agentic AI workflows via Model Context Protocol (MCP) to enrich the model with workplaces and connected production data. It takes hours instead of months. Through video walk-throughs and live demos, we’ll show two use cases we’re deploying this year—replacing our own third-party desk-sharing tool, and building a manufacturing digital twin. You’ll leave with a replicable pattern for AI-enabled design-to-operate workflows.

title: From good intentions to sustainable decisions
speakers: Michelle Aguilar, CTO, VAPAR | Amarpreet Singh, Team Lead, North America, One Click LCA | Becky Burns, Sustainability Technical Partner Program Manager, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Info360 Asset | Insight | Revit | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: Most sustainability strategies never make it into daily work. Teams struggle to turn ambition into decisions, data flows, and repeatable processes. This session will explore three sustainability workflows that are actually working today: design-phase carbon estimation, AI-enabled inspection, and material selection informed by connected product and carbon data. We’ll examine how these workflows are structured, where they break, and what it takes to implement them across tools, teams, and data sources—drawing on examples from technology partners such as One Click LCA and VAPAR. You’ll leave with a practical framework for turning sustainability goals into operational workflows.

title: Integrated Real-Time MIDP using Autodesk Forma Reviews and Autodesk Platform Services
speakers: Mateusz Lukasiewicz, Associate Director - Digital Technology, KEO International Consultants
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Keeping a Master Information Delivery Plan (MIDP) accurate on live projects is one of the biggest challenges for BIM managers and project managers. Issuing incomplete or unreviewed deliverables puts contracts at risk. In this class, we’ll show how Autodesk Platform Services Webhooks and the Reviews tool in Autodesk Forma transform the MIDP into a live system that validates deliverable metadata against information requirements and confirms review status before submission. Using real project examples and proven metrics, we’ll show how this ensures 100% compliance with contractual deliverables, eliminates manual tracking, and mitigates the risk of noncompliant submissions. Join us to learn how to build a QA/QC system that keeps your MIDP accurate, connected, and audit ready.

title: Preparing LAX for the 2028 Olympics: AI-Powered Digital Twins with Autodesk Tandem MCP
speakers: James Awe, Sr Distinguished Architect, Head of Tandem Connect, Autodesk | Mingxun Zou, BIM Administrator, Los Angeles World Airports | Michael Beale, SWE, AWS
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Autodesk Viewer | Forma | Tandem Connect | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract: With the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics approaching, Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) is modernizing to handle millions of visitors. Managing billions in capital assets across disconnected BIM, CMMS, and GIS systems is no longer viable. In this session, Mingxun Zou, James Awe and Michael Beale will reveal how Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA) built an AI-powered digital twin platform. We'll demonstrate the following: An Autodesk Tandem MCP server enabling natural language queries, a Python/Grasshopper automation extracting asset attributes to GeoJSON, and a real-time MapLibre visualization. Building on an Esri Dev Summit 2026 presentation, we'll show the evolution from manual CAD exports to AI-driven facility intelligence. Through live coding, you'll build the same integrations—preparing LAX for its Olympic moment.

title: Break the Desktop Barrier: Dynamo in the Cloud for Scalable Revit and Civil3D Automation
speakers: John (JT) Pierson, Product Manager, Autodesk | Achintya Bhat, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Civil 3D | Dynamo | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Ever ran the same Dynamo graph across multiple projects and waited hours while Revit or Civil 3D software was locked? What if you could hand it off instead? This session will dive into how Dynamo Switchboard enables cloud execution of Dynamo graphs across projects at scale. Rather than running workflows locally or building custom pipelines with Design Automation, you can now execute graphs through a simple, player-like interface. Learn how to run batch automations across multiple models without opening host applications, and review results through logs and the Dynamo graph web viewer. Through live demos, you’ll see how to launch runs and interpret results. We’ll also briefly explore connecting workflows with Autodesk Platform Services and AEC Data Models.

title: Powering Paperless Contractor Submissions and Tracking Across 50 Million Square Feet with Autodesk Forma and Data Analytics
speakers: Japneesh Singh, Deputy Manager, DLF | Ritesh Mittal, General Manager, DLF Limited
topics: Buildings | BIM 360 Build | Build | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Disconnected contractor submissions and manual tracking reduce visibility, slow approvals, and limit scalability. In this session, you’ll learn how a paperless submission framework was deployed across a 50-million-square-foot portfolio using Autodesk Forma. Integrated workflows were established using Submittals, RFIs, and Forms to standardize contractor interactions, enable consistent data capture, and ensure full traceability. Through APIs, disparate data sources were unified and transformed into intelligent data models that power advanced dashboards. Discover how this approach delivers real-time submission tracking, improved transparency, and faster data-driven decisions—providing a scalable blueprint for digital transformation at an enterprise level.

title: ​From Chaos to Control: ACC Model Coordination and API Strategies for Infrastructure Projects
speakers: Maria Albízuri, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | Adrian Fernandez Sanchez, Product Owner Autodesk Transport, Rambøll Norge
topics: Civil infrastructure | Docs | Model Coordination | Navisworks Manage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: In large-scale infrastructure, "coordination chaos" is a common reality. When teams use different tools and inconsistent methods, design mistakes are often caught too late. This leads to expensive rework, missed deadlines, and increased project risk. As projects grow across disciplines, keeping everyone aligned becomes a massive challenge. In this session, we’ll share how Ramboll tamed this complexity by building a standardized, scalable framework using Autodesk Forma industry cloud (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Using the 2025 IFC Viewer, Autodesk Platform Services, and Insight dashboards, Ramboll moved from disconnected software to a single, unified system. We’ve aligned our digital process with ISO 19650 to ensure data moves smoothly from one project phase to the next.

title: From Messy to Meaningful: Ground Truth, Update-Ready Site Context in Revit
speakers: Joseph Huang, Principal, Architect, BIM Design Team Lead, Stantec | Raghavendra Bhat, Principal, Sr. BIM Integration Specialist, Stantec
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma | InfraWorks | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Accurate site context is essential for coordination, yet many teams struggle with fragile or inconsistent site models in Revit. This session presents reliable workflows for building and maintaining site context using common upstream sources, including Forma Site Design generated Revit files, Civil 3D published surfaces, and native Revit tools such as TopoSolids and Building Pads. The focus is on stability and change management – showing how to keep site models update ready as upstream data evolves, while supporting design development, visualization, and downstream coordination with minimal rework or model failure. We'll walk through four practical workflows for bringing site context into Revit and discuss where each one shines and where each one breaks.

title: Design Fast, Validate Smart: Extending InfoDrainage with Parametric Workflows in Civil 3D and InfoWorks ICM to Deliver Multiple Benefits
speakers: Juan Aguirrebengoa, Principal Civil Engineer CEng MICE, Mott MacDonald | Pablo Souto, Global Discipline Leader - Water, Mott MacDonald Ltd
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfoDrainage | InfoWorks ICM | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Early-stage drainage design prioritizes speed, using simplified assumptions to test options quickly. However, challenges such as combined sewer overflows (CSOs), flooding, biodiversity loss, and wider community outcomes are increasingly interconnected and require a more systems-based approach that extends beyond the traditional boundaries of the water sector. This session explores how connected digital workflows can support the identification, design, and validation of sustainable drainage interventions that deliver multiple benefits. Using an anonymized case study, attendees will see how opportunities can be rapidly explored through parametric site-design workflows in Civil 3D and InfoDrainage, then assessed through system-scale modelling in InfoWorks ICM to understand impacts on flood risk and CSO frequency, volume, and timing. The session focuses on balancing speed, rigour, and confidence in decision-making, helping practitioners understand how technology, systems thinking, and proportionate modelling can support more resilient and integrated outcomes for communities and the environment.

title: Integrating Nature-Based Solutions in Civil 3D and
speakers: Carlos Rogeliz, Technical Director – N4W Facility, The Nature Conservancy
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfraWorks | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) are reshaping how civil teams deliver resilient water infrastructure. Yet integrating watershed-scale insights into detailed design remains a challenge. This session will show how The Nature Conservancy applied targeted training and InfraWorks and Civil 3D software to connect regional watershed analysis with site-level engineering workflows. Learn how to translate watershed data into design inputs, develop NbS concepts into constructible models, and maintain data continuity across planning and design phases. See how connected workflows improved cross-team collaboration, enabled earlier decision making, and reduced project risk in real-world water infrastructure projects.

title: Dr. Vibe: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Start Loving Autodesk Platform Services
speakers: Winston Pagliaro, Civil Infrastructure BIM and VDC Specialist, HNTB
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: This is a tale from a BIM manager’s foray into vibe coding—going from having no coding experience to building web applications that tap into the Autodesk Platform Services APIs to supercharge the capabilities of our Autodesk Forma-based CAD managers. Have you been curious about Autodesk Platform Services but haven’t pulled the trigger because you’re not “a developer”? With Dr. Claude’s help, you can be! Come to this session to learn tips on diving into the world of Autodesk Platform Services and large language models (LLMs). We’ll share lessons learned on working hand in hand with these LLMs in a safe and efficient way so that you can also share in this digital boon.

title: Predict Before You Model: How We Built an ML-Powered MEP Estimating Bot Trained on 300+Real Projects
speakers: Gustavo Gusmão, BIM Solution Architect, ENG | Gabriel Campos, BIM Solution Architect, ENG BIM
topics: Civil infrastructure | BIM 360 Docs | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: What if you could generate a reliable MEP cost estimate before modeling a single element in Revit software? That’s exactly what we built: a Python-based estimation bot trained on more than 300 real MEP projects from our historical data. Instead of relying on disconnected spreadsheets or manual takeoffs, the bot uses pattern recognition to generate estimates at the proposal stage before BIM begins. Our solution achieves more than 95% accuracy versus final costs, and it reduces estimation time by more than 70%. In this session, we’ll show how we structured the data, trained the model, and integrated it into our workflow. You’ll leave this session with a practical framework to turn historical data into a predictive asset.

title: Turning BIM into AI-Powered Digital Twins: Real-Time Predictive Maintenance with IoT
speakers: Tolga Bozkurt, AI Digital Twin & IoT Specialist, Metro Istanbul
topics: Civil infrastructure | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Docs | InfraWorks | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Intelligent models are often underused after design, remaining static and disconnected from real-world operations. This session will present a real-world deployment in a metropolitan rail system, where BIM is transformed into a live, AI-powered predictive maintenance platform. Using IFC-based workflows derived from Revit software, models are converted into lightweight, web-ready formats and integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data at the asset level. An AI layer enables anomaly detection and failure prediction, reducing unplanned downtime and improving maintenance efficiency. You will gain a practical understanding of how to extend BIM into an operational digital twin and implement scalable, data-driven maintenance strategies.

title: Data-Driven Water Utilities: BIM-GIS Validation and Digital Twins at Gruppo CAP
speakers: Antonio Devito, Technical Director, One team | Giuseppe Barberio, Head Of Digital Engineering & BIM, Gruppo CAP
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma | InfoWorks ICM | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: Inconsistent data across the water lifecycle hinders operational resilience. This session will present the technical framework developed for Gruppo CAP (Milan) to bridge this gap using Autodesk Forma as a unified cloud environment. Starting from scan-to-BIM modeling of a water plant, we’ll detail a custom validation engine built on Autodesk Platform Services that automates model checking against asset information requirem`ents (AIR) standards via specialized scripts. We’ll explore how validated BIM data flows into Esri Utility Network to fuel InfoWorks ICM solutions for advanced hydraulic modeling. You’ll evaluate how this scalable architecture, in a large-scale utility, uses Power BI to transform data into a simulation-ready digital twin for smarter asset management.

title: From Pilot to Competitive Advantage: Scaling Generative Design with Autodesk Forma and Infraspace
speakers: Kristoffer Spendrup Bugge, Digital Transformation Leader, Norconsult | Andreas Kjølseth, Founder & CEO, Infraspace
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma | Navisworks Manage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract:
Infrastructure projects face increasing demands for faster delivery, lower costs, and more sustainable outcomes. Meeting these demands requires teams to work smarter, deliver higher-quality designs, and make better decisions within tight project deadlines.

Following last year's session, Infraspace and Norconsult will share how they have moved from promising pilots to production use of generative design in real transportation and energy projects.

Powered by Infraspace and integrated with Autodesk Forma, they will demonstrate how engineering teams can streamline planning and early design, and reduce iteration time from weeks to minutes through automated generation of design alternatives for roads and other infrastructure assets.

Through real-world project examples, you will learn how generative design augments engineering expertise, improves project outcomes, and provides a competitive advantage through faster, better-informed design decisions.

title: End-to-End New Geolocation Solution Across Autodesk Platforms: From Civil 3D to Revit
speakers: Frank Huang, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Geolocation is essential for accurate positioning, data integration, and interoperability across architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) workflows. This session will introduce core concepts such as coordinate systems, datums, and spatial references—and show how they’re applied across Autodesk platforms. You will learn how to create and manage coordinate systems in Civil 3D software, define geolocation in Civil 3D and AutoCAD software, and understand how these support geographic information system (GIS) integration. The session will also cover legacy and modern geolocation workflows in Revit software, highlighting improvements in model alignment and interoperability. By connecting workflows across Civil 3D and Revit, this class will provide practical guidance on maintaining consistent geospatial positioning throughout a project’s lifecycle.

title: Scaling Rail Data at MRS Logística: From Fragmented Workflows to Real-Time Intelligence
speakers: Rafael Braida, Infrastructure Specialist - BIM Manager, MRS Logística
topics: Civil infrastructure | Build | Docs | Forma | Insight | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: In a reality of more than 200 railway infrastructure projects running simultaneously, data fragmentation is not a risk—it’s inevitable. This technical deep dive will show you how MRS Logística tackles this challenge by refining BIM requirements and building a standardized common data environment (CDE) in Autodesk Forma. From issues and daily reports to audits, model coordination, cost, and schedule, workflows are structured and connected at scale. Discover how Autodesk Assistant enables structured analysis and how the Insight Builder tool turns connected data into real-time intelligence—driving consistency, reliability, and faster decision making across projects.

title: IFC 4.3 for Infrastructure: From Export to Digital Delivery
speakers: Salwan Abbosh, IDT Lead, Ramboll | Morgan Smith, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | BIM Collaborate Pro | Civil 3D | Cloud Worksharing | Docs | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: IFC 4.3 enables open data exchange for infrastructure, yet many teams struggle to turn IFC exports into information that projects can rely on. This session will move beyond export steps and focus on using IFC effectively on infrastructure projects. You’ll learn how IFC 4.3 works once it leaves Civil 3D software, including how models are governed, versioned, reviewed, and trusted. Topics will include model view definitions, the IFC Reference View for civil infrastructure, and common mistakes that reduce value. The session will also introduce Autodesk Forma Data Management as a practical way to manage IFC delivery at scale, supporting controlled sharing and review. You’ll leave with guidance on positioning IFC as a trusted project resource.

title: From Borehole to Building: Advanced Ground Modeling Directly in Civil 3D with GeoDin Ground
speakers: Devrez Karabacak, Head of Product, GeoDin, Fugro
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Ground models are the missing link between site investigation and infrastructure design. Engineers make critical decisions on alignments, crossings, and foundations while the subsurface remains a black box—data arriving late, locked in static reports, or in formats incompatible with the design environment. GeoDin Ground for Civil 3D software is changing that. In this session, we’ll present the latest advances in 3D ground modeling inside Civil 3D, including direct AGS file ingestion and autoconversion—eliminating the need for a preexisting database and letting teams start directly with received data. You’ll see the ground take shape inside Civil 3D, evolving into a 3D model that drives critical design choices and reduces project risk from day one.

title: From Innovyze to Tandem: Digital Twins & AI for Climate‑Resilient Water Infrastructure
speakers: Priyanka Talkal, Associate-Water, WSP
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfoWater Pro | InfoWorks ICM | Tandem Connect | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Water infrastructure is entering a decisive decade. In 2026, utilities face climate volatility, aging assets, regulatory pressure, and rising expectations for resilient, transparent service. Traditional approaches based on static hydraulic models and reactive operations are no longer sufficient. This keynote will explore how connected digital twins and AI are reshaping water infrastructure across the full lifecycle—from planning and design to operations and maintenance. It will present a practical workflow showing how Innovyze modeling outputs evolve into a live operational digital twin in Autodesk Tandem software, enabling continuity from design to asset maintenance, and supporting predictive, risk‑based decision making.

title: AI Data Check for Civil 3D: Validating Models Against Project Requirements via APS
speakers: Mohamad M. KASSIR, Regional Digital Manager, Egis
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Docs | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: This session will present a platform built through vibe coding using Autodesk Platform Services APIs, Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), and AI code generation to automate the full data validation cycle for Civil 3D models. The platform pulls files from Forma, extracts metadata via the Model Derivative API, and ingests project requirement PDFs. An AI layer converts PDFs into structured validation rules, then runs them against the model to produce a detailed conformity report, flagging gaps, mismatches, and missing attributes without manual checks. The session will also cover key lessons from development, AI-driven architecture, and real-world use cases showing practical impact at scale.

title: Better Together: Drainage Design Best Practices with InfoDrainage and Civil 3D
speakers: Hunter Sparks, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfoDrainage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract:
With the release of drainage tools for Civil 3D 2026, users are asking: How do these tools fit into Autodesk’s drainage design ecosystem? 

This session provides a clear, practical comparison of drainage tools for Civil 3D and InfoDrainage, including how each solution integrates into your workflows. This session will demonstrate how to combine Autodesk tools with open-source solutions and LLM’s to unlock new possibilities. We streamline the drainage design process by using API and Civil 3D tools for catchment delineation. 

Walk away with a practical understanding of the tools, with the ability to navigate Autodesk’s evolving drainage design landscape and leverage a hybrid ecosystem for scalable, intelligent design.

title: Beyond Automation: AI Collaboration with Autodesk Assistant
speakers: Alex Lobos, Director, School of Design, Rochester Institute of Technology
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | D&M | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: This session will demonstrate how the recently introduced Autodesk Fusion AI Assistant enhances product development. AI Assistant accelerates early-stage design exploration, development, and fabrication by translating text into CAD, automating workflows, and accelerating implementation. Case studies of consumer products will illustrate how AI Assistant improves efficiency, when traditional methods are more effective, and how to best combine both. The session will cover prompt engineering techniques that improve output quality. By adopting these workflows, teams can reduce repetitive tasks, improve iteration speed, and focus human expertise on higher-value design decisions, ultimately achieving faster, more informed results.

title: Beyond the BOM: Using PLM to Drive Modern Product Management
speakers: Gus Quade, Sr. Technical Sales Specialist,  Fusion PLM, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Manage | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Product lifecycle management (PLM) is often treated as a system of record for BOMs—but leading teams are using it to drive product strategy, execution, and cross-functional alignment. In this session, we’ll show how to evolve PLM into a product management backbone that connects engineering, operations, and business decisions. You’ll learn practical workflows for managing product definitions, changes, and lifecycle data in a way that improves visibility, reduces delays, and enables better decision making. Walk away with patterns you can apply immediately to move beyond BOM management and unlock real business value from PLM.

title: Your Bottlenecks Are Showing: 10 Lessons from Thousands of Product Design and Development Companies
speakers: Jason Lichtman, Principal Technical Specialist,  Fusion, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Design Extension | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | Fusion Simulation Extension | Inventor Professional | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Designing great products is difficult. Successfully taking those products to market on time and under budget is even harder. After working with thousands of product design and engineering businesses, clear patterns have emerged between teams that struggle and those that consistently deliver. In this fast-paced 30-minute session, we’ll break down 10 key lessons that separate successful teams from the rest. We’ll dive into what worked for them as well as what didn’t. You’ll leave with practical strategies to reduce delays, improve alignment, and move from concept to production with greater speed and increased confidence. If you’re a business owner or business leader who wants to fast-track your company’s success, this session is for you.

title: From Prompt to Production: Designing Furniture at the Speed of AI with Fusion
speakers: Melike Ozdemir, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Manage | Fusion Nesting and Fabrication Extension | Fusion Operations | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Designing and manufacturing furniture often relies on disconnected tools and repetitive work. This session will explain how to create a connected, end-to-end workflow using the Autodesk Fusion platform. Starting from simple prompts, Autodesk Assistant accelerates design and enables fast creation of parametric furniture models. This workflow will show how models are refined for engineering, prepared for manufacturing with integrated CAM tools, and transferred to production using Autodesk Fusion Operations software—while Autodesk Fusion Manage ensures process and data continuity from request to delivery. It will also highlight how design intent is preserved and how a single data environment reduces errors.

title: Preparing Construction Data for AI
speakers: Matt Fern, National Digital Engineering Manager, Stowe Australia
topics: Construction services | Build | Docs | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Everyone wants AI in construction. Almost no one has data ready for it. Poor structure, inconsistent metadata, and fragmented workflows hold most teams back. This session will share real-world lessons from Stowe Australia, implementing Autodesk Forma as a common data environment (CDE) to fix that problem. Learn how ISO 19650 principles, standardized templates, and disciplined workflows turn messy project information into structured, usable data. The result? A scalable foundation for analytics, automation, and AI across projects, teams, and the wider business.

title: Industrialized Construction at Scale: Data-Driven Sustainability for Modular Systems
speakers: Mergim Hoti, BIM Specialist, Max Bögl Nederland B.V.
topics: Construction services | Revit | AECO | Impact & Sustainability | Industrialized Construction
abstract: How can industrialized construction, intelligent data, and integrated workflows turn sustainability from a reporting burden into a scalable design strategy? In this session for architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) leaders and delivery teams, Max Bögl Group will share how one company manages the value chain—from raw material sourcing and design to off-site production, delivery, assembly, and maintenance—to deliver modular buildings and bridge systems with measurable sustainability outcomes. As we use projects from Germany and the Netherlands, you’ll see how standardized, parametric products, connected models, and automated assessments help teams compare options faster, respond to strict European requirements, and build the data foundation for future AI-supported design decisions.

title: Digital Project Delivery, Forma Build Implementation
speakers: Rania Hassan, VDC Regional Manager, Ellisdon
topics: Construction services | Build | Forma | Model Coordination | Revit | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Our session will show how Autodesk Forma was implemented and governed on a live health care project, adapting workflows to project‑specific needs. We will demonstrate the application of standards during active delivery to maintain consistency and data integrity while teams adopt the platform and evolve digital practices in real time. You’ll learn how collaboration was structured across Autodesk, construction technology, operations, and BIM by deploying two Autodesk Forma Build projects to separate design coordination from construction execution, alongside targeted training. We’ll also cover license provisioning, role‑based access, content ownership alignment, and Power BI dashboards that deliver actionable insights for better decisions.

title: Connected Carbon Data for Construction: API-Powered Decisions at Scale
speakers: Marta Bouchard, Dir., Sustainability Solutions, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Forma | Quantity Takeoff | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Construction teams face growing pressure to make early, data-driven carbon decisions. Yet fragmented regional data sets limit consistency and scalability across tools. This session will explore how TBI, a leading construction firm, is advancing end-to-end carbon assessment by connecting data across planning, design, and preconstruction workflows. Using Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights (Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Forma Takeoff) and the Sustainability Data API, TBI will demonstrate how API-powered strategies enable early-stage carbon comparisons across multiple regions, reduce manual data handling, and scale assessments across projects. You’ll gain a strategic framework for driving better, data-informed decisions through connected, scalable carbon workflows.

title: How Cleveland Construction Added AI-Powered Submittal and Drawing Reviews to Autodesk Forma
speakers: Elliot Christiansen, Sr. Vice President of Operations, Cleveland Construction, Inc.
topics: Construction services | None | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: When Cleveland Construction migrated from Procore to Autodesk, company leaders saw an opportunity to build an intelligent document pipeline and agentic workflows on top of the wealth of data they run their business on in Autodesk. In this session, Elliot Christiansen, SVP of operations at Cleveland Construction, will share how his team configured their Autodesk environment to enable AI-powered workflows that automatically review submittals against specs and new bulletins against previous ones. Brandon Ramsey, VP of customer success from Trunk Tools, an App Marketplace Partner, will join Elliot to share Cleveland's winning playbook to transition from handshakes to driving deep adoption across their project teams.

title: Builders in the AI Loop: How We Accelerate Construction and Preserve Judgement
speakers: Richard Antczak, Senior Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: AI is increasing output across construction teams, but many leaders are seeing a quieter problem: more-polished work, less ownership. With more options come harder decisions. This strategy talk will use one concrete story and a practical framework to show how to adopt AI without eroding the judgment that experienced builders, designers, and owners have earned the hard way. You’ll learn how to separate AI-assisted production from the human decision making that takes decades to develop. We’ll discuss how leaders in the industry add thinking checkpoints within workflows that make teams faster while preserving their precious (and playful) cognition.

title: EDU1455 Unlock the power of AI for AutoCAD 2027 Toolsets
speakers: Lina El-Khoury, BIM Strategy & Digital Solutions Consultant, LEK | Hung Nguyen, Technical Consultant, SolidCAD
topics: Education | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Mechanical | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Fusion | Revit | EDU | AutoCAD & General Design
abstract: Unlock the full potential of AI in AutoCAD 2027 toolsets. Building on our AU 2024 award-winning class, this session will explore how AI-powered tools revolutionize CAD, driving unmatched efficiency. Experience how AutoCAD 2027 software’s AI automates complex workflows—from intelligent object recognition and predictive drafting to real-time generative design. With automated dimensioning, predictive error-correction, and material optimization, you’ll slash design cycles. Use AI-driven simulation to stress-test designs against real-world scenarios, ensuring peak performance. Transform your workflow with seamless, AI-enhanced interoperability that bridges multidisciplinary teams. Future-proof your craft with smarter, faster, and more creative CAD.

title: Don’t AI everything: Hybrid automation with APS and Revit.
speakers: Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk | Neil Lee, Director, Design Automation Systems Ltd | Will North, Director, Design Automation Systems Ltd
topics: Building products and fabrication | Autodesk Platform Services | Revit | D&M | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Automation specialists are increasingly tasked with finding areas to implement AI. But how do we decide when AI is the correct tool and when deterministic automation serves better? Through a live demo of an AI-augmented building regulation compliance checker running on Autodesk Platform Services, we will explore a practical hybrid framework. The Automation API and Revit software handle rule evaluation through a deterministic engine. Large language models (LLMs) extract compliance rules from regulation documentation and explain failures in natural language. And the Viewer SDK provides visual context. We’ll demonstrate a human-in-the-loop approach and show how AI architecture adapts rapidly when regulations change or new markets require new rule sets.

title: Rule-Driven Building Design: Connecting Structural Analysis, Autodesk Forma, and Informed Design
speakers: Steve Dewitt, Independent Contractor, Autodesk
topics: Building products and fabrication | Dynamo | Forma | Informed Design | Inventor | Revit | D&M | Industrialized Construction | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Learn how to automate decision making in type 5 designs by connecting structural analysis, product data, and off-site construction workflows across the Autodesk platform. This class will demonstrate how to integrate a Structural Analysis Design Engine (SADE) with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to automate shear wall placement, then propagate those requirements through Informed Design to drive product behavior. Using the Informed Design API and parametric logic authored in Inventor software, we’ll embed structural intelligence into configurable wall panels assigned to Autodesk Forma masses—enabling consistent, data-driven outcomes from early design through fabrication.

title: From Fragmented Workflows to a Digital Thread: Scaling Modular Construction with PLM at Faith
speakers: Darren Hartenstine, Senior Solutions Consultant, Symetri USA | Caleb Goins, Application Support Manager, FTI
topics: Building products and fabrication | Fusion Manage | Vault Professional | D&M | Industrialized Construction | PLM
abstract: Faith Technologies Incorporated (FTI) is rapidly scaling its modular construction and manufacturing operations. But disconnected systems, manual workflows, and poor data governance created barriers to growth. In partnership with Symetri, Faith is implementing a PLM-driven digital thread connecting Vault software, Autodesk Fusion Manage, Inventor software, and architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) systems. This transformation enables centralized data, automated design-to-fabrication workflows, and enterprise collaboration. This session will explore how Faith is moving from siloed processes to a connected, scalable ecosystem to accelerate productization and support rapid growth.

title: From Capture to AI: How Data Enrichment Unlocks the Value of Motion
speakers: Olivier Zurcher, Animation Researcher (Technical Animator), Autodesk
topics: Film and TV | Flow Production Tracking | Maya | M&E | Future Industry Innovations
abstract: AI-powered animation is only as good as the data behind it, but most motion data wasn’t designed for AI. In this session, we’ll demonstrate a projection-mapped capture app that guides performers in real time to produce more-structured motion. As well as how Label Maker, a tool integrated within the Autodesk ecosystem, uses AI to turn raw motion data and videos into richly tagged, reusable data sets. You will walk away with a clearer picture of how to make motion data actually usable for AI, and how to rethink their pipelines to get there. The real value of motion data isn’t in the capture—it’s in the enrichment.

title: Unlocking Connected Workflows: Vault Connector for Forma and Fusion Manage
speakers: Younes Yammouri, Director, Product Management, Autodesk | Senthil Kumar, Sr. Manager, Software Development, Autodesk
topics: Industrial machinery | Forma | Fusion Manage | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: This session will explore how the Vault Connector enables connected workflows between Vault, Autodesk Forma, and Autodesk Fusion Manage, helping organizations bridge the gap between engineering data and enterprise lifecycle processes. We’ll begin with an overview of the latest enhancements to the Vault Connector for Fusion Manage, highlighting improvements introduced in recent Vault releases. We’ll then move into a deep dive on the new Vault Connector for Autodesk Forma, exploring how it enables seamless data exchange between design environments and cloud platforms. You will gain insights into integration workflows and real-world use cases. The session will conclude with an interactive Q&A session.

title: Unlocking Autodesk Assistant: Secrets of World-Class Data Management with Vault, Common Data, & PLM
speakers: Allen Gager, Applications Expert - MSD, Rand | Tyson Copa, Platform Specialist, IMAGINiT Technologies
topics: Industrial machinery | Docs | Fusion Manage | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | Product Development
abstract: World-class implementations don’t happen by accident—they’re built on deep knowledge of how to make Autodesk tools work together intelligently. In this no-fluff session, Allen Gager will reveal the secrets every expert knows for maximizing Autodesk Assistant across the Autodesk platform while building a robust common data environment (CDE) powered by Vault and Vault PLM software. Discover how to use Autodesk Assistant (now integrated in Vault 2027, Autodesk Fusion, AutoCAD, Autodesk Forma, and beyond) as your always-on, context-aware AI partner. Learn natural language techniques to find files faster, automate routine tasks, get in-context guidance, query project data, and even drive simple automations—without ever leaving your workflow.

title: From Plant Design to Product Passport: Extending PLM and Autodesk Fusion Manage Across the Full Lifecycle
speakers: Andreas Nicolescu, Principal Account Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Industrial machinery | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Docs | Fusion Manage | D&M | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: By 2027, every manufacturer selling into the European market will be required to provide a Digital Product Passport (DPP)—and most are not ready. This session will show how Autodesk Fusion Manage software can close that gap, while also solving a longer-standing problem: disconnected data between process plant design and PLM. You'll see how equipment data from AutoCAD Plant 3D projects on Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) can automatically populate Fusion Manage BOMs—eliminating manual handoffs between plant design and PLM. And you’ll see how that same structure can generate EU-compliant DPPs on demand, without duplicate data entry—connecting project context from Autodesk Forma with product lifecycle data where it belongs. Both extensions are built on Autodesk Platform Services APIs and demonstrated live.

title: AI Data Ready: From Design to Construction to Operations
speakers: Gilbert Kwan, BIM Business Process Owner, Amgen | Stacy Goins, Senior Manager, Engineering Projects, Amgen | Victor Strausbaugh, Engineering Projects Sr Mgr, Amgen
topics: Life sciences manufacturing | Assemble Products | BIM 360 Build | Revit Cloud Worksharing | D&M | Construction Management
abstract: Design and construction projects involve diverse tools and stakeholders across phases, creating fragmented, inconsistent data and documentation. This session will show how we establish an AI-ready data foundation from day one using the Autodesk Forma Assets module, enabling a continuous digital thread from design through construction to operations. We’ll demonstrate how standardized data from Revit models and equipment lists—aligned with CSI MasterFormat and UniFormat—connects design, procurement, project controls, commissioning, and operations. By treating models and metadata as lifecycle deliverables, we reuse and enrich data instead of recreating it—with Forma serving as the central platform for integrated, reliable, AI-ready project data.

title: Building the Digital Thread: Connecting CRM, Vault PLM, MES, and ERP from Order to Delivery
speakers: Christian Gessner, Head of Research and Innovation, coolOrange S.r.l. | Markus Gundersen, Business Manager, COOLORANGE NORTHERN EUROPE
topics: Manufacturing Other | Autodesk Platform Services | Fusion Manage | Fusion Operations | Inventor | Vault Professional | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Manufacturing organizations often struggle with disconnected systems across sales, engineering, and production. This class will show how Vault PLM software forms the backbone of a connected digital thread spanning customer relationship management (CRM), CAD, product data management (PDM), product lifecycle management (PLM), manufacturing execution systems (MES), and enterprise resource planning (ERP). Starting from a CRM order, we’ll demonstrate rule-based CAD automation, engineering data management in Vault, and seamless Item and BOM synchronization into Autodesk Fusion Manage—driven by the built-in connector. Design reviews are handled through a web interface powered by the Vault Data API, manufacturing execution runs in Autodesk Fusion Operations, and business data flows into ERP—event-driven and AI-assisted. See how Vault PLM bridges engineering and enterprise to streamline the journey, from order to delivery.

title: The Truth Is Out There, But So Is the Nonsense: AI Tips & Tricks for iLogic and the Inventor API
speakers: Curtis Waguespack, Design Automation Solutions Architect, Topper Industries
topics: Manufacturing Other | Inventor | Inventor Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: You've seen how iLogic can tame tedious tasks and make you more efficient. Now AI promises to go even further, writing your rules, navigating the Inventor API, and transforming your automation overnight. Sounds great, right? Here's the truth: Great results from AI are out there, but so is the AI-induced nonsense. You might have seen AI confidently generate code that doesn't work. Or watched it invent API methods that don't exist. The promise is real. But so are the hallucinations, the dead ends, and the frustrations of vibe coding. Come to this session to cut through the hype with tips, tricks, and insights for getting real results from AI, knowing when to trust it, when to push back, and how to build automation that fulfills the prompt.
