title: Engineering Copilot: Real AI Workflows for Vault, BOMs, and Manufacturing Data
speakers: Christian Gessner, Head of Research and Innovation, coolOrange S.r.l. | Tyler Warner, Sr. Software Developer, IMAGINiT Technologies
topics: Manufacturing Other | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: AI is everywhere—but how does it actually help engineering teams working with CAD, BOMs, and Vault software? This class will demonstrate real-world applications of AI on top of Vault, focusing on engineering and manufacturing processes. Using live examples, we’ll show how structured data such as eBOMs and mBOMs can be interpreted, transformed, and enriched using AI while keeping engineers in control. You’ll see how natural-language interfaces, rule-based automation, and AI-assisted decision making support tasks like BOM transformation, process planning, and validation. The session will highlight proven architectures, integration patterns, and limitations when introducing AI into Vault-based environments.

title: Accelerating Manufacturing Design: Unlocking the Top 10 Hidden Productivity Tools in AutoCAD Mechanical
speakers: Sridhar Subramani, Sr. Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Mechanical | D&M | AutoCAD & General Design
abstract: Most manufacturing teams use AutoCAD daily but overlook the AutoCAD Mechanical toolset included in their subscription. This session will showcase 10 productivity features that cut repetitive drafting: intelligent commands with associative centerlines, automated hidden-line management, parametric content libraries, power dimensioning with tolerances, detail view automation, GD&T and welding symbols, integrated BOM with balloons, enterprise standards enforcement, built-in engineering calculators, and associative 2D documentation of Inventor 3D models. Through live demos and real-world scenarios, you’ll gain hands-on techniques to reduce cycle times, enforce ISO/ANSI compliance automatically, and bridge 2D-3D workflows using tools you already own.

title: From Inventor Design to Machined Part: Building a Real Digital Thread with Autodesk Fusion CAM
speakers: Edward Rose, Client Success Manager - Adoption Programs, Symetri
topics: Manufacturing Other | Fusion | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | Fusion Nesting and Fabrication Extension | Inventor | Vault Professional | D&M | Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: In this technical deep dive, we’ll walk through a real machined project designed in Inventor and programmed in Autodesk Fusion Manufacturing Extension. Follow the complete workflow: creating and iterating the part in Inventor, uploading to Fusion, applying toolpaths, generating G-code, and efficiently updating toolpaths after design changes using simple refreshes. We’ll cover both the cloud approach (AnyCAD linked references and Desktop Connector) and the enterprise version using Vault Professional software for controlled releases and revision management. We’ll share the actual files, challenges encountered, key lessons, and measurable time savings. You’ll leave with actionable steps to build an effective digital thread between design and manufacturing teams.

title: Building the Digital Thread: M2X’s Path from Engineering to Manufacturing Scale
speakers: Justin Johnson, M2X Energy | Nicholas Schwartz, Chief Manufacturing Officer at M2X Energy, M2X Energy
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Fusion Manage | Inventor | Vault PLM | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: What breaks when a 10-person engineering team becomes a 70-person manufacturing organization? This session will explore M2X’s real-world journey scaling with Inventor, Vault, AutoCAD Plant 3D, and Autodesk Fusion Manage software. Learn how the team transitioned from ad hoc design workflows to structured data management and a connected PDM/PLM strategy. We’ll cover how to time tool adoption, avoid common scaling missteps, and enable cross-functional collaboration between engineering and production. You’ll gain practical frameworks to structure product data, build a digital thread, and support rapid growth—while improving quality, reducing rework, and maintaining control across the product lifecycle.

title: Vault on Autopilot: AI-Driven PDM Automation Across Lifecycle, Revisions, and ERP
speakers: Enrique Galicia Tovar, Director of Innovations and AI, AvantLeap | Jose Baquero, Senior Consultant MGF - AI Solutions, Avant Leap
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | Inventor | Revit | Vault Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Vault Professional software manages thousands of engineering workflows—but property assignment, lifecycle transitions, revision management, approval routing, and enterprise resource planning (ERP) synchronization remain manual. Every operation is predictable and rule-governed. This session will deliver AU 2026's Intelligent Data theme in practice: an AI agent connected to the Vault API monitoring product data management (PDM) events and executing the right action autonomously via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) agent loop. The large language model (LLM) interprets PDM state against business rules, and the API executes without manual intervention. In controlled workflows, this has reduced administrative overhead by up to 70%. You’ll leave with an ROI-prioritized implementation road map.

title: From AutoCAD Toolsets to Inventor: Enabling Connected Workflows with Desktop Connector and Forma
speakers: Chaitanya Belsare, Sr Associate, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Sagar G S, Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Electrical | AutoCAD Mechanical | Forma Data Management Essentials | Inventor | D&M | AutoCAD & General Design
abstract: This session will demonstrate how to connect AutoCAD Electrical electromechanical workflows, AutoCAD Mechanical linked with Inventor software, and factory design workflows for seamless data exchange. Learn how to integrate layouts and models across tools, enabling accurate coordination from schematics to 3D design. Discover how cloud-based solutions like Desktop Connector and Autodesk Forma improve collaboration, maintain data continuity, and reduce rework. Through practical examples, see how connected workflows enhance efficiency and accelerate project delivery.

title: Save Time and Improve Quality: Dynamic Factory Design with Factory Design Utilities, Revit, and FlexSim Integrations
speakers: Justin Freeman, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Tyler Morrison, Industrial Systems Global Principal, Jacobs
topics: Process manufacturing | AutoCAD | Factory Design Utilities | FlexSim | Inventor | Revit | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: Discover how combining Factory Design Utilities, Revit, and FlexSim software transforms facility design through seamless integration of 2D layouts, 3D models, and process simulation. This case study will demonstrate significant time savings by eliminating redundant updates across platforms and enabling engineering teams to make objective, data-driven decisions with less rework. This class will present the end-to-end Factory Design Utilities workflow, showing how AutoCAD, Inventor, Revit, and FlexSim software work together to enable rapid, realistic simulations and models. Engineers from Jacobs will share real project examples demonstrating ROI, cost savings, and how simulations validate designs, communicate decisions, and extend value into production planning and continuous improvement.

title: Autodesk VRED: Latest Real-Time Visualization Trends combined with AI Transforming Automotive Design
speakers: Victor Perez, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Pascal Seifert, Sr. Technical Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Automotive and other transportation | Alias AutoStudio | Arnold | Fusion | VRED | VRED Professional | AUTO | D&M | XR
abstract: Autodesk VRED is known for rapidly adopting state of the art rendering technologies, open standards, and AI workflow tools. This Autodesk University session explores new key capabilities including Vulkan Ray Tracing, Gaussian Splat rendering, CloudXR streaming to Apple Vision Pro, and the use of constraints and physics. Learn how these technologies work together to deliver highly realistic visuals and physically plausible behavior for complex digital twins with minimal setup time. Discover how designers, engineers, and visual artists can accelerate projects, improve collaboration, and reduce costly errors early in the digital model. Ideal for visualization, XR, and automotive workflows focused on performance, realism, and scalability.

title: From Plan to Pour: Aurigo Primus Plan and Autodesk Forma for Asset Owners
speakers: Johann Potgieter,  Director of Product, Aurigo Software Technology
topics: Utilities and telecom | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Bridge the gap between capital planning and project execution. Led by Aurigo's director of product, this technical deep dive will explore Primus Plan and its powerful integration with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll showcase our AI-powered what-if scenario planning, demonstrating how to optimize multi-year capital portfolios before pushing them to downstream construction management. Walk through the technical architecture and data flows that move infrastructure projects from early-stage planning straight into execution within Autodesk Forma. Learn how to eliminate data silos, maximize funding, and maintain total visibility across the entire project lifecycle.

abstract:

topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management

title: The Hidden Cost of Information Silos
speakers: David Wagner, Vice President of Product Marketing, Newforma | Carl Veillette, CPO, Newforma
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Architecture services | None | AECO
abstract: The average AECO firm manages nearly 87 different software applications. At the same time, construction professionals spend more than 14 hours every week searching for information, resolving conflicts, and correcting mistakes. Coincidence? Probably not. As technology stacks continue to grow, so does the challenge of finding trusted project information when it matters most. In this session, we'll explore the hidden cost of disconnected information and why creating a consolidated view of truth has become essential for improving collaboration, reducing project risk, and giving teams confidence they're making decisions with the right information.

title: Lunch & Learn: More Performance, Less Power Needed: Lowering the Hidden Cost of Workstations
speakers: Daniel Stine, Director of Design Technology, Lake Flato | Trey Morton, Sr. Principal Engineer, Tech Marketing, Dell Technologies
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | Architecture services | Revit | AECO
abstract:
The workstations that run your Autodesk software require high performance CPUs and one of the most important advancements in CPU technology have to do with improvements in the power-to-performance ratio. In other words, the newest Intel CPUs are able to do more but need less power. That might not be an aspect of your technology stack cost, you've considered before.  

In this session, hear from Dell, Intel and industry experts on real world examples of this power-to performance improvements lowering power bills and increasing on-prem compute density all while giving your Autodesk users a system that is fast and effective for their design and engineering work.

title: AI-Ready Workstations: Powering the Next Generation of Autodesk Workflows in AEC
speakers: Rob Jamieson, Senior ISV Manager-ADM, AMD | Stephanie Berger, ACS Technical Manager, HP
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | None | AECO
abstract:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming the AEC space. Bringing new capabilities to Autodesk applications such as Revit, AutoCAD, Forma, Construction Cloud, and emerging AI-powered design and productivity tools. Realizing the full value of these innovations requires more than software—it demands modern, AI-capable hardware.

This session explores how workstation architecture, including high-performance CPUs, professional GPUs, dedicated AI accelerators, and optimized memory and storage configurations, enables faster design iteration, intelligent automation, real-time visualization, and enhanced collaboration. Attendees will learn how AI workloads are changing hardware requirements across BIM, CAD, visualization, simulation, and reality capture workflows, and how to future-proof their technology investments. Join us to discover why AI-ready workstations are becoming an essential foundation for the next generation of Autodesk-powered AEC projects.

title: PLM Summit | Welcome with Srinath Jonnalagadda, Vice President, Data Management, Autodesk
speakers: Srinath Jonnalagadda, VP, Data Management, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Manufacturing Other | Fusion | Fusion Manage | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | PLM
abstract: Kick off the PLM Summit with a high-impact keynote from Srinath Jonnalagadda, vice president of Data Management at Autodesk. He’ll dive into how organizations are tackling disconnected systems, data complexity, and relentless pressure to move faster. You’ll also gain insights into how Autodesk is addressing these challenges head-on—advancing connected data and process strategies and using the power of AI. This session will set the tone by spotlighting key themes, challenges, and opportunities you’ll explore during the PLM Summit. Lunch will be served immediately following the session in the same room, so plan to stay and join us.

title: Rethinking the Construction Workforce for the Next Decade
topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Brad Buckles, VP of Technology & Innovation of CPPI, and Mallorie Brodie, CEO and Co-Founder of Bridgit, return to the Digital Builder podcast to discuss how workforce challenges have evolved over the past six years. The conversation explores labor shortages, workforce planning, experience gaps, retention, AI, and what construction leaders must do to attract, develop, and support the next generation of industry talent.

title: The Stack Inversion Is Real: How AI Is Changing What CAD Managers Actually Do
speakers: Shaan Hurley, Engineering Software Lead, DOWL
topics: Architecture services | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Revit | AECO | Design & Engineering | Cross Industry
abstract:
AI tools are not just adding new features to CAD workflows. They are changing where the real work happens.

Some tasks that used to require deep CAD knowledge can now be researched, diagnosed, or automated faster than before. At the same time, more decisions about standards, support, compliance, and workflow ownership are landing on the CAD manager’s desk.

This session looks at what is actually changing in day-to-day CAD management, including advanced support research, complex CAD issue diagnosis, CER crash analysis, CAD standards compliance, and using real project and support data to develop better best practices. We will focus on the skills that are becoming more valuable and how to prepare your team before the shift catches you off guard.

title: Totally Carbon: Customizing Forma Carbon Insights to Your Project Needs
speakers: Annabelle Swain, BIM Manager, Dattner Architects | Dana Moore, Project Architect, Dattner Architects
topics: Architecture services | Insight | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: It's never polite to ask a Revit model its carbon—but now your 75% CD model is being asked for its embodied carbon estimates to establish LEED v5 benchmarks. Don't fret! Forma Carbon Insights (formerly Autodesk Insight) can give you real-time data without slowing your model's production team. Using the Total Carbon Analysis dashboard in Forma Carbon Insights, you can take all the work you’ve already done and transform it into carbon data. Then, you can dedicate some time to the online dashboard, refining carbon inputs without waiting for Revit buffer time or changing your family types. With your knowledge of local laws, client goals, and national averages, you can build out a holistic visual communications tool that toggles between options and their associated carbon costs in real time.

title: Production-Ready Auth for MCP Servers: A Practical Deep Dive for Autodesk Platform Services Developers
speakers: Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk | Akash Srivastava, Manager, Software Development, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Autodesk Platform Services | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Designing secure Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that integrate with Autodesk Platform Services requires choosing and implementing the right authentication strategy for each use case. This session will provide a technical deep dive into recommended MCP auth patterns, including 2-legged versus 3-legged flows, user-delegated access, and service-to-service scenarios. We’ll examine trade-offs, token handling, and common pitfalls. We’ll then walk through practical implementation patterns based on real examples from the Autodesk Platform Services MCP server reference. You’ll leave with actionable guidance for building secure, production-ready integrations.

title: AU Newbies Meetup
speakers: Todd Rogers, Civil Administration, Walter P Moore | Chris Benner, Community Manager, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Meetup
abstract: Welcome to the AU Newbies Meetup—designed specifically for first-time AU attendees. This engaging event will offer a unique opportunity to connect with community members, industry experts, and elite professionals who’ll provide invaluable insights into how to maximize your AU experience. Discover tips and tricks to navigate the conference, delve into the vast array of sessions and workshops, and learn how to use the networking opportunities that AU presents. Immerse yourself in the vibrant AU community, share your aspirations, and get personalized guidance on making the most of AU. Join us to kick-start your AU journey with confidence and excitement!

title: Autodesk Asian & Latinx Network Meetup
speakers: CARLOS ORONA, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | Curt Chan, Senior Account Executive, Regional Accounts, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Meetup
abstract: This meetup is sponsored by Autodesk Employee Belonging Groups (EBGs) to support connection and shared growth across communities. We bring employees and customers together through interactive, networking-focused experiences. Participants will engage in small-group conversations designed to encourage meaningful dialogue, knowledge sharing, and relationship building across teams, roles, and communities.

title: From Model to Diagram: Automating Electrical One-Line Generation in Revit
speakers: Zach Bratcher, AI Integrator, DBR Engineering
topics: MEP Engineering  | Engineering service providers | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Clear diagrams are critical for translating MEP designs into something contractors can build in the field. However, creating those diagrams is often a slow, manual process—drawing connection lines, placing detail items, and constantly checking the diagram against the model. Electrical one-line diagrams are prime examples, regularly taking several hours to draft for each project. What if that process could happen automatically? This session will demonstrate how you can use model data to generate clean, accurate one-line diagrams with the click of a button. Using pyRevit as the backdrop, we’ll walk through the process of transforming structured model information into fully drafted diagrams—reducing hours of manual drafting down to seconds.

title: Lessons from AI-Driven Software Engineering That Can Improve Design and Make Productivity
speakers: Anthony Ruto, Senior Director, Research Engineering, Autodesk | Andy Harris, Director, Research, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | None | AECO | Software Development | Cross Industry
abstract: As generative AI begins to automate software engineering, new principles are emerging that also apply to Design and Make processes. AI-enabled development shifts the focus toward clear requirements, structured documentation, and rigorous validation to guide and verify generated outputs. While execution becomes increasingly automated, professional oversight remains critical to ensure reliability and quality. This talk will explore how these lessons can transform Design and Make workflows—enabling faster design execution with AI while elevating the importance of design and manufacturing specifications, thoughtful application of AI where it adds value, and expert-driven verification to build trust in AI-enabled workflows.

title: The AutoCAD Plant 3D 2027 Treasure Chest: Unlocking Collaborative Efficiency in Process Plant Design
speakers: Bernd Gerstenberger, Principal Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | AutoCAD P&ID | AutoCAD Plant 3D | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Discover the revolutionary innovations in AutoCAD Plant 3D 2027 software that will transform the way you work in process plant design. Experience the new isometric sheet collection, where you’ll get an entire line number in a single isometric drawing. Streamline your work with improved AutoCAD P&ID Modeler, including the completion rate and status. Take advantage of P&ID enhancements such as the ability to substitute several components in one single step using the Property Palette. And learn more about several additional new features in AutoCAD Plant 3D 2027. This session will give you practical insights into how you can use these innovations to make your daily tasks more efficient and successfully complete your projects.

title: From Legacy to Next Generation: Modernizing HEC-RAS Model Libraries into Cloud-Ready InfoWorks ICM
speakers: Mustafa DAL, HEAD OF DEPARTMENT, GENERAL DIRECTORATE OF WATER MANAGEMENT | Cihat ADSIZ, Section Manager, General Directorate of Water Management | Özgüray AYDIN, General Manager, Viasu Teknoloji
topics: Water Infrastructure | Engineering service providers | ICMLive | InfoWorks ICM | InfoWorks ICM Flood | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: Many water authorities have built extensive HEC-RAS model libraries that remain valuable but are hard to standardize, scale, and adapt. This session will show how Türkiye’s General Directorate of Water Management is transforming legacy river models into a next-generation InfoWorks ICM environment for higher precision, performance, and future cloud use. We will outline a modernization strategy covering geometry transfer, standardization, terrain integration, and numerical stability. A benchmark shows improvement: 1 million cells, diffusion wave, 173 hours versus 7.5 million cells, shallow water, 22 hours. The result is faster, more accurate, and operational—enabling automation, scalability, and real-time readiness.

title: Designing for Everyone: How Mott MacDonald and Autodesk Are Advancing AEC Software Accessibility
speakers: Katrin Buehn, Director, Customer Relationship Mgmt, Autodesk | Tom Hughes, Head of Software Portfolio, Mott MacDonald | Ian Besford, Global Digital Delivery Leader, Mott MacDonald | Karla Ortloff, Director, User Experience, Autodesk | Conny Scheitz, VP, Platform Next, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | Engineering service providers | AECO | Inclusive Innovation, Culture, & Belonging | Cross Industry
abstract: Mott MacDonald and Autodesk are partnering to make architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) software more accessible for people with diverse needs. Through a joint accessibility working group, user research with colleagues with lived experience, and a pilot focused on inclusive design improvements, both organizations are shaping more-intuitive, barrier‑free workflows. This session will share practical lessons from our collaboration and provide a repeatable model for embedding accessibility into digital delivery.

title: Nomic at Scale: How AEC Firms Are Operationalizing AI
speakers: Andriy Mulyar, CEO and Founder, Nomic
topics: MEP Engineering  | Structural Engineering  | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Engineering service providers | ACC Connect | Data Management API | Forma | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Autodesk tools generate some of the most complex documentation in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC), yet reviewing and coordinating it still takes hours of manual effort, with errors slipping through. Join Nomic for a live 20-minute demo of purpose-built vision-language models that catch issues earlier, reduce rework, and give teams back time on every project. We'll show three workflows running on real AEC projects: 1) Drawing QA/QC: catching coordination issues and cross-discipline conflicts before they become RFIs or change orders; 2) Submittal reviews: extracting, comparing, and validating data against specs with findings cited to source; 3) Automated code compliance: surfacing violations on sheets early in design, referenced to applicable code sections. Each demo will pair with real ROI data from firms running Nomic in production, so you’ll leave with a clear picture of what deployment delivers. Nomic's AI is built for drawings, specs, and complex documentation: inspectable, governable, and grounded in your project data.

title: Stop Calculating. Start Designing for Biodiversity Net Gain.
speakers: Paul Reed, Principal Solution Architect, Autodesk | Vikki Patton, Global Biodiversity Metrics Lead, Ramboll
topics: Geospatial and GIS | Buildings | Civil 3D | Forma | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Biodiversity net gain is rapidly becoming a regulatory requirement across global markets, yet most assessments still rely on disconnected spreadsheets, manual calculations, and static reporting—creating risk, inefficiency, and limited design insight. In this session, Ramboll will share its "nature as an asset" perspective and explore evolving biodiversity frameworks across the United Kingdom, European Union, and United States. We’ll examine limitations of traditional workflows and demonstrate how Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), integrated with ArcGIS, enables geometry-driven habitat unit calculations via Ramboll's Biodiversity Calculator. Discover how digitalizing biodiversity assessment enables proactive, data-informed design—improving accuracy, transparency, and long-term project value.

title: Autodesk Tandem Connect in Action: Integrate Systems, Trigger Workflows, Drive Operations
speakers: Derek Milz, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Tandem Connect | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: In this hands-on session, explore how Autodesk Tandem Connect enables truly operational digital twins by integrating real-time data with building assets. Participants will connect external systems, visualize performance through heat maps, integrate with CMMS platforms to generate work orders, and trigger automated alerts. Learn how to transform raw signals into actionable workflows that improve maintenance, reduce downtime, and drive smarter facility operations. This session will focus on practical implementation, showing how connected data can power real-world decisions and outcomes.

title: Design Requirements Verification with BIM Automation and AI Agents
speakers: Alexandre HERSANT, Product Owner, Egis | Abdelhakim BENATTIA, BIM Developer, Egis
topics: Trust | Buildings | Revit | AECO
abstract: Verifying that a building meets project requirements - room sizing, adjacencies, equipment, performance - is still largely manual. This session presents a pipeline automating design requirements verification on BIM models. Rule-based engines extract properties, compare them to the project brief, and flag deviations. AI agents augment this pipeline - not replacing verification, but assisting decision-making: interpreting ambiguous requirements and suggesting resolution paths. Attendees see a live walkthrough: model ingestion, rule matching, deviation reporting, and AI-assisted decision support. We share lessons learned at Egis, including data quality pitfalls and balancing automation with human judgment.

title: Building Operational Twins with Indoor GIS: Where BIM, CAD, and Facility Data Go to Thrive
speakers: Gokce Ozcelik, Sr. Product Manager - Indoor GIS, Esri | Michael Davidson, Product Manager, Esri | Will Isley, CTO - PS R&D Center, Esri
topics: Geospatial and GIS | Buildings | AutoCAD | Forma Data Management | Revit LT | Revit Live | AECO
abstract: CAD and BIM have long served as foundational design and construction documentation, but their value often ends at project handoff. What if it didn't? Indoor GIS is a floor-aware system for visualizing, analyzing, managing, and navigating facilities. This session will demonstrate how AutoCAD, Revit, PDF, indoor reality, and imagery can be transformed into foundations for operational, living digital twins with ArcGIS Indoors. Learn how organizations support asset management, space planning, safety, and occupant experience while extending the life of design and construction data beyond project delivery. See how GIS integrates with Autodesk products, design and engineering data in Forma Data Management, and facility data to create long-term operational value.

title: Autodesk Forma Site Design for Infrastructure: Rapid Context and Site Setup
speakers: Shelby L Smith, BIM Manager, Bohler | Hilde Bakkeli, Sr. Manager, Product Mgmt, Autodesk
topics: Geospatial and GIS | Civil infrastructure | BIM Collaborate | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Autodesk Forma Site Design allows infrastructure professionals to take the lead in project setup by providing a high-fidelity data environment from the very beginning. This session will demonstrate how to jump-start projects by using open-source terrain, roadway, and property data to create a reliable conceptual foundation. We’ll explore how to define critical site zoning constraints—including property offsets and building height limits—to provide clear parameters for the building design team.  You will also learn how to apply preliminary grading design and add GIS data from the ArcGIS Connector. Finally, we will look ahead at the growing set of infrastructure capabilities coming to Forma, including new tools for urban street design and the upcoming integration with Civil 3D, and how adopting these cloud-first tools today positions your team to take full advantage of what's next.

title: From Autodesk Forma to IFC Compliance: Automating BIM Validation in Railway Projects
speakers: Thiago Dantas, Project Manager, TPF | Juliana Scanoni, Innovation Manager, TPF | Juliana Scanoni | Melissa Yamada, BIM Manager, TPF Engenharia
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Dynamo | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Ensuring BIM data quality in railway infrastructure projects remains a challenge due to manual checks, inconsistent requirements, and lack of standardization. This session will present a real-world workflow using Civil 3D software for railway design, integrated with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), to automate IFC model validation using IDS. Starting from structured tabular requirements, we’ll demonstrate how to generate IDS files using Python and apply automated validation workflows. We’ll also compare this approach with commercial solutions and highlight trade-offs in scalability, control, and collaboration. Attendees will learn how to reduce manual effort, improve data consistency, and implement a scalable openBIM validation process for infrastructure projects.

title: From Construction to Operations: Delivering a Seamless Handover
speakers: Yanissa De Jonghe, Head of Digital & Data, Lantis | Guillaume Neyrinck, Senior Technical Success Manager, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Geospatial and GIS | Civil infrastructure | Build | Docs | Forma | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: This session explains how Lantis—client of a €10 billion infraproject—prepares a seamless and data‑rich handover from construction to operations and maintenance (O&M) by combining Autodesk Forma, Autodesk Datum, the Autodesk Data Model, and Autodesk Tandem software. Discover how structured asset requirements, Autodesk Forma‑based data validation, automated property mapping, and federated model workflows ensure consistent, complete, and BIM‑to‑O&M‑ready information. Investing in asset lifecycle management has a potential ROI of €40.74 million. Learn how Lantis uses open standards, QA/QC automation, and twin‑based asset structuring to transition thousands of deliverables into a usable digital twin ecosystem that supports long‑term maintenance, inspection, and operations.

title: Data-Centered Delivery at Scale: Selective IFC Exports from Autodesk Forma Using Autodesk Data Exchange​
speakers: Adrian Fernandez Sanchez, Product Owner Autodesk Transport, Rambøll Norge | Aleksandra Gorczyca, Principal Consulting Project Manager, Autodesk | Marc Sleegers, Sr Principal, Business Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Civil infrastructure | Docs | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Ramboll’s shift to data-centered delivery moves beyond project-by-project file exchanges, transforming BIM data into a reusable, trusted, and scalable company-wide asset. This class will present a practical architecture and operating model to selectively export standardized IFC data from Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) using Data Exchange, enabling analytics, integration, digital twins, and lifecycle information management.

title: From a Work-Around to a Real Workflow: Duct Bank Design in Civil 3D
speakers: Vincent Sheehan, Sr. Designer, Timmons Group
topics: MEP Engineering  | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Designing duct banks in Civil 3D software can be challenging due to limited out-of-the-box tools for multiconduit systems. This class will present a practical workflow for creating, managing, and visualizing duct banks using surfaces, corridor assemblies, and custom subassemblies and pipe network structures. You’ll go over custom duct bank subassemblies using Subassembly Composer, learning how to model subsurface duct banks, use the duct banks in construction documents, and export the models to Revit or Navisworks software to coordinate with other disciplines.

title: Design Once, Use Many Times: The OpenBIM Strategies at the São Paulo Metro Company
speakers: Ivo Mainardi, BIM Manager, São Paulo Metro | Joyce Delatorre, Principal Territory Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Navisworks Manage | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Large rail and metro programs generate vast amounts of design data, yet information is often recreated or lost across phases and contracts. This session shows how infrastructure owners can apply OpenBIM strategies to truly “design once, use many times.” Based on real metro and railway programs, it demonstrates how open standards—especially IFC 4.3—enable consistent reuse of data from planning and design through construction, oversight, and long-term operations. Attendees will learn how owners can structure BIM requirements, governance models, and data workflows that support interoperability across multiple vendors and platforms, improving transparency, efficiency, and decision-making across the asset lifecycle.

title: Design Once, Use Forever: Automating Civil 3D Asset Data for Operations
speakers: Jelber Prado, BIM Manager | Infrastructure, Houston Airport System | George Cernetig, Sr. VDC Specialist, HNTB
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Dynamo | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: As owners and operators increasingly rely on digital twins, geographic information systems (GIS), and asset management platforms, expectations for consistent, accurate, and information‑rich civil deliverables continue to rise. Yet many Civil 3D workflows still rely on manual asset attribution, introducing risk, rework, and inconsistency. This session will explore how Civil 3D and Dynamo can be used to automate asset attribution, using a real‑world airport-infrastructure case study with the Houston Airports System (HAS). You will learn how rule‑based logic, Civil 3D object intelligence, and standardized data schemas are used to populate attributes for linear and point‑based assets, then export attribution‑ready data for GIS and asset management systems.

title: From Fragmented Inputs to Actionable Design Intent
speakers: Nigel Morris, Sr. Manager, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion Design Extension | Fusion Generative Design Extension | D&M | Future Industry Innovations | Cross Industry
abstract: Design teams rarely start with a complete and coherent requirements package. Instead, they work with fragmented inputs such as briefs, standards, legacy specifications, expert assumptions, performance targets, and evolving stakeholder constraints. This session will explore how AI-enabled workflows—combining information normalization, uncertainty quantification, human-in-the-loop review, retrieval-augmented generation, threshold-based routing, and decomposition/aggregation—can convert incomplete information into actionable, traceable design intent. Although developed in product design and simulation, the insights directly transfer across industries.

title: Understanding Project and Executive Insights with Insight Builder
speakers: William Fiallos, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | John Prior, Sr Technical Specialist, Construction, Autodesk | Sheryl Yang, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Build | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: This hands-on lab will help users understand how to begin using the Insight Builder tool within the Project and Executive Insights to obtain project and portfolio level reporting for RFIs, Submittals, Issues, and Cost data. We’ll walk through the following: accessing Insight Builder; building your first Insight Builder dashboard; generating visualizations from key project data; creating pixel-perfect reports to automate PDF generation of weekly reports; and sharing data to project teams. This session will focus on digesting Build data across many projects and helping users find ways to present key insights across projects and portfolios. If you’re looking to level up your analytics skills, this class will help you get started on your data journey.

title: Connected Coordination Level 3: Elevate Clash Resolution Using the Power of Model Coordination in Autodesk Forma
speakers: Deepak Maini, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | BIM Collaborate | BIM Collaborate Pro | BIM Collaborate Pro for Govt | Model Coordination | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: In fast-paced digital project delivery, timely communication and clear accountability across teams are fundamental to effective clash resolution. In this Connected Coordination Level 3 lab, we’ll build on the 2025 session to demonstrate how a structured, closed-loop approach to issue management allows you to assign, notify, track, and resolve clashes while maintaining a fully auditable record of every action. In this lab, you’ll learn to pull clash issues directly into their Revit models to visualize conflicts and act to ensure transparency and efficiency among stakeholders. This lab will also build on exporting active clash data and integrating it with Power BI dashboards for real-time insights and better decision making.

title: Using Autodesk Forma Takeoff for Carbon Offset and Sustainability Requirements
speakers: Nathan Love, Construction BIM Manager, Multiplex | Adam Sheather, Sr Principal, Solution Architect – APAC Lead Technical Advisory, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Autodesk Access | Cloud Worksharing | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: As more projects are being mandated to demonstrate reduced carbon impact during construction, managing contractors are now tasked with finding solutions to easily calculate and track the change in materials that affect Green Star ratings for their clients. This presentation will show you how Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) can use the project models using Forma Takeoff and the EC3 plug-in to effectively report and track carbon offsets to international standards.

title: From Prompts to Project Outcomes: Using Autodesk Assistant in Autodesk Forma
speakers: Shir Rustici, BIM Program Manager, Turner & Townsend | Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+
topics: Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: AI is now embedded directly into Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) through Autodesk Assistant. But its real value comes from how it improves decisions, not just how it responds to prompts. This session will show how to use Autodesk Assistant in real workflows, grounded in the shared data and industry context that power Autodesk Forma. Through practical examples, we’ll explore how teams can use AI to support design exploration, generate project insights, and streamline everyday tasks without leaving their workflows. You’ll learn how to structure effective prompts, refine responses, and build on outputs to turn AI-generated information into actionable decisions. We’ll also cover where Autodesk Assistant delivers the most value today and where its limitations lie.

title: From Prompts to Project Outcomes: Using Autodesk Assistant in Autodesk Forma
speakers: Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+ | Shir Rustici, BIM Program Manager, Turner & Townsend
topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: AI is now embedded directly into Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) through Autodesk Assistant.
