title: Get Connected: Simplify Navigation of Project Tools for Everyone
speakers: Kelli Lubeley, Construction Technology Manager, Cupertino Electric Inc
topics: Construction services | BIM 360 Docs | Build | Forma | PlanGrid | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: In this session, we’ll explore how trade contractors can provide streamlined navigation to the applications and platforms used by field, project management, and safety teams, ensuring each team member can easily obtain and share the information needed to perform their roles. We’ll review the solution Cupertino Electric uses on our projects, and outline the core functionality required to replicate this approach, regardless of vendor or specific products.

title: The Design and Make Marketplace: Perspectives That Scale
speakers: Vasini Govindarajan, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Prashant Potadar, Manager - App Store Operations, Autodesk | Brent Scannell, Group Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | None | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Autodesk is building the Design and Make Marketplace to power a new era of AI-driven automation—connecting customers to both Autodesk and third-party capabilities in a unified experience. This panel will bring together perspectives from across that ecosystem: an end user discovering and combining solutions, a publisher building and monetizing capabilities, an enterprise leader managing adoption at scale, and Autodesk shaping the platform. Together, they’ll explore how AI-powered services, agents, and workflows are discovered, acquired, and used—and what it takes to make solutions from multiple providers work seamlessly. Learn how this shift is redefining how work gets done.

title: From PlanGrid to Platform: How a Specialty Contractor Built an Enterprise Data Strategy on Autodesk Forma
speakers: Niklas Janetzky, Technology Strategy Manager, Pan-Pacific Mechanical
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | Autodesk Platform Services | Build | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: When we, one of the larger MEP design-build contractors on the US West Coast, decided to replace PlanGrid, our mission was clear: We want to update our tool suite, and quickly standardize data quality across all projects. But a platform decision is more than just a tool swap. This session will walk you through the generalized strategic framework that we used to evaluate, select, and roll out Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) as the enterprise backbone for both office and field teams. Learn how a three-stage rollout from exploration, a year-long pilot with rigorous standardization, and a fine-tuned enterprise deployment delivered measurable results: unified dashboards, and a data foundation that helps us to build custom solutions with Autodesk Platform Services.

title: A Smarter Asset Strategy for Data Center Delivery with Autodesk Forma
speakers: Matthew Harraka, Technology Consultant, Forma, ARKANCE | Bobby Hinojosa, Technology Consultant, ARKANCE
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Construction services | ACC Connect | Forma | Forma Build | Forma Building Design | Forma Construction Connect | Forma Data Management | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Data center lifecycle transition is a critical milestone where minor handover gaps can cause multimillion-dollar operational delays. In mission-critical delivery, establishing an institutional data-center asset strategy must begin well before closeout. This session will examine how Autodesk Forma serves as a strategic driver for rigorous data-center asset planning, complex systems architecture organization, and comprehensive operational readiness throughout design and construction. Executives and project leaders will gain a high-level framework to align cross-functional data-center teams, mitigate handover liabilities, and secure high-fidelity facility intelligence for day-one operational excellence.

title: What Becomes Possible When Fabricators Join the Design Process? A Design-to-Fabrication BIM Study.
speakers: Takashi Fukushima, STRUCTURAL ENGINEER, Nikken Sekkei
topics: Structural Engineering  | Building products and fabrication | AutoCAD | Revit | D&M | Structural Engineering & Fabrication | AECO
abstract: Designers make responsible decisions on details—but fully reflecting fabricators' knowledge of real production difficulty and cost is not straightforward. Quantities often emerge only once drawings reach the contractor. What becomes possible when fabricators engage as technical consultants during design? This session shares a joint study with a steel fabricator. Positioning Revit as a single source of truth, connection rules for diaphragms and splices were implemented as components in Tekla via IFC, automating detail generation and takeoff. Fabricators proposed cost improvements; designers made the final geometry decisions. We also examine data retention, the limits of automation, and role boundaries—showing both what became possible and the challenges that remain.

title: Rule-Driven Building Design: Connecting Structural Analysis, Autodesk Forma, and Informed Design
speakers: steve dewitt, Owner, Custom Building Configurators | Kelly Justin Wilson, Founder, SADE
topics: Building products and fabrication | Dynamo | Forma | Informed Design | Inventor | Revit | D&M | Industrialized Construction | Structural Engineering & Fabrication | AECO
abstract: Learn how to automate decision making in type 5 designs by connecting structural analysis, product data, and off-site construction workflows across the Autodesk platform. This class will demonstrate how to integrate a Structural Analysis Design Engine (SADE) with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to automate shear wall placement, then propagate those requirements through Informed Design to drive product behavior. Using the Informed Design API and parametric logic authored in Inventor software, we’ll embed structural intelligence into configurable wall panels assigned to Autodesk Forma masses—enabling consistent, data-driven outcomes from early design through fabrication.

title: Get started with iLogic Configuration - Learn Configurator workflows by Building one
speakers: Paul Munford, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect - D&M, Autodesk
topics: Industrial machinery | Inventor | Inventor Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Change a few parameters and watch your Inventor model reconfigure itself! Configuration is the dream! However, applying configurations to some models can be migraine-inducing. Let’s start with assemblies built for configuration. In this hands-on lab, you’ll experience assemblies prepared for configuration from the beginning. Through guided exercises, you’ll explore model-building best practices for configuration with Inventor iLogic. You'll experience driving top-down design changes, adding and removing components, and learning how to incorporate Model States and iLogic. You’ll leave with an understanding of model configuration best practices, including checklists and guidance to apply to your own configuration projects.

title: Stop Searching, Start Knowing: Item-Driven Classification in Vault
speakers: Bill Shaner, CAD Administrator, FS Elliott
topics: Data and Document Management | Industrial machinery | Inventor | Vault Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Learn how to bring structure, clarity, and powerful searchability to your engineering data using Vault Items as the foundation for classification. Many organizations rely on files and folders to organize models, drawings, and documents, but this approach can quickly become difficult to manage as data grows. By using Items, you can create a consistent classification framework in a more meaningful way.

title: Vault 2027: What’s New and Where We’re Headed
speakers: Irvin Hayes, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | Fusion Manage | Inventor | Vault Basic | D&M
abstract: Vault software continues to evolve to support modern engineering and enterprise needs. And Vault 2027 delivers focused improvements in workflow efficiency, productivity, and platform integration. In this 60‑minute session, we’ll explore what’s new in Vault 2027. You’ll learn how these enhancements support real‑world CAD, engineering, and IT workflows. And you’ll see how they fit into enterprise environments. We’ll also look ahead at the Vault roadmap, highlighting strategic themes and future direction. Learn how customer feedback helps shape Vault and how to prepare your organization for what’s coming next.

title: Vaultify Your Inventor Add-In
speakers: Tiffany Hayden, Application Developer, KETIV Technologies Inc.
topics: Manufacturing Other | Inventor Professional | Vault Professional | D&M | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Learn how to “Vaultify” an existing Inventor add-in by integrating Vault API functionality. This session will focus on adding Vault connectivity and using Vault data directly within Inventor to enhance your design workflows. You’ll see how to search for existing parts using both system and user-defined properties, helping reduce duplicate designs and improve reuse of existing data. We’ll also explore how this approach can support smarter decision making during design, streamline processes, and lay the foundation for more-advanced Vault-driven automation within your custom add-ins.

title: Restructuring Your Construction Data for the Future
speakers: Josh Weese, Director of Construction Services, ATG USA
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | Revit | Tandem | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: This session will explore how construction teams can transform fragmented project data into a connected, intelligent workflow using Revit, Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), and Autodesk Tandem. You’ll learn how to overcome common challenges such as data silos, inconsistent standards, and manual processes, and replace them with integrated pipelines for quantities, progress tracking, and digital twins. You’ll discover practical strategies for structuring data, automating workflows, and preparing your organization for AI-driven construction delivery.

title: The Future of Drainage Workflows with InfoDrainage and Civil 3D
topics: Civil infrastructure | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Join this session with Autodesk Water experts exploring site drainage design workflows using Civil 3D and InfoDrainage. This session brings together proven approaches to show how Autodesk Water Infrastructure solutions work together to support efficient, data driven drainage design.

title: Making AI Stick in Estimating
speakers: Brad Klick, Estimating Manager, Victaulic
topics: MEP Engineering  | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | None | AECO
abstract:
AI is changing estimating today, and will continue to evolve workflows in the future. The challenge is knowing which opportunities are worth pursuing. 

Drawing on 14 months of real-world implementation, this session shares a practical framework for identifying AI use cases with the greatest potential based on three factors: impact, frequency, and visibility. It then tackles what happens after a solution works: driving adoption, creating repeatable processes, establishing ownership, and scaling across the team.

Attendees will leave with a framework for prioritizing AI opportunities and a roadmap for turning individual wins into lasting, scalable workflows.

title: From Revit Projects and Simple Renderings to Interactive and Immersive VR Apps
speakers: ALAN ARAUJO, Architect, Bee1
topics: Architecture services | 3ds Max 2 | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Project presentations in AutoCAD or Revit software are essential for the technical development of construction. However, what truly captivates the end client is the visual experience. Today, simple renders or videos are no longer enough. The real difference is telling a story through the project or allowing the client to explore the environment interactively, visiting and engaging with the space through virtual reality or immersive applications. This transforms the presentation into a memorable and engaging experience.

title: Beyond the PDF: Synchronizing Large-Scale Teams via the Autodesk-Forma-to-Autodesk-Workshop XR Pipeline
speakers: Amar Hromo, Senior Architect, KEO International Consultants
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Architecture services | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | Workshop XR | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Strategic alignment: integrated workflows, convergence across tools (Forma + Revit + Workshop XR) to create impact. This focuses on "business outcomes" by eliminating the "render-review-rework" cycle. Coordination gaps between master planners and building designers often lead to costly rework during design development. Using the KEO project as a case study, this session demonstrates how to establish Autodesk Forma as a "single source of truth." We showcase a scalable strategy applied across our projects and a workflow demo where design constraints are pushed through Revit into Workshop XR for 1:1 scale review. Learn how this integrated approach allows global teams to make instant, data-backed decisions from massing and orientation to design details, ensuring total stakeholder alignment before construction.

title: Designing for Inclusion: Solving Low-Battery Anxiety in AEC and Design and Make
speakers: Melody Lindenberger, Dir., Tax, Autodesk | Ian Pendlebury, Vice President Fusion Platform, Autodesk | Teresa Valenzuela, Founder | CEO, Well-Able Platforms | Alexis Womble, Senior Security Program Manager, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | Architecture services | Fusion | AECO | Inclusive Innovation, Culture, & Belonging | Cross Industry
abstract: What if your designs unintentionally limit who belongs in the spaces you create? This strategy talk reveals the hidden infrastructure gap behind “low battery anxiety” for power mobility users and why it matters to AEC and Design & Make professionals. Through Teresa Valenzuela’s story, discover how culture, empathy, and inclusive innovation can reshape design. Learn to uncover overlooked user needs, design for accessibility at scale, and apply practical strategies that expand access and participation. Walk away with actionable ways to embed accessibility and belonging into your next project.

title: From Data Exchange to Spatial Computing: Building Immersive Autodesk Platform Services Experiences
speakers: Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk | Lejla Secerbegovic, Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Autodesk Platform Services | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Explore how Autodesk Platform Services enables a new class of immersive design applications. This session will dive into the Autodesk Data Exchange API and the Geometry Utilities SDK, showing how to extract, transform, and stream architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) data into custom 3D experiences. Using a real-world example on Apple Vision Pro, we’ll demonstrate how subsets of Revit models can be converted into lightweight, queryable geometry and rendered in spatial computing environments. You’ll gain practical insights into data pipelines, geometry processing, and performance considerations for building production-ready immersive apps on top of Autodesk Platform Services.

title: AutoCAD Plant 3D Custom Plug-ins Save Our Customers Hundreds of Engineering Hours
speakers: Nuria Martinez, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: MEP Engineering  | Engineering service providers | AutoCAD Plant 3D | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Engineering teams often spend hundreds of hours on repetitive manual tasks during CAD design that can lead to inefficiencies and errors. In this class, discover how Autodesk Consulting works closely with customers to understand their unique needs and develop custom AutoCAD Plant 3D plug-ins and scripts that automate complex workflows, improve data quality, and accelerate project execution. Learn how Plant 3D extensibility can deliver measurable productivity gains in areas such as report generation, instrument patterns, P&ID and PFD management, custom data queries, instrument loops, pipeline management, and recovery of legacy drawings.

title: AI-Driven Digital Twins: Standardizing and Scaling Mission-Critical Infrastructure
speakers: Juliana Mizumoto, Head of Bid Management, Start Campus
topics: Construction Operations | Engineering service providers | Forma | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: The rapid growth of data centers is challenging traditional approaches to design and delivery. Project-by-project workflows are no longer scalable, leading to inefficiencies and inconsistent outcomes. This session will explore how AI-driven digital twins—developed through Autodesk Tandem software and enabled by collaborative workflows in Autodesk Forma—can support a scalable and repeatable approach to mission-critical infrastructure. You’ll learn how to connect early-stage planning, detailed design, and operations into a continuous data-driven process. And you’ll see how to replicate solutions across multiple sites while maintaining performance, quality, and speed.

title: Operationalizing Autodesk Forma: Lessons from Scaling Infrastructure Delivery
speakers: Allison Maclellan, Design Manager, Heirloom Carbon Technologies
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Account | Build | Docs | Forma | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Heirloom Carbon, a direct air capture (DAC) company, shares how its infrastructure team turned Autodesk Forma (including Forma Data Management, Forma Build, and Forma Takeoff) into a reliable, daily delivery platform. Like many architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) teams, they faced inconsistent onboarding, fragmented document control, and unclear governance across projects. This session will break down how the team established a scalable common data environment (CDE) through standardized templates, permissions, and workflows issues. You’ll see how they improved collaboration, reduced rework, and increased delivery capacity, and you’ll understand what failed or took longer than expected. Walk away with a practical playbook to configure and standardize Autodesk Forma for consistent, scalable project delivery.

title: From Good Intentions to Sustainable Decisions
speakers: Becky Burns, Sustainability Technical Partner Program Manager, Autodesk | Amarpreet Singh, Team Lead, North America, One Click LCA | Michelle Aguilar, CTO, VAPAR
topics: Water Infrastructure | Buildings | Info360 Asset | Insight | Revit | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: Most sustainability strategies never make it into daily work. Teams struggle to turn ambition into decisions, data flows, and repeatable processes. This session will explore three sustainability workflows that are actually working today: design-phase carbon estimation, AI-enabled inspection, and material selection informed by connected product and carbon data. We’ll examine how these workflows are structured, where they break, and what it takes to implement them across tools, teams, and data sources—drawing on examples from technology partners such as One Click LCA and VAPAR. You’ll leave with a practical framework for turning sustainability goals into operational workflows.

title: Data Center Design Automation: A New Paradigm for Feasibility and Early Design
speakers: Nuno Mourao, Chief Software Architect, Podium.io
topics: MEP Engineering  | Buildings | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract:
Data center projects must move faster while managing increasing complexity in power, cooling, and cost.
Traditional feasibility workflows are fragmented and slow, limiting iteration and delaying decisions. This session presents a new approach through a real customer case study, showing how integrating Podium with Autodesk Forma and Revit enables teams to move from site analysis to coordinated design in a single day. By automating layout generation and enabling rapid scenario testing, teams can evaluate more options, align stakeholders earlier, and reduce risk. Learn how feasibility becomes a fast, iterative, and data-driven process.

title: AutoCAD Electrical Meets Vibe Coding: Building a Complex Dashboard Without DAX/M Expertise
speakers: Shinu Mathew, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Electrical | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Turn messy AutoCAD Electrical data into a working dashboard—without deep Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) or Power Query expertise. This session will reveal a real-world journey using “vibe coding”: iterative problem-solving with AI, trial and error, and constant refinement. From duplicate tags and broken relationships to the rebuilding of structure and debugging in loops, every step reflects practical challenges and breakthroughs. Learn how structured thinking, smart prompting, and persistence can transform chaotic engineering data into meaningful insights—without waiting to become an expert.

title: Predict Before You Model: How We Built an ML-Powered MEP Estimating Bot Trained on 300+ Real Projects
speakers: Gustavo Gusmão, BIM Solution Architect, ENG | Gabriel Campos, BIM Solution Architect, ENG BIM
topics: Civil infrastructure | BIM 360 Docs | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: What if you could generate a reliable MEP cost estimate before modeling a single element in Revit software? That’s exactly what we built: a Python-based estimation bot trained on more than 300 real MEP projects from our historical data. Instead of relying on disconnected spreadsheets or manual takeoffs, the bot uses pattern recognition to generate estimates at the proposal stage before BIM begins. Our solution achieves more than 95% accuracy versus final costs, and it reduces estimation time by more than 70%. In this session, we’ll show how we structured the data, trained the model, and integrated it into our workflow. You’ll leave this session with a practical framework to turn historical data into a predictive asset.

title: Data-Driven Water Utilities: BIM-GIS Validation and Digital Twins at Gruppo CAP
speakers: Giuseppe Barberio, Head Of Digital Engineering & BIM, Gruppo CAP | Antonio Devito, Technical Director, One team
topics: Water Infrastructure | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma | InfoWorks ICM | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: Inconsistent data across the water lifecycle hinders operational resilience. This session will present the technical framework developed for Gruppo CAP (Milan) to bridge this gap using Autodesk Forma as a unified cloud environment. Starting from scan-to-BIM modeling of a water plant, we’ll detail a custom validation engine built on Autodesk Platform Services that automates model checking against asset information requirem`ents (AIR) standards via specialized scripts. We’ll explore how validated BIM data flows into Esri Utility Network to fuel InfoWorks ICM solutions for advanced hydraulic modeling. You’ll evaluate how this scalable architecture, in a large-scale utility, uses Power BI to transform data into a simulation-ready digital twin for smarter asset management.

title: From Pilot to Competitive Advantage: Scaling Generative Design with Autodesk Forma and Infraspace
speakers: Andreas Kjølseth, Founder & CEO, Infraspace | Kristoffer Spendrup Bugge, Digital Transformation Leader, Norconsult
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma | Navisworks Manage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract:
Infrastructure projects face increasing demands for faster delivery, lower costs, and more sustainable outcomes. Meeting these demands requires teams to work smarter, deliver higher-quality designs, and make better decisions within tight project deadlines.

Following last year's session, Infraspace and Norconsult will share how they have moved from promising pilots to production use of generative design in real transportation and energy projects.

Powered by Infraspace and integrated with Autodesk Forma, they will demonstrate how engineering teams can streamline planning and early design, and reduce iteration time from weeks to minutes through automated generation of design alternatives for roads and other infrastructure assets.

Through real-world project examples, you will learn how generative design augments engineering expertise, improves project outcomes, and provides a competitive advantage through faster, better-informed design decisions.

title: Using Autodesk Forma to Modernize Digital Delivery and Information Management in Public Transit
speakers: Casey Gallagher, AEC Technology Specialists, Sound Transit | Greg Smith, Digital Delivery Lead, Mott MacDonald
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: Join us for an in-depth demonstration of a real-world approach to modernizing digital delivery for a public transit agency that delivers one of the largest US infrastructure expansion programs. This session will explore how Autodesk Forma is being used to support ISO 19650-aligned workflows by addressing the challenges of legacy CAD and Revit record data. The discussion will focus on improving data consistency, enabling earlier information alignment, and transforming record documentation into operationally useful data beyond project closeout.

title: AI Assistants Connected by Claude MCP and GPT Agents Using Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Autodesk Platform Services Workflows
speakers: Manuel Meneses, Business Intelligence & Data Analytics, Independent | Enrique Meneses, BIM Administrator, Bayer
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Build | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Autodesk Forma Data Management (formerly Autodesk Docs) and Revit hold powerful data, yet teams still spend hours on model QA, quantity takeoffs, and reporting. In this two-presenter session, we build a practical AI assistant for Revit and Forma Data Management on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), driven from both Claude and GPT. A Revit add-in bridges natural language drives structured, deterministic tool calls instead of unreliable prompt-only behavior.

title: How Cleveland Construction Added AI-Powered Submittal and Drawing Reviews to Autodesk Forma
speakers: Elliot Christiansen, Sr. Vice President of Operations, Cleveland Construction, Inc. | Dr. Sarah Buchner, Founder & CEO, Trunk Tools
topics: Construction services | None | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: When Cleveland Construction migrated from Procore to Autodesk, company leaders saw an opportunity to build an intelligent document pipeline and agentic workflows on top of the wealth of data they run their business on in Autodesk. In this session, Elliot Christiansen, SVP of operations at Cleveland Construction, will share how his team configured their Autodesk environment to enable AI-powered workflows that automatically review submittals against specs and new bulletins against previous ones. Sarah Buchner, founder and CEO of Trunk Tools, an App Marketplace Partner, will join Elliot to share Cleveland's winning playbook to transition from handshakes to driving deep adoption across their project teams.

title: PLM Summit | Lifting the Weight of Product Development at Overhead Door
speakers: Greg Fineran, Project Manager, Overhead Door Corporation | Todd Clark, Senior Engineering Manager, Overhead Door
topics: Building products and fabrication | AutoCAD | Fusion Manage | Revit | Token Flex | D&M | PLM
abstract: Learn how Overhead Door shaved 18 months off its new product development (NPD) timeline. What once averaged 30 months now follows a standardized phase-gated process in Autodesk Fusion Manage to be completed in under 12 months—with most projects tracking ahead of schedule. This session will explore this journey of improving resource visibility, strengthening cross-functional collaboration, and creating leadership visibility into bottlenecks.

title: Autodesk Flow Production Tracking, Maya, and Flame: Building a Natural-Language AI-Driven VFX Pipeline
speakers: Abraham Borbujo, Sr Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk | Fernando Novo Paz, Sr Technical Account Manager, Autodesk
topics: Film and TV | Flame | Flow Production Tracking | Maya | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract: Fragmented VFX pipelines rely on manual asset handoffs, inconsistent data, and disconnected tools across tracking, digital content creation (DCC), and finishing. This session will demonstrate a connected workflow linking Autodesk Flow Production Tracking, Maya, and Flame software through a natural language-driven orchestration layer. Asset ideas defined by text or images are transformed into timely prototypes for rapid iteration, automatically loaded into Maya, published to Autodesk Flow Production Tracking, and rendered to Flame for downstream work. The session will break down architecture, data flow, and automation patterns, including safeguards for reliability. You’ll learn how to apply these patterns incrementally. A documented implementation supports exploration and reuse.

title: Vault Professional Mastery: 13 Modern Tips to Supercharge Your Workflow
speakers: Radu Stancescu, CAD Specialist, Permasteelisa North America | Benson | Raffaele Sammarco, Principal Consulting Project Manager, Autodesk | Douhet Wilcox, CAD Lead, Permasteelisa North America | Benson
topics: Data and Document Management | Industrial machinery | AutoCAD | Inventor | Vault Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Stop clicking through menus and start maximizing your data. In this fast-paced, 30-minute session, we’ll dive into 13 high-impact tips and tricks for Vault Professional software that often go overlooked. From optimizing lifecycles and advanced searching to using the latest "modern" features in the 2027 release, these hacks are designed to eliminate bottlenecks and supercharge your daily workflow. Whether you’re a CAD manager or a power user, you’ll leave with a practical toolkit to automate repetitive tasks, improve data security, and get the most out of your Vault environment.

title: Engineering Copilot: Real AI Workflows for Vault, BOMs, and Manufacturing Data
speakers: Christian Gessner, Head of Research and Innovation, coolOrange S.r.l. | Tyler Warner, Sr. Software Developer, IMAGINiT Technologies
topics: Data and Document Management | Manufacturing Other | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: AI is everywhere—but how does it actually help engineering teams working with CAD, BOMs, and Vault software? This class will demonstrate real-world applications of AI on top of Vault, focusing on engineering and manufacturing processes. Using live examples, we’ll show how structured data such as eBOMs and mBOMs can be interpreted, transformed, and enriched using AI while keeping engineers in control. You’ll see how natural-language interfaces, rule-based automation, and AI-assisted decision making support tasks like BOM transformation, process planning, and validation. The session will highlight proven architectures, integration patterns, and limitations when introducing AI into Vault-based environments.

title: AI-Powered Inventor: Design Faster, Work Smarter
speakers: Maulik Patel, Sr. SW Eng. Test, Autodesk | Rena Andrews, Senior Software QA Engineer, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | Inventor | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: In this session, discover how AI assistance is transforming Inventor workflows from concept to production. See how Autodesk Assistant uses natural language to analyze models, create model states, suppress components, generate parameters, and automate repetitive tasks—without leaving Inventor or writing code. Learn how AI works alongside Inventor software’s parametric, rules-based, simulation and documentation tools to accelerate design, improve manufacturability, and reduce errors in complex assemblies. Walk away with practical insights to boost productivity and design smarter, faster.

title: No Line of Sight, No Leveling: Syncing Field Reality to Revit with Topcon Origo
speakers: William Palmgren, Product Business Owner, Topcon Positioning Group
topics: Reality Capture | Construction Operations | Construction services | AutoCAD | Revit Cloud Worksharing | Revit LT | Revit Live | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Traditional field layout is a disconnected process plagued by line-of-sight obstructions, tedious equipment leveling, and office-to-field data gaps. When conditions shift on chaotic jobsites, the central design model is left completely out of date. This fast-paced, 20-minute session closes the loop entirely. See how to generate precise field points using Autodesk Point Layout (APL), execute high-precision layout with the Topcon Origo ecosystem—requiring zero equipment leveling or line-of-sight constraints—and seamlessly pull "as-staked" and field conditions directly back into your model using ClearEdge3D Tools for Revit. Stop fighting site obstructions—learn to build a true two-way Revit workflow.

title: Building the Talent Pipeline for Industrialized Construction
topics: Construction services | AECO | Industrialized Construction
abstract: Ryan MacMahon, Senior Director and General Manager of Manufacturing Informed Design at Autodesk, and Chad Ray, Provost and Chief Campus Officer at Wake Technical Community College, join the Digital Builder podcast to discuss how education and industry are preparing the workforce for industrialized construction. The episode explores prefab, manufacturing, curriculum development, workforce readiness, and the future skills needed to transform how buildings are delivered.

title: XR Meetup: real conversations about extended reality
speakers: Mingus New, Customer Community Manager, Workshop XR, Autodesk
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | VRED | Workshop XR | Meetup
abstract: Join the 5th Annual Extended Reality (XR) Meetup for an open, interactive conversation on how people are using virtual, augmented, and mixed reality technologies today. Hear real experiences from across industries about what’s working, where XR fits, and what people are still figuring out. This is a space to connect with your people: ask questions, share insights, and connect with others exploring XR. Whether you are just getting started or building on existing workflows, you will leave with practical insights, new connections, and a clearer view of how XR is being used right now.

title: Innovators Stage | Preserving What Matters: Digital Innovation and the Future of Historic Stewardship
speakers: Rachel Tuller, VP, Global Partner Ecosystem Sales, Autodesk | Ramesh Sridharan, Director, Reality Solutions, Autodesk | Justin Gunther, Director of Fallingwater, Fallingwater | Touf Hassoun, President/CEO, Case Technologies
abstract: Historic landmarks carry memory, identity, and community—but preserving them is increasingly complex as age, climate, and visitor demand put new pressure on cultural sites. The session will open with the premiere of a short documentary offering an intimate look at Fallingwater, Frank Lloyd Wright’s architectural masterpiece, and the people, partnerships, and technology working together to preserve a UNESCO world heritage site. Following the screening,  Rachel Tuller, VP, Global Partner Ecosystems Sales, Autodesk, will moderate a conversation to explore how craft, expertise, and connected technologies are transforming preservation from reactive repair to proactive, data-informed stewardship. Justin Gunther, Vice President and Director of Fallingwater, will share the realities of stewarding this iconic landmark and balancing preservation for future generations. Touf Hassoun, CEO of CASE Technologies, will discuss how reality capture, digital twins, and AI are helping preservation teams better understand and protect historic places. Ramesh Sridharan, Director of Reality Solutions, Autodesk will share Autodesk's perspective on how connected platforms, data, and emerging technologies are enabling new approaches to preserving our built heritage.

title: Innovators Stage | Preserving What Matters: Digital Innovation and the Future of Historic Stewardship
speakers: Ramesh Sridharan, Director, Reality Solutions, Autodesk | Rachel Tuller, VP, Global Partner Ecosystem Sales, Autodesk | Justin Gunther, Director of Fallingwater, Fallingwater | Touf Hassoun, President/CEO, Case Technologies
abstract:
Historic landmarks carry memory, identity, and community — but preserving them is increasingly complex as age, climate, and visitor demand put new pressure on cultural sites. Justin Gunther, Vice President and Director of Fallingwater, will share what it takes to steward one of Frank Lloyd Wright’s masterpieces for future generations. Touf Hassoun, CEO of Case Technologies, will discuss how reality capture, digital twins, and AI are helping preservation teams better understand and protect historic places. Autodesk Chief Customer Officer Elisabeth Zornes will moderate a conversation on how craft, expertise, and technology can move preservation from reactive repair to proactive, data-informed stewardship with innovation at the center.

Short documentary

title: AI: A Practical Guide to Implementation and Risk Management
speakers: May Winfield, Global Director of Legal + Digital Risks, Buro Happold
topics: Architecture services | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM 360 Build | Forma | AECO | Software Development | Cross Industry
abstract: This talk will offer a clear, practical road map for using AI without sleepwalking into liability minefields. Drawing on real disputes, emerging case law, and live industry data, we’ll explain where AI can go wrong in design, delivery, and operations, and what this means for contracts, professional duties, and insurance. Using vivid, real-world examples of AI hallucinations, flawed outputs, and disputed responsibility, we’ll demystify what good practice looks like in reality. You’ll learn how to cut through AI hype, how to embed internal processes and procedures, and how to structure effective internal training and implement proportionate governance, assurance, and documentation that satisfy clients, regulators, and insurers while still enabling innovation.

title: Connected Design: Real-World Collaboration Workflows Across Autodesk Forma and Revit
speakers: Matt Arsenault, Principal Product Manager - Forma Connected Clients, Autodesk | Caoimhe Loftus, Product Manager, Forma Model, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | BIM 360 Docs | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma | Forma Site Design | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Architecture
abstract: The way architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) teams work across tools has long been fragmented: models reimported manually, analyses running outside the authoring environment, and design intent lost at every handoff. Forma Connected Clients is here to change that. Two of the product managers behind Forma Connected Clients will share insights into the strategy and walk you through a real workflow connecting Autodesk Forma Site Design, Forma Building Design, Forma Board, and Revit software. Hear from customers on what's already shifting. See Autodesk Forma analyses spanning across design applications, keeping multiple models aligned without reimport, and collaborative live design review with Forma Board—all in one connected process.

title: Ask the Experts Panel: AI in AutoCAD and Civil 3D, From Today's Tools to Tomorrow's Workflows
speakers: Anum Mithani, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Alëna Iouguina, Director, User Experience, AutoCAD, Civil 3D and Reality Capture, Autodesk | Peter Qian, Sr Director, Software Engineering, Autodesk | Sachin Singh, Senior Product Manager, AutoCAD Web, Autodesk | Tim Yarris, Sr. Group Product Manager, Civil 3D and Infrastructure Product Line, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | AutoCAD | AutoCAD LT | AutoCAD web app | Civil 3D | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Curious how AI is actually showing up in AutoCAD, AutoCAD Web, and Civil 3D, and where it's headed next? In this interactive "Ask the Experts" panel, our experts will go beyond the hype to talk about how AI is starting to change the way design work gets done. We'll explore where AI shows up in your workflows today, how Autodesk Assistant is evolving with Model Context Protocols (MCPs) to support faster, smarter decisions, and what's coming as AI becomes a more active partner in the design process across desktop and web. Expect a candid conversation about the opportunities, the open questions, and how you can start putting AI to work right now. The session is moderated, with plenty of time for audience questions, so come ready to ask.

title: Ask the Experts Panel: AI in AutoCAD and Civil 3D, From Today's Tools to Tomorrow's Workflows
speakers: Anum Mithani, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Alëna Iouguina, Director, User Experience, AutoCAD, Civil 3D and Reality Capture, Autodesk | Peter Qian, Sr Director, Software Engineering, Autodesk | Sachin Singh, Senior Product Manager, AutoCAD Web, Autodesk | Tim Yarris, Sr. Group Product Manager, Civil 3D and Infrastructure Product Line, Autodesk
