title: The Foster + Partners Journey to ISO 19650 Certification and BSI Kitemark—Enabled by Autodesk Forma
speakers: Lola Carbajal Moro, Digital Delivery, Foster + Partners | Daniel Roca Monteagudo, Senior BIM & Design Systems Coordinator, Foster + Partners
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Forma | Navisworks Manage | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Achieving BSI Kitemark certification for ISO 19650 Information Management as a Lead Appointed Party requires sustained effort, careful governance, and consistent project delivery. This session will explain how Foster + Partners undertook the work required to achieve certification, embedding ISO 19650 principles into everyday practice across complex, multidisciplinary projects. It will outline key steps taken, including defining roles, establishing proportionate information-management processes, developing project-ready documentation, and evidencing consistent application across live projects. The session will also explore challenges such as scaling processes and meeting audit expectations, giving you a view of how to prepare effectively for certification.

title: AI from Anywhere: Building Secure Hybrid AI Workflows for Autodesk Users
speakers: Mark Hirst, World Wide Solutions Manager, Lenovo
topics: MEP Engineering  | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Geospatial and GIS | Architecture services | AutoCAD | Fusion | Revit | VRED | AECO
abstract:
AI is transforming design workflows, but many firms face the same challenge: how do you encourage innovation while maintaining data privacy, security, governance, and control of escalating cloud costs?
In this session, Lenovo explores how architects, engineers, and designers are building AI capability from the ground up using a hybrid approach that combines Autodesk cloud services, AI PCs powered by Intel Core Ultra processors, local AI inference, remote workstations, and centralized AI resources. Learn how organizations are creating safe environments for AI experimentation, enabling teams to test ideas using real project data, evaluate business value, and scale successful workflows with confidence.
Discover how firms are empowering users to innovate from anywhere while balancing performance, flexibility, security, and cost.
Key message: Experiment locally. Collaborate globally. Scale in the cloud.

title: Building Custom AEC Apps in Minutes: AI-Assisted Development with FORMA and VIKTOR.AI
speakers: Jordana Rosa, Autodesk | Peter Madlener, CEO, VIKTOR
topics: Data and Document Management | Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract:
Design teams increasingly need trusted workflows that connect Autodesk Forma, Autodesk Platform Services (APS), agentic AI, engineering tools, proprietary company knowledge, and cloud automation to solve real project challenges. This session explores how organizations can use open APIs and modern development platforms to build custom applications and intelligent workflows around Forma Site Design and Building Design.

Attendees will learn how to integrate project data, automate engineering and design processes, connect cloud services, and extend Autodesk workflows with company-specific logic. We will also introduce the Autodesk Marketplace and discuss how developers can package and distribute solutions that strengthen the Autodesk ecosystem.

Using VIKTOR.AI as the application, workflow, and agentic automation layer, we will demonstrate how Autodesk technologies can be combined with AI, engineering software, and internal knowledge. We will show how organizations can move beyond isolated AI prompts by creating transparent, controlled, and verifiable workflows in which agents execute tasks, use engineering tools, and present traceable results for expert review.

title: AI for Ideation: Telling a Good Story with Generative AI and Autodesk Platform Services
speakers: Zachary Smith, Autodesk Platform Developer, HDR | Andrell Laniewicz, East Region RBG Digital Delivery Lead, HDR
topics: Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | Forge | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Imagine this scenario: You’re a developer and a user identifies a problem that, when solved, could save hundreds of hours per project. Moreover, there doesn’t appear to be a solution on the market that solves this problem adequately, so you get to build something. In an industry where users are more likely to buy a story than a product, how do we tell a good story? This discussion will center around our approach to collaboratively translating ideas into prototypes. We’ll use generative AI and Autodesk Platform Services as our low-barrier-to-entry tools for the code, and demonstrate the value of building trust in the solution by building it together.

title: Symetri Presents: The Revit Family Feud
speakers: Heather Volk, Strategic Implementation Manager - MEP, Symetri | Abra Cooley, Strategic Implementation Manager - MEP, Symetri
topics: MEP Engineering  | Engineering service providers | Revit Live | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract: Survey says... there's a better way to work in Revit. Join Heather Volk and Abra Cooley for an interactive game-show-style workflow challenge that puts common project tasks, coordination issues, and productivity bottlenecks center stage. Through real-world MEP scenarios, attendees will compare traditional and optimized workflows while estimating the time and effort behind everyday Revit tasks. Using Revit, Naviate MEP, and Naviate Accelerate, this engaging session will combine live demonstrations, audience participation, and friendly competition to showcase practical ways to improve efficiency, reduce rework, streamline coordination, and increase productivity.

title: Demystifying AI: Find the sweet spot for starting up in AI using LLMs, Autodesk Assistant, and MCPs in your company
speakers: David Banyard, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk | STEPHANIE CATALINA, Principal Professional Services Consultant, Autodesk | Xiaoxuan Peng, Director of Digital Delivery, stv
topics: Buildings | Build | Forma | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Learn how large language models (LLMs) and model content protocols (MCPs) work, when to use them, and how to get better results with effective prompting. See how STV began their journey into AI, and learn about their process. Explore practical ways to use Autodesk Assistant across tools and discover how AI is integrated into Forma to support design decisions. Walk away with real workflows, tips, and confidence to apply AI in your daily work. Learn how to use LLMs to create add ins, dynamo scripts, and general design automation.

title: Precast Concrete Solutions: Achieving Convergence Through Revit-Inventor Data Exchange
speakers: 岩倉巧 TakumiIwakura, BIM Manager, HAZAMA ANDO CORPORATION | Shuhei Tazawa, Associate Professor, Toyo University
topics: Buildings | Docs | Informed Design | Inventor | Revit | Vault Professional | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: In this session, you’ll learn how to move beyond drawing-based coordination and establish a connected design-to-manufacturing workflow based on data convergence. Through an actual project of a general contractor operating a precast concrete plant, this session will explain how Revit and Inventor software were integrated via Autodesk Forma and Informed Design to enable the convergence of design and manufacturing data. You will see how configurable and reusable manufacturing models are created, and how data can flow consistently from BIM to production. The session will demonstrate how this convergence-driven approach reduced workload by more than 40%, and how it provides practical insights that designers and manufacturing engineers can apply to reduce rework, improve quality, and strengthen cross-team collaboration.

title: Shift to Next-Generation Construction: From Connected Processes to Predictive Decision Making
speakers: Yui Kikuchi, Chief, Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd. | Yoshinori 慶典, Chief, Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd. | Takuya Ogawa, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Build | Forma | Insight | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: During construction, fragmented information and decision making across multiple teams remain a major challenge. At Daiwa House, Autodesk Forma projects are launched across more than 400 design and construction projects each year, supporting collaboration across departments. About 130 of these projects use Autodesk Forma Site Design to establish concurrent processes from the early design stage and reduce information gaps. Building on this track data, we’re developing an integrated construction platform for schedule and cost forecasting and recommendations. The goal is to connect these predictions and make decision making itself more predictable. This session will present future processes, technology, and organizational change for next-generation construction.

title: From Design Intent to Preconstruction Reality: Closing the Carbon Data Handover Gap
speakers: Andrea Colombo, BIM & Design Systems Coordinator, Foster + Partners | Blerina Celniku, Carbon Lead, Multiplex | Abril Rueda, BIM Coordinator Specialist, Arcadis | Daniel Traver, Decarbonization Specialist, DPR Construction | Marta Bouchard, Dir., Sustainability Solutions, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | BIM 360 Build | Build | Quantity Takeoff | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Decarbonization is accelerating across the built environment, yet the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry lacks consistent ways to manage carbon data across project phases. Through a collaboration led by the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD) and Autodesk, 11 leading AEC firms are working to define and improve how carbon data transitions from design to preconstruction. Based on applied learnings, this panel will examine data challenges in the preconstruction handoff, including gaps in material quantities, nonmodeled elements, specifications, and assumptions—and we’ll highlight emerging best practices and recommendations. Gain practical strategies for your projects and ways to improve carbon data consistency, transparency, and decision making across phases.

title: From Design Intent to Preconstruction Reality: Closing the Carbon Data Handover Gap
speakers: Marta Bouchard, Dir., Sustainability Solutions, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | BIM 360 Build | Build | Quantity Takeoff | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Decarbonization is accelerating across the built environment, yet the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry lacks consistent ways to manage carbon data across project phases. Through a collaboration led by the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD) and Autodesk, 11 leading AEC firms are working to define and improve how carbon data transitions from design to preconstruction. Based on applied learnings, this panel will examine data challenges in the preconstruction handoff, including gaps in material quantities, nonmodeled elements, specifications, and assumptions—and we’ll highlight emerging best practices and recommendations. Gain practical strategies for your projects and ways to improve carbon data consistency, transparency, and decision making across phases.

title: ​From Chaos to Control: Model Coordination in Autodesk Forma and API Strategies for Infrastructure Projects
speakers: Adrian Fernandez Sanchez, Product Owner Autodesk Transport, Rambøll Norge | Maria Albízuri, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | Docs | Model Coordination | Navisworks Manage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: In large-scale infrastructure, "coordination chaos" is a common reality. When teams use different tools and inconsistent methods, design mistakes are often caught too late. This leads to expensive rework, missed deadlines, and increased project risk. As projects grow across disciplines, keeping everyone aligned becomes a massive challenge. In this session, we’ll share how Ramboll tamed this complexity by building a standardized, scalable framework using Autodesk Forma industry cloud (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Using the 2025 IFC Viewer, Autodesk Platform Services, and Insight dashboards, Ramboll moved from disconnected software to a single, unified system. We’ve aligned our digital process with ISO 19650 to ensure data moves smoothly from one project phase to the next.

title: Level Up Your Corridors: Unlocking Advanced Civil 3D Modeling Techniques
speakers: Shelby L Smith, BIM Manager, Bohler | Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc.
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Think Civil 3D corridors are just for roads? Time to think again. Corridors have a secret life as high-performance grading machines for infrastructure design. In this technical deep dive, we’ll push familiar Civil 3D tools to their limits to solve complex geometry. Through scenarios like cul-de-sacs, knuckles, parking lot grading, and driveway connections, you’ll see how dynamic corridor models maintain design control in both site and roadway environments. We’ll demonstrate advanced workflows for modeling precision and show how Subassembly Composer extends these possibilities. Gain the expertise to build adaptable models that reduce manual rework and streamline digital delivery for every project.

title: One Digital Playbook – Scaling Lessons Across Level Crossing Removal
speakers: Jack Donaghy, Digital Lead, Beca Ltd
topics: Civil infrastructure | BIM 360 Build | BIM 360 Docs | Civil 3D | Navisworks Manage | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: This session will explore how Auckland’s road-rail level crossing program used the Autodesk platform to deliver complex infrastructure under a fast‑tracked delivery program. Using Autodesk Forma as a common data environment, the team standardized site visit reporting with Forma Build, automated asset data management through Autodesk APIs, and enhanced design quality with improved clash detection workflows. Design models were integrated with site time‑lapse imagery using Viewer APIs and augmented reality to improve construction insight. The program also used Revit software to produce high‑quality renders, video fly‑throughs, and 3D‑printed pedestrian bridge models, improving stakeholder engagement and decision making.

title: End-to-End New Geolocation Solution Across Autodesk Platforms: From Civil 3D to Revit
speakers: Frank Huang, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk | Ivy(Ruoqian) Lu, Senior Product Owner, Autodesk
topics: Geospatial and GIS | Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Geolocation is essential for accurate positioning, data integration, and interoperability across architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) workflows. This session will introduce core concepts such as coordinate systems, datums, and spatial references—and show how they’re applied across Autodesk platforms. You will learn how to create and manage coordinate systems in Civil 3D software, define geolocation in Civil 3D and AutoCAD software, and understand how these support geographic information system (GIS) integration. The session will also cover legacy and modern geolocation workflows in Revit software, highlighting improvements in model alignment and interoperability. By connecting workflows across Civil 3D and Revit, this class will provide practical guidance on maintaining consistent geospatial positioning throughout a project’s lifecycle.

title: Get the Most Out of the Drainage Tools in Civil 3D
speakers: Brian Hailey, CAD Manager, GEI Consultants
topics: Water Infrastructure | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Moving data back and forth between multiple design and modeling programs can be time-consuming and prone to error. The Civil 3D drainage design environment addresses this by allowing engineers to model complete stormwater systems in one place. This session will demonstrate a practical workflow for building a drainage network using the rainfall manager, catchments, channels, ponds, and underground storage components. You’ll learn how to define rainfall events, generate runoff through catchments, create storage and conveyance elements, and run hydraulic analyses to evaluate system performance.

title: Better Together: Drainage Design Best Practices with InfoDrainage and Civil 3D
speakers: Hunter Sparks, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | AJ Czubai, Technical Specialist, Water, Autodesk
topics: Water Infrastructure | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfoDrainage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: With the release of drainage tools for Civil 3D 2026, users are asking: How do these tools fit into Autodesk’s drainage design ecosystem? This session provides a clear, practical comparison of drainage tools for Civil 3D and InfoDrainage, including how each solution integrates into your workflows. We will demonstrate how to combine Autodesk tools with open-source solutions and LLM’s to unlock new possibilities. We streamline the drainage design process by using API and Civil 3D tools for catchment delineation. Walk away with a practical understanding of the tools, with the ability to navigate Autodesk’s evolving drainage design landscape and leverage a hybrid ecosystem for scalable, intelligent design.

title: Inside the Factory Experience: How We Design Hands-On Manufacturing for AU
speakers: Brittany Evans, Senior Technology Consultant, Autodesk | Phil Eichmiller, Principal SW Eng. Test, Autodesk | Jonathan Odom, Community Manager, Fusion, Autodesk | Rhett Moore, Director, Digital Design & Eng. Content, Avnet, Inc. | Brian DeSmith, Senior Solutions Engineer, Xometry
topics: Consumer products | FlexSim | Fusion | Fusion Machine Connect | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | D&M | Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: The Factory Experience gives AU attendees a hands-on way to build a simple electronic device—but creating that experience requires coordination across design, manufacturing, and delivery. This panel will bring together Autodesk and industry partners to share how the Factory Experience is conceived, developed, and brought to life on the expo floor. Panelists will discuss how teams align on design intent, navigate real-world production constraints, and deliver a scalable, repeatable experience for AU attendees. Topics will include cross-company collaboration, prototyping-to-production workflows, and the role of emerging technologies like AI. You’ll gain insight into how complex systems are transformed into engaging educational experiences.

title: Stop Filling Out Forms: Auto-Generating Autodesk Forma Forms at Scale
speakers: Dominic Martens, Group Construction Technology Manager, Icon Construction
topics: Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Every construction project uses forms, but creating and managing them manually can quickly become time-consuming and inconsistent across teams. This session will explore how Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) forms can be automatically generated and populated using Forma Construction Connect (formerly ACC Connect) and Workato. Learn how automation can trigger forms from project events such as inspections, workflows, or schedule activities, and prefill information from project data and external systems. Using real project examples, we’ll demonstrate how automated form generation can reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and ensure critical project information is captured accurately across large construction portfolios.

title: Building an Industry-Class Electrical Subcontractor Revit Template
speakers: Derek Renn, Director of BIM Technology, Bergelectric Corporation
topics: Construction services | BIM Collaborate | Desktop Connector | Docs | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: In this session, we’ll walk through the process of building an electrical detailing and prefabrication Revit template that supports more than 50 detailers in multiple regions across the United States. Then we’ll examine what it takes to evolve it to the next level with EVOLVE Electrical.

title: People Before Platforms: How Gamuda Made Change Stick with Autodesk Forma
speakers: Jowenn Lua, Sr Principal, Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | Arthur Mun Siew Meng, Group Digital Engineering Acting Sn Manager, Gamuda | Kelsey Stein, Sr Manager, Consulting Services, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Docs | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Digital transformation in construction fails far more often than it succeeds, largely due to resistance to change, legacy system complexity, and poor adoption planning. In this AU class, we’ll explore how Gamuda successfully navigated these challenges while scaling Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) across a global construction organization. Using real examples from Gamuda’s journey, this session will focus on aligning leadership, empowering champions, and supporting end users through continuous training and engagement. We'll examine how Gamuda addressed cultural resistance, integrated Autodesk Forma with legacy systems using open APIs, and implemented robust data governance aligned to ISO 27001 standards.

title: AEC Roadmap: Forma - Cost Management + GCPay and Payapps
speakers: Cassie Bustos, Principal Product Marketing Manager, Construction, Autodesk | Mark Ballinger, Dir, Product Strategy, PayApps, Autodesk | Ian Turner, Group Product Manager, Autodesk | Evan Zachmann, Sr Product Strategy  Manager, GC Pay, Autodesk
topics: Project Financials | Construction Operations | Construction services | Build | AECO
abstract: Construction teams need strong project financial controls to reduce risk and protect the bottom line. Join this session to learn how Autodesk is evolving cost management across Autodesk Forma Build, GCPay, and Payapps to deliver greater visibility, accuracy, and confidence. We’ll cover what’s new and what’s coming next across budget and change management, forecasting, and payment workflows. And we’ll explore how these solutions work together to create a more connected financial ecosystem. Get a behind-the-scenes look at our product strategy and key investments focused on helping teams manage costs more proactively, reduce financial risk, and improve project outcomes.

title: General Contractor Meetup
speakers: Kellie Herring, Customer Success Manager, ACS, Autodesk | LaShawn Hodge, Principal Account Services Rep, Autodesk | Jared McKibben, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | Build | Insight | TradeTapp | Workshop XR | AECO | Construction Management | Meetup
abstract: Join us in a session designed to connect general contractors around the United States so they can exchange best practices, wins, and lessons learned that enhance the construction customer experience. This is a place to network with like-minded contractors and owners to share ideas and dive deeper into workflows you wouldn’t normally find in an Autodesk webinar. We want to connect YOU with your peers to elevate the way you manage your facilities, helping Autodesk create the most valuable tool for your needs—based on your feedback, presented by your peers.

title: Mastering Autodesk Fabrication: Advanced ITM Content Management Tips and Strategies
speakers: Darren J Young, Consultant, Self Employed | Scott Hendricks, Owner, Virtual Building Supply
topics: Construction services | Fabrication CADmep | Fabrication CAMduct | Fabrication Data Manager | Fabrication ESTmep | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Managing Fabrication ITM content effectively is critical to keeping projects on track and teams working efficiently. This session will cover advanced strategies for connector naming and connectivity, helping you build smarter, more consistent content from the ground up. We'll explore tips and tricks using a hybrid workflow—using MEP Content Editor in the cloud alongside local products like Fabrication CADmep, Fabrication ESTmep, and Fabrication CAMduct—to build and manage content with precision. You'll also learn how to execute mass content changes while modeling jobs are in progress, minimizing disruption and avoiding costly errors. Walk away with strategies you can implement immediately.

title: Bridge the Gap: Syncing Autodesk Forma, Procore, and HCSS with ProjectReady WorkBridge
speakers: Jordan Bullock, MBA, ACI, Manager, Design Software & Training, Topcon Solutions | Joe Giegerich, CEO, ProjectReady
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Autodesk Platform Services | BuildingConnected | Construction Cloud | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Are you tired of manually re-entering data between Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), Procore, and HCSS? ProjectReady WorkBridge eliminates that burden. In this live product demo, Topcon Solutions and ProjectReady will walk through three real-world workflows: bidirectional sync between Autodesk Forma and Procore for submittals, RFIs, issues, and photos; project data transfers from Procore to Autodesk Forma; and the connecting of HCSS HeavyBid to BuildingConnected for a seamless preconstruction-to-construction handoff. See WorkBridge's scheduling engine, audit logs, and no-data-at-rest architecture in action—and leave knowing how to connect your platforms and keep every team aligned.

title: Agentic AI for Next‑Generation AEC Workflows
speakers: Ken Denton, Global Segment Lead AEC / PD&M, HP
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | None | AECO
abstract:
This session will be presented by Greg Schleusner, AIA, owner of 2611 Labs, former Principal Director of Design Technology at HOK, and Adjunct Assistant Professor at Columbia University.

Lightweight laptops with large, unified memory pools have crossed an important threshold: they can now run capable AI assistants locally. For AEC professionals, this creates something fundamentally different from a chatbot or copilot that waits for prompts and returns suggestions. A local assistant can remain connected to design tools, carry out multi-step assignments in the background, and even create new utilities when existing tools fall short—all without an internet connection or sending project data to the cloud.

This session will demonstrate the power of  such an assistant by combining state-of-the-art models, tool integrations, workflows, and agent harnesses into a practical working example of the power of one machine.  It will also examine the larger shift this makes possible: as models and inference software improve, the hardware you can buy today, becomes increasingly capable. We are only beginning to understand what becomes possible when every practitioner can have a private, persistent, and extensible AI collaborator working alongside them.

title: Unlocking Connected Workflows: Vault Connector for Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Fusion Manage
speakers: Senthil Kumar, Sr. Manager, Software Development, Autodesk | Younes Yammouri, Director, Product Management, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Industrial machinery | Forma | Fusion Manage | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: This session will explore how the Vault Connector enables connected workflows between Vault, Autodesk Forma, and Autodesk Fusion Manage, helping organizations bridge the gap between engineering data and enterprise lifecycle processes. We’ll begin with an overview of the latest enhancements to the Vault Connector for Fusion Manage, highlighting improvements introduced in recent Vault releases. We’ll then move into a deep dive on the new Vault Connector for Autodesk Forma, exploring how it enables seamless data exchange between design environments and cloud platforms. You will gain insights into integration workflows and real-world use cases. The session will conclude with an interactive Q&A session.

title: PLM Summit | Connected Data and Change-Management Process
speakers: Justin Williams, Engineering Manager, Humanetics
topics: Data and Document Management | Manufacturing Other | Fusion Manage | Inventor | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | PLM
abstract: Discover our successful transition from a heavily customized, end-of-life forms automation system—processing more than 600 engineering change orders (ECOs) annually—to Autodesk Fusion Manage integrated with Vault Professional software. Learn how we mitigated critical system-failure risks that could have doubled annual change-process costs from ~$130,000 to more than $250,000 and disrupted on-time shipments of multimillion-dollar orders worldwide. Explore the enhanced change-management capabilities we now benefit from, including task and milestone assignments, approval tracking, and metric dashboards. We’ll also share our road map and planned next steps for expanding into quality processes linked to product data as well as future enterprise resource planning (ERP) integration.

title: Building the Digital Thread: M2X’s Path from Engineering to Manufacturing Scale
speakers: Justin Johnson, M2X Energy | Nicholas Schwartz, Chief Manufacturing Officer at M2X Energy, M2X Energy
topics: Data and Document Management | Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Fusion Manage | Inventor | Vault PLM | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: What breaks when a 10-person engineering team becomes a 70-person manufacturing organization? This session will explore M2X’s real-world journey scaling with Inventor, Vault, AutoCAD Plant 3D, and Autodesk Fusion Manage software. Learn how the team transitioned from ad hoc design workflows to structured data management and a connected PDM/PLM strategy. We’ll cover how to time tool adoption, avoid common scaling missteps, and enable cross-functional collaboration between engineering and production. You’ll gain practical frameworks to structure product data, build a digital thread, and support rapid growth—while improving quality, reducing rework, and maintaining control across the product lifecycle.

title: Why AI Struggles in Real-World Making—And How to Make It Work
speakers: Kelvin Hamilton, Sr. Manager, Technology Consulting, Autodesk | Nathan Kutz, Director of Physics Informed AI, Autodesk | Fope Bademosi, Circular Economy and Construction Researcher, Autodesk | Adam Allard, Senior Manager, Technical Environments, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | None | D&M | Industrialized Construction | Future Industry Innovations | Cross Industry
abstract: AI has transformed design and simulation, yet its role in real-world making—where materials, tolerances, and human judgment converge—remains emergent. Fabrication is variable, unforgiving, and governed by physics that challenge AI tools. This panel will explore the current state of AI in manufacturing and construction, focusing on how agentic systems can augment, not replace, skilled practitioners. Drawing on applied research from the Autodesk Technology Centers, we’ll share how we train AI on real fabrication data, develop physics-informed models, and test intelligent, automated manufacturing workflows. Join experts across domains to examine how human-AI collaboration can drive impactful outcomes from factory floors to jobsites.

title: Revit Family Building for Facility Management 101
speakers: Dzan Ta, Autodesk Technical Specialist, Symetri | AU Speaker, Test | ARGELIA Barcena, Head of Regional Leads - North America, Women in BIM | Howard Munsell, Sr. Design Application Specialist II, Whitman Requardt & Assoc
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Architecture services | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Do you want to learn how to build families properly? Do you want to know how to build them with custom parameters? Do you want to know how to build them for facilities management use? If so, this class is for you. If not, come anyway and learn something cool and fun. Unlock the power of creating your own custom content. In this hands-on lab, you’ll learn about the art of building Revit families from the ground up, specifically tailored for facility management. We’ll guide you through setting up the framework, crafting geometry, adding character, and defining custom parameters. By the end, you’ll know how to schedule your data and use these families to streamline your facility management workflows.

title: Stop Rebuilding Your Project: The Autodesk Forma Lifecycle Challenge—From AI Planning to Built Outcomes
speakers: Beatriz Davi Medola, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk | Danielle Foss, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk | Ignacio Suque, Sr Technical Account Manager, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Build | Docs | Forma | Model Coordination | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Projects shouldn’t feel like starting over at every phase—yet they often do, leading to lost data, and rework. This interactive lab tackles that challenge through a full lifecycle experience with Autodesk Forma. Experience how one connected workflow can take a project from AI-powered site planning in Forma Site Design, through data management and collaboration, to construction outcomes. Along the way, you'll step into different project roles, experience real-world scenarios, make critical decisions, and achieve the best results across the lifecycle. You won’t just learn the workflow—you’ll experience it, making it memorable and directly applicable to your projects.

title: Pipe Design in InfoWorks ICM: Penalty Configuration and Automatic Constraint Relaxation
speakers: Samer Muhandes, Senior Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk | Ahmed Elsayed, Technical Specialist, Water, Autodesk
topics: Water Infrastructure | Engineering service providers | InfoWorks ICM | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: This hands-on lab will teach you the practical use of the InfoWorks ICM Network Design logic for both stormwater and sanitary networks. Through guided exercises, you’ll configure design constraints, explore the new penalty configuration parameters and the concept of automatic relaxation of constraints, apply design locks and backdrops, build and edit pipe network catalogs and selection lists, and interpret the design report to diagnose infeasible pipes. During the session, you’ll use the Rational Method and intensity-duration-frequency (IDF) curves to calculate peak flows for stormwater design. And then you’ll move to sanitary design using population-based peak flows with validation and troubleshooting best practices so you can apply InfoWorks ICM design logic confidently.

title: Design-Driven Reinforcement in Revit: From Analysis Results to Automated Rebar and Documentation
speakers: Irina Cojocaru, R&D Product Director, Graitec | Stevens Chemise, Product Manager, Graitec Innovation
topics: Structural Engineering  | Buildings | Revit | Robot Structural Analysis | Robot Structural Analysis Professional | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Revit software is evolving into a design-driven environment for structural engineers, enabling a seamless transition from analysis to reinforcement and documentation. In this hands-on session, you’ll integrate results from FEM software—such as Robot Structural Analysis, GRAITEC Advance Design, or other tools—directly into Revit to perform code-based checks and generate reinforcement for concrete members, including beams, columns, footings, and walls. You’ll automate rebar cage generation, produce engineering reports, and generate drawings and schedules within a single BIM-integrated platform, reducing manual work, improving coordination, and ensuring compliance with US and European standards.

title: Design. Optimize. Connect. Build Smarter Products with Autodesk Fusion.
speakers: Ignacio Madina, Sr Technical Specialist,  Fusion, Autodesk | David Sabaté, Sr Territory Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Design Extension | Fusion Generative Design Extension | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | Fusion Simulation Extension | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Have you ever wanted to design a part but weren’t sure how to approach it using the available tools and materials? Would you like to analyze existing products to identify optimizations or potential failures before they occur—or transform current designs into smarter, more capable products? In this hands-on lab, we’ll use Autodesk Fusion to work more effectively across key stages of the product lifecycle—from initial concept to optimization and intelligent enhancement. Using a smart desk lamp as our example, we’ll explore three distinct workflows: designing a manufacturable component from scratch, analyzing and optimizing critical parts, and finally enhancing the product by integrating electronics to create a smarter, connected system.

title: From Emerging Tech to Enterprise Adoption: Autodesk & Arcadis Shaping the Future of AEC
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Architecture
abstract: How does a 36,000-person design and engineering firm decide what new technology is worth adopting? In this fireside chat, leaders from Autodesk and Arcadis discuss what it really takes to introduce emerging tools into a global AEC practice. The conversation covers the promise of Autodesk Forma Site Design and Building Design, and a candid look at how both parties are testing and shaping these products together.

title: How AI Agents are reshaping the way AEC works
speakers: John Meyer, Founder & CEO, Mosaic
topics: Structural Engineering  | Project Financials | Construction Operations | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Architecture services | None | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Architecture and engineering firms are going agentic. The ones moving now will set the pace for everyone else. This session will get into what that actually means for your practice, with a concrete plan you can act on immediately. An agent isn't a smarter chatbot. It's a system you give instructions, skills, tools, and context—and then trust to do real work. Chello, Mosaic's AI planning assistant, shows what that looks like in practice: it watches project deadlines, catches scope creep before it eats your profit, forecasts workload and revenue, and keeps the whole firm's plan current, so leadership is always in control and never caught off guard. We'll cover how agents connect to your existing systems through Model Context Protocol (MCP), how to capture your firm's expertise so it scales across every team member, and when to build versus buy. The firms that get this right will operate at a level their competitors can't match. This session will be your starting point.

title: Innovators Stage | The Power of Storytelling in a Data-Driven World
speakers: Tom Kelley, Founder & Advisor, D4V (Design for Ventures)
abstract: Whether you're proposing a new product, presenting a design, or helping clients imagine a better future, storytelling is often what moves ideas from possibility to reality. In today's data-driven world, storytelling has become an essential skill for anyone who wants to gain influence, inspire action, and help others see what's possible. In this engaging session, Tom Kelley shares memorable examples from business, design, and innovation, along with practical techniques for transforming data and insights into stories that resonate with colleagues and decision-makers. Along the way, you'll have a live "thumbs up or thumbs down" moment, as you help decide which topic Tom explores next. You'll leave with practical storytelling tools and a fresh perspective on how compelling stories help turn promising ideas into reality by first helping other people imagine a future that doesn't yet exist.

title: From Massing to Metrics: Integrating Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights for Outcome-Based Design
speakers: Michael from Chile Sturm, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | Jessica Carson, Architect, GHD Design | Isaac McCormack, Architect, GHD Design
topics: Architecture services | Forma | Insight | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Around 80% of a building’s environmental impact is determined in the first 20% of design, yet this phase often relies on intuition rather than data. This presentation will introduce GHD’s outcome-based workflow that embeds predictive AI and cloud simulation into early design, providing carbon insights when decisions matter. Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) enables real-time evaluation of wind, thermal comfort, and early embodied carbon from simple massing models. As designs progress, Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights (formerly Autodesk Insight) calculates energy-use intensity and examines trade-offs between operational and embodied carbon. The result is an iterative, data-driven approach that integrates carbon performance into design and enables credible sustainability narratives from project inception.

title: Automating ISO 7817 Compliance: A Practical Workflow Using Dynamo, Revit, and LLMs
speakers: Idris Bahadur, Co-Founder Architect, ROP Architects
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Producing and controlling data from project models at a defined level is still largely a manual and error-prone process. This session will present ISO 7817 (Level of Information Need), the emerging standard beyond traditional Levels of Detail, and show how BIM execution plan requirements link to a Revit model. The session will explore a closed-loop workflow that tracks data from requirements to reporting. The method includes transferring information requirements from Microsoft Excel into Revit elements as parameters using Dynamo, guiding modelers by showing what data to input and why within element properties, collecting data back into Excel, and automatically generating performance reports by doing a row-by-row comparison of “Required” and “Provided” data using a large language model (LLM).

title: Agentic Design Exploration: How LA28 and Autodesk Research Partnered to Lower Carbon and Cost
speakers: Arthur Harsuvanakit, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: Agentic design exploration marks a new frontier in sustainable architecture, shaped through partnerships like Autodesk and LA28. In this real-world case study, you’ll see how the approach aligned design, cost, and climate goals. By combining domain expertise with AI workflows, the team addressed ambitious targets using agent-based tools across the project's site, building, and assembly scales—integrating codes, performance, and program needs. These workflows enabled rapid generation and refinement of design options, helping identify high-performing, buildable solutions earlier, reducing carbon and costs. You’ll compare where AI-driven workflows succeed, where they fall short, and how to apply them at scale.

title: Right Knowledge, Right Time: Transforming Scattered Training into Scalable Learning
speakers: Joshua Bradshaw, Director CORE Delivery, Thornton Tomasetti | Mike Federspiel, Customer Success Manager, Eagle Point Software | Mary Forbes, Customer Success Team Lead, Eagle Point Software
topics: Structural Engineering  | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Architecture services | Civil 3D | Forma | Navisworks Manage | Revit | Workshop XR | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Engineering firms struggle to scale technology training beyond one-off classes and static PDFs, especially when teams are fully billable and tool stacks evolve rapidly. At Thornton Tomasetti, the CORE technology team addresses this by combining Eagle Point Software's Pinnacle Series with Glean—an AI-powered enterprise search platform—to transform fragmented standards, institutional knowledge, and vendor content into structured, role-based learning journeys. This session will show you how workflow-integrated training and enterprise search deliver the right guidance at the moment of need, embedding learning into daily work, and improving adoption, consistency, and future competency pathways.

title: AI and the Architect: Designing Human-AI Workflows That Preserve Authorship
speakers: Kari Schutte, Regional Digital Delivery Lead, US South, Stantec | Eitan Sarfati, CEO, SWAPP.AI
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Architecture services | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: When Stantec deployed AI agents on a 190,000-square-foot health care project, this question stopped being theoretical: Where does AI execution end and architect authorship begin? This session—co-presented by Stantec's senior BIM administrator and SWAPP's CEO—will walk through the actual decisions made on that project. We’ll look at which documentation tasks the AI was allowed to execute, which were held back for human review, and what happened when AI agents moved a fixture during an ADA compliance check. You’ll leave with a workflow categorization framework that separates judgment-dependent work from execution-dependent work, applied live to 20 common tasks, plus the standards-governance playbook used to keep firm authorship intact under AI execution.

title: AI-Ready AECO: A 90-Day Revit and Autodesk Forma Data Management Scorecard
speakers: Michael Echave, Design Revenue Manager, ATG
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | Forma | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) firms want better automation, reporting, and AI outcomes. But inconsistent Revit parameters, unmanaged content, weak naming standards, and disconnected Autodesk Forma Data Management workflows often get in the way. This session will give BIM, virtual design and construction (VDC), and digital practice leaders a practical 90-day scorecard for identifying the data that matters most, scoring current-state readiness, and prioritizing what to fix first. You’ll see how to evaluate model health, content governance, metadata, coordination workflows, and handoff structure so you can build a realistic road map for stronger delivery, better collaboration, and future AI readiness.

title: The AI-Ready Project: How to Structure Information That Agents Can Actually Use
speakers: Benjamin Bazso, CTO, Newforma
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Architecture services | None | AECO
abstract:
AI is only as good as the data behind it - but what does that actually mean in practice? As AI continues to reshape the AECO industry, firms are beginning to realize that success depends on more than adopting the latest tools. How do you structure, connect, and manage project information so it's ready for the next wave of AI, especially agentic AI that needs to act on information, not just retrieve it? 

In this session, we'll move beyond the theory and into the practical steps firms can take today to make project information AI-ready, helping position your organization for what's next instead of scrambling to catch up.

title: AI Without Chaos: AutoCAD and Revit Plug-In Development with Spec-Driven Development
speakers: Fernando Malard, Chief Technology Officer, ofcdesk, LLC
topics: Engineering service providers | AutoCAD | Revit | AECO | Software Development | Cross Industry
abstract: AI coding tools are changing how software is developed in architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO). Inconsistent outputs, lack of standards, and tight coupling to platform APIs often lead to fragile and unstable plug-ins. This class will introduce Spec-Driven Development (SDD) as a practical, tool-agnostic approach to bring structure and reliability to AI-assisted development. Instead of prompts and chat history, SDD uses persistent specifications as the source of truth. Using plug-ins in AutoCAD and Revit software, we’ll demonstrate how to separate business logic from platform-specific implementations. You’ll learn how SDD can use modern AI tools such as OpenAI Codex to transform AI from a source of chaos into a controlled software development asset.

title: Inventor Meetup: What’s Working, What’s Not, What’s Next
speakers: Dan Szymanski, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Riya Ghosh, Sr Customer Advocate, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | Inventor | Inventor CAM | Inventor LT | Inventor Professional | Vault Professional | AECO | Meetup
abstract: Do you want to talk about what’s working in Inventor, what creates friction, and what should come next? Join the Inventor Meetup for a conversation with Autodesk’s Inventor product team and fellow users. Share experiences, compare challenges, discuss workflow practices and solutions, and explore the future of Inventor through automation tasks (iLogic, drawings), Model States, Vault-connected workflows, Content Center and data governance, AI-assisted productivity, and performance at scale. Come for honest discussion, practical insight, fresh perspectives from peers, and the opportunity to influence future priorities for Inventor in a more direct, collaborative way. Whether you’re a long-time user or a newer voice, your perspective matters.

title: Strengthening Your Core: Working with AutoCAD Core Console
speakers: Matt Miyamoto, ISD Professional Services Manager, IMAGINiT Technologies
topics: Engineering service providers | AutoCAD | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Process hundreds—or even thousands—of drawings in a fraction of the time using the AutoCAD Core Console, a powerful headless version of AutoCAD software built for high-performance batch automation. This session will go beyond theory to show how you can use the AutoCAD Core Console to execute scripts, run custom applications, and automate repetitive CAD tasks without ever opening the AutoCAD interface. You will learn how to build scalable workflows that dramatically reduce manual effort while improving consistency across large drawing sets.

title: Autodesk Forma Standardization at Scale: Jacobs’ Road to 30,000 Users
speakers: Thomas Crawford, Director of Information Management, Jacobs | Margarita Kreternova, Digital Delivery Manager - Data Centers, JACOBS | Michael McKeon, Global Principal Civil Tools, Jacobs | Nathaniel Coombs, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk | Bruce Johnson, BTS Autodesk Platform Lead, Jacobs Engineering Group
topics: Data and Document Management | Engineering service providers | Build | Civil 3D | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: The idea of global standards for any large and diverse business is often a pipe dream. How can you empower people to work in similar ways when they’re located in all corners of the world, hold different roles, and work across many markets requiring unique solutions? We can’t promise the perfect answer, but we can promise that we gave it a shot and it’s going well. We hope to share our experiences, our strategy, and our tactics, and help others around the industry solve a complex problem. Whether it’s less than 100 people or more than 1,000, the value of working in a single source of truth in a consistent way pays dividends in the quality of your deliverables, the user experience, and the time you spend kicking off and managing a project. We hope to see you there!

title: BIM Intelligence Agent: Live QTO, Carbon, Cost, and Compliance from Autodesk Forma via AI and AEC Data Model
speakers: Parthasarathi Mishra, Associate, WSP Global | Vijaya Adigopula, Technical Director, WSP
topics: Buildings | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Docs | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: What if one AI prompt returned live QTO, carbon, cost, compliance, and a 4D schedule from your Revit models in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud)—no exports or plug-ins? This session will present a working BIM Intelligence Agent built at the APS Accelerator Bangalore 2026 in four days, connecting to the AEC Data Model GraphQL API via Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Azure GPT-4.1. Ten BIM intelligence tools, all natural language. Real WSP project data live on screen will include: walls 1,860 square meters; floors 6,089 square meters; 380 tCO₂e carbon; $1.44 million cost; ISO 19650 compliance check; and a 38-week 4D schedule. One conversation, zero manual work. Learn the architecture, undocumented GraphQL patterns, 3LO OAuth flows, and 10 production bugs fixed. Code shared.

title: From Change to Clarity: Better Multidiscipline Coordination Model in Revit and Autodesk Forma Data Management
speakers: Mihaela Stan, Sr. Manager, Software Development, Autodesk | Leslaw Janus, Senior Principal Experience Designer, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | BIM Collaborate | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Discover how to effectively use Revit software’s Coordination Model Changes to monitor and manage updates across disciplines. In this hands-on session, architects and engineers will learn practical methods to detect, review, and act on element changes directly within their models. The session will cover step-by-step workflows for identifying additions, deletions, and modifications, using visual cues, filters, and structured object data. You’ll also explore how to assess geometry, properties, and transformations of updated elements to support better decision making. By the end, you’ll be able to reduce manual coordination effort, improve accuracy, and confidently integrate change tracking into your daily Revit workflows.

title: Create Your Own AI Assistant That Interacts with Revit and Other Programs at the Same Time
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E
topics: Buildings | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Current AI assistants for Revit software typically operate within a single application. This class will explore a different approach by creating a custom AI assistant that can interact with Revit and other programs simultaneously using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. The assistant can be extended to interact with additional tool applications to help solve interoperability. When creating a custom AI assistant, the available actions are defined explicitly. You’ll configure which Revit functions are exposed to the assistant and which are not. For example, you can restrict commands that delete elements, remove views, or make unwanted model changes. No prior AI or server development experience is necessary.

title: Why Universities Aren't Teaching the Offsite Industry We're Building—And the Solution
speakers: Jason Van Nest, Executive Director, Center for Offsite Construction
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | Fusion | Revit | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: The offsite construction industry is scaling, but the graduates entering it have been trained for a world of bespoke ETO delivery. No accredited degree program teaches configure-to-order workflows, manufacturing product definition, modular interface standards, or offsite logistics. The industry is hiring for skills that schools don't yet teach. This session will present the MBI-CfOC Offsite Construction Accreditation Initiative—a joint effort between the Modular Building Institute and the Center for Offsite Construction to establish the first accredited degree pathway for the industrialized construction workforce. With materials nearly complete and first accreditation discussions happening, let's understand what the next generation of offsite-trained talent will know, and how to build a firm that can absorb them.

title: AutoCAD Tips, Tricks, and the Most-Human Drafting Techniques
speakers: Donnie Gladfelter, Design Technologist, The CAD Geek
topics: Buildings | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Architecture | Civil 3D | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: You keep asking your assistant to act like an Autodesk Expert Elite member specializing in AutoCAD software, but your artificially intelligent relationship with it remains … complicated. Because somewhere between the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and the suspiciously effective large language model (LLM) that completes your sentences, your drawings still need a human. In this ninth installment of AU's top-rated AutoCAD Tips session, Autodesk Expert Elite Member Donnie "The CAD Geek" Gladfelter will deliver the most-human drafting techniques backed by the intelligence of AutoCAD 2027, including Geometry Cleanup, Smart Blocks, and Checkout that ends read-only standoffs. Plus, you’ll get deep cuts no chatbot can replicate. That's why yours flagged this session for excessive human productivity and hoped you'd never find it.

title: Break the Desktop Barrier: Dynamo in the Cloud for Scalable Revit and Civil 3D Automation
speakers: Achintya Bhat, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | John (JT) Pierson, Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Civil 3D | Dynamo | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Ever ran the same Dynamo graph across multiple projects and waited hours while Revit or Civil 3D software was locked? What if you could hand it off instead? This session will dive into how Dynamo Switchboard enables cloud execution of Dynamo graphs across projects at scale. Rather than running workflows locally or building custom pipelines with Design Automation, you can now execute graphs through a simple, player-like interface. Learn how to run batch automations across multiple models without opening host applications, and review results through logs and the Dynamo graph web viewer. Through live demos, you’ll see how to launch runs and interpret results. We’ll also briefly explore connecting workflows with Autodesk Platform Services and AEC Data Models.

title: Same Building, Different Data: Why Owners and Construction Still Miss Each Other
speakers: Andy Burg, Vice President, Messer Construction | Jacob Pfenning-Wendt, Solutions Manager, UPS | Julie Jernigan, Digital Delivery Leader - Buildings, RS&H | Mark Mergenschroer, Technical Success Manager (NAMER Adoption), Autodesk | Robert Brown, Sr. Project Controls Systems Manager, DFW Airport
topics: Data and Document Management | Buildings | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Everyone says they’re delivering “the data”—but whose data is it really? Construction teams manage RFIs, submittals, schedules, and models to get the building delivered. Owners need something very different: trusted, structured asset data they can use on day one—and for the next 30 years. In this panel, we’ll break down the disconnect between construction data and owner data, discuss why handover still fails, and examine what operational readiness actually looks like. From defining asset requirements early to validating data in the field, we’ll challenge assumptions and share what it takes to move from project closeout to lifecycle value. Because delivering everything isn’t the same as delivering what matters.

title: AEC Meets GIS: Autodesk Platform Services Viewer and Esri's MapLibre SDK for Construction and Asset Intelligence
speakers: George Owen, Product Engineer — Developer Experience team, Esri | Michael Beale, SWE, AWS
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Geospatial and GIS | Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | InfraWorks | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Esri's MapLibre GL JS software development kit (SDK) brings ArcGIS power to open-source maps: feature layers, vector tiles, terrain, geocoding, spatial analysis, and routing. Now add the Autodesk Platform Services Viewer rendering intelligent models directly into that same canvas. It’s a match made in heaven for construction and asset management. This session will show how Esri and Autodesk are converging on MapLibre to deliver unified AEC-GIS experiences. Esri demonstrates their SDK's visualization and analysis—POIs, feature styling, elevation, and basemaps—while Autodesk fuses Revit models into the scene via shared WebGL rendering with synchronized cameras. Together, we build a complete construction-site intelligence view: geospatial context meets BIM precision, in about 300 lines of code.

title: Building an Operational Digital Twin for a Health Care Facility
speakers: Naman Patwari, Head of Automation, Pinnacle Infotech | Barry Brunet, VP - Strategic Solutions, Pinnacle FutureBuild
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Buildings | ACC Connect | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma Construction Connect | Navisworks Manage | ReCap | Tandem | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Discover how Healthworld Hospitals implemented a complete Autodesk and InnoMaint CMMS‑powered digital twin to transform facility operations and maintenance workflows. This session will showcase the end-to-end journey—from site survey, laser scanning, and as-built BIM creation to real-time asset monitoring, dashboard visualization, and data-driven decision making. Learn how the digital twin improved operational efficiency, reduced downtime, and enabled smarter, safer hospital management.

title: Design Fast, Validate Smart: Extending InfoDrainage with Parametric Workflows in Civil 3D and InfoWorks ICM to Deliver Multiple Benefits
speakers: Pablo Souto, Global Discipline Leader - Water, Mott MacDonald Ltd | Juan Aguirrebengoa, Principal Civil Engineer CEng MICE, Mott MacDonald
topics: Water Infrastructure | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfoDrainage | InfoWorks ICM | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Early-stage drainage design prioritizes speed, using simplified assumptions to test options quickly. However, challenges such as combined sewer overflows (CSOs), flooding, biodiversity loss, and wider community outcomes are increasingly interconnected and require a more systems-based approach that extends beyond the traditional boundaries of the water sector. This session explores how connected digital workflows can support the identification, design, and validation of sustainable drainage interventions that deliver multiple benefits. Using an anonymized case study, attendees will see how opportunities can be rapidly explored through parametric site-design workflows in Civil 3D and InfoDrainage, then assessed through system-scale modelling in InfoWorks ICM to understand impacts on flood risk and CSO frequency, volume, and timing. The session focuses on balancing speed, rigour, and confidence in decision-making, helping practitioners understand how technology, systems thinking, and proportionate modelling can support more resilient and integrated outcomes for communities and the environment.

title: IFC 4.3 for Infrastructure: From Export to Digital Delivery
speakers: Morgan Smith, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | Salwan Abbosh, IDT Lead, Ramboll
topics: Civil infrastructure | BIM Collaborate Pro | Civil 3D | Cloud Worksharing | Docs | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: IFC 4.3 enables open data exchange for infrastructure, yet many teams struggle to turn IFC exports into information that projects can rely on. This session will move beyond export steps and focus on using IFC effectively on infrastructure projects. You’ll learn how IFC 4.3 works once it leaves Civil 3D software, including how models are governed, versioned, reviewed, and trusted. Topics will include model view definitions, the IFC Reference View for civil infrastructure, and common mistakes that reduce value. The session will also introduce Autodesk Forma Data Management as a practical way to manage IFC delivery at scale, supporting controlled sharing and review. You’ll leave with guidance on positioning IFC as a trusted project resource.

title: When BIM and GIS Stay Connected: Esri and Autodesk’s Path to True Cloud Interoperability
speakers: Nora Nanov, Product Manager, Esri | Michael Davidson, Product Manager, Esri
topics: Geospatial and GIS | Civil infrastructure | Autodesk Platform Services | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Discover how Esri and Autodesk are advancing BIM and GIS interoperability through their strategic alliance. Today, teams rely on manual conversion, translation, and duplicate publishing to bring BIM into GIS context - creating friction, slowing decisions, and making it harder to trust the right information is available when needed. This session explores the art of the possible: a future where BIM and GIS data stay connected across Autodesk and Esri environments. Attendees will see how evolving interoperability efforts can reduce handoff friction, improve continuity, and make it easier to bring BIM into GIS and GIS into BIM. Join us to learn about the patterns enabling true cloud-to-cloud workflows!

title: Taming 3D Scans: STL Model Cleanup Using Meshmixer Then Moving to Autodesk Fusion for Reverse Engineering
speakers: Nicholas Kloski, Co-Founder, HoneyPoint3D, LLC
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | MeshMixer | D&M | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: 3D scanning is more accessible than ever, with consumer and prosumer scanners flooding the market. But the real challenge begins after the scan is complete. Raw STL files are often heavy, messy, and filled with artifacts—especially when capturing organic subjects like the human body. In this session, we’ll dive deep into Meshmixer software, the ultimate Swiss army knife for STL manipulation. We’ll cover essential scan triage, basic cleanup, and targeted reconstruction techniques to repair complex holes and smooth organic artifacts. Then we’ll transition into Autodesk Fusion software to enable reverse engineering workflows. We’ll explore techniques to accurately build and drive solid parametric models on top of your scanned data.

title: Autodesk Forma R&D Meetup
speakers: Cary Mandell, Principal Customer Advocate, Autodesk | Pete GilMurray, Sales Specialist, Enterprise Emerging Solutions, Autodesk | Kellie Herring, Customer Success Manager, ACS, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Build | Forma Data Management Essentials | Model Coordination | Quantity Takeoff | AECO | Meetup
abstract: Are you an administrator, manager, or user of Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud)? Join the Autodesk Forma R&D Meetup! You’ll dive into candid conversations, share real-world experiences, and explore forward-thinking ideas that are shaping the future of construction technology—whether that involves Forma Data Management, Forma Build, Forma Design Collaboration, the Cost Management tool, or others. This meetup is designed for attendees to share insights as well as discuss best practices and exchange strategies for all things Autodesk Forma. Don’t miss this opportunity to learn, grow, and connect with a supportive community of industry and design professionals.

title: Perfect Quality Control with Autodesk Forma Construction Connect: How Integrated Data Delivers a 45% Workload Reduction
speakers: hideaki takimoto, Senior Manager, TAKENAKA Corporation
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Autodesk Platform Services | Build | Forma | Revit | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: This session will present a practical case in which Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) connects project data across design, preconstruction, procurement, cost, and construction workflows. Traditionally, inspections required time-consuming drawing checks, record creation, document handling, and information sharing. In this initiative, models, drawings, inspection records, and progress data are centrally managed in Forma Build, enabling standardized inspections and real-time collaboration. Automated status updates and stakeholder communication through Autodesk Forma Construction Connect reduce document search time, support early issue detection, and cut overall workflow effort by 45%. Success depends not only on technology, but also on the right team structure to support common data environment (CDE) operations.

title: Preparing Construction Data for AI
speakers: Matt Fern, National Digital Engineering Manager, Stowe Australia
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Build | Docs | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Everyone wants AI in construction. Almost no one has data ready for it. Poor structure, inconsistent metadata, and fragmented workflows hold most teams back. This session will share real-world lessons from Stowe Australia, implementing Autodesk Forma as a common data environment (CDE) to fix that problem. Learn how ISO 19650 principles, standardized templates, and disciplined workflows turn messy project information into structured, usable data. The result? A scalable foundation for analytics, automation, and AI across projects, teams, and the wider business.
