speakers: Justin Lipsey, Senior Product Marketing Manager, Construction, Autodesk | Joan Allen, Dir., Product Management, Autodesk | Audrey Boguchwal, Senior Group Product Manager, Autodesk | Craig Godfrey, Senior Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk | Shani Sharif, Senior Group Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Desktop Connector | Docs | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO
abstract: Connected project data is the foundation of Autodesk Forma. Join this roadmap session to see how Autodesk is advancing Autodesk Forma Data Management as the common data environment (CDE) that connects teams, workflows, and phases across the architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) lifecycle. The product team will share the latest developments, what’s coming next, and the future direction of Forma Data Management.

title: PLM Summit | From Fragmented Workflows to a Digital Thread: Scaling Modular Construction with PLM at Faith
speakers: Darren Hartenstine, Senior Solutions Consultant, Symetri USA | Caleb Goins, Application Support Manager, FTI
topics: Building products and fabrication | Fusion Manage | Vault Professional | D&M | Industrialized Construction | PLM
abstract: Faith Technologies Incorporated (FTI) is rapidly scaling its modular construction and manufacturing operations. But disconnected systems, manual workflows, and poor data governance created barriers to growth. In partnership with Symetri, Faith is implementing a PLM-driven digital thread connecting Vault software, Autodesk Fusion Manage, Inventor software, and architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) systems. This transformation enables centralized data, automated design-to-fabrication workflows, and enterprise collaboration. This session will explore how Faith is moving from siloed processes to a connected, scalable ecosystem to accelerate productization and support rapid growth.

title: Building the Digital Thread: Connecting CRM, Vault PLM, MES, and ERP from Order to Delivery
speakers: Markus Gundersen, Business Manager, COOLORANGE NORTHERN EUROPE | Christian Gessner, Head of Research and Innovation, coolOrange S.r.l.
topics: Manufacturing Other | Autodesk Platform Services | Fusion Manage | Fusion Operations | Inventor | Vault Professional | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Manufacturing organizations often struggle with disconnected systems across sales, engineering, and production. This class will show how Vault PLM software forms the backbone of a connected digital thread spanning customer relationship management (CRM), CAD, product data management (PDM), product lifecycle management (PLM), manufacturing execution systems (MES), and enterprise resource planning (ERP). Starting from a CRM order, we’ll demonstrate rule-based CAD automation, engineering data management in Vault, and seamless Item and BOM synchronization into Autodesk Fusion Manage—driven by the built-in connector. Design reviews are handled through a web interface powered by the Vault Data API, manufacturing execution runs in Autodesk Fusion Operations, and business data flows into ERP—event-driven and AI-assisted. See how Vault PLM bridges engineering and enterprise to streamline the journey, from order to delivery.

title: Can AI Help Construction Understand the Jobsite in Real Time?
topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Chris Baze, Director of Construction Technology @ Hawaiian Dredging and Fikret Kalay, Director @ Autodesk Research join the Digital Builder podcast to discuss research exploring whether AI can create a continuously updated digital understanding of active construction sites. The conversation examines jobsite intelligence, digital twins, project readiness, risk detection, and how connected data could help project teams make better decisions before problems affect schedule and cost.

title: Sabesp Digital Transformation: Largest Water CAPEX in the Southern Hemisphere Powered by Autodesk Portfolio
speakers: Marcel Costa Sanches, Engineering Corporate Director, SABESP
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Utilities and telecom | Autodesk Platform Services | Docs | Info360 Asset | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Come to this session to hear how Sabesp powers a $15 billion+ CAPEX program, universalizing water and sewer systems for 28 million people across 375 municipalities with more than 1,100 work fronts. Over five years, custom Civil 3D/Revit/AutoCAD Plant 3D libraries and Autodesk Forma Data Management (engineering CDE) enable full intelligent modeling of water intake, transport, treatment, reservoirs, distribution, sewage collection, pumping stations, and effluent treatment plants (ETPs)—replacing 2D workflows. Forma Data Management and Autodesk Forma Build orchestrate CAPEX, from planning to commissioning. Autodesk Forma Design Collaboration streamlines model coordination. Water solutions—including InfoDrainage, InfoWorks WS Pro, and SCM6—handle hydraulic modeling and rehab planning. ArcGIS supports CAPEX spatialization and BIM publishing. Pioneering AI via Autodesk Platform Services automates Sabesp standards compliance checking.

title: PM Break
abstract: Recharge, refuel, and reconnect during our afternoon break. Enjoy light refreshments designed to give you an energy boost, spark fresh conversations, and help you return to the next session ready to dive back in.

title: Fall in Love with the Problem: Redefining Visual Storytelling
speakers: David Weir-McCall, Head of Product, Lumion
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Architecture services | Revit | AECO
abstract:
The way we visualise and tell stories has evolved from static 2D rendering, to real-time 3D, to AI. The underlying problem these technologies serve has never gone away; it has changed shape as the needs of the industry have evolved.

In this session you will hear from Lumion’s Head of Product and explore the new ways of addressing, validating and building architectural solutions that are guided by customer feedback and experience.

As a live case study you will experience Project Compass, a brand new Lumion product being shown to the public for the first time at AU, which addresses an intrinsically important stage of the visual communication pipeline in your architecture portfolio. You will follow the whole journey, from ideation, identifying the problem, exploring the solution space, and most importantly validating the outcome with the wider industry.

title: Go Slow to Go Fast: Dome Construction’s Real-World Roadmap to Autodesk Forma Build
speakers: John Mack, Construction Technology Consultant, Dome Construction | Jason Dodds, Principal Business Consultant, Construction, CDE & Data Strategy, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Construction services | Autodesk Platform Services | Build | Docs | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Dome Construction's transition to Forma Build wasn't planned; it was driven by clients. As owners across Life Sciences, Technology, and Foodtech began requiring Autodesk Build, the question quickly shifted from if to how fast. Leadership set a two-year mandate. This session shares Dome's real journey from pilot to rollout: uncovering platform gaps, navigating commercial strategy, and building a change approach grounded in "doing it right." Instead of rushing, Dome adopted a Lean mindset (go slow to go fast) waiting for field readiness before go-live. Through close collaboration with Autodesk, Dome is shaping a practical, experiential roadmap for contractors facing similar mandates, backed by real lessons and early results from live projects.

title: Inside Forma Building Design
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Architecture
abstract: What if building design could be more fluid, intelligent, and connected from the start? Get an inside look at Forma Building Design, Autodesk’s upcoming detailed design solution that brings intuitive modeling and integrated analytics together. Explore how teams can create purposeful designs with real-time performance insights and generative AI, work flexibly across parametric, manual, and AI-assisted tools, and bring BIM and non-BIM contributors together in one cloud workspace. Discover how integration with Revit helps teams transition smoothly to BIM, reducing rework while preserving design intent.

title: Stop Sharing Screens – Start Sharing Space: Practical XR for Model Coordination
speakers: Joseph Huang, Principal, Architect, BIM Design Team Lead, Stantec | Raghavendra Bhat, Principal, Sr. BIM Integration Specialist, Stantec
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Buildings | Forma Data Management Essentials | Navisworks Manage | Pype | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | XR | Cross Industry
abstract: Immersive technologies are often promoted as the future of model coordination, yet most teams remain stuck in screen sharing and pilot demos. This session challenges that pattern, presenting a practical playbook for using shared immersive space as a deliberate coordination tool rather than a novelty. Through real project scenarios, it shows when XR enables faster understanding and better decisions, when desktop review works better, and how to structure immersive meetings so technical and non-technical stakeholders collaborate effectively. Hardware, visualization, and platforms matter – but only when paired with clear intent, facilitation, and decision focused workflows.

title: Bridging the Knowledge Gap: An Open-Source RAG Approach to Reliable Revit Development
speakers: 兰辉 徐, Product Developmenter, TYDI
topics: Architecture services | Revit | Revit LT | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: What if anyone could automate Revit software—without writing a single line of code? This session introduces an open-source AI agent that turns natural language into executable Revit operations. Built on retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and Model Context Protocol (MCP), it retrieves knowledge from Revit API Docs, generates C# code, and executes it inside Revit in real time. Key highlights include the following: There are no hardcoded rules—the large language model (LLM) reasons from real API signatures. There are no preset commands—never-seen operations are reasoned and created on the fly. Successful operations solidify into reusable templates—non-developers replay them instantly. And there’s a live Revit connection via TCP JSON-RPC with Roslyn dynamic compilation. No C# experience or plug-in background is needed. And there’s no command library to maintain. Just describe what you want.

title: That's YOUR Opinion: Revit Workflow Point / Counter Point
speakers: Howard Munsell, Sr. Design Application Specialist II, Whitman Requardt & Assoc | Matthew Preston, Senior Design Application Specialist I, Whitman Requardt & Associates, LLP | John Selbe, Senior Design Application Specialist I, Whitman, Requardt & Associates, LLP
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | Architecture services | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Opinions can be wonderful things. Don’t rule anything out because you’ve never tried it before. From the best use of curtain walls to using AI and cloud services, everyone has their own opinions on how things should be done. Some work. Some work better. Some don’t work at all. Follow along as we discuss and flesh out workflows and some best practices. A lot of these are tools you use every day when designing and innovating. But are you using them correctly? Is there something else you could be doing, or is there a better way to do it? Join Matt Preston and Howard Munsell as they provide their unique perspectives on daily tools.

title: Unleashing Dynamo with Autodesk Assistant and MCP: From Intent to Inspectable Graphs
speakers: John (JT) Pierson, Product Manager, Autodesk | Achintya Bhat, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Civil 3D | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Dynamo is evolving from manual graph authoring to intent-driven co-creation. In this session, you’ll see how Autodesk Assistant can drive Dynamo through the Dynamo Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to create, modify, and run graphs using natural language—while keeping results deterministic, inspectable, and shareable. We’ll walk through real examples: generating a graph from a workflow description, refactoring an existing graph, and validating outputs. You’ll learn where MCP fits in the Dynamo stack, what makes tool-based AI safer than free-form code generation, and which patterns keep AI-assisted automation maintainable across teams.

title: Your Firm's Brain: AI-Powered Knowledge Repositories for Smarter Project Execution
speakers: Peter Pincic, Global Director - Software, AI, Enterprise, Neilsoft | Pravin raijade, CTO - Software, Neilsoft
topics: Project Financials | Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Architecture services | Autodesk Platform Services | Civil 3D | Forma | Forma Building Design | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) firms accumulate irreplaceable institutional knowledge—buried in drawings, RFIs, submittals, intelligent models, and lessons learned no one reads twice. Drawing on firsthand conversations with North American AEC firms, we’ll demonstrate how retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), multimodal AI, and lightweight agents—layered on Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) and Autodesk Platform Services—can mine project data to surface precedent details, validate firm standards, classify specifications, predict RFI risk, and accelerate new-hire onboarding. You’ll leave with a practical implementation road map, governance and data-readiness checkpoints, build-versus-buy decision criteria, and three pilot patterns proven on real Revit, Civil 3D, and Autodesk Forma workflows.

title: Agentic AI in Action: How Autodesk and AWS Build Intelligent Agents for Design and Make
speakers: Zaiba Jamadar, Senior Solutions Architect, AWS | Anuj Butail, Principal Solutions Architect, AWS | Taha Topiwalla, Principal Account Manager, AWS
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Architecture services | Autodesk Platform Services | Construction Cloud | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Autodesk and AWS are building agentic AI to design and construct at scale. Autodesk has deployed several AI agents—orchestrated through Autodesk Assistant, powered by Amazon Bedrock, and connected via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In this session, we’ll dive deeper into Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: an agentic platform for building, deploying, and operating highly effective agents securely at scale using any framework and foundation model. Learn real-world patterns that combine MCP, AgentCore, and generative AI services for construction and manufacturing. Whether you're starting your AI journey or scaling intelligent systems, you’ll walk away with actionable insights and tools to accelerate innovation.

title: Autodesk Black & Indigenous Network Meetup
speakers: Jason Harjo, Sr Account Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Meetup
abstract: This meetup is sponsored by Autodesk Employee Belonging Groups (EBGs) to support connection and shared growth across communities. We bring employees and customers together through interactive, networking-focused experiences. Participants will engage in small-group conversations designed to encourage meaningful dialogue, knowledge sharing, and relationship building across teams, roles, and communities.

title: Live XR Coordination: In-Person BIM Reviews with Workshop XR, ACC, and Web Participants
speakers: SEBASTIEN CLICHE, BIM Manager & Innovation, Technology Expert, Tetratech | Chris Fries, Design Technology Manager, Tetra Tech
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Engineering service providers | Build | Forma | ReCap | Revit | Workshop XR | AECO | XR | Cross Industry
abstract: Step beyond screen-based coordination and see how immersive design reviews can drive faster decisions in the room. In this in-person session, you’ll learn how Tetra Tech uses Autodesk Workshop XR, Autodesk Construction Cloud, and mixed headset/web participation to review BIM models at full scale, validate designs against existing conditions, and capture issues live. Through practical workflows and project examples, we’ll show how to connect Revit, Navisworks, and segmented mesh data into repeatable XR review sessions that improve stakeholder alignment, reduce late-stage surprises, and support more efficient project delivery.

title: Building an MCP Server for BIM: Connect Any AI to Live Autodesk Forma Models via AEC Data Model
speakers: Parthasarathi Mishra, Associate, WSP Global | Vijaya Adigopula, Technical Director, WSP
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Engineering service providers | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is transforming how AI assistants interact with engineering data. Instead of building separate apps, you expose your data as MCP tools—and any large language model (LLM) connects natively. In this session, we’ll show how WSP built a production MCP server using FastMCP and Python that exposes AEC Data Model GraphQL APIs as intelligent tools—enabling engineers to query live Autodesk Forma Revit models conversationally via the Claude Desktop app or GPT-4. Ask "What is the total embodied carbon for Level 3?" or "List all structural columns over 5m" and you’ll get live answers directly from Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), with no separate UI. This was built and demonstrated at the Autodesk APS Accelerator Bangalore 2026. Attendees will leave with a replicable MCP server blueprint for Autodesk Forma.

title: Which Revit Structural Model to Use for Analysis? Analytical or Physical or Both?
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E
topics: Engineering service providers | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: This class will explore whether structural analysis workflows in Revit software should rely on the analytical model, the physical model, or a hybrid of both. Traditionally, structural analysis platforms use only the analytical model to translate geometry and structural properties from Revit. Why limit workflows to just the analytical model? With analytical and physical models now able to act independently, users can choose which representation best fits their needs. This class will compare approaches and evaluate when each method—or a combined strategy—provides the most reliable and efficient structural analysis workflow. We’ll also explore customizing structural analysis tools to accept physical model geometry.

title: What's New in Revit 2027 for Structural Professionals: Hands-On Lab
speakers: Tomasz Fudala, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect – AECO, Autodesk
topics: Structural Engineering  | Buildings | Advance Steel | Dynamo | Revit | Robot Structural Analysis Professional | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: As structural projects move from analysis and design intent into detailing and fabrication readiness, teams often struggle with rework, inconsistent model behavior, and repetitive documentation tasks. In this 90-minute lab, you’ll create analytical models with improved automation, editing, loads, and boundary conditions. You’ll also apply new rebar modeling techniques and detailing workflows, work with detailed steel modeling, and automate element numbering with rule-based controls. Guided exercises will demonstrate how these capabilities improve analytical model accuracy and editability, strengthen reinforcement definition and documentation, reduce manual effort, and support more-reliable downstream delivery.

title: Eaton and Trane: 1-GW Data Center Codesign with BIM and Autodesk Forma
speakers: Victor Mirasola, General Manager - TRACE, Trane Technologies | Justin Carron, Director of Segment Marketing, Eaton | Matt Lemay, Principal Account Executive, Enterprise, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Buildings | Docs | Forma | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: This class will showcase how Trane, Eaton, and Autodesk enable collaborative codesign for gigawatt-scale data centers using BIM and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). You will see how data center reference kits become live, cloud-based environments for real-time collaboration between owners, engineers, and contractors. These environments centralize BIM and engineering data into a shared source of truth, enabling coordinated design of mechanical and electrical systems at massive scale. The session will demonstrate how Autodesk Forma Build supports structured codesign workflows, role-based collaboration, and asset-centered data models. This approach enables faster iteration, reduced risk, and scalable delivery for data centers of 1 gigawatt capacity.

title: Full Project Delivery with Autodesk Forma Build: From CDE to QA/QC, EDMS, and Handover
speakers: Juan Camilo VALDES, Digital Engineering & Quality Lead, HEB (Vinci) | William L. Guauque Castaneda, Digital Delivery Manager, HEB Construction - VINCI NZ
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | Build | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Project delivery is often fragmented across systems, with disconnected data between common data environments (CDEs), QA/QC, electronic document management systems (EDMSs), and handover processes creating inefficiencies and delays. This session will explore how Autodesk Forma Build enables full project delivery through a connected data platform, integrating workflows across RFIs, Submittals, NCRs, snags, scheduling, and QA/QC closeout. You’ll learn how to structure and manage data from design through construction to achieve progressive closeout and successful handover. Real-world examples will demonstrate how connected workflows improve data quality, reduce rework, and enable earlier, more reliable project completion.

title: Civil 3D and Dynamo with ReCap 2026: Automating Tunnel Section Extraction and Comparison for Rehab
speakers: David Pastor, Sr Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk | Goyo Grzeskow, Sr Enterprise Account Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Reality Capture | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Dynamo | ReCap | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Tunnel rehabilitation projects lack a single, bulletproof workflow for comparing complex point cloud data with design corridors. Instead of chasing a one-size-fits-all solution, successful projects require selecting the right toolset for the specific job. This session explores the current state of the art in working with tunnel point cloud meshes using ReCap, Civil 3D, and Dynamo. Rather than presenting a single rigid path, we will dissect multiple methodologies, analyzing the practical pros and cons of each. You’ll leave with a clear understanding of what is realistically possible right now, how to automate section creation, and how to select the optimal workflow to balance accuracy against automation scale.

title: Get Workforce Ready with Autodesk Certifications!
speakers: Dania Eter, Principal Autodesk Certification Program, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | BIM 360 Build | Forma | Fusion | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Certification is more than a badge—it’s a signal of capability and a demonstration of skills applied in real industry workflows. Employers are looking for people who can step into projects and make an impact. As tools and workflows continue to evolve especially with the growing influence of AI- demonstrating applied capability is becoming even more important. That’s why certification is shifting from a one-time milestone to something more continuous part of how professionals build, demonstrate, and validate their skills over time. We will explore how to navigate Autodesk certifications from foundational to professional levels, align them to career goals, and use preparation to build skills that translate into effectiveness on the job.

title: Cracking the Code: Automating Block Editor Workflows with DocumentManager CommandAsync
speakers: Scott Mizsak, CAD Coordinator, Bolton & Menk
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Thirty-seven offices and seven unique borders. Discover how to eliminate hours of repetitive tasks by using AutoCAD software’s DocumentManager and asynchronous command execution to automate Block Editor operations. This session will demonstrate techniques for automatically managing the dynamic blocks with visibility states in these drawings using the Block Editor API. Learn how to combine Editor.CommandAsync, transaction management, and proper document locking to update these seven drawings based on a single database. This session will cover how to get the final solution, and attendees will walk away with the practical code patterns, debugging strategies, and approaches that transformed hours of manual updates into a process that takes just seconds.

title: Subassembly Composer and Corridor Transitions for Repeatable Complex Road Design
speakers: Ben Wardell, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Russ Nicloy, Civil Solutions Specialist, MACER Technologies, Inc.
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: In more-complicated designs, users can see efficiency gains from using customized subassemblies that do the work of multiple assembly regions. In this lab, users will experience using Subassembly Composer to create a subassembly that uses a Decision function to facilitate multiple end conditions along a design with a single assembly or region. Then, using that custom subassembly in Civil 3D software, we’ll use the Corridor Transition tools to adjust the design with a high level of control.

title: Unlocking the CADD Manager’s Bag: What's Inside? Keys to Navigate Disruption and Speed Transformation.
speakers: Joseph Gaffney, Director of Design Technology Services, Colliers Engineering & Design
topics: Civil infrastructure | None | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Today’s CADD manager isn’t carrying the same old bag. Step inside the modern toolkit where digital strategy, change leadership, and transformation know-how sit right alongside technical expertise. This fast‑paced, story‑driven session will reveal how CADD managers across industries are shedding the “CAD cop” stereotype and emerging as influential technology leaders who shape business outcomes. You’ll hear examples of teams that moved from reactive chaos to confident, future‑focused momentum by redefining the role and embracing disruption. If you’re ready to elevate your impact and lead your organization through digital change with clarity and confidence, this session will show you exactly what’s possible—and what belongs in your upgraded bag.

title: From Borehole to Building: Advanced Ground Modeling Directly in Civil 3D with GeoDin Ground
speakers: Devrez Karabacak, Head of Product, GeoDin, Fugro
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Ground models are the missing link between site investigation and infrastructure design. Engineers make critical decisions on alignments, crossings, and foundations while the subsurface remains a black box—data arriving late, locked in static reports, or in formats incompatible with the design environment. GeoDin Ground for Civil 3D software is changing that. In this session, we’ll present the latest advances in 3D ground modeling inside Civil 3D, including direct AGS file ingestion and autoconversion—eliminating the need for a preexisting database and letting teams start directly with received data. You’ll see the ground take shape inside Civil 3D, evolving into a 3D model that drives critical design choices and reduces project risk from day one.

title: Beyond Automation: AI Collaboration with Autodesk Assistant
speakers: Alex Lobos, Director, School of Design, Rochester Institute of Technology
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | D&M | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: This session will demonstrate how the recently introduced Autodesk Fusion AI Assistant enhances product development. AI Assistant accelerates early-stage design exploration, development, and fabrication by translating text into CAD, automating workflows, and accelerating implementation. Case studies of consumer products will illustrate how AI Assistant improves efficiency, when traditional methods are more effective, and how to best combine both. The session will cover prompt engineering techniques that improve output quality. By adopting these workflows, teams can reduce repetitive tasks, improve iteration speed, and focus human expertise on higher-value design decisions, ultimately achieving faster, more informed results.

title: Connected Buildings at Scale: From Construction to Operations
speakers: Adam Allard, Senior Manager, Technical Environments, Autodesk | Fikret Kalay, Director, Research Science, Autodesk | Amr Raafat, Chief Innovation Officer (CIO), Windover Construction
topics: Construction services | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Navisworks Manage | Revit | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Preconstruction
abstract: Construction and building operations remain disconnected across projects, limiting efficiency and long-term performance. This session will bring together leaders from Windover Construction, KONE, and STRABAG, along with Autodesk Research, to show how connected workflows improve delivery and operations. KONE systems move 2 billion people daily, demonstrating the impact of connected building systems at scale. Windover and STRABAG workflows, combined with prefab and vertical logistics, can reduce schedules by up to 30% during construction. In operations, linking real-time occupancy data and digital twins has achieved up to 36% in energy savings. You’ll gain strategies to connect BIM, construction, and operations into a continuous lifecycle.

title: Why Rhumbix Is Critical to Autodesk Forma
speakers: Zach Scheel, Director, Construction Strategy, Autodesk | Sidharth Haksar, VP,  Construction Strategy and Industry Partnerships, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Autodesk Forma industry cloud connects design, preconstruction, and field coordination within a single platform. But one critical layer has been missing: real-time workforce data from the field. Labor is the largest cost on most construction projects—and the least measured. That’s why Autodesk acquired Rhumbix. In this session, we’ll explain the strategic vision behind the acquisition and why Rhumbix is essential to the future of Autodesk Forma. You’ll learn what field and resource management data Rhumbix captures and how it will flow into the Forma platform to support cost, schedule, estimating, and planning workflows, enabling a more complete field-to-finance operation for construction.

title: AEC Roadmap: Autodesk Forma Build
speakers: Emilio Mercado, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Sagi Zeberger, Group Product Manager, Autodesk | David Kadyshewich, Group Product Manager, Autodesk | Courtney Wright, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Adam Arcus, Senior Product Marketing Manager, Construction, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | Build | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: From punch lists to submittals and RFIs, your tools must be jobsite-ready and drive project progress. Strong field execution and project management rely on connected, efficient workflows. Join the Autodesk Forma Project Management and Field Delivery teams for a deep dive into what’s new and what’s next for project management and field across Forma Build Essentials, Forma Build, and the Forma Mobile app. See how we’re designing core field and project management tools that help teams plan, execute, and close work on-site, in the trailer, and in the office. Learn how data flows between field and project workflows to improve visibility, accountability, and decisions. And see how your feedback is shaping the roadmap, including Autodesk AI.

title: Building at the Speed of Demand: A Data Center Meetup
speakers: Julia Cook, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk | Jayanth Iyengar, Sr Principal, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk | Sarah O' Sullivan, Senior Customer Success Manager, Construction, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma | Model Coordination | Quantity Takeoff | AECO | Industrialized Construction
abstract: Data center demand is accelerating at an unprecedented pace—bringing tight schedules, complex MEP coordination, constant change, and high-stakes commissioning. This meetup aims to be a curated networking space for owners, developers, designers, and builders to connect with peers and share practical thoughts on “what’s working” in the field. Join the conversation to exchange real-world strategies across delivery, standardization, prefabrication, design coordination, commissioning readiness, and transformation of project data into operational value. Whether you're scaling programs or managing aggressive timelines, you’ll leave with new connections, fresh ideas, and a clearer view of how others are accelerating delivery while managing risk.

title: The Good, the Bad, and the Wildcard: Big Lessons from Autodesk Forma Cost Management Implementation
speakers: Ariel Castillo, Subject Matter Expert, Preconstruction, Autodesk | Richard Antczak, Senior Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | Brad Buckles, VP, Technology and Innovation, Charles Perry Partners, Inc. | Tim Kelleher, Ops. Standards and Innovation Manager, Brinkman Construction Inc.
topics: Project Financials | Construction Operations | Construction services | Build | Docs | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Cost management implementations don’t fail on software—they fail on assumptions. This session will break down the good, the bad, and the wildcard moments from real-world deployments, highlighting what actually drives success (and what quietly derails it). From aligning workflows between field, PMs, and accounting to managing data structure, contracts, and change processes, we’ll share practical lessons learned from implementing cost management in live projects. You’ll walk away with clear strategies to improve adoption, avoid common pitfalls, and confidently lead your own implementation.

title: People and AI: Building Your Workforce Planning Strategy in the Agent Era
speakers: David Pimiskern, VP, Strategy & Operations, Bridgit
topics: Construction Operations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | None | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Construction companies are navigating more workforce challenges than ever—and those staying ahead are doing it with a powerful combination of technology, data, and AI. But the game’s changing. A new era of AI agents is shifting workforce planning from reactive to strategic—giving contractors instant command of their people data, smarter staffing decisions, and a clearer view of what's on the horizon. Join David Pimiskern, Bridgit’s VP of strategy and operations, for an in-depth look at how North America's leading contractors are building their workforce planning strategies for the agent era—and what it means to put AI to work without losing the human expertise at the center of it all. You’ll leave with a fresh perspective on where construction workforce planning is headed, and what forward-thinking leaders are doing today to stay ahead of the curve.

title: First to the Chow Bowl: How Claiming Your Spot and Data Early Pays Off Throughout Coordination
speakers: Aaron Szymanski, Chief Product Officer, Augmenta
topics: MEP Engineering  | Construction services | Revit | AECO
abstract: Electrical VDC teams routinely enter coordination late, racing to populate models while other trades claim space first. This talk shows how Owen Electric used AI-powered conduit routing to shift that dynamic across three complex jobs in three months. Instead of manually entering electrical data, the team embedded that information from the start and then explored routing options allowing for faster decisions and optimal layout. The result: modeling time cut in half, tens of thousands of feet of conduit populated, in days rather than weeks, returning time back to specs, submittals, and constructability reviews. Attendees leave with a framework to walk into the first coordination meeting fully populated as well as practical tactics to build infill data early so a lean team can take on bigger, more complex scope and meaningfully grow capacity.

title: From Classroom to Jobsite: Building Design-to-Make Curriculum with Autodesk
speakers: Kate McElligott, Workforce Innovation & Investment Lead, Autodesk | Jovan Madjovski, Vice President, CEED Global SME Green Advancement Initiative | Regan Brewer, President, Jane Addams Resource Corporation | Agata Zytniak, Senior Automation Engineer and Information Manager, Bechtel
topics: Trust | Education | Forma | Fusion | EDU | Impact & Sustainability | Cross Industry
abstract: How do you turn Design-to-Make workflows into job-ready curriculum? This panel brings together JARC, SEAF, Bechtel, and Autodesk to show how Fusion, Revit, and Autodesk Forma power scalable workforce training. Through real-world examples, see how learners move from concept modeling to fabrication and site execution using the same tools and data as in industry. Panelists will share how curriculum is structured, how employer input shapes projects, and how digital workflows enable delivery. Attendees will gain practical models to align training with production workflows and improve job readiness.

speakers: Jovan Madjovski, Vice President, CEED Global SME Green Advancement Initiative | Regan Brewer, President, Jane Addams Resource Corporation | Kate McElligott, Workforce Innovation & Investment Lead, Autodesk | Agata Zytniak, Senior Automation Engineer and Information Manager, Bechtel

title: Collaborate Better with AutoCAD and Autodesk Forma Data Management: Share, Trace, Multi-User Markups, Checkout
speakers: Helen Chen, Principal QA Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Building products and fabrication | AutoCAD | AutoCAD LT | AutoCAD Mechanical | AutoCAD Plant 3D | AutoCAD web app | D&M | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: See how AutoCAD software and Forma Data Management (formerly Autodesk Docs) work together so your team can collaborate without confusion. This hands-on session will walk you through Share—sending view or edit links so others can open drawings in the browser or in AutoCAD on the web—and Trace—adding markups on a syncing overlay and bringing them into the main drawing. You’ll try multi-user markups so several people can add feedback to the same design from web and desktop, and see how to use checkout to reserve entities for edit, submit for review, then merge approved checkout back into the drawing. Whether you work in AutoCAD desktop, on the web, or with Forma Data Management, you’ll leave with a clear workflow to share, review, and manage drawings as a team.

title: Reliable Techniques for Complex Drawings and Detailing in Inventor
speakers: Paul Munford, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect - D&M, Autodesk
topics: Industrial machinery | Inventor | Inventor Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: You update your Inventor model and suddenly your drawing is a complete mess! Your views, sections, and details have moved all over the sheet, and your dimensions are pink with confusion! (This always seems to happen at 4 PM on a Friday.) In this class, you’ll learn how updating a drawing can be as predictable and efficient as any other part of your design process. The class is a continuation of the AU classes “Reliable Modeling Techniques for Complex Part Design in Inventor” and “Reliable Techniques for Complex Assembly Design in Inventor.”

title: From Plant Design to Product Passport: Extending PLM and Autodesk Fusion Manage Across the Full Lifecycle
speakers: Zoé Bezpalko, Sr. Manager, Sustainability Innovations, Autodesk | Andreas Nicolescu, Principal Account Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Industrial machinery | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Docs | Fusion Manage | D&M | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: By 2027, every manufacturer selling into the European market will be required to provide a Digital Product Passport (DPP)—and most are not ready. This session will show how Autodesk Fusion Manage software can close that gap, while also solving a longer-standing problem: disconnected data between process plant design and PLM. You'll see how equipment data from AutoCAD Plant 3D projects on Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) can automatically populate Fusion Manage BOMs—eliminating manual handoffs between plant design and PLM. And you’ll see how that same structure can generate EU-compliant DPPs on demand, without duplicate data entry—connecting project context from Autodesk Forma with product lifecycle data where it belongs. Both extensions are built on Autodesk Platform Services APIs and demonstrated live.

title: The New Backbone of Pfizer's Data Infrastructure
speakers: Justin Dewell, Engineering Systems Senior Associate, Pfizer | STEPHANIE CATALINA, Principal Professional Services Consultant, Autodesk | Brian Schanen, Principal Business Consultant, PLM/PDM, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Life sciences manufacturing | AutoCAD | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Vault Professional | D&M | Software Development
abstract: The new backbone of Pfizer’s data management brings transformation in how engineering data is managed. By a strategic data migration into Autodesk Vault and Forma, legacy information has been consolidated into a more structured, reliable system. Previously fragmented datasets are organized, enabling cleaner access, better traceability, and improved governance. This modernization enhances project communication and collaboration across teams, ensuring stakeholders are aligned throughout the engineering project lifecycle. With streamlined file handover processes and centralized control, project management becomes more efficient. Vault and Forma establish a robust foundation that supports scalability and consistency across Pfizer’s operations.

title: Accelerating Manufacturing Design: Unlocking the Top 10 Hidden Productivity Tools in AutoCAD Mechanical
speakers: Sridhar Subramani, Sr. Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Mechanical | D&M | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Most manufacturing teams use AutoCAD daily but overlook the AutoCAD Mechanical toolset included in their subscription. This session will showcase 10 productivity features that cut repetitive drafting: intelligent commands with associative centerlines, automated hidden-line management, parametric content libraries, power dimensioning with tolerances, detail view automation, GD&T and welding symbols, integrated BOM with balloons, enterprise standards enforcement, built-in engineering calculators, and associative 2D documentation of Inventor 3D models. Through live demos and real-world scenarios, you’ll gain hands-on techniques to reduce cycle times, enforce ISO/ANSI compliance automatically, and bridge 2D-3D workflows using tools you already own.

title: PLM Summit | Driving Business Impact with PLM: A Customer Panel Discussion
speakers: Josh Smith, Engineering Manager, UMD AUTOMATED SYSTEMS | Thomas Ward, Engineering Manager, Made By Gather | Andrew Pitman, Application & Data Lead, Spirax Group | Dimitri Van Nuland, Project Manager Digitization, Reynaers Aluminium | Mike Vesperman, Director, Expansion & Strategic Accounts, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Manufacturing Other | Fusion | Fusion Manage | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | PLM
abstract: Hear directly from leading organizations across industries as they share how PLM is helping them transform the way they work. In this dynamic panel, customers will discuss how they connect data, streamline processes, and improve collaboration to tackle real business challenges. From accelerating time to market to improving product quality and reducing costs, you’ll gain practical insights into what’s working, what they’ve learned, and how they’re achieving measurable results. Whether you're early in your connected data and processes journey or you’re looking to scale, this session will offer actionable takeaways. This session is part of the PLM Summit—a curated learning and networking experience. To explore related sessions, select “PLM Summit” track.

title: Innovators Stage | AECO Design Slam: Designing the Future of Event Cities
speakers: Jake Storey, Manager, Field Events, AMER, Autodesk | Ali Nasiri, Director of Computational Design, Flad Architects | Thesla Collier, Design Technology Manager, HNTB | Matt Menendez, Design Project Manager, LDA partners | Philip Ra, Design Principal, Flad Architects
abstract: Can great urban design turn a global event into a permanent destination? Watch two teams compete live as they reimagine the corridor between Allegiant Stadium and the Las Vegas Strip into a climate-smart, hospitality-driven district designed for the FIFA World Cup™ and beyond. Using Autodesk Forma, Forma Building Design, sustainability analysis, and AI visualization, competitors will create bold concepts that improve mobility, enhance the fan experience, and deliver lasting value for residents and visitors. You'll see every decision happen live—and cast the vote that crowns the Design Slam champion.

title: When the Airport Disappears: Building a Smarter ATL with Autodesk Tandem
topics: Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract: How do you keep the world’s busiest airport running so smoothly that passengers never notice the infrastructure behind it? Chris Harmon of WSP shares how Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is bringing 100 years of data together with Autodesk Tandem to better understand assets, anticipate issues, and connect operations back to planning and design, all while keeping the passenger experience at the center.

title: From More Data to Better Data: Rethinking Information in AEC
topics: Buildings | AECO | Future Industry Innovations
abstract: Join Eddy Krygiel from AEC Data Strategy on this episode of the Digital Builder podcast to explore why more data doesn’t automatically mean better data. Learn how AEC firms and owners are tackling the challenge of managing information quality at scale, the growing role of data specialists and more intentional approaches to keeping information accurate and aligned, and why trusted data is becoming essential as AI and automation create new opportunities across AEC.

title: Breakfast
abstract: Grab coffee and a bite to eat to fuel your second day at AU.

title: Whodunit? Building a System That Remembers Every Hand in the Work.
speakers: Renee Dua, student, srishti manipal institute of art deign and technology
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Inclusive Innovation, Culture, & Belonging | Cross Industry
abstract: Creative work is always collaborative. But the record rarely reflects that. Fabricators, assistants, mentors, and technicians disappear from the story—while credit consolidates around whoever has the loudest voice. This session will introduce ETCH, a trust-based documentation platform built on a custom blockchain, designed to make invisible labor visible. We'll walk through the design problems that shaped the system and discuss how to document a messy, nonlinear process. How do you attribute equitably across skill types? How do you build trust without financial incentives? The answer is a working system built by a design student who got frustrated enough to build the thing they needed.

title: One Shader to Rule Them All: Universal Lookdev with MaterialX and LookdevX in Maya
speakers: Kaan Zorlu, Lead 3D Artist, Leo Production
topics: Film and TV | 3ds Max 2 | Arnold | Maya | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract: The era of "siloed" shading is over. As pipelines move toward OpenPBR and MaterialX, artists must learn to build materials that are platform-agnostic. This session will explore the power of LookdevX in Maya 2026 software for creating high-fidelity, universal shaders. We’ll break down how to move away from legacy shading networks toward a unified MaterialX workflow that ensures visual consistency across various renderers and applications. Explore the technical logic of LookdevX, learn how to use the new OpenPBR standard for both realism and stylization, and discover the secrets to "packaging" your lookdev so it survives the transition from Maya to the rest of your pipeline. Build once, render everywhere.

title: Operational Intelligence with Autodesk Tandem: Driving Maintenance ROI from Digital Twins
speakers: Saverio Camillo Saviello, Sr Solution Architect, Autodesk
topics: Industrial machinery | Docs | Tandem Connect | D&M | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: Digital twins offer operational insight, yet their value is often unrealized when data remains disconnected from daily operational workflows. Asset models exist, but maintenance decisions, cost analysis, and ticket creation still happen in separate systems, limiting adoption and measurable ROI. This session will explore how integrating Autodesk Tandem with maintenance operations transforms digital twins into practical decision-making tools. We’ll show how you can calculate maintenance ROI by correlating maintenance costs, downtime, and potential fault costs using AI, and how these insights accelerate maintenance ticket creation and support predictive, data-driven strategies.

title: Separating Hardware Reality from Hype
speakers: Jamie Gwilliam, WW User & Industries Lead, Workstations, Intel
topics: XR & Immersive Tech
abstract: Join Lenovo with Intel’s global workstation user and segment lead for an inside look at the technologies transforming professional workstations. Discover how hardware is evolving, what’s driving other companies’ hardware decisions, and which key challenges today’s users face. We’ll also explore the three engines powering today’s System-on-a-Chip (SoC)—the CPU, GPU, and NPU—and how they work together to accelerate modern workflows, including AI. You’ll also learn how Intel develops and optimizes its graphics drivers, and how these innovations support Autodesk applications. Whether you're planning your next workstation upgrade or trying to separate AI hype from reality, this session will help you understand how workstation technology is changing and what it means for your Autodesk workloads.

title: Lunch & Learn: Unleash Peak Performance: Optimizing Dell Pro Max Workstations for Autodesk and Local AI
speakers: Rob Jamieson, Senior ISV Manager-ADM, AMD
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Architecture services | Arnold | Fusion | Revit | AECO
abstract: • Discover how the new Dell Pro Max 14 and 16 mobile workstations—powered by AMD Ryzen™ processors for workstations —deliver desktop-class performance for demanding Autodesk workflows. In this session, we'll show you how to tune your laptop for maximum output, fine-tune Autodesk application settings for optimal responsiveness, and harness the power of agentic workflows and local AI to accelerate your everyday design and engineering tasks. Whether you're modelling in Revit, rendering in Arnold, or iterating in Fusion, learn practical tips to work faster, smarter, and untethered from the cloud.

title: From Sketch to BIM: Forma Building Design and Revit
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Discover how Forma Building Design and Revit 2027 connect in a sketch-to-BIM workflow that keeps design intent intact. See how teams can move from conceptual massing into early schematic design, explore options with environmental analysis and unit metrics and layouts, and continue development in Revit with site context and connected Forma scenarios. We’ll also show how Revit users can run environmental analysis, such as wind, directly in Revit—giving teams the flexibility to start in Forma or Revit, depending on their workflow.

title: Your AI Is Only as Smart as Your Project Data
speakers: Philip Townsend, Principal Solutions Architect, Egnyte Inc. | Aaron Vorwerk, AEC Practice Leader, Architects + Owners, Egnyte
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | AutoCAD | BIM Collaborate | Forma | Revit | AECO
abstract: Every firm is piloting AI. Most pilots stall for the same reason, and it isn't the model. It's the data. Decades of drawings, RFIs, specs, and contracts sit scattered across servers, inboxes, and forgotten project folders. The firms winning with AI in 2026 treat project history as an asset. They make it findable, permissioned, and trusted before pointing AI at it. This talk  shows how to fix the data layer first: what to organize, how to govern access, and how to build the foundation that makes AI accurate and safe. You'll leave with fresh insights on how to turn scattered project data into firm knowledge your teams, and your AI, can actually use.

title: AI-Enabled Design for Excellence: Advancing Industrialized Construction from Design to Fabrication
speakers: Karla Saldana, Assistant Professor, University of Florida
topics: Architecture services | 3ds Max 2 | Forma | Revit | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Architecture
abstract: This session introduces a next-generation design for excellence (DfX) framework for industrialized construction, which combines design for manufacturing, assembly, disassembly, and sustainability into an AI-enabled decision-making system. This framework seeks to shift construction from a project-based approach to a performance-driven, product-based approach, focusing on constructability and lifecycle optimization early in the design phase. Demonstrated through a pilot building in six stages—loading, learning, programming, assembly, experimentation, and exhibition—it incorporates computational design, large-scale 3D concrete printing, robotic assembly, and prefabrication, and serves as a living laboratory for advancing industrialized construction systems.

title: From Existing to Extraordinary: Reinventing Renovations with Autodesk Forma Site Design, Revit, and Dynamo
speakers: Isabella Nascimento, Technical Specialist, PARS
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Forma | Forma Site Design | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Renovation projects are often slowed by fragmented data and limited early-stage insight, leading to rework and inefficient decisions. This session will demonstrate how Autodesk Forma Site Design and Dynamo automate data-driven workflows and enable early-stage analysis within Revit software. By connecting design to execution, teams reduced manual effort, accelerated scenario evaluation, and improved coordination across multiple buildings. You’ll learn how to structure connected workflows that support scalable, data-driven renovation strategies and deliver measurable improvements in speed, consistency, and sustainability.

title: Revit in the Age of Agents: A Clear-Eyed Guide for the Perplexed
speakers: Adi Shavit, CTO, SWAPP.AI
topics: Architecture services | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Dynamo scripts, Autodesk Assistant, Model Context Protocol (MCP) plug-ins, and embedded agents are four fundamentally different approaches to AI in Revit—all promising productivity, none interchangeable. This session is for BIM managers who don’t have a structured answer to the question, “Which one should we use?” We’ll walk through a practical evaluation framework: three questions that separate what each approach can and cannot do, demonstrated live inside Revit. You’ll leave with a comparison matrix you can use in your next vendor meeting, your next build-versus-buy discussion, or the next time someone on LinkedIn tells you the future is here.

title: Revit Community Meetup: Connect, Share, and Unwind
speakers: Kimberly Fuhrman-Jones, Community Manager, Autodesk | Scott D Davis, Sr Territory Technical Lead, Autodesk | Cesar Escalante, Sr. Technical Marketing Manager, Building Products, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | Revit LT | AECO | Meetup
abstract: Join fellow Revit users for a casual, community-focused meetup during AU. This informal gathering offers a space to connect, share experiences, and engage in real conversations—no presentations or formal agenda. Step away from the busy schedule to swap stories, compare workflows, and meet others who understand the daily realities of working in Revit. Whether you're looking to expand your network or just recharge with like-minded peers, this session is for you. Autodesk team members will be there to listen, but the focus is on the community—you. Drop in anytime and stay as long as you’d like.

title: From Intelligent Model to Environmental Outcomes: AI-Powered Tools for RE2020 Compliance
speakers: Alexandre PARENA, BIM MANAGER / COORDINATOR, CHABANNE
topics: Architecture services | Forma | Revit | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: How do you turn an intelligent model into a lever for real environmental performance? At the Chabanne office, we developed a suite of custom Revit plug-ins directly connected to live environmental databases (INIES/RE2020). This enabled our teams to query material carbon data, track biosourced ratios, and monitor energy indicators directly inside the model in real time. This outcome-based BIM helped us across different projects—especially Thoiry's Kindergarten—to reach Passivhaus-level energy needs, exceed the RE2020 2028 carbon threshold, and achieve 1.5 times the Level 3 biosourced label. Through Autodesk Platform Services, plug-ins, Autodesk Forma, Forma Site Design, Forma Building Design, Model Context Protocol (MCP), API, and AI, the intelligent model turned into a decision-making engine for our whole team.

title: Autodesk Community User Group Meetup
speakers: Eric DeLeon, Founder & Principal Consultant, DeLeon Consulting & Coaching | Sam Karas, Program Manager - Community, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Meetup
abstract: The Autodesk Community User Group Meetup is your chance to connect with group leaders and members, learn how to start your own group, and understand the value these communities offer. Hear about best practices for running successful user groups, and make connections that will enhance your experience at AU and beyond. Join us to share knowledge, grow your network, and become part of a thriving community.

title: Autodesk Fusion Roadmap
speakers: Daniel Graham, VP, Manufacturing, Autodesk | Srinath Jonnalagadda, VP, Data Management, Autodesk | Jon den Hartog, VP, Design, Autodesk
topics: Trust | Data and Document Management | Design & Engineering | D&M
abstract: Explore the future of product development with Autodesk Fusion. This roadmap session will provide insight into where Fusion is headed across design, manufacturing, data, and AI-driven workflows. You’ll get an early look at upcoming innovations, strategic priorities, and how Autodesk is evolving Fusion to help teams work in a more connected, intelligent, and efficient way across the entire product development process. This session is ideal for anyone interested in understanding the future of Autodesk Fusion.

title: Autodesk Fusion Roadmap
speakers: Daniel Graham, VP, Manufacturing, Autodesk | Srinath Jonnalagadda, VP, Data Management, Autodesk | Jon den Hartog, VP, Design, Autodesk
topics: Design & Engineering
abstract: Explore the future of product development with Autodesk Fusion. This roadmap session will provide insight into where Fusion is headed across design, manufacturing, data, and AI-driven workflows. You’ll get an early look at upcoming innovations, strategic priorities, and how Autodesk is evolving Fusion to help teams work in a more connected, intelligent, and efficient way across the entire product development process. This session is ideal for anyone interested in understanding the future of Autodesk Fusion.

title: Boosting Autodesk Development Using AI with AutoLISP and C# .NET
speakers: James Johnson, Application Developer, Synergis Software
topics: Engineering service providers | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Architecture | AutoCAD Electrical | AutoCAD Mechanical | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Learn how to use AI as a practical coding assistant to accelerate AutoCAD development. This 30-minute strategy session will show how AI can generate AutoLISP routines and C# .NET code, assist with debugging, and support code translation—enabling faster iteration and higher-quality results. Attendees will gain strategies to evaluate AI-generated code, integrate it into existing projects, and apply AI-assisted workflows effectively across both legacy and modern Autodesk development.

title: AI Changes the Cost Curve. But Connected Data Changes Value Creation.
speakers: Knut Ramstad, CTO and Partner, Registered Architect, Nordic Office of Architecture | Marius Jablonskis, Digital Transformation Leader, Norconsult ASA
topics: Engineering service providers | None | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: AI is often discussed in terms of efficiency, but the bigger shift may be how connected data improves the quality, consistency, and usefulness of expert delivery. This session will share Norconsult’s perspective on how AI and connected data are beginning to influence decision support, delivery workflows, and client value across architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO). We’ll explore why the impact goes beyond isolated productivity gains, where connected data makes AI more relevant in practice, and what leaders should consider as technology starts to affect how value is created in engineering and project delivery. The session will focus on practical implications and lessons emerging from real industry needs.

title: End-to-End Drainage Design with Autodesk Forma, InfoDrainage, and Civil 3D
speakers: Javier Soto, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk | Daniel'le DeVoss, Drainage Technical Account Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Water Infrastructure | Engineering service providers | Civil 3D | Forma | InfoDrainage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract:
InfoDrainage and Autodesk Forma will soon work together as part of a connected workflow for site drainage design. In this session, you'll work with Civil 3D and InfoDrainage models hosted in Forma, using live references such as surfaces and CAD background data to keep design information connected across applications. 

 Starting from a site design, you'll develop and optimize a drainage network in InfoDrainage, leveraging connected site data to accelerate hydrologic design. 

 The workflow continues with dynamic hydraulic simulation, exceedance assessment, and review of results, followed by compliance-ready reporting. The session concludes by synchronizing the completed drainage design back to Civil 3D, demonstrating a streamlined, connected workflow from site model to validated drainage design.

title: From Promises to Performance: Hands-On Workplan Commitments and Metrics in Autodesk Forma Build
speakers: Ovais Mattoo, Principal Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk | Dhruvesh Shah, Principal Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | BIM 360 Build | BIM 360 Plan | Build | Desktop Connector | Docs | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Construction teams often struggle to translate high-level schedules into reliable short-term execution. While master schedules define what should happen, they rarely capture what actually gets done on-site. In this hands-on lab, you will explore how to use Workplan Commitments and Metrics in Autodesk Forma Build to improve planning reliability, accountability, and performance tracking. Through guided exercises, you will do the following: create and manage short-term work plans, assign ownership and commit to tasks, track execution using Percent Plan Complete (PPC), analyze root causes for delays, and improve planning outcomes. By the end of the session, you will understand how to move from reactive scheduling to data-driven planning.

title: Industrialized Construction, Prefabrication, Modular, and Informed Design: Meet Your Peers at AU 2026
speakers: Clair Stone, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk | James Youmatz, General Adoption Manager, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Forma Data Management Essentials | Fusion | Informed Design | Inventor | Revit | AECO | Industrialized Construction
abstract: Join fellow AU attendees for an informal meetup focused on industrialized construction, prefabrication, modular workflows, and Informed Design. This session will bring together owners, designers, builders, fabricators, and Autodesk Partners who are shaping the future of how buildings are designed and delivered. Whether you’re advancing off-site construction, exploring connections between design and manufacturing, or learning from peers across the ecosystem, this meetup will be a space to network, exchange ideas, and discuss challenges and opportunities across the AU community.

title: Converge at Sweco How Integrated Workflows & XR Enhanced, Revolutionized a Multidisciplinary Project
speakers: Zinta Rize, Water and Wastewater Engineer, Sweco Norge | Jani Pehkonen, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Civil 3D | Desktop Connector | Inventor | Revit | Workshop XR | AECO | Design & Engineering
abstract: Can a multidisciplinary team across countries and companies deliver a better wastewater treatment plant, faster, by working as one? At AU 2026, Sweco’s Zinta Rize shares the Kongsberg WWTP: a project that doubled capacity while meeting strict EU standards. Using Plant 3D, Revit, Civil 3D, and ACC as a single source of truth, plus VR reviews in Autodesk Workshop XR, the team broke silos and improved coordination. Results: 25% efficiency gain, 15% less 3D effort, and major reductions in 2D drafting. Discover how integrated BIM, cloud workflows, and immersive collaboration enabled smarter decisions, faster delivery, and a more sustainable, future-ready facility.

title: What Owners Want: Honest Guidance on BIM, CDEs, and Becoming a Preferred Digital Partner
speakers: ahmed alwaeel, Director of planning and design, Ministry of energy and infrastructure | abdulrahman alkholy, Digital transformation lead & AI, Ministry of energy and infrastructure
topics: Construction Operations | Buildings | BIM 360 Build | Bridge Design for InfraWorks 360 | Civil 3D | InfraWorks (ICD) | Revit | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: You’ve set up the common data environment (CDE). You’ve trained the team. You’ve delivered the models. So why does the owner still complain? Because owners do not think like consultants. In this candid 30-minute session, the United Arab Emirates Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MOEI) will share what an infrastructure owner actually expects from BIM deliverables, CDE workflows, and digital submissions. You’ll hear how we assess consultant performance, what builds trust, and which common mistakes immediately signal weak digital delivery capability. This is not a product demo or a generic case study. It’s an owner-side view of what really influences decisions, repeat work, and preferred-partner status on major government projects.

title: Decision-Driven Parametric Tunnel Design Using Shared Project Data
speakers: Mikhail SEMENENKO, BIM Manager, Bouygues Construction | Nicolas RAGEUL, Digital Transformation Leader, Bouygues TP
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | Autodesk Platform Services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Many tunnel projects rely on static design approaches that limit the ability of stakeholders to anticipate construction risks and adapt to evolving constraints. This session will present a decision-driven parametric design approach for tunnel and cross-passage modeling using shared project data accessible to stakeholders. Based on a real tunnel project in the United Kingdom, we’ll demonstrate how Dynamo-driven workflows enable rapid iteration of design scenarios and validation of geometric constraints. The session will also highlight collaboration between design and construction teams using shared linear references. We’ll also share how value was assessed, including reduced design iterations, improved risk anticipation, and faster decision making.

title: Carbon Intelligence in the Cloud: Connecting ORIS to Autodesk Forma and Your Enterprise Data Ecosystem
speakers: Jón Gunnar Hilmarsson, Chief BIM Manager, Ramboll | Sheena Zhang, Sr. Manager, AECO Sustainability Strategy, Autodesk | Guilhem de Montaignac, BIM Advocate & Software Engineer, ORIS | Nolwenn LANCIEN, Head of partnership, ORIS Material Intelligence
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | Autodesk Platform Services | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Carbon assessment still happens outside the tools where infrastructure teams actually work. In this panel discussion, Autodesk, Ramboll, and ORIS explore what it looks like when that changes, bringing carbon intelligence directly into the cloud environment where project data already lives. Drawing on a concrete project from Ramboll, panelists will share how their team embedded carbon workflows into their existing Autodesk Forma environment without disrupting data governance or forcing manual exports. The conversation will surface the technical and practical realities of connecting carbon assessment to the project data ecosystem, from integration architecture to day-to-day workflow impact.

title: From Legacy to Cloud: Enterprise Migration Strategies for Civil Infrastructure to Autodesk Forma
speakers: Drew Theis, Technology Consultant, ARKANCE
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma Data Management | InfraWorks | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Civil infrastructure firms manage complex portfolios across fragmented legacy environments like network drives, ProjectWise, Microsoft SharePoint, and BIM 360. Transitioning to Autodesk Forma Data Management establishes a unified, cloud-native ecosystem. But doing so at scale introduces high operational risks. How do you migrate massive Civil 3D data sets without disrupting active data shortcuts and xrefs? Where do heavy InfraWorks models and point clouds reside? What is the governance strategy for historical deliverables? This session will deliver a strategic, repeatable migration playbook engineered for complex multi-office environments. Moving beyond theory, we’ll provide a tool-by-tool, phased workflow. You’ll learn how to audit file dependencies across legacy storage, map structures to the Autodesk Forma architecture, and execute staged migrations that maintain business continuity. You’ll leave with an enterprise decision framework and an immediate deployment checklist.

title: One Platform, Zero Guesswork: Seamlessly Connecting 2D and 3D Takeoff with Estimation
speakers: Deepak Maini, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Docs | Quantity Takeoff | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: A recent QuickBooks survey found that one in four construction companies risk closure if they make two or three inaccurate estimates. The estimation inaccuracy is caused by the complexity of 2D and 3D data and the frequent updates to bid packages. It’s compounded by siloed takeoff and estimation processes. Autodesk addresses this by seamlessly integrating takeoff and estimation within Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). This lab will give you firsthand experience in workflows that improve takeoff accuracy and estimation using a unified, connected platform. You’ll link 2D and 3D takeoffs to cost data, enabling real-time estimation. Walk away with learnings to perform faster, data-driven takeoffs, and deliver predictable project estimates through a connected source of truth.

title: ReCap Meshing for BIM Coordination
speakers: Gabriel Hernandez, VDC Project Manager, Turner Construction | Melinda Hoffman, Subject Matter Expert, Construction, Autodesk | Brad Lane, VDC Reality Capture Manager, Turner Construction
topics: Reality Capture | Construction services | Navisworks Manage | ReCap | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: In this session, we’ll share a strategy discussion into ReCap software’s new mesh workflow for creating scan-derived meshes that perform reliably in Model Coordination in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) and Navisworks software. Using a confidential project case study, you will see how our team processed 1 TB of scan data across 1.2 million square feet and resolved repeated model crashes that disrupted access for virtual design and construction (VDC) engineers and trade partners. By moving from Leica Cyclone 3DR to ReCap-generated meshes, we improved mesh quality, stabilized performance, streamlined scan-to-coordination workflows, and enabled automated clash detection with existing conditions for more-reliable downstream delivery.

title: Innovators Stage | Skills to Pay the Bills: Creating Claude Skills for Autodesk Workflows
speakers: Poyraz Yildirim, Developer Advocate Manager, Autodesk | João Martins, Principal Systems Integration Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Docs | Forma | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Claude skills provide a standard way to create reusable capabilities that help AI complete complex tasks. This session will focus on creating skills that automate design and project delivery workflows in Autodesk. You’ll learn what a skill is, when it should be used instead of prompts or Model Context Protocols (MCPs), how to design skills that interact with Autodesk Platform Services and Autodesk Forma, and how to adopt these automations across an organization. We’ll explore how skills can be used together with tools like MCP and custom scripts, and we’ll build practical examples such as querying BIM metadata, automating design data checks, and producing design documentation.

title: Innovators Stage | Skills to Pay the Bills: Creating Claude Skills for Autodesk Workflows
speakers: Anthony Sertorio, Principal Enterprise Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Docs | Forma | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Claude skills provide a standard way to create reusable capabilities that help AI complete complex tasks.
