title: Why Construction Needs World Models
speakers: Mo Han, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk | Yuri Bartzis, Construction Industry Fellow, Autodesk | Xin Yang, Senior Research Scientist Construction, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Build | Docs | Forma | Revit | AECO | Future Industry Innovations | Cross Industry
abstract: Construction does not have a data shortage; it has a decision-support shortage. What project teams lack is a reliable way to continuously assemble the live state of a project across time, space, and cost, using that understanding to make better project decisions. This session will introduce the grounded world model as that missing layer, fusing multisensor site signals with previously siloed project evidence such as drawings, site photos, and BIM. Unlike a digital twin, which reflects current conditions, a world model can reason over relationships and support action when conditions start to shift, while supporting agentic issue detection. This points to a fundamentally different way of managing construction from a living model of the site.

title: Immersive Design Reviews: Evaluating Informed Design Models in Workshop XR
speakers: Shane McDonald, BIM Design Manager, Murphy | Matthew Lenehan, Mechanical Design Engineer, Murphy
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Construction services | Forma | Inventor | Navisworks Manage | Revit | Workshop XR | AECO | XR | Cross Industry
abstract: This class would show how configurable, manufacturable content created through Informed Design can be reviewed at scale in Workshop XR, helping teams catch spatial clashes, access BIM data, and raise issues before construction. This would be especially suited to a Revit-to-review workflow for BIM/VDC teams because Workshop XR is built for collaborative model reviews, supports issue management, and connects directly to Autodesk Forma.

title: Breaking Down Silos: Modernizing AutoCAD-Inventor-Revit Interoperability with Data Exchange
speakers: Jonathan Crowson, CAD Support Manager, EFCO Corp. | Gaurav Bhamre, Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk | Trevor Love, CAD Administrator, EFCO Corp.
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Construction services | AutoCAD | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | Inventor | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: For EFCO's team of 250 engineers, moving design data across AutoCAD, Inventor, and Revit software meant constant rework, misaligned models, lost parameters, and no path to incremental updates. By adopting Data Exchange, EFCO built a consistent, update-aware pipeline that scales reliably across the firm’s full team. But the real power of this story extends beyond EFCO: Its workflow is a blueprint for any industry where manufacturing and architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) teams must collaborate across domains. You’ll leave this session with practical techniques for modernizing multitool workflows and a model for enabling seamless cross-domain collaboration, from design to construction.

title: From Ground Data to Cost Certainty: Outcome-Based Excavation Analysis in Forma with GroundIQ
speakers: Nigel Peters, Senior Product Manager - Rail, Autodesk | Arno Koldewee, Head of Product, Fugro | Ben Wardell, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Forma | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract:
Early-stage site design moves fast, but ground conditions rarely keep up. Excavation costs are a top risk driver, yet reliable estimates arrive long after key decisions are made. 

This session demonstrates outcome-based BIM in practice: directly from Forma, GroundIQ generates a 3D ground model from site investigation data and delivers excavation volumes and cost estimates automatically without specialist intervention. 

Attendees see a live demo: footprint placed, ground intelligence derived, cost insight surfaced instantly. BIM that connects subsurface conditions to project outcomes.

title: Change Orders: Chaos to Order
speakers: Tim Kelleher, Ops. Standards and Innovation Manager, Brinkman Construction Inc.
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Construction services | Build | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Before adopting Cost Management, our change order process lived primarily in Microsoft Excel. Looking back, it’s honestly impressive (and a little terrifying) that it worked at all. Moving to Cost Management allowed us to standardize the process and drive more-consistent outcomes. But giving up the flexibility and freedom of spreadsheets left many of our project managers feeling stuck. In this class, we’ll show how we use the Change Order tools in Cost Management to simplify the process without losing the flexibility our teams need. You’ll learn how we balance structure where it matters and flexibility where it doesn’t—streamlining workflows in a way that improves PM productivity and keeps them happy, without sending them back to Excel.

title: Beyond the Migration: From Discovery to Momentum
speakers: David Smith, Technology Integration Manager, Vankirk Electric
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Build | Docs | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Migrating an organization to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) requires a sophisticated balance of technical automation and cultural change management. This session will explore the comprehensive migration journey at VanKirk Electric, focusing on the development of internal AI-assisted tools to automate legacy project transfers. We’ll detail how we addressed complex technical hurdles—such as long-file-path limitations—while coordinating across departments to ensure the new environment met the specific needs of every team. Furthermore, we’ll showcase our "ACC Training Hub," a centralized Microsoft SharePoint ecosystem designed to drive high adoption rates through on-demand training, support ticketing, and peer-to-peer engagement forums.

speakers: David Smith, Technology Integration Manager, Vankirk Electric
topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management

title: AEC Roadmap: Autodesk Forma for Model Management
speakers: Marco Ramolla, Sr. Manager, Product Mgmt, Autodesk | Monserrat Elaskar, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk | Paul Walker, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Tori Anderson, Product Marketing Manager, Construction, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | BIM Collaborate | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma | Model Coordination | Navisworks Manage | AECO
abstract: Models should not live in silos. They should drive decisions. This session will explore how Autodesk connects BIM and virtual design and construction (VDC) workflows across design and construction, from early concept through handover and beyond. Learn how teams can better coordinate, collaborate, and use models across tools and roles. We’ll share what’s coming in Autodesk Forma to make models more usable, accessible, and valuable in both the field and the office. Explore the recent and future capabilities for Autodesk Forma Design Collaboration, Autodesk Forma for Model Management, and Navisworks Manage users to better coordinate models and collaborate across teams.

title: Year of the Owner: Owner and Contractor Collaboration Using Autodesk Forma
speakers: Jacob Pfenning-Wendt, Solutions Manager, UPS
topics: Construction services | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: During this session, we’ll explore from an owner’s perspective how we’re collaborating with our contractors using Autodesk Forma. We’ll discuss lessons learned, how we overcame difficulties, and how we’ve laid out groundwork for continued and increased collaboration in future projects. Transitioning to Forma has allowed for processes to become more efficient, but it has also shown gaps where new checks were implemented to ensure delivery of a quality product.

title: Enabling Next-Generation Autodesk Workflows: Can a Slim Mobile Workstation Really Keep Up with Your Autodesk Work?
speakers: Jamie Gwilliam, WW User & Industries Lead, Workstations, Intel | Lindsay M Benjamin, ISV Partner Marketing Manager, INTEL CORPORATION | Catherine Rocha, Platform Readiness Lead, Intel
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Construction services | None | AECO
abstract:
As AI, visualization, and increasingly complex 3D workflows reshape how teams design, review, render, and simulate, professionals need more than raw specifications—they need a system that performs reliably wherever work happens.

 

Join us and an Autodesk industry expert from the Elite Experience program for a real-world look at modern mobile workstation workflows across Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD, and Fusion. The session will share firsthand experience using a slim mobile workstation as a primary device, including the performance, responsiveness, mobility, battery-life, and day-to-day usability factors that matter beyond a benchmark score.

Attendees will learn how to evaluate the right balance of CPU, GPU, memory, storage, and connectivity for their own workloads; when local, cloud, or hybrid workflows make sense; and how to identify where a hardware upgrade will deliver meaningful value

title: Collaborating at the Heart of Design and Manufacturing
speakers: James Wainwright, Technical Lead, Team Bath Heart | Aksharaa Gupta, Team Lead, University of Bath- Team Bath Heart
topics: Education | Fusion | Fusion Simulation Extension | EDU | Manufacturing Engineering | D&M
abstract: Discover the inspiring collaboration of Team Bath Heart and Autodesk at the Autodesk Technology Centre in Birmingham, merging creativity with advanced technology to create a revolutionary artificial heart. Team Bath Heart is a multidisciplinary engineering team from the University of Bath in England. Two-time champions of the international Heart Hackathon, the team is pioneering innovations in artificial-heart design—combining advanced simulation, manufacturing, and biomedical insight to push the boundaries of medical engineering. The team uses the Autodesk Fusion collaborative features, CAM profiling, and generative design tools to accelerate the design, testing, and prototyping of their next-generation artificial heart.

title: Don’t AI Everything: Hybrid Automation with Autodesk Platform Services and Revit
speakers: Will North, Director, Design Automation Systems Ltd | Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk | Neil Lee, Director, Design Automation Systems Ltd
topics: Building products and fabrication | Autodesk Platform Services | Revit | D&M | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Automation specialists are increasingly tasked with finding areas to implement AI. But how do we decide when AI is the correct tool and when deterministic automation serves better? Through a live demo of an AI-augmented building regulation compliance checker running on Autodesk Platform Services, we will explore a practical hybrid framework. The Automation API and Revit software handle rule evaluation through a deterministic engine. Large language models (LLMs) extract compliance rules from regulation documentation and explain failures in natural language. And the Viewer SDK provides visual context. We’ll demonstrate a human-in-the-loop approach and show how AI architecture adapts rapidly when regulations change or new markets require new rule sets.

title: VRED to Flame using Python: Standardizing Image Pipelines from Render to Finishing
speakers: Mark Taylor, Sr Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk | Ruediger Ambs, Sr Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Film and TV | Flame | VRED | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract: Rendering Autodesk VRED scenes can result in Open EXR sequences that require manual handling before they can be used in Autodesk Flame. This creates delays, inconsistencies, and avoidable errors in high-end commercial finishing workflows. This session will discuss example pipelines using both VRED and Flame Python tools to render Open EXR sequences from VRED and ingest them into Flame as clips. We will cover render jobs, structuring output, managing naming, and simplifying Flame imports. You should leave with a repeatable, production-ready workflow that reduces manual ingest and connects visualization to finishing with speed and reliability.

title: Digital Factory Summit | From Reactive to Resilient: How MaintainX Is Powering Intelligent Maintenance
speakers: Ozella Bowman, Sr Systems Integration Consultant, Autodesk | Colin Morris, Head of Solutions Consulting, MaintainX, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | Factory Design Utilities | Forma | Revit | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract:
Keeping operations running has never been more critical. Maintenance and
operations leaders must maximize asset performance, reduce downtime, control costs, and do
more with leaner teams - all while keeping production moving.

Join leaders from MaintainX, now an Autodesk company, to explore how leading manufacturers are rethinking maintenance as a driver of operational performance and a competitive differentiator. Drawing on insights from thousands of customers, this session will share how data from frontline workers, real-time machine connectivity, and artificial intelligence (AI) help frontline teams improve asset reliability, increase productivity, and make faster, more informed decisions.

You'll learn how digital maintenance platforms help teams reduce unplanned downtime,
standardize work, and turn operational data into actionable insights. This session will also cover what's next for intelligent maintenance and asset management  - and why manufacturers are making this a priority today.

title: Transforming Construction Planning with Digital: Site Plans in Action with Laing O'Rourke and McCarthy
speakers: Javier Glatt, Co-Founder, cmBuilder.io | Paul Drayton, Head of Digital, Laing O'Rourke | Khoi Pham, Sr. VDC Manager, McCarthy Building Companies, Inc.
topics: Reality Capture | Construction Operations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | None | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Join construction leaders from cmBuilder.io, Laing O'Rourke, and McCarthy Building Companies as they explore how digital site planning is transforming the way complex projects are won and delivered. Learn how empowering field teams with intuitive 3D and 4D planning tools is democratizing construction logistics—reducing reliance on specialists while enabling project managers, superintendents, and site teams to take ownership of planning and coordination. Discover how digital simulation of construction sequencing, logistics, and site operations helps teams validate plans before work begins, identify risks earlier, improve stakeholder communication, and optimize project execution. Through real-world case studies from major projects in the United Kingdom and North America, this session will demonstrate how digital site logistics plans are helping contractors win more work, improve collaboration, and deliver safer, more efficient projects.

title: Harnessing AI for AECO: Live Workflows Connecting Design, Engineering, and Fabrication
speakers: Manuel Liedot, CEO, GRAITEC | Emmanuel LEROY, Chief Product and Strategy Officer, GRAITEC
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Engineering service providers | Advance Steel | Revit | AECO
abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping AECO, but most solutions remain disconnected from engineering and fabrication workflows where technical decisions are made. Through live demonstrations, this session will show AI embedded within production environments, leveraging engineering standards, deterministic calculation engines, fabrication rules, and BIM data. Explore AI-assisted model management, load generation, detailing, and cross-platform workflows enabled through AI skills and APIs/MCPs, delivering reliable, auditable results while keeping engineers and fabricators in control.

title: Dara Treseder on Building Trust, Brands, and Leadership in an AI World
topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Dara Treseder, Chief Marketing Officer at Autodesk, returns to the Digital Builder podcast to discuss what it takes to build trust and brand relevance in the era of AI. The conversation explores authenticity, thought leadership, marketing strategy, reputation building, and why organizations of all sizes must find new ways to stand out as information becomes increasingly abundant and accessible.

title: AI-Powered Visual Storytelling for AEC Projects
speakers: Duane Rutkowski, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Flow Studio | Maya | Revit | AECO | Media & Entertainment | M&E
abstract: Autodesk Flow Studio software is a generative solution in the Autodesk Media & Entertainment Collection. This software helps artists produce layout, create content, and drive home visuals across film, television, and games. This solution can also be used in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) space to help standup Revit content and aid with visuals to maximize customer impact.

title: You’ve Heard About Autodesk Assistant in Revit. Now Here’s How to Actually Use It.
speakers: Shir Rustici, BIM Program Manager, Turner & Townsend | ARGELIA Barcena, Head of Regional Leads - North America, Women in BIM
topics: Architecture services | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: In this session, we’ll focus on how the new Autodesk Assistant in Revit fits into real modeling and documentation workflows inside Revit 2027. From making modeling easier to troubleshooting issues and supporting documentation, we’ll walk through practical examples you can apply right away. You’ll see how to ask better questions, how to refine the responses, and how to turn those responses into something useful. We’ll also discuss how AI can support and complement your design process, not replace it. We’ll cover where Autodesk Assistant works well, where it still falls short, and how to use it in a way that actually saves time. Come to this session to learn how to make Autodesk Assistant in Revit work for you, not against you.

title: From Unique to Scalable: Modular School Design with BIM, Industrialization and Resilience
speakers: Gabriela Hoffmann Fiuza, Coordinator, Secretariat of the State of RS | Júlia Akemi Motoshima, BIM Manager, Secretariat of the State of RS
topics: Architecture services | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Industrialized Construction
abstract: After the 2024 floods in southern Brazil, the Rio Grande do Sul State faced an urgent challenge: how to deliver public schools faster with quality and at scale. This session presents the Escola+ project, a modular and standardized school model developed using BIM. Instead of unique designs, schools are assembled from a catalog of more than 60 modules that can be combined to meet different educational and site requirements. Using Autodesk Revit and Forma, the digital workflow integrates design data, cloud collaboration, and data-driven decision-making, accelerating project delivery while improving coordination, consistency, and predictability. Attendees will learn how modular BIM workflows can help scale resilient public-school infrastructure.

title: Prompt to Procurement: AI Research at MIT on Closing the Render-to-Build Loop
speakers: Richa Gupta, Researcher and Forward Deployed Engineer, Massachusetts Institute of Technology |Nomic
topics: Architecture services | Autodesk Rendering | Forma | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Architects and BIM teams are generating AI images faster than ever. But outputs rarely connect back to real materials, specifications, or fabrication. This session will draw on three MIT Architecture and Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) research projects to show exactly where the design-to-build pipeline breaks down and what fixes it. What we’ll cover includes steering AI image generation with element-level references, matching rendered materials back into BIM specifications, and connecting natural language to robotic assembly—each finding maps to a workflow that practitioners can act on. You’ll leave with research-backed behavioral changes where AI tools genuinely add value in their pipelines and where the gaps need bridging.

title: Building an AI-Ready BIM Data Backbone with Autodesk Platform Services
speakers: Moritz Mombour, Head of Digitalization EPCM REI, Drees & Sommer SE | Valeriia Vlasenko, Expert, Drees & Sommer
topics: Trust | Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) organizations struggle to scale automation and AI because BIM data is fragmented, inconsistently governed, and tied to individual projects. This session will show how Drees & Sommer and AnkerDB built a centralized BIM data backbone using Autodesk Platform Services and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to enable reliable automation and consistent data quality at scale. The collaboration started as a rapid proof of concept at DevCon 2025, was validated across multiple projects, and is now scaling at the business-unit level. The session will explain how Autodesk Forma data, Autodesk Platform Services software, and downstream systems were connected to support automated validation, data enrichment, analytics, integrations, and AI-supported workflows for cost management and lifecycle assessment (LCA).

title: Downstream Starts Upstream: How Governance Turns Project Data into Operational Value
speakers: NATALIA CASTILLO, Workplace Strategy Director RM and BIM, CBRE | Robert S. Olsen, Senior Director, CBRE
topics: Data and Document Management | Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: For too long, BIM data quality for operations has been treated as a downstream problem—discovered late, remediated manually, and handed over with gaps that limit long-term value. In reality, these are rarely technical failures, but governance failures. This class will explore how organizations can shift from reactive records remediation to upstream prevention by introducing a BIM governance coordinator role: bridging client requirements, internal standards, and multidisciplinary delivery teams to ensure expectations are understood, tracked, and enforced throughout the project lifecycle—turning BIM deliverables into more-reliable operational assets.

title: From Disconnected Tasks to Standardized Construction Workflows: Connected by Autodesk Forma with a Database
speakers: Saori 櫻井, Project Manager, Shimizu Construction Co., Ltd.
topics: Data and Document Management | Buildings | Autodesk Account | Forma | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Construction work often struggles not because information is missing, but because tasks, people, and decisions remain disconnected. Has the push for accurate data increased input and broken workflows? This isn’t anyone’s fault. It happens when work isn’t connected properly—and that’s where Autodesk Forma helps. This session will show how Autodesk Forma links technical feedback, project coordination, and management information. In one workflow, standardizing how information reached the right people at the right time reduced office-side coordination by 70%, site response effort by 50%, and initial review meeting time by 20%. We’ll also show how this approach supports repeatable workflows and easier transfer of technical knowledge.

title: Dr. Vibe: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Start Loving Autodesk Platform Services
speakers: Winston Pagliaro, Civil Infrastructure BIM and VDC Specialist, HNTB
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: This is a tale from a BIM manager’s foray into vibe coding—going from having no coding experience to building web applications that tap into the Autodesk Platform Services APIs to supercharge the capabilities of our Autodesk Forma-based CAD managers. Have you been curious about Autodesk Platform Services but haven’t pulled the trigger because you’re not “a developer”? With Dr. Claude’s help, you can be! Come to this session to learn tips on diving into the world of Autodesk Platform Services and large language models (LLMs). We’ll share lessons learned on working hand in hand with these LLMs in a safe and efficient way so that you can also share in this digital boon.

title: Drilling Down with BIM: Automating Tunnels and Rock Bolts in a Hydropower Megaproject
speakers: Emmanuel CHOCQ, Head of BIM Department, Tractebel | Maher DJEDIDI, BIM Manager, TRACTEBEL
topics: Structural Engineering  | Civil infrastructure | BIM 360 Docs | Civil 3D | Docs | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Large-scale underground infrastructure projects push BIM workflows to their limits, especially when dealing with tens of kilometers of tunnels and tens of thousands of repetitive elements. This session will present a real-world case study from a major Australian hydropower project where BIM was implemented across both design and construction phases. We’ll focus on the processes developed to efficiently model more than 40 kilometers of tunnels and more than 35,000 rock bolts, ensuring consistency, performance, and constructability. By combining Revit, Civil 3D, Dynamo, and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), we established automated workflows for geometry generation, data structuring, and model coordination.

title: Beyond the BOM: Using PLM to Drive Modern Product Management
speakers: Gus Quade, Sr. Technical Sales Specialist,  Fusion PLM, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Manage | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Product lifecycle management (PLM) is often treated as a system of record for BOMs—but leading teams are using it to drive product strategy, execution, and cross-functional alignment. In this session, we’ll show how to evolve PLM into a product management backbone that connects engineering, operations, and business decisions. You’ll learn practical workflows for managing product definitions, changes, and lifecycle data in a way that improves visibility, reduces delays, and enables better decision making. Walk away with patterns you can apply immediately to move beyond BOM management and unlock real business value from PLM.

title: Technical Adoption of XR in Construction: Connecting VR, AR, and Autodesk Forma Workflows
speakers: Gary Cowan, Head of Digital Construction/VDC, Kane Group
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Construction services | Cloud Worksharing | Forma | Revit | Workshop XR | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Discover how VR and AR create a practical, end‑to‑end BIM workflow from design to construction. See how Autodesk Forma can be integrated with Autodesk Workshop XR to enable immersive design reviews and collaborative decision making in VR. Then discover real-life integration with GAMMA AR to validate installation, reduce errors, and connect design intent directly to construction for a seamless, circular, virtual design and construction (VDC) workflow.

title: Prestige NEXTRA: From Fragmentation to Control—Scaling 180 Million Square Feet of Real Estate with Autodesk Forma
speakers: Vishesh Vishesh Kaul, Chief Information & Digital Officer, Prestige Group | Vishwajeet S. Patil, Engineering Transformation Head, Prestige Group
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Managing one of India’s largest RE portfolios, Prestige is transforming project delivery to address fragmented systems, siloed data, and limited cross-functional visibility. This session will introduce Prestige NEXTRA, an enterprise initiative to create a connected and standardized delivery ecosystem. We will showcase how Autodesk Forma integrates systems such as SAP, Primavera P6, procurement, and cost tools to improve information flow across design, planning, and execution. You will gain insights into enterprise rollout, governance, and adoption, along with key lessons from scaling digital processes across a large portfolio.

title: Digital Project Delivery. Autodesk Forma Build Implementation.
speakers: Rania Hassan, VDC Regional Manager, Ellisdon
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Build | Forma | Model Coordination | Revit | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Our session will show how Autodesk Forma was implemented and governed on a live health care project, adapting workflows to project‑specific needs. We will demonstrate the application of standards during active delivery to maintain consistency and data integrity while teams adopt the platform and evolve digital practices in real time. You’ll learn how collaboration was structured across Autodesk, construction technology, operations, and BIM by deploying two Autodesk Forma Build projects to separate design coordination from construction execution, alongside targeted training. We’ll also cover license provisioning, role‑based access, content ownership alignment, and Power BI dashboards that deliver actionable insights for better decisions.

title: Lessons from Cost Management Implementation Ninjas
speakers: Nick Prato, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | Tyler Patton, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | Build | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Whether you're exploring Cost Management in Autodesk Forma Build, actively using it, or pushing the limits as a power user, this session is for you! Join this 30-minute ask-the-experts session to connect directly with the Autodesk Forma Cost Management implementation experts. Get answers to your toughest questions, learn proven best practices, and hear how leading teams are optimizing cost workflows and enterprise resource planning (ERP) integrations to drive better outcomes. Discover practical tips and real-world strategies, and see how AI can help solve complex cost challenges. Plus, bring your scenarios to the table during an open Q&A and walk away with actionable insights you can apply immediately.

title: Autodesk Forma Isn’t the Hard Part. Leading Through Change Is.
speakers: Lil Magallanes, Construction Technology Program Manager, DPR Construction
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Implementation of Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) is often treated as the finish line, when it’s only the starting point. The real challenge is leading through continuous change—balancing field needs, data, and evolving technology. This session will share how a shift toward proactive engagement, stronger internal alignment, and deeper partnership with Autodesk transformed how we operate and scale Autodesk Forma. By combining field feedback with user data, we built an operating model that supports better decisions and long-term success. You’ll leave with a strategic lens and practical approach to leading Autodesk Forma beyond implementation.

title: From Capture to AI: How Data Enrichment Unlocks the Value of Motion
speakers: Olivier Zurcher, Animation Researcher (Technical Animator), Autodesk | Larasika Nadela, Machine Learning Developer, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Film and TV | Flow Production Tracking | Maya | M&E | Future Industry Innovations | Cross Industry
abstract: AI-powered animation is only as good as the data behind it, but most motion data wasn’t designed for AI. In this session, we’ll demonstrate a projection-mapped capture app that guides performers in real time to produce more-structured motion. As well as how Label Maker, a tool integrated within the Autodesk ecosystem, uses AI to turn raw motion data and videos into richly tagged, reusable data sets. You will walk away with a clearer picture of how to make motion data actually usable for AI, and how to rethink their pipelines to get there. The real value of motion data isn’t in the capture—it’s in the enrichment.

title: Maximizing the Value of InfoWorks ICM: A Model-Driven Approach to CSO Reduction
speakers: Alexandre Gil, General Manager, SUEZ Optimatics | Josh Cantone, President, Optimatics | Joel Knight, NA Business Development, Optimatics
topics: Water Infrastructure | Utilities and telecom | InfoWorks ICM | Innovyze Cloud Service | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract:
Utilities managing combined sewer systems are increasingly challenged to reduce overflow events while controlling capital costs. This presentation highlights how the InfoWorks ICM hydraulic model was used as the foundation for advanced system optimization in the SUEZ SEVESC wastewater network in the western suburbs of Paris.
The calibrated InfoWorks ICM model enabled detailed simulation of network performance across a range of storm events, forming the analytical backbone for decision-making. Building on this, Optimizer™ (by Optimatics) was integrated to systematically evaluate thousands of operational and infrastructure scenarios, including regulator settings, pump operations, and real-time control (RTC) strategies.

title: Catch a first look: The Future of Street Design
topics: Civil infrastructure | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract:
Get a live look at new street design capabilities in Autodesk Forma. See how we’re expanding Forma into street and roadway design and how these new capabilities will connect with Civil 3D.

Whether you’re a civil engineer, road engineer, transportation planner, or similar, discover how Forma can help you explore more options, identify risks earlier, and align your team around a strong design direction—faster and with greater confidence.

title: Vibe Coding for AECO Professionals—The Master Class
speakers: Charles Berteaux, VDC/Tech Manager, SSOE Group
topics: Architecture services | Build | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: This comprehensive 90-minute presentation will cover the entire vibe-coding landscape for architecture, engineering, construction, and owner (AECO) professionals. We’ll provide platform-agnostic coverage of AI-powered development tools, prompt engineering, token economics, deployment strategies, and real-world AECO workflows—from proof of concept to production.

title: Using MCP to Build Self-Improving AEC Data Workflows
speakers: Nabil Sadeg, CTO, Nacorm
topics: Architecture services | Autodesk Platform Services | Revit | AECO | Software Development | Cross Industry
abstract: Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) data stays raw because processing it manually does not scale. This session will demonstrate a working pipeline where AI classifies documents, extracts structured information, enriches records, and validates outputs at every stage. Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects AI agents to Revit, Autodesk Platform Services, and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), letting them read and write connected data across tools in a single workflow. A live walk-through of a real pipeline used on AEC projects will show how feedback loops capture user corrections so results improve with every iteration. You will leave with a reusable architecture pattern you can adapt to your own challenges, from tender analysis to intelligent models to construction submittals.

title: Industrialized Construction Summit | Industrialized Construction: What Will It Take to Reach the Tipping Point?
speakers: Donna Laquidara-Carr, Industry Insights Research Director, Dodge Construction Network | Ray Boff, National Prefab Leader, DPR Construction | Paul Drayton, Head of Digital, Laing O'Rourke | Martin Fischer, Professor, CIFE-Stanford | Az Jasat, Dir., Strategic Planning/Analytics, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | None | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: Industrialized construction is widely discussed but unevenly implemented. This panel will bring together perspectives from research, technology, academia, and industry to examine what it will take to scale prefabrication, productization, and design for manufacturing and assembly (DfMA). Drawing on new global research with Dodge Construction Network across five markets, the session will explore why fewer than half of organizations report scaled use despite strong intent. Panelists will test these findings against real-world experience, focusing on procurement, early design decisions, supply chain integration, and workforce capability to identify what must change to reach industry-wide adoption.

title: From POC to Product: Building an AI-Powered Revit App
speakers: Roderick Bates, Senior Director, Product Operations, Chaos
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Architecture services | Revit Live | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Go behind the scenes on the development journey of an AI-powered generative design tool for architecture and MEP. See the unfiltered reality of evolving a simple proof of concept into a full-fledged product that converts text prompts and reference images directly into native Revit geometry that streams live into Enscape, where you can visualize, adjust, and iterate in real time. We’ll share the conflicts, pivots, and technology decisions that got us across the finish line, pulling back the curtain on what it really takes to deliver a truly innovative product that provides real efficiency gains for architects and engineers in an architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) technology landscape where AI is compressing years of technology change into months.

title: Keep Your Scanner. Unlock Your Point Clouds.
speakers: Sun-Yen Tan, Associate Product Manager, Matterport | Dominick Gallegos, Director of Product Marketing - AEC / FM, Matterport
topics: Reality Capture | Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Geospatial and GIS | Architecture services | AutoCAD | Docs | Forma Build | Forma Data Management | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: You own a survey-grade scanner. The point clouds it produces sit on a drive, hard to share and useless to anyone who is not a surveyor. This session will show you a different path. See how a point cloud from a Leica, FARO, Trimble, or other scanner becomes a navigable Matterport digital twin, then feeds Autodesk Forma, Revit, AutoCAD, or other design software through the integration your team already uses. You keep the hardware you bought. You make its output usable for the whole project team, not just the person who captured it. Through a live workflow, you’ll see Point Cloud Import turn a raw scan into a true 3D model with scan-to-BIM and scan-to-CAD output, and where that model fits against the photo-based documentation tools you may already run. You’ll leave able to map your own capture-to-coordination plan and put the scan data you’ve already paid for to work across design, construction, and closeout.

title: From 2D to Digital Twin: Connecting Design to Operations in Retail Lifecycle with BIM, IoT, and AI
speakers: Caterina Peretti, Global Innovation Manager, EssilorLuxottica | Giorgio Radojkovic, Global Engineering & Innovation, Essilorluxottica | Enrico Trovato, Head of AECO Automation & Intelligence, EssilorLuxottica
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Desktop Connector | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: Retail construction still relies heavily on fragmented 2D documentation, creating a disconnect between design, construction, and operations. This session will explore how EssilorLuxottica is transforming that model by converting 2D assets into structured 3D BIM and building a connected digital lifecycle. By linking design data to Internet of Things (IoT) sensors and maintenance workflows, stores evolve from static deliverables into dynamic, data-driven digital twins. This session will present a scalable approach to connect design to operations, improve asset visibility, and enable predictive maintenance, turning retail environments into fully integrated intelligent assets.

title: Autodesk Women’s Network Meetup
speakers: Christi Clay, Senior Program Manager, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None
abstract: This meetup is sponsored by Autodesk Employee Belonging Groups (EBGs) to support connection and shared growth across communities. We bring employees and customers together through interactive, networking-focused experiences. Participants will engage in small-group conversations designed to encourage meaningful dialogue, knowledge sharing, and relationship building across teams, roles, and communities.

title: Designing 3D Spaces using AI World Models
speakers: Ben Mildenhall, Cofounder, World Labs
topics: Future Industry Innovations | Cross Industry
abstract: Existing AI image and video models allow for rapid iteration from text or concepts to images and videos but can only produce 2D outputs allowing for limited downstream interaction and editing. World models such as World Labs’ Marble can create complete and visually rich 3D environments in minutes from just a handful of real images, concept sketches, 360 panoramas, or a 3D layout. This session will walk through a variety of workflows combining AI image models and Marble together to rapidly build, edit, and visualize 3D worlds, as well as ways to export the resulting 3D Gaussian splat files into other tooling for further iteration.

title: Designing 3D Spaces using AI World Models
speakers: Ben Mildenhall, Cofounder, World Labs
topics: Future Industry Innovations | Cross Industry
abstract: Existing AI image and video models allow for rapid iteration from text or concepts to images and videos but can only produce 2D outputs allowing for limited downstream interaction and editing. title: Agentic AI Running Project Workflows in Autodesk Forma with MCP
speakers: Luis Salmeron, Senior Digital Systems Engineer, Professional Engineering Consultants (PEC) | Farzad Towhidi, Senior Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Software Development | Cross Industry
abstract: This session will explore how PEC is implementing agentic AI to run real project workflows within Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). By using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server as a governed orchestration layer, AI agents can securely connect to Autodesk APIs, query live project data, perform QA/QC checks, and execute tasks across project systems. You’ll see how this architecture moves beyond automation into true workflow execution—enabling scalable, consistent, and intelligent project delivery. We’ll share real-world examples, implementation strategies, and lessons learned to help teams begin adopting AI-driven workflows today.

title: AECO Roadmap: Vision and Strategy
speakers: Jen Suerth, Senior Director, Construction Strategy, Autodesk | Theo Agelopoulos, VP AEC Design Strategy, Autodesk | Julie Chen, Sr. Dir., Strategic Business Dev., Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Civil 3D | Forma | Revit | AECO
abstract: The AECO industry is entering a new era where granular data, connected workflows, and AI are transforming how projects are planned, delivered, and operated. This session explores Autodesk’s AEC vision for a unified cloud foundation that helps teams define outcomes earlier, carry context across the lifecycle, and make better decisions from day one. With a focus on outcome-based BIM, Autodesk is advancing an approach where data is more meaningful, accessible, and actionable. This enables stronger alignment, better visibility, and improved coordination, while laying the groundwork for intelligent guidance and automation across the project journey.

title: AECO Roadmap: Vision and Strategy
speakers: Nicolas Mangon, VP, AEC Industry Strategy, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | AECO
abstract: The AECO industry is entering a new era where granular data, connected workflows, and AI are transforming how projects are planned, delivered, and operated.
