title: Connecting BIM to Citizen-Scale Digital Twins: Sustainability, Compliance, and Connected Infrastructure
speakers: Francesco Cappilli, Head of Digital Engineering, Infrastrutture Milano Cortina 2026 Spa
topics: Data and Document Management | XR & Immersive Tech | Engineering service providers | Build | Civil 3D | Revit | Workshop XR | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: SIMICO S.p.A delivered infrastructure to the 2026 Winter Olympics (Livigno, Cortina, Milano, Verona, Bormio) using a full Autodesk pipeline: Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), Autodesk Forma Build, Autodesk Platform Services, Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD, and Navisworks software. Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Build managed cost, schedule, and field workflows. Autodesk Platform Services connected everything bidirectionally. This Autodesk-Azure dual common data environment (CDE) enabled a complex environment where BIM authoring changes synced with Forma cost tracking, Build field logs, and compliance docs. These pipelines preserved data integrity from Autodesk tools to digital XR experiences (VR/AR/pixel streaming), making the twin accessible to all stakeholders. Tailored as such, this system delivered an organic ecosystem, reducing risk and accelerating decisions on complex public infrastructure in Italy.

title: Bridging BIM and Hydraulics: Civil 3D and InfoWorks WS Pro for Smart Pressure Networks
speakers: Nathan Gerdts, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Ahmed Elsayed, Technical Specialist, Water, Autodesk | Mahmoud Najmeddine, BIM Manager, Khatib and Alami
topics: Water Infrastructure | Engineering service providers | Civil 3D | InfoWorks WS Pro | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Discover a new integration between Civil 3D and InfoWorks WS Pro software that connects BIM-based pressure pipe network design with detailed hydraulic analysis. See how bidirectional data exchange helps teams create constructable 3D networks using real parts while validating pressure, flow, and performance in InfoWorks WS Pro. Learn how this workflow improves design quality, reduces rework, and supports more-cost-effective outcomes. An industry expert will share real-world workflows, key benefits, lessons learned, and practical recommendations for successful adoption.

title: Find Answers, Not Artifacts: One Search Across All Your Project Systems
speakers: Philip Townsend, Principal Solutions Architect, Egnyte Inc. | Aaron Vorwerk, AEC Practice Leader, Architects + Owners, Egnyte
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Engineering service providers | AutoCAD | BIM Collaborate | Forma | Revit | AECO
abstract: Your firm already holds the answer to almost every question your teams ask. It's buried in specs, RFIs, submittals, drawings, and contracts across hundreds of projects. The problem was never a lack of data. It was getting an answer without digging for the artifact. This session shows what changes when AI is grounded in your real project data. We start simple, asking a question of one folder. Then we go historical: what did we spec for the curtain wall on our last three hospital projects? Then live across your active systems. The part that separates this from every generic AI demo: you watch permissions respected in real time. Change who's asking, and the answers change with them.

title: Feature, Add-In, or AI? Should You Buy, Build, or Hack in 2026?
speakers: Carl Storms, Technical Success Manager, Newforma | Mostafa EL AYOUBI, CEO, Oorkestra Online | Michael Kilkelly, Senior BIM Developer, Ulteig | John (JT) Pierson, Product Manager, Autodesk | Brodi Scott, Research, Development and Innovation Manager, BIM One
topics: Buildings | None | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: AI is changing how work gets done in architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO), but it’s also complicating the path forward. Do you wait for a feature, bolt on an add-in, or hack together an AI solution? In this panel, industry experts will respond to real-world scenarios and rapid-fire questions. Drawing from experience across platforms, add-ins, and AI workflows, they’ll weigh trade-offs between features, integrations, and fast AI solutions, including what works, what breaks, and what creates risk. This session is for teams working within real constraints. Whether you have development resources or you’re figuring it out on your own, you’ll leave better equipped to decide what to buy, what to build, and when a quick solution makes sense.

title: Autodesk Operations Roadmap: What's new and next in Operations
speakers: Robert Bray, VP, Tandem Platform, Autodesk | Seth Hindman, Sr Director, Product Management, Industry Strategy, & XD, Autodesk | Tim Kelly, Director, Tandem Platform Strategy, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Tandem Connect | AECO
abstract: In this roadmap session, we'll explore why operations is emerging as the next frontier of digital transformation and how Autodesk is helping organizations move from disconnected systems to connected operations that continuously learn and improve. We'll share the vision behind Autodesk Operations, the market forces reshaping the industry, and the latest innovations across FlexSim, Fusion Operations, Autodesk Tandem, Autodesk Connect and more. You'll gain insight into how Autodesk is connecting Design, Make, and Operate to close the loop across the asset lifecycle, transforming operational knowledge into actionable insights that improve future decisions, optimize performance, and drive continuous improvement. Discover how this connected approach creates greater lifecycle visibility, builds operational intelligence, and lays the foundation for more predictive, proactive, and ultimately autonomous operations.

title: Building Insight: Using FARO Reality Capture, Qbitec Visualization, and Autodesk Solutions to Drive Better Decision Making
speakers: Ritesh Chandawar, Lead Product Manager - AECO, FARO Insight, a business of AMETEK Inc. | Irene Radcliffe, Product Manager, AEC Software, FARO Insight
topics: MEP Engineering  | Structural Engineering  | Reality Capture | Construction Operations | Geospatial and GIS | Buildings | Advance Steel | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Forma | ReCap | Revit | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design
abstract: Every project starts with assumptions—but misalignment with reality leads to costly rework. What if decisions were grounded in real-world conditions from day one? This session will present a practical AECO workflow from field to design, showing how reality capture combined with ReCap, Revit, AutoCAD, and Autodesk Forma becomes a true decision engine. Discover how point clouds and 360-degree imagery enable early validation, risk identification, and trusted data integration into design environments. With FARO Sphere XG, Qbitec, and FARO As-Built, learn how to accelerate modeling, improve coordination, and reduce uncertainty—empowering teams to shift from reactive problem-solving to proactive, confident project delivery.

title: Innovators Stage l AutoCAD and Autodesk Forma: A CAD Manager's Playbook for Connected Project Data
speakers: Amarjeet Sonkar, Senior Principal Experience Designer, Autodesk | Damian Willcox, Distinguished Experience Architect, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | AutoCAD LT | Civil 3D | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Autodesk Forma Data Management Essentials is now included with stand-alone AutoCAD subscriptions, connecting desktop design workflows to unified, cloud-based project data without changing how your team works. In this technical deep dive, we’ll show CAD managers how to turn fragmented file management into integrated workflows that reduce friction and accelerate delivery for your teams. We’ll look at Connected Support Files for project-aware support files that load automatically, Connected References that fixes broken xrefs, Connected Sheet Set Manager, Checkout, and much more.

title: Innovators Stage l AutoCAD and Autodesk Forma: A CAD Manager's Playbook for Connected Project Data
speakers: Amarjeet Sonkar, Senior Principal Experience Designer, Autodesk | Damian Willcox, Distinguished Experience Architect, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | AutoCAD LT | Civil 3D | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design
abstract: Autodesk Forma Data Management Essentials is now included with stand-alone AutoCAD subscriptions, connecting desktop design workflows to unified, cloud-based project data without changing how your team works. In this technical deep dive, we’ll show CAD managers how to turn fragmented file management into integrated workflows that reduce friction and accelerate delivery for your teams. We’ll look at Connected Support Files for project-aware support files that load automatically, Connected References that fixes broken xrefs, Connected Sheet Set Manager, Checkout, and much more.

title: MASTERING MEGA PROJECTS: AN INFRASTRUCTURE BLUEPRINT TO PROJECT DELIVERY
speakers: Matt Keogh, Associate Technician, Buro Happold | Tom Ryder, CAD / Software Manager, Buro Happold
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Desktop Connector | Dynamo | Forma | Navisworks Manage | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Mega projects. How well do we understand them? As a Lead Design Consultant, let us try and get to the bottom of it. This session will focus through an Infrastructure lens on how to navigate these large scale, multi-disciplinary projects. Utilising Forma, we have to manage multiple stakeholders and consultancies with thousands of deliverables to constrained timeframes. Learn how we developed tools to decrease deliverable output times by 60%, created workflows to simplify coordination with other teams using Autodesk products and used live collaboration with Autodesk themselves to streamline solutions whilst live on the project. We will give you the blueprint on digital delivery with your own mega project.

title: Right from the Start: Setting Up the Civil 3D Survey Environment
speakers: Tom Richardson, Owner, T2 Consulting Services, LLC
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: A successful Civil 3D survey workflow begins with a properly configured survey environment. This session will focus on configuring Civil 3D to support consistent and predictable movement of data from field crews to survey deliverables. Topics will include establishing the survey working folder, managing equipment databases, creating and maintaining figure prefix databases, configuring linework code sets, organizing description key sets, and structuring point groups. You’ll gain a clear understanding of how these components work together and why each setup decision matters, enabling better control over how field-collected data is interpreted in the office and translated into reliable survey drawings with minimal manual intervention.

title: Help Lead Autodesk Fusion into the Future
speakers: James Mann, Senior Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk | Peter Champneys, Principal Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk | Kyle Williams, Senior Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Design Extension | Fusion Manage | Fusion Signal Integrity Extension | Fusion Simulation Extension | D&M | Meetup
abstract: Join this interactive “Inside the Factory” session where your feedback will directly influence the future of Autodesk Fusion software. Explore emerging capabilities across AI-driven design, connected workflows, and advanced manufacturing—and gain early insight into product direction. Through guided discussions and hands-on exploration, you’ll share challenges, evaluate new features, and help prioritize what matters most. This collaborative session will connect real-world workflows to product development—ensuring Fusion evolves to meet your needs.

title: Schedules That Talk: Connecting Data, Lean Planning, and Project Decisions
speakers: Elizabeth Soto, BIM Manager, Grupo Hermosillo | Pablo Buensuceso, VDC Manager, Grupo Hermosillo
topics: Construction services | Build | Docs | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Most schedules don’t fail because of planning. They fail because they aren’t measured. In this session, you’ll discover how teams transform schedules into data-driven tools that improve coordination and alignment with project milestones. By integrating lean practices—such as weekly look-ahead planning—with plans, teams can automatically generate metrics through the built-in PPC summary, reducing reporting time by up to 40%. Discover how schedules data enables key metrics for supporting faster and more informed decisions. Walk away with practical strategies to connect schedules with plans within Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Join us in empowering project teams and creating better collaborative project delivery workflows.

title: Bridging the Field-to-Office Gap: Centralizing Workflows in Autodesk Forma
speakers: Shree Kabra, Digital Technology Specialist, AECOM - Hunt | Brandon Kisner, Quality Superintendent, Penta Building Group
topics: Construction services | Docs | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Moving from decentralized PDFs and paper to a unified digital ecosystem requires more than just software—it requires a cultural shift. This session explores how the Convention Center project transformed fragmented punch lists and labor tracking into streamlined Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) workflows.

title: Business Intelligence Without Leaving Your Browser: Autodesk Forma Data into Microsoft Fabric
speakers: Nathaniel Coombs, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk | Santhosh Krishna Sekar, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk | Joe Fields, Sr Principal, Business Consultant, AEC Analytics, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Build | Docs | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Long gone are the days of CSV files and IT requests to download software to create your dashboards and reports. Also long gone is the need for a data scientist to help you start taking advantage of YOUR data. During this technical deep dive, we’ll walk you through the fundamentals of bringing your Autodesk Forma data into Power BI via Microsoft Fabric without ever leaving your preferred internet browser. From there we’ll share some tips and tricks to kick-start your dashboarding journey. Your data pipeline to business intelligence has never been more direct, and we hope to teach you just how easy it is to start building your own reports in the cloud. From blank canvas to a dashboard in under 60 minutes - let us shepherd you into the new era of data and reporting.

title: BIM Rebar Revolution: Information Management Standard for Rebar and Its Impact on Chilean Industry
speakers: Manuel Saavedra, CEO, AEC Shift | Ivana Kermen, Principal Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Alejandro Marinelli, Principal Account Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Construction services | Forge | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Is it possible to eliminate uncertainty between structural design and the fabrication plant? This session will reveal the milestone of creating the first BIM information management standard for reinforced concrete, a strategic development transforming productivity in Chile. We’ll analyze how the ecosystem—integrated by the new national standard, AEC Rebar, the ICDM web platform, and Nexo BIM Power Data—achieves a robust and auditable data flow. Through real-world success cases, we’ll demonstrate how automation from Revit to industrial fabrication eliminates critical interpretation errors, optimizes the procurement cycle, and finally connects all stakeholders in a high-efficiency digital environment.

title: From Scans to Decisions: Turning Reality Capture into Actionable Digital Twins with AI
speakers: Prashanth Dommeti, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | Shubhamkar Bapat, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Build | Forma | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Are your scans just visuals or are they driving real project decisions? Reality capture is widely used, but most workflows stop at geometry, leaving critical insights untapped. This session will demonstrate how to transform scan data into actionable digital twins by integrating Revit, Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), and asset data workflows. Learn how AI can detect deviations, connect model elements to structured data, and surface insights that influence coordination, cost, and project outcomes. If your scans aren’t informing decisions, you’re missing their true value. This session will show how to unlock the potential of scanned data and workflow.

title: From Silos to Shared Insight: How Construction Teams Deliver Better Outcomes
speakers: Saadet Yilmaz, VP of Development, Reef Capital Partners | Christy Steffen, Assistant Director of Gaylor University, Gaylor Electric | Tawnya Reitz, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk | Heather Soderquist, VP, Construction Innovation, Jacobsen Construction | Jacob Pfenning-Wendt, Solutions Manager, UPS
topics: Project Financials | Data and Document Management | Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract:
Projects aren’t delayed by effort—they’re slowed by disconnects. When teams work in separate systems, visibility drops, costs drift, and decisions lag.

 

Join leaders from Reef Capital Partners, Jacobsen Construction, Gaylor Electric, and UPS to learn how they’re using Autodesk Forma to bridge these gaps. Discover how owners, general contractors, and specialty contractors are leveraging Forma—including new Bridge functionality—to connect workflows, improve cross-organizational collaboration, and enable more data-driven cost management.

 

Walk away with practical ways to improve coordination and drive better project outcomes.

title: Turning Data into a Strategic Advantage in AEC
speakers: GB Cazes, President, Data Solutions, ATG USA | Kent Watson, VP Technology, ATG USA
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Design Collaboration | Forma | Forma Data Management | AECO | Architecture
abstract: The architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry is at a turning point. Firms have invested heavily in digital tools, yet most aren’t unlocking the full value of their data. Information remains fragmented across systems and phases, limiting visibility, slowing decisions, and constraining innovation. This session will explore a core idea: Data is becoming AEC’s most strategic asset, if it’s structured, connected, and activated. We’ll outline how leading firms are shifting to a data-first strategy, leveraging Autodesk Forma as a unifying foundation. You’ll leave with a practical framework to standardize, connect, and activate data—turning fragmentation into a measurable competitive advantage.

title: Does Your Workstation GPU Still Make the Cut? How Local AI Is Raising the Bar for Autodesk Workflows.
speakers: Ken Denton, Global Segment Lead AEC / PD&M, HP | Michael Katz, Sr Manager Software Development, AMD
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Construction services | 3ds Max 2 | AutoCAD | Fusion | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO
abstract:
The workstation GPU that handles your Revit models and 3ds Max renders may be showing its age — not because Autodesk got more demanding, but because AI did.

Local AI tools are rapidly becoming part of how design and engineering professionals work: generating concepts, automating repetitive tasks, and running inference without sending sensitive project data to the cloud. These workloads are GPU-hungry, and they compete directly with your Autodesk applications for the same critical resource: graphics memory.

In this session, we'll give Autodesk users a practical framework for understanding GPU memory requirements across the workflows that matter to them. You'll see how real Autodesk applications perform under varying VRAM configurations, what happens when local AI enters the picture, and where the common pain points emerge. We'll also look at what the next generation of workstation GPUs brings to the table — and whether an upgrade is warranted or premature.

title: From Image to Groom: AI Workflows for Production-Ready Character Hair
speakers: Hilmar Koch, Director, M&E Research, Autodesk | Derek Cheung, Principal Machine Learning Engineer, Autodesk
topics: Film and TV | Maya | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract: As media and entertainment pipelines accelerate, digital hair creation still requires hours of work, with artists meticulously crafting guide curves and tuning modifiers to match reference. This session will demonstrate a research prototype of an AI-powered tool for Maya software that converts one or more images into fully editable grooms. We’ll show how this approach reduces grooming time by up to five times through automation of repetitive work, and how it integrates with simulation and downstream departments. We’ll also detail our wholly owned, synthetic data strategy for training AI models designed for transparency and control. See this workflow in action and understand how image-to-groom can accelerate your character production workflows.

title: Nightmares in Motion: Animating the Creatures of IT in Welcome to Derry
speakers: Scott Holmes, Animation Supervisor, Rodeo FX
topics: Film and TV | Maya | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract: Few characters in modern horror are as unpredictable as Pennywise, whose terrifying transformations lie at the heart of IT: Welcome to Derry. In this session, Rodeo FX Animation Supervisor Scott Holmes will reveal how the team used Maya software to design rigs and craft performances for Pennywise’s many monstrous forms. Through production examples and animation breakdowns, the talk will explore the creative process behind building creatures that can shift from subtle unease to full nightmare, while remaining believable, expressive, and terrifying on screen.

title: Community Meetup: Media and Entertainment - Creators & Artists
speakers: Joaquim Moral, Senior Community Manager, Autodesk | Didier Raphael Ramirez Darjo, Autodesk Expert Elite, Independent consultant | Felipe Fierro, Film Director - Autodesk Expert Elite, Pigmalion Animation Studio
topics: Film and TV | 3ds Max 2 | Arnold | Flow Studio | Golaem | Maya | M&E | Meetup
abstract: The media and entertainment industry is evolving rapidly, driven by advances in AI, emerging technologies, shifting audience expectations, and new creative possibilities. Join us for a meetup where industry professionals come together to explore how creators, studios, and production teams are adapting, innovating, and thriving in this dynamic landscape. Designed for artists, creators, producers, technologists, and other media and entertainment professionals, this event is a chance to network, exchange ideas, and discover trends shaping the future of content creation, storytelling, and production.

title: Animation in Maya with AI: Creating a Game Cinematic with MotionMaker
speakers: Marcio Goncalves, Assistant Professor of Game Art and Design, State University of New York - Empire State
topics: Games | Maya | Maya Creative | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract: MotionMaker is an exciting new feature released with Maya 2026 software. It uses the power of AI to help 3D artists animate characters and creatures quickly and efficiently. This is AI at its best—not trying to replace the 3D artists but helping them. This class will introduce you to MotionMaker and teach you how to use it to create an exciting game cinematic. First, you’ll learn what MotionMaker is and how it compares to other tools. Then, you’ll learn the basic elements and components of the MotionMaker interface. Finally, we’ll use MotionMaker to create an exciting game cinematic, taking advantage of the three proxy characters available (biped, canine, and horse)—and then we’ll export the game cinematic to a game engine.

title: Digital Factory Summit | Autodesk Forma: The Common Data Environment for Gigafactory Development
speakers: Mark Rickabaugh, Lead, VDC & Reality Capture, Tesla | Genavera Gannon, Staff Engineering Program Manager, Tesla
topics: Data and Document Management | Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | Forma | Model Coordination | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: In this session, we’ll go over how to use Autodesk Forma projects for managing the design of gigafactories and comparable megaprojects. Learn how Tesla brings together inputs from manufacturing teams, design groups, and construction management into one common repository to streamline project delivery. Explore how cloud-workshared Revit projects organize inputs from AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and other industry CAD tools to bring manufacturing context into your Revit files, and send factory context to your manufacturing teams or vendors. Finally, see how tools within Forma allow for coordination, clash resolution, and field documentation to support successful project execution.

title: Designing the Digital Factory for Process Plants: Bridging AEC and Manufacturing Workflows
speakers: Peter De Strijker, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Bas Claassen, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Process manufacturing | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Fusion Manage | Inventor Factory | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: Process plant projects require tight alignment between plant design and manufacturing. Yet, these areas are often disconnected, causing rework, delays, and fabrication errors. This session will show how design decisions impact manufacturing using a water treatment plant example. We’ll demonstrate how Autodesk’s Architecture, Engineering & Construction Collection and Product Design & Manufacturing Collection create a connected, design-led workflow from layout to fabrication. The session will also highlight common breakdowns in design-to-manufacturing workflows and how Autodesk Platform Services and structured data improve collaboration. This session is relevant for water treatment, energy, and industrial facilities industries.

title: Autodesk VRED: Latest Real-Time Visualization Trends combined with AI Transforming Automotive Design
speakers: Pascal Seifert, Sr. Technical Product Manager, Autodesk | Victor Perez, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Automotive and other transportation | Alias AutoStudio | Arnold | Fusion | VRED | VRED Professional | AUTO | D&M | XR | Cross Industry
abstract: Autodesk VRED is known for rapidly adopting state of the art rendering technologies, open standards, and AI workflow tools. This Autodesk University session explores new key capabilities including Vulkan Ray Tracing, Gaussian Splat rendering, CloudXR streaming to Apple Vision Pro, and the use of constraints and physics. Learn how these technologies work together to deliver highly realistic visuals and physically plausible behavior for complex digital twins with minimal setup time. Discover how designers, engineers, and visual artists can accelerate projects, improve collaboration, and reduce costly errors early in the digital model. Ideal for visualization, XR, and automotive workflows focused on performance, realism, and scalability.

title: Where Innovation in Standards Takes Flight: How Massport Advances BIM, GIS, and EAM Integration
speakers: Jason Del Signore, VDC Manager, Massport
topics: Automotive and other transportation | AutoCAD Map 3D | Build | Forma | ReCap | Revit | AUTO | D&M | Infrastructure Owners | AECO
abstract: The Massachusetts Port Authority (Massport) will share key lessons learned from its journey toward using BIM, geographic information system (GIS), and asset management for better project delivery and capital planning. Large project and asset owners will learn how Massport turns project, spatial, and asset data into actionable insights for better decision making. This session will highlight how Massport manages more than 200 capital projects across five airport/seaport campuses using BIM-enabled workflows. You’ll learn how Autodesk Forma is used as a common data environment to collaborate with design and construction teams, enable on-time digital delivery, and create a virtual campus as a single source of truth—supporting Massport’s broader digital transformation goals.

title: ReCap Pro Mesh to Revit Lab: Get Hands-On Structured Mesh and IFC Workflow for Faster Intelligent Modeling
speakers: Idoia Martinez, Sr Technical Account Manager, Autodesk | Carlos Aquise, Sr Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Reality Capture | Construction services | Model Coordination | Navisworks Manage | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Turning point clouds into reliable BIM inputs is still a challenge for many architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) teams. In this lab, you’ll execute a complete, field-tested ReCap Pro workflow that transforms scan data into structured, interoperable mesh models ready for enhanced design and collaboration. Guided by subject matter experts, you’ll apply automatic classification to generate clean meshes, standardize outputs using Template Manager, map Revit categories, and export IFC models for downstream BIM use. You’ll then use these outputs as modeling references in Revit and validate them through coordination workflows in Navisworks and Model Coordination. Walk away with a repeatable, end-to-end scan-to-BIM process that reduces manual remodeling and accelerates coordination across project teams.

title: Building a CIP Concrete Dashboard with Autodesk Data Exchange and Autodesk Power BI Connector
speakers: Ihsan Gin, Regional BIM/VDC Manager, Baker Construction - Eastern US Commercial
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Autodesk Viewer | BIM Collaborate Pro | Docs | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: In this hands-on lab, you’ll learn how to build an on-demand model-driven data dashboard for your project teams using the Autodesk Data Exchange API and Autodesk Power BI Connector. Model-driven data dashboards will give your project teams on-demand access to model-based information and will help them forecast their jobsite needs. By building model-driven, filterable dashboards, you empower your team members by placing at their fingertips the data they require daily to run a lean and efficient jobsite.

title: You Don't Know the Power of the API: Extending Inventor iLogic with API
speakers: Chelsea Kastanek, Sr. Technology Consultant - Automation, Symetri
topics: Manufacturing Other | Inventor | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: You’ve taken your first steps into automation with iLogic. Now it’s time to expand your toolset and make The Force even stronger. This hands‑on classroom session will help you transport into the wider galaxy of API‑powered automation. Instead of diving deep into theory, we’ll focus on how to access the Inventor API, understand what’s possible, and confidently begin using it alongside iLogic. Using a guided example, you’ll learn to connect iLogic to the API, locate key objects, and extend automation across parts, assemblies, and drawings. While it might look like The Dark Side at first, this class will break it into simple concepts and practical examples. By the end, you’ll leave with the confidence and foundation to continue your automation voyage.

title: Building the AI Ecosystem for Better Engineering in AEC
topics: Construction services | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Ben Cochran, Vice President of Engineering at Autodesk, and Peter Madlener, CEO of VIKTOR, join the Digital Builder podcast to discuss how AI is moving beyond experimentation and into real engineering workflows. The episode explores AI agents, connected ecosystems, domain expertise, trust, automation, and how organizations are beginning to transform practical business processes using emerging AI capabilities.

title: From Chat to Commands to Agents: The Evolution of AI Automation in Revit for AEC Teams
speakers: Ali Najmi, Director, BIMLOGIQ
topics: MEP Engineering  | Structural Engineering  | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Architecture services | Autodesk Developer Network | Revit | AECO
abstract: AI in AEC is moving fast, but most teams are still stuck at the chat window. This session maps the three stages of AI maturity in BIM workflows: conversational chat, saved commands, and agents. Using real deployments inside Autodesk Revit, we'll show how firms turn one-off AI prompts into reusable commands their whole team can run (think add-ins created in minutes, not months), and how agent-based systems go further: planning multi-step work, using tools, and even creating new tools when a workflow demands it. Drawing on lessons from enterprise teams automating modelling, documentation, and QA/QC, we'll cover what worked, what failed, and how to judge where your organization sits on the chat-to-agent curve. You'll leave with a practical framework for scaling AI beyond individual experiments to team-wide automation and how agents can provide adoptive solutions to workflows.

title: There Is Now a Level Zero: Getting Started with Autodesk Platform Services to Access Your Autodesk Forma Data
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E
topics: Architecture services | Autodesk Platform Services | Docs | Dynamo | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Autodesk Platform Services documentation, website, and sample files all assume the user is an experienced web developer. Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) professionals who want to take advantage of using Autodesk Platform Services to access their Autodesk Forma data are not web developers, and they need to understand how to start from level zero. This class will introduce a level zero approach for connecting Autodesk Platform Services to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll walk through creating an Autodesk Platform Services application, obtaining authentication, and connecting to Autodesk Forma. Once connected, we’ll retrieve basic project information, and we’ll review the structure of the Autodesk Forma data.

title: Multi-AI-Agent BIM Orchestration: Building Autonomous Query. Check. Fix Loops for Revit.
speakers: Phuc Le, Account Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: What if your Revit model could check itself—and fix what it finds—autonomously? This session will introduce a multi-agent system where specialized AI agents collaborate in a loop: a Query agent will read model data via Model Context Protocol (MCP), a QC agent will check it against configurable standards, and a Design agent will propose corrections - each previewed, human-approved, and audited before any write. The cycle will repeat until the model passes. We’ll demo three live scenarios: Naming Convention Fix, Parameter Completeness, and Geometry Checking - built with Revit MCP Server, Forma MCP, Python, LangGraph, and configurable YAML rules. We'll also cover transaction management, convergence control, and the points where human oversight remains essential.

title: Building Resilient Communities: A Collaborative Revit 2027 Sample Model
speakers: Paul Aubin, Author/Consultant, Paul F Aubin Consulting Services, Inc. | Harlan Brumm, Director, Product Management, Revit Core Capabilities & Collaboration Services, Autodesk | Rachel Martinelli, Co-Founder / Board Member, Foothill Catalog Foundation
topics: Architecture services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Docs | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Following the 2025 Los Angeles fires, The Foothill Catalog Foundation and Autodesk partnered to accelerate rebuilding through a collection of preapproved residential designs. This session will go behind the scenes of creating the new Revit 2027 residential sample model that is part of this catalog. We’ll explore the unique collaboration between a nonprofit and Autodesk to develop the design with interchangeable options. Discover the challenges of balancing municipal standards with modeling best practices, and see the "split" where the model evolved into both a product asset and a real-world home. Join representatives from The Foothill Catalog Foundation and Autodesk to learn how Revit can transform residential workflows and empower communities. Build better, together.

title: AI-Ready BIM Foundation: Push-Button Cross-Discipline Automation with Revit MCP, Dynamo, and pyRevit
speakers: Mayank Sharma, Director, Virtual Design and Construction, Mazzetti | Julide Bozoglu, Director of Technology, Goettsch Partners
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: The first days of a building project are consumed by repetitive start-up tasks across architecture and MEP teams—validating models, aligning levels and grids, creating spaces, and generating documentation. This session will show how teams can reduce start-up from 40 staff hours to under 60 minutes using Revit MCP, Dynamo, and pyRevit software. Revit MCP validates levels, grids, rooms, and naming conventions through natural-language queries. Dynamo then synchronizes linked architectural data into MEP models, while pyRevit batch tools automate spaces, views, sheets, and standards-compliant documentation. You’ll leave with a scalable cross-disciplinary framework that improves coordination quality and builds an AI-ready BIM foundation.

title: Sustainability and AI in Practice: Driving Better Outcomes with Connected Data, Workflows and Tools
speakers: Emily Edelstone, Impact Growth Enablement Manager, Content & Tools, Autodesk | John Locke, Sr Mgr, Research Science, Autodesk | Kat Mitchell, Senior Impact Growth & Engagement Manager, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | None | AECO | Meetup
abstract: Join professionals across industries for an engaging meetup exploring how sustainability is showing up in practice today and in the future. As design, make, and operate industries face growing pressure for more traceable, verifiable outcomes, teams are exploring new approaches. Connected data, workflows, and tools like agentic AI are playing a bigger role in decision making. This is an open conversation and networking opportunity to share and learn from peers. Discuss what’s working, challenging, and where opportunities lie across areas like carbon analysis, sustainable design, net zero, biodiversity, and water stewardship. By exchanging ideas and building relationships, we’ll explore how to tackle today’s challenges and scale impact.

title: The CDE Is Not Only Storage—It’s Decision Control
speakers: Gustavo Ubriaco Contreras, BIM Manager, The Palace Company | Didier Raphael Ramirez Darjo, Autodesk Expert Elite, Independent consultant
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Build | Docs | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: This session will demonstrate how to implement a common data environment (CDE) from scratch for teams using Autodesk Forma Data Management. Drawing on real-world experience with constantly changing projects, the session will address challenges such as version-control issues, rework, permission control, uncoordinated deliveries, and time wasted between disciplines. Participants will learn how to structure folders, define review workflows, assign responsibilities for each stage, and control the flow of information to reduce errors and accelerate decision making. We’ll also cover how to create a learning notebook to help avoid repeating the same mistakes in the future.

title: Autodesk Forma to Energy: AI-Powered Workflows for Carbon Insight
speakers: Chris Balbach, Director of R&D, Performance Systems Development of NY, LLC | Tetsuya Hishida, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk | Daniel Stine, Director of Design Technology, Lake Flato
topics: Architecture services | Forma | Insight | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Energy and carbon analysis often arrives too late—after key decisions have been made. Despite tools like Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Insight software, most teams rely on manual, disconnected workflows that limit iteration. This session will introduce a connected, data-driven approach. By embedding performance data in BIM and using AI to generate simulation logic, teams can automatically produce carbon and energy analyses—earlier, more frequently, and without deep simulation expertise. Through a live demo, you’ll see design data flow from Autodesk Forma through Revit into automated workflows and into Insight for actionable results. Attend this class to learn how to replace one-off analysis with scalable, repeatable carbon workflows.

title: AEC Roadmap: Architecture
speakers: Lauren Poon, Senior Product Line Manager, Architecture, Autodesk | Matt Arsenault, Principal Product Manager - Forma Connected Clients, Autodesk | Daniel Gameiro, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Andrea Vallés, Senior Architecture Industry Strategy Manager, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | Docs | Forma | ReCap | Revit | AECO
abstract: Designing for impact means designing with agility, insight, and collaboration. In this session, Autodesk product and strategy leaders will share what’s new, and what’s coming next, for architects across Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Autodesk’s cloud collaboration tools. Learn how we’re advancing workflows from planning and schematic design to performance analysis, documentation, and multidisciplinary coordination. See how deeper connections between desktop tools and the Forma industry cloud, through the Forma Connected Client initiative, can help teams move data, context, and insights across solutions, reducing rework, supporting sustainability, and unlocking creativity.

title: AEC Roadmap: Architecture
speakers: Matt Arsenault, Principal Product Manager - Forma Connected Clients, Autodesk | Lauren Poon, Senior Product Line Manager, Architecture, Autodesk | Daniel Gameiro, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Andrea Vallés, Senior Architecture Industry Strategy Manager, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | AECO
abstract: Designing for impact means designing with agility, insight, and collaboration. In this session, Autodesk product and strategy leaders will share what’s new, and what’s coming next, for architects across Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Autodesk’s cloud collaboration tools. Learn how we’re advancing workflows from planning and schematic design to performance analysis, documentation, and multidisciplinary coordination. See how deeper connections between desktop tools and the Forma industry cloud, through the Forma Connected Client initiative, can help teams move data, context, and insights across solutions, reducing rework, supporting sustainability, and unlocking creativity.

title: An Owner’s Digital Blueprint for Airports: Mandated BIM, GIS‑Led Master Planning, and Digital Twins
speakers: Rahul Khanna, Head of Design & Master Planning, Adani Airport Holdings Limited | Malishka Gupta, BIM Manager, ADANI GROUPS
topics: Architecture services | Build | Docs for Government | Dynamo | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) is building a unified digital ecosystem by mandating BIM across all projects and adopting geographic information system (GIS) as the foundation for master planning. Progress toward digital twins is independently certified through global, standards‑driven bodies such as the BSI Kitemark. AAHL is proud to have the world’s first and second airports certified to BSI Kitemark Stage 2 for Design and Construction, and to be the first organization globally with all seven airports achieving Stage 3. This session will demonstrate how scan‑to‑BIM and full airside scan‑to‑GIS establish accurate digital baselines to govern and protect the aerodrome, improving design coordination, safety compliance, and operational and long‑term expansion through BIM‑GIS integration.

title: An Owner’s Digital Blueprint for Airports: Mandated BIM, GIS‑Led Master Planning, and Digital Twins
speakers: Rahul Khanna, Head of Design & Master Planning, Adani Airport Holdings Limited | Malishka Gupta, BIM Manager, ADANI GROUPS
topics: Architecture services | Build | Docs for Government | Dynamo | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) is building a unified digital ecosystem by mandating BIM across all projects and adopting geographic information system (GIS) as the foundation for master planning. Progress toward digital twins is independently certified through global, standards‑driven bodies such as the BSI Kitemark. AAHL is proud to have the world’s first and second airports certified to BSI Kitemark Stage 2 for Design and Construction, and to be the first organization globally with all seven airports achieving Stage 3. This session will demonstrate how scan‑to‑BIM and full airside scan‑to‑GIS establish accurate digital baselines to govern and protect the aerodrome, improving design coordination, safety compliance, and operational and long‑term expansion through BIM‑GIS integration.

title: The Fun Hardware Talk
speakers: Jamie Gwilliam, WW User & Industries Lead, Workstations, Intel
topics: Trust | Architecture services | 3ds Max Design | AutoCAD | Fusion | Inventor | Revit | AECO
abstract: Don’t attend this session if you’re looking for yet another boring hardware session. This won’t be that. Join Lenovo with Intel’s global workstation user and segment lead for an engaging, (almost) vendor-agnostic look at how Autodesk workstations are evolving—and what it means for your projects and future investments. Is an AI PC good enough for Autodesk software? Are more CPU cores always better? Which upgrades deliver real value—and which just add cost? We'll cut through the hype to explore how Autodesk workflows use CPUs and GPUs, and we’ll examine how the NPU is used by other software, as well as for AI technologies. Learn how modern SoC architectures are reshaping visualization, simulation, rendering, and AI-enabled workflows. You'll also discover workstation buying trends, future technology directions, cost-saving opportunities, and critical security considerations often overlooked by professionals. Whether you're evaluating AI PCs, planning your next workstation refresh, or future-proofing your Autodesk environment, you'll leave with practical insights and a clear understanding of what matters most in the next generation of workstations.

title: Visual Context Intelligence: Empowering AI to Work Better in the Design Journey
speakers: David Weir-McCall, Head of Product, Lumion
topics: Construction Operations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Architecture services | Revit | AECO
abstract:
While AI has shown popularity and power in ideation and early concept, it still has issues with consistency and iteration. Design is a journey. It is collaborative and, most importantly, design accuracy absolutely matters.

In this session you will hear from Lumion's Head of Product on how Lumion is building a new process called Visual Context Intelligence into its AI tools in order to strengthen and refine AI in later stage visualisation. 

You’ll also hear Lumion’s thoughts on where and when AI should be used. You will go behind the curtain on Visual Context Intelligence, see it working in the latest AI tools, and hear what industry testing has shown so far about consistency and accuracy across iterations.

title: Designing for Agriculture at Scale: Autodesk Tools for Crop Productivity and Processing
speakers: Ayush Sharma, Co-Founder & COO, Kheyti | Vaibhav Tidke, CEO and co-founder, S4S Technologies
topics: CFD | Fusion | Inventor | Revit | Robot Structural Analysis | Design & Engineering | D&M
abstract: Smallholder farmers face climate volatility, energy constraints, and post-harvest loss. Yet many products are not designed for their realities. This session will show how Kheyti and S4S Technologies apply Autodesk tools—including Revit, Robot Structural Analysis, Autodesk Fusion, and Inventor with Autodesk CFD—to design greenhouse systems, agrivoltaics, and food processing technologies that improve yield and income reliability, reduce energy and material use, and minimize crop loss. You’ll gain practical approaches for embedding human-centered design into engineering workflows, building internal technical capability through pro bono and E4C support, and applying Autodesk-enabled methods to drive resilience, sustainability, and equitable impact at scale.

title: Revit Structural Connections for Design Engineers
speakers: Desiree Mackey, CFE, BD Mackey Consulting | Brian Mackey, Head Geek, BD Mackey Consulting
topics: Engineering service providers | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: The Revit Structural Connections tool brings steel connections into the design environment, and using it as a structural design consultant might require borrowing strategies from detailing and fabrication workflows. This session will share lessons learned from developing connections for the Revit 2027 Snowden Towers Sample Project, focusing on how engineers can effectively use the tool in a design workflow. Through practical examples, we’ll explore approaches to connection modeling, as well as key considerations and ways to get useful results without overcomplicating the process. The goal is to help structural engineers understand where the tool fits, how to use it efficiently, and how to make it work within their projects.

title: Revit MEP Fundamentals and New Tricks
speakers: Matthew Collier, Technical Product Manager, IMEG Corp. | Sean Fruin, Mechanical Applications Product Owner, IMEG
topics: MEP Engineering  | Engineering service providers | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Many teams still rely on outdated Revit MEP habits that slow coordination and create inconsistent models. This session will cover how to build a strong foundation in spaces, connectors, systems, circuits, and documentation. Then we’ll show how recent Revit improvements support better analysis, clearer panel and circuit workflows, improved analytical visibility for duct and pipe systems, and a smoother path from design to fabrication. We’ll share practical methods that help newer users build confidence and experienced users work faster, model more accurately, and reduce rework.

title: Top Firms Share How to Build Knowledge Infrastructure to Scale AI-Powered Digital Adoption
speakers: Holly Brattberg, Founder & Chief Strategy Officer, Global eTraining | Susan Brattberg, Founder & Chief Customer Officer, Global eTraining
topics: MEP Engineering  | Structural Engineering  | Construction Operations | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Geospatial and GIS | Engineering service providers | AutoCAD | AutoCAD MEP | Civil 3D | InfraWorks | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Hear from a panel of top firms including Jacobs, Tetra Tech, IDOM and HDR as they share best practices on building the human intelligence and knowledge infrastructure layer across the AI-enabled tech stack. Learn how to elevate human plus agentic AI workflows to close digital skills gaps to realize the ROI of improved performance, reduced rework and risk and a competitive edge to win more bids. Imagine the AI-powered digital adoption platform where information from trusted sources is instantly converted into consumable and actionable knowledge, personalized for every learner and delivered in the flow of work through mainstream applications connecting the field and office. GeT tangible data on knowledge gaps and skills matrices through organized learning content and skills challenges aligned with company workflows and project standards. Drive tech adoption at scale with AI-powered "just enough, just in time, and just for me" verified knowledge—because the best training is training your way. GeT IT Your Way.

title: Unified Production Environment: How AI and Data Transformed Ramboll’s Engineering
speakers: David Thomson, Principle Product Owner Digital Design, Ramboll | Marc Sleegers, Sr Principal, Business Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Buildings | Civil 3D | Forma | Model Coordination | Revit | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: Ramboll is reinventing itself as a data-centered, AI‑powered engineering firm. Through its Together for Better Outcomes (T4BO) partnership with Autodesk, Ramboll has productized a unified production environment (UPE) to accelerate AI adoption. By embedding the Autodesk AI tool Autodesk Assistant into daily workflows, productivity increases while more-sustainable client value is delivered. This session will show how data-centered design and AI‑assisted engineering are transforming project delivery and ways of working, reinforcing Ramboll’s role as a partner for sustainable change. We’ll share tangible outcomes, such as higher delivery quality, deeper sustainability insights, and increased project capacity without adding headcount.

title: Inside Autodesk Certification: Strategies from the Exam Authors
speakers: ARGELIA Barcena, Head of Regional Leads - North America, Women in BIM | Rina Sahay, BIM Lead, Wade Trim | Eric Wing, BIM Director, C&S Companies
topics: Buildings | BIM Collaborate | Docs | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Unlock the secrets behind Autodesk Certification. These exams are designed to validate real-world workflow skills required across the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Yet many candidates struggle to understand what’s truly being evaluated or how to prepare. Join exam authors for a behind-the-scenes look at how exams are designed to reflect industry practice and skills being tested. Learn from contributors to Certified Professional Exams in BIM Management and Revit Architectural, Structural, and Electrical Design. They will present certification-style examples inspired by real exam objectives and explore interpretation strategies. You’ll leave with a clearer understanding of how certification aligns with project workflows and how to improve skills needed to succeed.

title: Digital Factory Summit | Digital Twins Unplugged: Platforms, Practices, and Lessons from the Field
speakers: Farzad Moghbel, VP of Technology Products, Michael Baker International | Marin Pastar, VP, Digital Practice Executive, Michael Baker International | Marc Banning, Senior Business Development Executive, Autodesk | Andrew Davis, Regional Technology Lead - Canada, Jacobs | Jacob Noltner, Section Leader, Mechanical Engineer, Jacobs
topics: Buildings | FlexSim | ReCap | Revit | Tandem Connect | AECO | Digital Factory | D&M
abstract: Digital twins are moving from concept to reality, but success looks different for every organization. This session will bring owners, operators, technologists, and consultants together to discuss moving from digital models to operational twins. Panelists will highlight different types of digital twins, from simulation-based twins like FlexSim to operational and asset-based twins like Autodesk Tandem, enabling connected asset data and certainty from design through operations. The discussion will compare platform ecosystems, use cases, and scaling strategies across the asset lifecycle. You can expect examples, lessons learned, and open dialogue on what works and what doesn’t, while connecting with peers shaping the future of digital twins.

title: Digital Twins in Practice: A Blueprint for Moving from Design to Operations
speakers: Mohamed Abdelhameid, Digital Sales Director, Johnson Controls | Troy Gates, Senior Solutions Consultant, ARKANCE | Nick Miller, Pre-Sales Director, ARKANCE
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: Digital twins promise to connect design and operations, but what does it take to make this real? In this session, Johnson Controls and ARKANCE will share how they helped a customer transition from disconnected intelligent models to a scalable digital twin through aligned roles, workflows, and cross‑industry collaboration. Learn how to prepare BIM data for operations by structuring Revit deliverables for Autodesk Tandem software and downstream workflows, including auditing, cleanup, and standardization. We’ll also cover integrating Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, mapping physical assets, and building a practical sensor strategy. Finally, we’ll explore long‑term success factors, including governance, ownership, maintenance, and stakeholder adoption to ensure your digital twin delivers lasting value.

title: From Reality to Simulation: Capturing, Predicting, and Replaying the Experience of Design with APS and AI
speakers: Kean Walmsley, Dir., Systems Design/Architecture Engrg, Autodesk | Andrés Sebastián Diaz Vargas, Systems Engineer I  COP, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | AECO | Software Development | Cross Industry
abstract: How do you capture or predict the human experience of design and replay it to build empathy and drive better design decisions? This session will present a technical workflow spanning three research projects: real-world experience capture (The Bentway, Toronto), XR-based capture in virtual environments, and agentic simulation of human behavior. Learn how Autodesk Platform Services powers a system where human-experience data—whether captured using sensors, or in VR, or predicted using AI—can be replayed by designers to better appreciate the diversity of the human experience of design. We’ll explore the technology that will power future human-experience-driven workflows, from sensors and VR headsets to knowledge graphs and vision language models.

title: No More “BIM Guy”: Driving Real Digital Transformation Across Construction
speakers: Danielle Dy Buncio, CEO, VIATechnik | Ravi Wood, BIM Director, Samsung Semiconductors | Prateek Shailesh Chitnis, BIM Manager, Dennis Group | Morgan Drivas, VDC Manager, JTM Construction | Brett Settles, VDC Director, Alberici Constructors, Inc
topics: Buildings | None | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: "That's the BIM guy's job." Whether you've heard it on a job site, in a coordination meeting, or in a boardroom, you know the gap this panel is here to close. An owner, a heavy industrial GC, a self-perform contractor, and a specialty MEP contractor join moderator Prateek Chitnis for an unfiltered conversation about what digital transformation actually costs across the construction ecosystem. No polished success stories. No vendor pitches. Just four practitioners from different seats at the table, each with a different definition of what "BIM adoption" means, and each with failures they haven't talked about publicly. Yet.

title: BIM to EAMS: Building the Bridge Between Digital Delivery and Asset Lifecycle Management
speakers: Matt Anderle, AVP, Director of Digital Strategy, AECOM | Chris France, Digital Operations Manager, AECOM
topics: Buildings | Civil 3D | Forma | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: The most powerful moment in digital delivery isn't when the model is complete. It's when an owner traces a work order back to a verified asset record and makes a better decision because the data was there. This session will show how to make that moment possible. Drawing on large-scale aviation and transportation infrastructure experience, you’ll learn to structure BIM/CIIM deliverables that deliver value beyond handover. Asset data schemas, COBie deliverables, and Revit models connected through Autodesk Forma become the foundation for an operational ecosystem where owners and delivery teams share a single source of truth, driving smarter operations and measurable facility performance for the life of the asset.

title: An Owner's Playbook for a Common Data Environment
speakers: Jon Dalton, Sr. BIM Manager, NV5
topics: MEP Engineering  | Structural Engineering  | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Buildings | ACC Connect | Forma Build | Forma Construction Connect | Forma Data Management | Tandem | AECO
abstract: Most common data environments (CDEs) are set up for the delivery team. They solve coordination during design and construction, then get handed to the owner who lives in them for decades. The folder structures and workflows that suited the project rarely fit how a facilities team works. This session will be a practical guide for owners. We'll cover what to specify before a project starts, the contract language that protects your access to the data, where standard handovers break down, and how to organize information so it stays useful over the life of the asset. You'll leave with a checklist you can apply to your next project, whether you're standing up a CDE for the first time or trying to fix one you inherited.

title: Tangled Up in Blue: Untangling a ProjectWise Migration to Autodesk Forma
speakers: Andy Bosch, Designer, Kimley Horn | Sean Hulbert, Sr Principal, Professional Services Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Cloud Worksharing | Desktop Connector | Docs | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: When the project teams saw files taking up to 45 minutes to open and AutoCAD crashes becoming routine, they knew their platform was failing them and driving project costs higher. Adding to the pressure, the project was advancing from 60% to 90% plan submittals, a stage when most avoid major platform changes. Migrating off ProjectWise meant transitioning roughly 14,000 files and enabling more than 300 users and 10 subconsultants—while keeping design moving forward. This session will show how the Blue Line Light Rail project, a 13-mile corridor, was transitioned to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Learn how a strong proof of concept, Civil 3D workflows, Autodesk-developed tools (including the bulk migration tool), and external Civil 3D tools helped identify and resolve issues during a midproduction migration.

speakers: Andy Bosch, Designer, Kimley Horn | Sean Hulbert, Sr Principal, Professional Services Consultant, Autodesk

title: Integrating Nature-Based Solutions in Civil 3D and InfraWorks for Resilient Infrastructure Design
speakers: Carlos Rogeliz, Technical Director – N4W Facility, The Nature Conservancy | Jonathan Nogales, Science Associate, The Nature Conservancy
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfraWorks | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) are reshaping how civil teams deliver resilient water infrastructure. Yet integrating watershed-scale insights into detailed design remains a challenge. This session will show how The Nature Conservancy applied targeted training and InfraWorks and Civil 3D software to connect regional watershed analysis with site-level engineering workflows. Learn how to translate watershed data into design inputs, develop NbS concepts into constructible models, and maintain data continuity across planning and design phases. See how connected workflows improved cross-team collaboration, enabled earlier decision making, and reduced project risk in real-world water infrastructure projects.

title: BIM Meets Real World: Geospatial Data Integration Best Practices
speakers: Erika Bocian, Principal Consultant, ESRI | Shiori Sasaki, Senior Consultant, Esri
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Geospatial and GIS | Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Forma | Revit | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: To plan, design, build, and manage projects suited to a more sustainable and resilient future, owners and design teams need spatial context of the built and natural environment in their workflows. The Esri-Autodesk partnership delivers out-of-the-box tools and capabilities that bridge BIM and geographic context, putting location at the center of informed decision making. This session will explore the range of available integration approaches, strategies for enriching existing workflows rather than disrupting them, downstream considerations that also benefit early conceptual design, and real-world governance practices that can make or break a successful integration.

title: Industrialized Construction Summit | Design Once, Fabricate Many: Scaling Industrialized Construction with Bouygues Construction
speakers: Antoine MORIZOT, CAD Engineer, Bouygues Construction | Clair Stone, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Build | Informed Design | Inventor | Revit | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: Bouygues is industrializing construction with a multidiscipline modular landing shaft integrating water and electrical systems. We'll demonstrate how Autodesk Informed Design software connects BIM, fabrication, and installation into a seamless workflow. Using a modular MEP cabinet as a real-world case study, attendees will see how a single configurable design can generate fabrication-ready outputs, automate documentation, and ensure consistent quality across projects. We’ll explore the impact of the Informed Design approach: reducing coordination errors, accelerating installation, and enabling scalable prefabrication strategies. We'll highlight how design rules and structured data allow teams to move from project-based delivery to repeatable, productized construction.

title: Innovators Stage | Autodesk Forma Jeopardy!
speakers: Danielle Foss, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Build | Cloud Worksharing | Docs | Forma | Model Coordination | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Calling all game show enthusiasts—come participate in an Autodesk Forma-focused game of Jeopardy, where you can test your knowledge of the platform and pick up new tips and insights. Structured like the US game show, audience members can “buzz in” to answer questions, accumulate points, and compete for prizes. In this session, we’ll showcase Autodesk Forma capabilities in an interactive and fun format. Expect to walk away with fresh insights and practical applications to deliver your projects more efficiently.

title: Did We Build What We Designed? Using AI and Autodesk Forma to Prevent Material Risk and Rework Failures.
speakers: Blake Jackson | Joe Butterworth, Head of Growth, NA, Qualis Flow
topics: Construction services | Build | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Construction projects do not fail because of design. They fail when what gets built does not match specifications. Rework costs about 9% of US project budgets—more than $30 billion annually—driven mainly by design errors, omissions, and specification mismatches, worsened by poor data and fragmented communication. Wrong or unverified materials cause rework, delays, disputes, margin loss, and safety risks. This session will show how to intervene earlier by closing the loop between design intent and construction reality using AI and Autodesk Forma. You will see real-time material verification, automatic issue detection, and proactive risk management, with insights from a customer co-presenter.

title: Future-Proof Modeling: Building Universal Pipeline Assets with USD in Maya
speakers: Kaan Zorlu, Lead 3D Artist, Leo Production
topics: Film and TV | 3ds Max 2 | Arnold | Maya | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract: Modeling is no longer just about clean quads and edge loops—it’s about data integrity for a global pipeline. As studios transition to OpenUSD, Maya artists must evolve their workflows to ensure assets are portable and performant. In this technical deep dive, we’ll move beyond basic topology to explore the authoring of "smart" USD assets. We’ll cover the latest Maya 2026 USD modeling tools, demonstrating how to manage complex hierarchies, variants, and metadata within a single file. You will learn how to optimize meshes for seamless deformation across platforms and avoid common pitfalls in a multisoftware environment. Stop modeling for a single scene—start building assets that thrive in a universal production ecosystem.

title: Semiconductor Factory Digital Twin: Information Foundations
speakers: Michael Potts, Director of Architecture & Engineering, Arcadis
topics: Manufacturing Other | Factory Design Utilities | FlexSim | Forma | Inventor | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: This session will provide an overview of the foundational information that is used to develop a semiconductor factory digital twin, including data and formats, 2D graphical information, 3D spatial information, reality capture, and relevant ISO and SEMI industry data and information standards. This foundational information has a lifecycle that spans planning, engineering, fabrication, construction, operation, and manufacturing—and their related technology stacks and AI infrastructure.

title: Design and Manufacturing Community Meetup
speakers: Tiffany Hayden, Application Developer, KETIV Technologies Inc. | Chris Benner, Community Manager, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD Mechanical | AutoCAD P&ID | Fusion | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | Inventor | D&M | Meetup
abstract: The design and manufacturing industry is experiencing rapid advancements, driven by innovative technology and evolving market demands. Join us for a meetup where industry professionals will come together to explore how designers and manufacturers are navigating, innovating, and excelling in this dynamic landscape. Tailored for designers, engineers, and other industry professionals, this event will provide a unique opportunity to network, share insights, and discover the latest trends shaping the future of design and manufacturing. Be part of the conversation and engage with fellow experts to collectively push the boundaries of our industry.

title: Discover Forma: From Site to Building Design
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Forma is transforming planning and building design. See how Forma Site Design brings AI-powered workflows, real-time analysis, and collaboration to early-stage planning, and how Forma Building Design extends that journey with intuitive modeling, integrated analytics, and connected workflows with Revit.

title: PM Break
abstract: Recharge, refuel, and reconnect during our afternoon break. Enjoy light refreshments designed to give you an energy boost, spark fresh conversations, and help you return to the next session ready to dive back in.

title: Small Business Roundtable - Design & Manufacturing
speakers: Jon den Hartog, VP, Design, Autodesk
topics: Building products and fabrication | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract:
Hosted by Jon den Hartog, Autodesk's VP of Product Development and Manufacturing Solutions, this session will bring together fellow entrepreneurs, builders, and creators for an intimate, conversation-driven roundtable designed exclusively for small business customers. Limited to under 50 attendees, this session creates space for honest, two-way dialogue—no slides, no pitches, just real talk.

 Share what's working well in your Autodesk experience, discuss the challenges you're navigating, and tell us what you'd love to see next. Autodesk leaders will be on hand not just to answer questions, but to genuinely listen and learn from the businesses that use our products every day.

title: Data-Rich: Meeting the Model Standard Owners Now Expect
speakers: Francesco Iorio, CEO, Augmenta Inc
topics: MEP Engineering  | Construction services | Revit | AECO
abstract:
What an owner expects inside the model has changed dramatically in recent years. The model has stopped being just a coordination artifact, it feeds prefab, production tracking, field deliverables, and facilities maintenance. On mission-critical work, and especially data centers, the stakes climb even higher because electrical infrastructure sits on the critical path and schedules leave no room for delay. The gap between a standard model and what is expected now shows up as measurable hours per project, and it lands hardest on teams that are already running at capacity.

This session draws on patterns Augmenta is seeing across a wide range of mission critical projects, breaking down how teams are meeting demand by generating data rich models from the start rather than back filling detail under deadline pressure.

title: What’s New in Revit 2027: AI, Data, and Connected Workflows
speakers: Dan Peticila, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Cesar Escalante, Sr. Technical Marketing Manager, Building Products, Autodesk | Scott D Davis, Sr Territory Technical Lead, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Model Coordination | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Revit 2027 software advances a more connected, data-driven BIM workflow, linking design, analysis, and documentation with the Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) ecosystem. In this session, Revit product managers will demonstrate how AI-powered assistance, extended cloud data, and collaborative carbon insights transform everyday production workflows. Learn how Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights connects Revit models to shared sustainability dashboards, how extended properties bring cloud-managed data directly into the model, and how automation and performance improvements accelerate documentation. See how connected workflows reduce rework, improve decision making, and align multidisciplinary teams from early design through detailed delivery.

title: Why Operations Is Becoming AEC’s Next Competitive Advantage
topics: Construction services | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract: Stephen Hooper, Senior Vice President of Autodesk Operations Solutions, and Chris Turlica, Head of MaintainX at Autodesk, join the Digital Builder podcast to explore why operations is emerging as a major opportunity in the built environment. The conversation examines connected operations, asset performance, maintenance, operational intelligence, AI, and how organizations can unlock greater value across the lifecycle of their buildings and infrastructure.

title: Innovators Stage I Hybrid Intelligence and a Pro-Social AI Future
speakers: Cornelia walther, Professor, Sunway University | Maxim Williams, VP, Global Culture & Belonging, Autodesk | Mike Haley, SVP, Research, Autodesk | Heather McIntosh Cassano, VP, User Experience, AEC Solutions, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, & Belonging
abstract:
Artificial intelligence is reshaping how we design, build, manufacture, and create. But as AI becomes more capable, the most important question isn't what AI can do, it's how people and organizations can use it to amplify human potential.
Autodesk’s Mike Haley (SVP, Research, Autodesk) and Heather McIntosh Cassano (VP, User Experience, AEC Solutions) will engage in a conversation with Dr. Cornelia Walther on how AI is rapidly changing the ways we work, collaborate, and what it means culturally as it's used to solve and innovate on increasingly complex challenges. The conversation will be moderated by Maxim Williams (VP, Global Culture and Belonging, Autodesk).
Together, the panel will explore the meaning of pro-social AI and hybrid intelligence, where combining human judgment with artificial intelligence can create better human centered outcomes for individuals, businesses, and society.
Attendees will leave with practical insights into how leaders, teams, and practitioners can navigate AI responsibly while maximizing its potential to unlock innovation, creativity, and opportunity.
This session is sponsored by Autodesk Global Culture & Belonging team.
