abstract:
Artificial intelligence is reshaping how we design, build, manufacture, and create. But as AI becomes more capable, the most important question isn't what AI can do, it's how people and organizations can use it to amplify human potential.
Autodesk’s Mike Haley (SVP, Research, Autodesk) and Heather McIntosh Cassano (VP, User Experience, AEC Solutions) will engage in a conversation with Dr. Cornelia Walther on how AI is rapidly changing the ways we work, collaborate, and what it means culturally as it's used to solve and innovate on increasingly complex challenges. The conversation will be moderated by Maxim Williams (VP, Global Culture and Belonging, Autodesk).
Together, the panel will explore the meaning of pro-social AI and hybrid intelligence, where combining human judgment with artificial intelligence can create better human centered outcomes for individuals, businesses, and society.
Attendees will leave with practical insights into how leaders, teams, and practitioners can navigate AI responsibly while maximizing its potential to unlock innovation, creativity, and opportunity.
This session is sponsored by Autodesk Global Culture & Belonging team.

title: Beyond Design: The Evolving Role of Architects and Engineers in the Age of AI
speakers: Deepika Khowal, Principal Account Executive, Enterprise, Autodesk | Steve Cayea, CIO, TYLin International | Lauren Collier, Chief Technology Officer, PBK | Natasha Luthra, Chief Technology Officer, HKS | Sam Omans, Head of AI Growth Strategy, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Forma | None | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Hear directly from technology leaders at some of the most innovative architectural/engineering firms (HKS Architects, PBK Architects, TYLin Group) as they share how AI is reshaping practice at scale. This panel will explore how global architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) organizations are integrating AI into design, engineering, and delivery workflows—moving from pilots to enterprise adoption.  Panelists will share real-world use cases, lessons learned, and the organizational changes required to successfully scale innovation. The discussion will also examine how the role of architects and engineers are evolving and the skills that will be critical for success in an AI-driven future.  You’ll gain practical insights into how leading firms are using AI and power of technology to drive efficiency, improve decision making, and stay competitive in a rapidly changing industry.

title: Shaping Low-Carbon Buildings from the Start: A Hands-On Lab with Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Insight
speakers: Giuseppe Ardito, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk | Corina Marinescu, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk | Justin Taylor, Sr Principal, AEC Solutions Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Insight | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Today’s architects are integrating sustainability analysis early to reduce environmental impact and meet carbon targets. Yet early design has traditionally relied on intuition due to limited data. This hands-on lab will introduce an outcome-based workflow that brings actionable carbon insights into early-stage design. You’ll use Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Insight to move from conceptual massing with real-time operational and embodied carbon feedback to detailed analysis, including Energy Use Intensity (EUI) and carbon trade-offs across design options. Through dashboards, metrics, benchmarks, and simulation factors, you’ll learn to optimize carbon performance and enable cross-disciplinary, data-driven design decisions.

title: From Revit Stills to Stories: AI Video Workflows for Architectural Communication
speakers: Qian Huang, Design Technology Specialist, HOK
topics: Architecture services | 3ds Max 2 | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Architects increasingly need to communicate design intent through motion before there is time or budget for traditional animation and for audiences who do not read drawings. This session shows how approved design assets from Revit based rendering views, diagrams, sketches, physical model, photos, can become short AI-assisted motion assets for design reviews, competitions, and client presentations. Attendees will learn a repeatable still-to-video workflow, see where AI video supports architectural communication and where it falls short, and apply QA guardrails for review and trust before using outputs in practice. A 5 minute case study assembled from 30 AI-assisted clips will also demonstrate how short generations become a coherent story.

title: Beyond Copilots: Agentic AI Workflows for Design and Engineering
speakers: Sean Young, Director of AEC, NVIDIA
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Architecture services | None | AECO
abstract:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly evolving from chat assistants into autonomous workflow agents capable of completing meaningful engineering tasks. For design and engineering organizations, the greatest opportunity isn't replacing designers—it's eliminating the repetitive work that consumes the time of design technologists, and other highly skilled experts.
This session explores running secure, high-performance agentic workflows with local AI models alongside Autodesk applications on Dell Pro Max and Precision workstations powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs and NVIDIA Grace Blackwell AI superchips. Local open models keep sensitive design data and IP on-premises, reduce inference costs, and deliver always-on, low-latency automation.
Through practical Autodesk-focused examples, we'll demonstrate AI agents that review models against CAD and BIM standards, validate customer requirements, automate quality control, generate documentation, and orchestrate multi-step engineering workflows.

title: AEC Roadmap: AutoCAD
speakers: Dan Whitcombe, Senior Group Product Manager, Autodesk | Tedman Martinez, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Anum Mithani, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Shiva Kashalkar, Senior Director, Product Management, AIR, Autodesk
topics: AutoCAD | AutoCAD & General Design | AECO
abstract: Get a front-row seat to what’s next for AutoCAD software. In this session, the AutoCAD product team will walk you through the latest enhancements and offer a preview of upcoming features that are redefining design and drafting. From improved collaboration tools to AI-powered productivity boosts, you’ll see how Autodesk is evolving AutoCAD to meet the needs of today’s and tomorrow’s complex projects. You’ll also get insight into the product strategy guiding our development, and see how your feedback is helping shape what’s coming next.

title: Autodesk Community Meetup: Meet Expert Elites
speakers: Shir Rustici, BIM Program Manager, Turner & Townsend | Chris Benner, Community Manager, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Meetup
abstract: Looking to deepen your connection with the Autodesk community? Join us for an exclusive meetup where you can engage with Autodesk's esteemed subject matter experts: Autodesk Expert Elites. These exceptional individuals are recognized for their significant contributions in sharing product knowledge, best practices, and expertise—playing vital roles in helping our customer community thrive. During this event, you'll hear insightful tips and experiences straight from Expert Elites, enhancing your understanding of Autodesk products. Don't miss this opportunity to connect, ask questions, and learn from community leaders in a collaborative environment. We look forward to seeing you there!

title: One Data‑Driven App to Rule BIM Documents and Automated Requirements Checks via ACC APIs
speakers: Jérémy Mols, BIM Director, Artelia
topics: Data and Document Management | Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | Build | Docs | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract:
Have you ever started a project with a BIM Execution Plan that slowly drifted away from real project? Documents become outdated, requirements fade, and no one can confirm that models and the common data environment still match what was agreed.

This class introduces a data‑driven approach where project requirements are not static documents but become active data in a single source‑of‑truth app (Power App). From that same data, it generates and updates project documents, runs checks across Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) and 3D models using APS APIs. AI helps interpret results and flag mismatches.

You’ll see an end‑to‑end demo and leave with a reusable pattern to keep what’s specified, documented, and modeled telling the same story.

title: Electrical Analytical Systems and Loads
speakers: Jacob Miller, Electrical Applications Product Owner, IMEG
topics: MEP Engineering  | Engineering service providers | Autodesk Access | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Electrical engineers are often forced to make major design decisions early, with limited information and rapidly changing project conditions. In this hands-on lab, you will use Revit Electrical Analytical Systems tools to create connected, data-rich workflows for schematic and early design. You’ll define analytical area loads and analytical equipment loads, create analytical equipment, and connect and evaluate loading scenarios to make better design decisions with minimal model information for better project outcomes. Using these tools early in your design process can give you better understanding of current loading scenarios and help you plan for future expansions with minimal effort.

title: Measuring the Impact of Autodesk Forma Data Management on Design Applications
speakers: David Butts, Virtual Design and Construction Manager, Kimley-Horn | David Neill, Firmwide Forma Administrator, Kimley Horn | Todd Rogers, Civil Administration, Walter P Moore | Rina Sahay, BIM Lead, Wade Trim
topics: Data and Document Management | Engineering service providers | Civil 3D | Forma Data Management Essentials | InfraWorks | Inventor Professional | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Transitioning from traditional network environments to cloud-based systems such as Autodesk Forma Data Management can be challenging. Understanding the advantages can be difficult without clear guidance for what works best. For this panel discussion, we’ll include industry-leading Autodesk experts to provide opinions and tips based on years of project and product experience. This session will start with a discussion on file management and move to Revit, Inventor, and Civil 3D tips for enhanced features when working in Forma Data Management. Next, we’ll cover content compatibility and end with recommendations for future projects to help your teams be as efficient as possible. Join us as we help you avoid many of the common challenges that accompany technology changes.

title: Agents of Change: Mastering Agentic AI and MCP Workflows for the Multidiscipline AEC Firm
speakers: Michael Gustafson, SVP of Strategic Growth, QNECT LLC | Andrew Sundal, Structural Engineer/Comp Design Specialist, HGA
topics: Structural Engineering  | Engineering service providers | Docs | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: The AEC industry is undergoing a paradigm shift where the lines between software developers, industry groups, and design firms are blurring. This session explores how AI strategies are being collaboratively shaped to move beyond basic research into high-impact implementation within multi-discipline engineering environments. We will examine the evolution of AI maturity, moving from foundational context engineering to the deployment of agentic services and Model Context Protocols (MCPs) that automate complex engineering tasks. Drawing on real examples, business leaders will gain a clear view of the emerging landscape and a practical way to balance AI’s potential against the demands of modern design practice.

title: The Electrical Design Triangle: Keeping Your Revit Model, Single-Line Diagram, and Calculations in Sync
speakers: David Robison, Founder and President, Design Master Software
topics: MEP Engineering  | Engineering service providers | Revit | AECO
abstract:
Every electrical project depends on three things agreeing: the Revit model, the single-line diagram, and the load calculations. In vanilla Revit they live in three places, and engineers keep them aligned by hand. Rename one panel, and you update it three times. Resize a transformer, and you update the single-line diagram, the upstream breaker size on the Revit panel schedule, and the voltage drop calculation.

Generating a diagram from the model once is the easy part. The cost shows up on revision twelve, when the model has moved and the diagram hasn't. This session presents a practical framework for treating the Revit model as the single source of truth, with the single-line diagram and calculations synchronized to it. Using real projects, we'll show which changes should propagate automatically instead of being redone by hand. You'll leave with a simple test for your own workflow: does a change propagate, or do you redo it by hand?

title: Industrialized Construction Summit | From BIM to Factory: Turning Building Design into Scalable Manufacturing Systems
speakers: Ihab Ramlawi, Co-Founder & Managing Director, DuPod
topics: Buildings | BIM 360 Build | BIM 360 Coordinate | Forma | Informed Design | Inventor | Revit | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: This session will explore the strategic shift from traditional construction to industrialized construction and what it means for the future of the built environment. Using DuPod as a case study, this session will examine how integrating engineering, digital platforms, and manufacturing creates a new delivery model for buildings—one based on productization, scalability, and predictable outcomes. Rather than treating buildings as one-off projects, industrialized construction applies manufacturing logic to create repeatable building systems and supply chains. This discussion will focus on how this shift can reshape productivity, risk, and value creation across the construction industry.

title: AECO Data Community Meetup: AEC Data Model Fan Club
speakers: Eddy Krygiel, Sr. Manager, AEC Data Model Strategy, Autodesk | Alexine Gordon-Stewart, Sr Manager, Chief of Staff, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM Collaborate | Docs | Model Analytics | AECO | Meetup
abstract: Do you get a thrill from liberating data from files, models, and all the places it hides? Do dashboards, connectors, and clean schemas spark joy? Then come hang out with your fellow data enthusiasts! We’re gathering AEC data pros, beginners, and the data curious. This one-hour session is designed to celebrate real-world wins, discuss future visions, talk open standards, and everything in between. Whether you’re a seasoned AEC Data Model expert or just dipping your toes into structured data goodness, you’re invited to join us in person to trade war stories, compare best practices, and generally geek out together. Calling all fans of the AEC Data Model API, Content Catalog, Datum, Model Analytics, and Parameters Service.

title: Revit and CAD to Operational Digital Twins: Indoor GIS for Facilities Teams
speakers: Adan Banda, Sr. Geospatial Data Manager, Dallas Fort Worth International Airport | Will Isley, CTO - PS R&D Center, Esri | Gokce Ozcelik, Sr. Product Manager - Indoor GIS, Esri
topics: Buildings | AutoCAD | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Many owners have rich Revit and AutoCAD data—but after handoff, that information is often difficult for operations teams to use in workflows. This session will show how to turn design data into a floor-aware indoor geographic information system (GIS) that supports operations across campuses, airports, and other facilities. You’ll learn how to transform CAD/BIM data into an indoor system of record for maps, assets, spaces, safety, and occupants. We’ll walk through implementation patterns and data import methods from CAD/BIM into ArcGIS Indoors, using location as a framework to move from handoff to operational value. See real examples from Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, where BIM data was converted into operational twins for assets, spaces, and situational awareness.

title: Reimagining Facility Operations: A Client’s Strategy for a Living Digital Twin
speakers: Dan Kolimar, Vice President, NV5
topics: Buildings | Civil 3D | Docs | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: A Confidential Client is redefining facility operations through an Autodesk Tandem-powered digital twin that transforms survey (ReCap software), scan-to-BIM (Revit and Civil 3D software), and project data into a living operational platform, not just documentation. Integrated with SkySpark and a CMMS, the twin enables machine-learning-driven fault detection and diagnostics, submetering analysis, and optimization control at the building level today—with a GIS-enabled, facility-wide decision layer on the horizon. The result: faster operational decisions, measurable efficiency gains, and a scalable model for AI-driven facilities management. Hear how a Client's digital delivery workflow became the foundation for continuous operational improvement, and see what it takes to get there.

title: Steel Design with Confidence: From Layout to Documented Connections
speakers: Dumitru Berteanu, Senior Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
topics: Structural Engineering  | Buildings | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Structural engineers often skip steel connection tools because they don't want to model every fastener. This hands-on lab will prove they don't have to. You’ll configure connections by adjusting key parameters and watch geometry respond in real time, also discovering how Revit software now keeps consistent geometry and parameters when the workflow moves from design to steel connections. Toward the close of the session, we’ll tag plans, annotate detail views, assemble sheets, and build connection schedules. Whether you’re transitioning from 2D or looking to enhance your steel workflows, this session will equip you with hands-on skills to design with confidence.

title: Integrating Structural Analysis Workflows in BIM with Revit
speakers: Catalin Lang, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk | Konrad Ociepka, Senior Product Owner, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Revit | Robot Structural Analysis Professional | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: In this hands-on lab, you’ll learn how to create, manage, and maintain analytical models in Revit for the purpose of structural analysis, BIM coordination, and design documentation. You’ll explore how to keep analytical and physical models coordinated as your design evolves, prepare your model for structural analysis, and bring analysis results back into your BIM workflow. By the end of the session, you’ll be able to close the loop between design and analysis, improving accuracy, efficiency, and collaboration in your structural projects. The session is for structural engineers and technicians who design and coordinate for BIM.

title: Beyond Tool Adoption: Orchestrating Change with Autodesk Forma
speakers: Koichi Murata, Sr Principal, Solutions Architect, Autodesk | Arisa Takahashi, Manager, Obayashi Corporation | Gen Morimoto, Archi / Data Engineer, Obayashi Corp.
topics: Buildings | BIM Collaborate Pro | Build | Docs | Forma | Revit | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Is adopting digital solutions and AI alone truly sufficient? This session will offer a point of view on how we scaled digital delivery across an organization of more than 5,000 engineers. As highlighted in Autodesk’s State of Design and Make, owners are increasingly demanding outcomes enabled by data-driven decision making. To connect digital initiatives to these outcomes, we’ll show how Autodesk Forma acts as a foundation for aligning value streams and driving organizational transformation. You will gain two vision frameworks that enable transformation in conditions of rapid change and ambiguity, along with real-world examples of how Forma accelerated consensus-building and supported owner decision making on complex projects.

title: From Messy to Meaningful: Ground Truth, Update-Ready Site Context in Revit
speakers: Joseph Huang, Principal, Architect, BIM Design Team Lead, Stantec | Raghavendra Bhat, Principal, Sr. BIM Integration Specialist, Stantec
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma | InfraWorks | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Accurate site context is essential for coordination, yet many teams struggle with fragile or inconsistent site models in Revit. This session presents reliable workflows for building and maintaining site context using common upstream sources, including Forma Site Design generated Revit files, Civil 3D published surfaces, and native Revit tools such as TopoSolids and Building Pads. The focus is on stability and change management – showing how to keep site models update ready as upstream data evolves, while supporting design development, visualization, and downstream coordination with minimal rework or model failure. We'll walk through four practical workflows for bringing site context into Revit and discuss where each one shines and where each one breaks.

title: Generative Design for Smart Catenary Systems Using Adaptive Parametric Families
speakers: Ayman SALEH, BIM R&D Manager, Colas Rail
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Dynamo | Inventor | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Designing overhead catenary systems is highly constrained and repetitive. This session will introduce a generative workflow that automates catenary design using an advanced Revit adaptive parametric family capable of handling more than 350,000 configuration combinations. The family embeds engineering logic and formulas that evaluate geometry, spans, clearances, and structural conditions to automatically select the optimal mast configuration. Attendees will learn how Generative Design or Dynamo drives this parametric engine, enabling the model to adjust the catenary mast as track geometry changes. The result is a smart, self‑adapting catenary system that reduces manual work and increases design reliability across long rail corridors.

title: Generative Design for Smart Catenary Systems Using Adaptive Parametric Families
speakers: Ayman SALEH, BIM R&D Manager, Colas Rail
topics: Civil infrastructure | AECO | Civil Engineering

title: AI-Assisted AutoLISP in AutoCAD: A Practical Workflow for Nonprogrammers
speakers: Fabian Raaijman, Team Lead of Rail Digital Engineering, Haskoning
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Map 3D | Civil 3D | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Most AutoCAD users never touch AutoLISP. So many small, repetitive design tasks stay manual. This session will show how AI-assisted AutoLISP workshops helped rail engineers who have little or no coding experience build useful automations themselves. You’ll discover how to identify good automation candidates, prompt AI for workable routines, validate and refine the results, and add lightweight governance through version control and testing. The outcome? Faster design work, more self-sufficient teams, and a practical path from AI curiosity to repeatable workflow improvement.

title: Delivering Kentucky Lock with BIM, GIS, and Federated Models: A USACE Case Study
speakers: Chris Miller, CAD-BIM Regional Technical Specialist, US Army Corps of Engineers
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Inventor | Navisworks Manage | Revit | Vault Professional | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: The Kentucky Lock Addition Project is a high-priority U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) effort requiring coordination across multiple districts, agencies, and contractors. This session will provide a technical deep dive into how BIM, CAD, and GIS were integrated through an Advanced Modeling Project Execution Plan (PxP) to support design, coordination, and construction. Using tools that include Civil 3D, Revit, Inventor, and Navisworks software, teams developed federated models for clash detection, sequencing, and as-built deliverables. You will see how model-based workflows improved coordination, reduced errors, and supported better decision making across the project lifecycle.

title: AI Data Check for Civil 3D: Validating Models Against Project Requirements via Autodesk Platform Services
speakers: Mohamad M. KASSIR, Regional Digital Manager, Egis
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Docs | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: This session will present a platform built through vibe coding using Autodesk Platform Services APIs, Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), and AI code generation to automate the full data validation cycle for Civil 3D models. The platform pulls files from Forma, extracts metadata via the Model Derivative API, and ingests project requirement PDFs. An AI layer converts PDFs into structured validation rules, then runs them against the model to produce a detailed conformity report, flagging gaps, mismatches, and missing attributes without manual checks. The session will also cover key lessons from development, AI-driven architecture, and real-world use cases showing practical impact at scale.

title: Headless Civil 3D: Batch Exporting to NWC and IFC Without Ever Opening the Drawing
speakers: Sobeshan Pillay, Associate, WSP
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Navisworks Freedom | Navisworks Manage | Navisworks Simulate | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: If you've ever opened 35 DWGs™ one at a time to extract corridors, surfaces, and pipe networks for Navisworks software, you know the pain—file locks, memory ceilings, and a week of clicking. Then the design updates … and you start again. This session will cover the batch-processing of Civil 3D models headlessly—scanning, extracting, and exporting without opening the UI. The pipeline includes: a Microsoft Excel manifest, headless discovery, solid extraction, surface meshing, pipe transfer, property attachment, and export via AcCoreConsole. We’ll also cover the five approaches that failed—Explode destroying pipe intelligence, ConvertToSolid crashing headless databases, wBlock corrupting styles, zero-triangle access violations, and PropertySet zombie objects. Each one cost days.

title: Driving Certainty On-Site: 4D Workflows for Program, Progress, and Risk to Managing Contractors
speakers: Quoc Pham, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk | Nathan Love, Construction BIM Manager, Multiplex
topics: Construction services | 3ds Max 2 | Docs | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: A key industry challenge is accessing reliable, real‑time progress data, which is critical to reducing the risk of project overruns and cost escalation. This presentation will show how managing contractors can use data within design models and Autodesk Forma to deliver effective 4D workflows. We’ll showcase practical uses of Autodesk Forma and Revit software to plug into construction software that provides more-accurate site data, enabling teams to confidently measure progress against program.

title: The Comeback Tour: How Barton Malow Rebuilt Trust in Desktop Connector
speakers: Elizabeth Fox, Sr. Technology Implementation Manager, Barton Malow
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | Build | Desktop Connector | Docs | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: When your net promoter score (NPS) is –23 and nearly half your users are detractors, you don't just relaunch a tool—you rebuild a relationship. Starting with only 32% of 1,200 project delivery team members on Desktop Connector, Barton Malow's construction technology team launched a 14-month, three-phase adoption campaign—and finished at 92%, well past their 80% goal. In this session, we'll share the honest playbook: how we used survey data to make the business case, how we structured a phased rollout across a distributed workforce, how we built a support ecosystem to sustain momentum, and how we quantified 150,000 hours of potential annual savings. Transparency included.

title: From Chaos to Clarity: The Data Exchange Strategy Behind a $1.3 Billion Dubai Harbour Icon
speakers: Ahmad ElGammal, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk Forma, Autodesk | Derek Bourke, Digital & BIM Manager, Khansaheb Civil Engineering
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: What happens when intelligent data connects teams who’ve never spoken the same language? On a $1.3-billion Dubai Harbour tower, we built an integrated workflow unifying BIM, planning, and commercial teams. The planning schedule defines the data standard, enforced through Autodesk Forma Library parameters. Data Exchange extracts data live from Revit into Power BI—no exports, no delays, no conflicts. Commercial teams get a weekly dashboard filterable by work package with a live 3D model view. Quantities are now a click away, even on your tablet. Leave with a replicable framework connecting decision makers using live collaboration and Revit, Forma Library, Data Exchange, and Power BI—proven on one of the Middle East's most ambitious towers.

title: Solving 90% of Rebar Issues in Design: Construction Through Standards, Automation, and Co-Creation
speakers: Hiromitsu 曽根, General Manager of Project, Maeda Corporation | Nobuya Watanabe, Manager, Maeda Corporation
topics: Construction services | AutoCAD | Docs | Navisworks Simulate | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: A challenge faced in rebar construction was that many RFIs (requests for information) with architects emerged only during the construction phase. Limited early discussion with specialty contractors delayed issue resolution, leading to additional data creation and rework that increased rebar construction costs by over 6%. To resolve the problem, architects, engineers, and constructors adopted a collaborative workflow from design using Autodesk Forma to support a shared data environment. Rebar data was standardized for manufacturing, and automated placement was enabled by combining structural and rebar data during design. At the end, the early design-phase collaboration reduced construction inquiries by about 90%, nearly eliminated rework, and cut data preparation effort by around 90% through automation.

title: Procurement Without Chaos: Building Consistency with Best Practices and Connected Systems
speakers: Sam Young, Solutions Architect, DPR Construction | Sadanand Sahasrabudhe, CEO, ConstructivIQ
topics: Construction Operations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Procurement issues cause roughly 50% of project delays, and using inconsistent, manual processes for planning/tracking is a recipe for cost overruns and missed deadlines. DPR Construction manages more than 2,000 projects annually, so the stakes couldn’t be higher. Success demands disciplined best practices across process, tools, and metrics. In this session, we’ll present a proven, measurable procurement planning and tracking approach using tools like Autodesk Forma, ConstructivIQ, and more. DPR has already implemented this across hundreds of projects—moving from disconnected workflows to a scalable, connected system. Join us to learn how you can apply the same principles within your own organization to drive more-predictable and efficient outcomes.

title: How to Build a Business Case for Reality Capture: Insights from the Nation's Biggest Builders
speakers: Roy Malcolm, Central Region VDC Leader, DPR Construction | Ahmad Sabbouri, Vice President of Customer Success, Cupix | Jonathan Caceres, VDC Manager, The Whiting-Turner Contracting Company
topics: Reality Capture | Construction services | Forma | Revit | AECO
abstract: Reality capture technology promises to reduce rework, settle disputes, and give project teams eyes on site without being there. Getting support for this new technology internally can be an uphill battle. In this session, you’ll learn what it takes to make a successful business case for reality capture programs from leaders at some of America’s biggest construction companies. They'll cover what sparked their search for solutions, what use cases they were targeting, what got them past executive skepticism, and what KPIs they measure. You’ll leave with a practical framework for building your own business case, including the specific language, metrics, and project examples that moved the needle with leadership.

title: Unlock the Power of AI for AutoCAD 2027 Toolsets
speakers: Hung Nguyen, Technical Consultant, SolidCAD | Lina El-Khoury, BIM Strategy & Digital Solutions Consultant, LEK
topics: Education | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Mechanical | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Fusion | Revit | EDU | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Unlock the full potential of AI in AutoCAD 2027 toolsets. Building on our AU 2024 award-winning class, this session will explore how AI-powered tools revolutionize CAD, driving unmatched efficiency. Experience how AutoCAD 2027 software’s AI automates complex workflows—from intelligent object recognition and predictive drafting to real-time generative design. With automated dimensioning, predictive error-correction, and material optimization, you’ll slash design cycles. Use AI-driven simulation to stress-test designs against real-world scenarios, ensuring peak performance. Transform your workflow with seamless, AI-enhanced interoperability that bridges multidisciplinary teams. Future-proof your craft with smarter, faster, and more creative CAD.

title: Advanced Maya and Unreal Integration for Game Cinematics: Motion Capture, Characters, and VFX
speakers: Marcio Goncalves, Assistant Professor of Game Art and Design, State University of New York - Empire State
topics: Games | Maya | Maya Creative | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract: This class will present an intermediate-to-advanced workflow integrating Maya software and Unreal Engine software to create more-complex and exciting game cinematics—including characters animated with motion capture, manually animated vehicles, particles, and dynamics. This class will show you how to create and layout an advanced game cinematic in Maya, preparing it for export to Unreal Engine. Then we will show you how to import and set up the exported Maya scene in Unreal Engine, setting up materials, cameras, mocap, particles, and dynamics. Finally, we’ll implement industry-standard best practices while working between Maya and Unreal Engine, and rendering the final cinematic in Unreal Engine. This hands-on class has the indie game dev and 3D artist in mind.

title: Hand-Key Gameplay Animation Workflow Using Autodesk Maya and Flow Studio
speakers: Alex Ferreira Simoes, Senior Gameplay Animator & Director, Riot Games - Agora Community | Brendan Russert, Senior Animator, Riot Games
topics: Games | Flow Studio | Maya | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract: In this session, we'll take a deep dive into how AI can help your team’s animators in a nondestructive and efficient way. We’ll cover how to use Autodesk Flow Studio software as a base and bring that into Maya software for the regular hand-key stylized animation workflow for gameplay animations—later exporting it to Unreal Engine to create a gameplay-ready asset. This workflow can also be used for film and TV animations.

title: Fireside Chat with the Inventor Product Team
speakers: Steven Dennis, Sr Principal Engineer, Autodesk | Patrick Cataldo, Distinguished Architect, Autodesk | Andrew Faix, Senior Principal Experience Designer, Autodesk | Johnson Shiue, Sr. Principal SW Eng. Test, Autodesk | Dan Szymanski, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Industrial machinery | Inventor | Inventor LT | Inventor Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Sit down with the Inventor product team and discuss your most-pressing issues, concerns, and questions about Inventor. Many Inventor team members will be available to answer your questions. What are the best practices for maximizing your Inventor use? How are Inventor projects prioritized and chosen for each release? Where is Inventor going in the near future? AI, Model States, Drawings, Sheet Metal, Autodesk Fusion versus Inventor—all your favorite topics will be open for discussion.

title: The Truth Is Out There, but So Is the Nonsense: AI Tips and Tricks for iLogic and the Inventor API
speakers: Curtis Waguespack, Design Automation Solutions Architect, Topper Industries
topics: Manufacturing Other | Inventor | Inventor Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: You've seen how iLogic can tame tedious tasks and make you more efficient. Now AI promises to go even further, writing your rules, navigating the Inventor API, and transforming your automation overnight. Sounds great, right? Here's the truth: Great results from AI are out there, but so is the AI-induced nonsense. You might have seen AI confidently generate code that doesn't work. Or watched it invent API methods that don't exist. The promise is real. But so are the hallucinations, the dead ends, and the frustrations of vibe coding. Come to this session to cut through the hype with tips, tricks, and insights for getting real results from AI, knowing when to trust it, when to push back, and how to build automation that fulfills the prompt.

title: Digital Factory Summit | From Spreadsheets to Simulation: M2X's Journey of Factory Simulation with FlexSim
speakers: Harshit Gole, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Nicholas Schwartz, Chief Manufacturing Officer at M2X Energy, M2X Energy
topics: Manufacturing Other | Factory Design Utilities | FlexSim | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: This project addresses the challenge of optimizing a highly labor-intensive manufacturing process for GTM systems at M2X Energy, where welding and pipe fabrication dominate both cycle time and total hours. Traditional spreadsheet-based analysis lacks the ability to capture dynamic interactions between resources, workflows, and constraints. Using FlexSim software, we built a discrete-event simulation of the factory to model real-world operations, identify bottlenecks, and make accurate process decisions based on data. Combined with design inputs such as weld reduction strategies, this approach enables data-driven decisions to reduce manufacturing hours, improve throughput, and support scalable factory and product design.

title: From Inventor Design to Machined Part: Building a Real Digital Thread with Autodesk Fusion CAM
speakers: Edward Rose, Client Success Manager - Adoption Programs, Symetri
topics: Manufacturing Other | Fusion | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | Fusion Nesting and Fabrication Extension | Inventor | Vault Professional | D&M | Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: In this technical deep dive, we’ll walk through a real machined project designed in Inventor and programmed in Autodesk Fusion Manufacturing Extension. Follow the complete workflow: creating and iterating the part in Inventor, uploading to Fusion, applying toolpaths, generating G-code, and efficiently updating toolpaths after design changes using simple refreshes. We’ll cover both the cloud approach (AnyCAD linked references and Desktop Connector) and the enterprise version using Vault Professional software for controlled releases and revision management. We’ll share the actual files, challenges encountered, key lessons, and measurable time savings. You’ll leave with actionable steps to build an effective digital thread between design and manufacturing teams.

title: Digital Twin for Factories: Enabling Smart, Connected, and Collaborative Manufacturing
speakers: Santosh Kulkarni, President - Software Engineering Services, Neilsoft | Aniruddha Phatak, AVP-Strategic Market Development (Software), Neilsoft | Varun Bansal, AVP - Strategic Market Development (MFG), Neilsoft
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | Autodesk Platform Services | FlexSim | Inventor | D&M | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: Manufacturing companies face inefficiencies from disconnected systems across factory design, engineering, and shop-floor operations. This session will demonstrate how a digital twin approach using Autodesk Tandem software integrates BIM-based factory models with live production data for smarter decisions. For greenfield projects, FlexSim integration enables simulation of layouts, production lines, and material flows before execution, optimizing throughput and reducing project risk. Energy Monitoring and Management System (EMMS) integration adds early visibility into energy and sustainability. For brownfield plants, connecting programmable logic controllers (PLCs), supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA), and a manufacturing execution system (MES) creates a unified operational view, enabling real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and bottleneck identification.

title: Industrialized Construction Summit | Productization Goes Global: Designing Scalable Entertainment Venues
speakers: Nathan Tobeck, Head of Digital APAC, Populous
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: How do you deliver iconic, high-quality venues at speed and scale? This session will explore how productization, systemization, and kit-of-parts strategies are transforming the design and delivery of large-scale entertainment venues. Drawing on global case studies—from temporary World Cup stadiums to immersive venues like Sphere—this talk will demonstrate how standardized components and platform-based approaches enable flexibility, performance, and rapid deployment. It will also examine how digital workflows, BIM, and data-driven design all support convergence between design, manufacturing, and operations. You’ll gain practical insight into applying industrialized construction principles without compromising experience or design quality.

title: Building Smarter with AI in Construction
topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Join Tomer Rosenthal, Principal Product Manager for AI at Autodesk, to explore and demo practical AI-powered workflows that help construction teams make faster, more informed decisions, reduce manual effort, and turn project data into actionable insights. And learn how smarter, more connected ways of working can help teams deliver better project outcomes.

title: AEC Roadmap: Civil Infrastructure
speakers: Andrew Milford, Sr. Group Product Manager, Infrastructure and APAC Product Lead, Autodesk | Can Anbarlilar, Sr. Group Product Manager, Infrastructure Product Line and Strategic Projects, Autodesk | Prakriti Khanna, Sr. Group Product Manager, Collaboration Product Line, Autodesk | Shiva Kashalkar, Senior Director, Product Management, AIR, Autodesk | Tim Yarris, Sr. Group Product Manager, Civil 3D and Infrastructure Product Line, Autodesk
topics: Reality Capture | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfraWorks | ReCap | AECO
abstract: Infrastructure projects are growing in scale, complexity, and urgency—and Autodesk is evolving to meet that challenge. In this session, you’ll hear from the teams behind Civil 3D, InfraWorks, ReCap, and Collaboration for Civil 3D as they share what’s new and what’s next for civil engineers and infrastructure professionals. Learn how modeling, analysis, and collaboration workflows are evolving to support more-sustainable, connected, and efficient project delivery. You’ll also get an early look at features in development and have the opportunity to provide input that will help shape Autodesk’s infrastructure roadmap.

title: Meet Rhumbix: Connecting your Field-to-Finance Workflows
topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Join the Rhumbix team to discover how connected field and finance workflows can help construction teams turn jobsite activity into actionable insights. In this session, we’ll demo how Rhumbix streamlines the capture of labor, time, and production data from the field and connects it to downstream cost and financial workflows. And, share how better connections between the field and office can reduce manual processes and improve visibility into project performance.

title: Building MEP Automation Tools with pyRevit: Real Examples from High-Rise Project Delivery
speakers: Zaid Fahed, MEP BIM Manager, KEO International Consultants
topics: MEP Engineering  | Engineering service providers | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: As MEP engineers, we spend too much time on repetitive tasks that could be automated. In this session, we’ll show how we used pyRevit at KEO International Consultants to build custom automation tools inside Revit software, transforming our workflow on high-rise projects. Using two real tools as examples—a chilled water pipe autosizer based on pressure drop criteria (150-300 Pa/m) and a domestic water pipe autosizer following CIBSE Guide G—we’ll demonstrate how pyRevit can automate complex MEP tasks in a single click. This session is for MEP engineers and BIM managers who want to build their own automation tools, regardless of programming background.

title: Beyond Automotive: Scaling Autodesk VRED for Industrial Design Reviews
speakers: Prashant Kalyani, Jr Project Associate, Desapex Engineering Consultants LLP | AkshayKumar Pawar, Project Associate L2, Desapex Engineering Consultants LLP
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Engineering service providers | Inventor Professional | VRED Design | VRED Presenter | VRED Professional | AECO | XR | Cross Industry
abstract: Autodesk VRED is well known in automotive, but the same real-time visualization workflow can accelerate collaboration across industrial manufacturing. This Technical Deep Dive shows how teams can use VRED, Python scripting, and immersive reviews to create shared virtual prototypes for switchgear, pumps, and engineered products. Attendees will see how to structure review sessions, add scripted interactions, validate design intent before physical build, and shorten feedback cycles across design, engineering, and program teams.

title: RACING AHEAD WITH DATA: Delivering a F1 Circuit with Autodesk Forma
speakers: Jesus Fuentes, BIM Manager, EIFFAGE CONSTRUCCIÓN | Irene Ruiz-Castillo, BIM Manager, ACCIONA CONSTRUCCIÓN
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Build | Dynamo | Forma | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: This session demonstrates an advanced workflow for linear infrastructure using Autodesk Forma, Dynamo, and Power BI, focusing on automation, interoperability, and data-driven decision-making. Participants will learn how to use a civil alignment as a parametric driver to automate asset placement through Dynamo, leveraging coordinate logic (X,Y) and terrain adaptation. The workflow integrates generated assets into Revit with structured data and parameter control. During construction, Autodesk Build enables asset tracking and status management. Finally, Power BI dashboards provide real-time insights, KPIs, and lifecycle visibility, improving coordination, efficiency, and project outcomes.

title: Forma CS Summit l The Autodesk Forma Admin & Standardization Roundtable: Building a Scalable Data Foundation
speakers: Will Marinos, Director of Design Technologies, Hazen and Sawyer | Ross Collinson, Dir., Product Management, Autodesk | Neree Croteau, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
abstract: Join this interactive Forma Roundtable, hosted by Autodesk Customer Success, focused on Forma administration and standardization strategies. Designed for Forma admins, platform owners, and operations leaders, this session uses facilitated peer discussion to explore governance and scalable adoption that enable streamlined, standardized practices. Engage directly with Autodesk Product and SMEs as active contributors and partners, alongside industry peers sharing knowledge and real‑world insight in a collaborative, feedback‑driven environment. Attendees leave with actionable strategies, expanded peer networks, and stronger partnership with Autodesk.

title: Rendering Reality: The Rise of Gaussian Splats
speakers: Logan Foster, Product Owner, Autodesk | Aaron Dabelow, Senior Technical Lead & Producer, MAKE | Mark Kauffman, Asst. VP/Technical Lead, WSP
topics: Reality Capture | Architecture services | 3ds Max 2 | AECO | Media & Entertainment | M&E
abstract: Join industry experts from design visualization and VFX as they explore how Gaussian Splats and solutions from Autodesk Interactive Media & Entertainment are transforming digital workflows. Learn what these techniques are, how they enable highly accurate digital twins and immersive world building, and where they fit in real-world production pipelines. Through examples and firsthand insights, speakers will share what excites them about this approach—along with the practical pros, cons, and challenges of adopting it.

title: Accelerating Real Estate Development with Autodesk Forma and Revit
speakers: Joe BIMtucci, Senior Project Design Technologist, Cuningham | Emily Bisaga Dunne, Executive Director of Design Technology, Cuningham
topics: Architecture services | Forma | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Early-stage real estate decisions are often constrained by slow, fragmented workflows between site analysis and building design. This session will demonstrate a tightly integrated workflow using Autodesk Forma Site Design and Revit software to rapidly generate, evaluate, and iterate development scenarios. You’ll learn how to move from contextual site intelligence to parametric building systems, enabling faster feasibility studies, improved stakeholder alignment, and data-informed decision making. The session will include live demonstrations, workflow diagrams, and implementation strategies for practice.

title: Structural Engineering at the Core: Integrated Digital Delivery at Foster + Partners
speakers: Andrea Colombo, BIM & Design Systems Coordinator, Foster + Partners | Ash Rahman, Structural BIM Lead/Manager, Foster + Partners
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Forma | Forma Data Management | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: By showcasing several case studies, we’ll explore how the in-house structural engineering team at Foster + Partners successfully delivers high-complexity, global projects through an integrated design approach. We’ll highlight how deep engineering expertise is combined with advanced digital workflows and close multi-disciplinary collaboration through Autodesk products, enabling efficient, innovative, and architecturally expressive outcomes. Central to this success is the team’s ability to ensure that design-informed decisions are data-driven, coordinated, and efficiently communicated across all project stakeholders.

title: I Shall Call You C3PO: A Guide to Using Autodesk Assistant for Revit As Your Production Sidekick
speakers: Kimberly Fuhrman-Jones, Community Manager, Autodesk | Paul Aubin, Author/Consultant, Paul F Aubin Consulting Services, Inc. | Harlan Brumm, Director, Product Management, Revit Core Capabilities & Collaboration Services, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: With today’s AI tools, science fiction truly meets reality. We can all have a handy “droid” by our side. But instead of calling it Siri, Claude, or Gemini, we can call it: C3PO! Can Autodesk Assistant for Revit tell you the odds of outrunning an Imperial Star Destroyer? Perhaps not. But it can tell you how many chairs are in an auditorium or the size of a room, or it can even create a floor plan and apply a view template. Want advice on what kind of space to put in an empty retail unit? It can do that, but don't ask it to draw the layout—that's on you! In this lab, we'll explore this new tool that brings AI directly into your Revit workspace. And if you want to call it by everyone's favorite droid name, it probably won't mind.

title: Autodesk PRIDE & Mental, Inclusion, Neurodiversity, and Disability (MIND) Network Meetup
speakers: Alexis Womble, Senior Security Program Manager, Autodesk | Madison Burnell, Executive Assistant, Autodesk | Jason Swenton, Director, AMER Go-To-Market & Customer Experience Talent Acquisition, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Meetup
abstract: This meetup is sponsored by Autodesk Employee Belonging Groups (EBGs) to support connection and shared growth across communities. We bring employees and customers together through interactive, networking-focused experiences. Participants will engage in small-group conversations designed to encourage meaningful dialogue, knowledge sharing, and relationship building across teams, roles, and communities.

title: Maximizing Autodesk Platform Services Value: Smarter Usage, Greater Control, AI-Ready Scale
speakers: Dwanill Mehta, Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Autodesk Platform Services continues to evolve to better support how customers build, scale, and optimize applications in an increasingly AI-driven world. APIs and Model Context Protocols (MCPs) are becoming foundational to agentic AI workflows, making it more important than ever to understand and optimize Autodesk Platform Services use. This session will highlight the features Autodesk Platform Services is building to help you make the most of cloud APIs and MCPs, whether developing directly on Autodesk Platform Services or integrating through third-party applications. You’ll also see new capabilities that provide greater visibility and control, including Autodesk Platform Services reporting, cost management tools, and AI-powered usage prediction through Autodesk Assistant. Join us to learn how to scale with confidence and maximize value from Autodesk Platform Services.

title: Design and Manufacturing Industry Deep Dive
speakers: Sanjay Aggarwal, Vice President, D&M Industry Strategy, Autodesk | Vik Vedantham, Sr. Director, D&M Business Intelligence & Strategy, Autodesk
topics: Trust | Product Development | D&M
abstract: Explore the trends, challenges, and technology shifts shaping the future of design and manufacturing. This session will examine how organizations are connecting data, people, and processes across the product lifecycle to increase agility, improve sustainability, and accelerate innovation. Gain practical insights into evolving industry priorities and the opportunities they create for business transformation.

title: No More Blind Spots: Autodesk MCP Driving AI Across Multi-CDE Platform Projects
speakers: Aaron Traylen, Utopia Digital / University of Technology Sydney
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Engineering service providers | BIM 360 Docs | Docs | Tandem Connect | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: On a live transport megaproject, a major infrastructure contractor recovered 37 days of lost labor and $137,000 in the first week—anchored by Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Most major projects don't run on a single common data environment (CDE). Autodesk Forma sits at the center, but teams still operate across ProjectWise, Aconex, Microsoft SharePoint, and others. That's where coordination breaks down and no one sees the risk coming. This panel will bring together Autodesk, UTS, and Utopia Digital—co-investigators on Australia’s Economic Accelerator research program. Together we're building SyncSight: an AI governance layer that uses Autodesk's Model Context Protocol (MCP) to extend the Autodesk Forma intelligence across every CDE on a project—detecting coordination failures before they become delays.

title: Leakage Modeling Workflows for Calibrating Water Distribution Models
speakers: Chris Adams, engineer, Arcadis | Ben Chenevey, Principal Water Engineer, Arcadis | Nathan Gerdts, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Water Infrastructure | Engineering service providers | Info360 Insight | InfoWater Pro | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Water utilities increasingly rely on hydraulic models to improve water-loss management. Yet, explicitly representing real losses remains a common challenge. This session will present a practical, repeatable workflow for modeling leakage using InfoWater Pro software. You will learn how to go beyond traditional water-loss representations and incorporate system pressures, SCADA data, and district metered areas into calibrated models to quantify and spatially allocate real losses. We’ll demonstrate how pressure-dependent leakage formulations can improve calibration accuracy and identify high-leakage zones. Real-world examples will show how, when calibrated, these models support operational decision making, targeted leak detection, and capital planning.

title: Automation API: The Execution Engine for Autodesk at Scale
speakers: Sualp Ozel, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Rami Kuret, Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | 3ds Max 2 | AutoCAD | Fusion | Inventor | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: The Automation API is evolving from a job-processing service into the execution layer for running Autodesk engine workloads at scale. This session traces that evolution, from reusable automation bundles toward flexible, agent-driven workflows, and where it is heading next. We will look at how the platform is being built for reliability at scale, how it provides dedicated, isolated compute and flexible compute options for demanding workloads, and how it is becoming the place where AI agents run Autodesk engine work: supporting always-on engine sessions for iterative agents, surfacing core desktop capabilities to agent-driven workflows, and enabling no-code workflow integration. Using real-world scenarios, we will connect these pieces into the broader Autodesk Platform Services story. This session is relevant whether you are building on Autodesk Platform Services or planning for the future of automation in your workflows.

title: AEC Roadmap: Water
speakers: Trevor English, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, Water, Autodesk | Brian Deeley, Dir., Product Management, Autodesk | Mike Maylone, Sr. Manager, Product Mgmt, Autodesk | Brett Singley, Manager, Product Mgmt, Autodesk
topics: Water Infrastructure | Engineering service providers | Info360 Insight | InfoDrainage | InfoWater Pro | InfoWorks ICM | InfoWorks WS Pro | AECO
abstract: Water infrastructure is changing fast, and your tools need to keep up. Join Autodesk water experts to explore the latest innovations across InfoDrainage, InfoWorks ICM, InfoWorks WS Pro, InfoWater Pro, and Info360 Insight. Discover how you can streamline workflows for drainage design, hydraulic modeling, and asset management, alongside expanding integrations with Civil 3D and the Architecture, Engineering & Construction Collection. Discover what’s new, what’s coming next, and how it all connects. You’ll get a sneak peek at in-development capabilities, and you’ll have the chance to connect directly with the teams behind these solutions, ask questions, and share feedback that helps drive the roadmap forward.

title: From Content to Control: Structuring MEP BIM Production with Content Catalog
speakers: Florencia Kossman, Job Captain MEP, ENG | Valentín David, Project Manager, ENG
topics: Data and Document Management | Engineering service providers | AutoCAD | Cloud Worksharing | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Have you ever tried using Content Catalog to structure MEP content during construction stages? This session will show you how to use metadata to manage content for QA/QC and use granular search to organize it by phase and construction status. Going beyond traditional libraries, this cloud-based system treats assets as connected data, supporting coordination, production, and fabrication workflows. Learn how to reduce content search time by up to 30% and minimize rework by using Content Catalog as a control system—guiding modeling, improving coordination, and integrating automated quality process into production. You’ll gain a practical framework to implement workflows and enable faster decisions across design and fabrication teams.

title: Continuous Versus Periodic Clash Detection: Can Model Coordination and Autodesk AI Replace Navisworks?
speakers: Karan Singh, Digital Delivery Manager, Burns & McDonnell India | Stephen Brooke, Digital Delivery Manager, Burns & McDonnell
topics: Engineering service providers | Cloud Worksharing | Forma | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Is the Navisworks silo holding your project back? For 20 years, coordination was a "once a week" event locked on a desktop. No more. This session will explore the leap to continuous, cloud-native coordination in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll dive into how Model Coordination democratizes BIM, using Autodesk AI and Autodesk Assistant to validate clashes against specs in real time. Learn to ditch static PDF reports for a closed-loop workflow that connects designers directly to fixes. We’ll settle the debate: Where does Model Coordination win, and when do you still need the Navisworks "power user" kit? Join us to build a road map for a faster, AI-augmented and integrated future. Stop clashing. Start coordinating.

title: Drawing from Experience: CAD Management Is More Than Being a CAD Expert
speakers: R.K. McSwain, IT Customer Service Manager / CAD Manager, LJA, Inc. | Eric DeLeon, Founder & Principal Consultant, DeLeon Consulting & Coaching | Robert Green, Owner, Robert Green Consulting | Kate Towne, Lead IT Applications Specialist, TYLin | Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+
topics: Engineering service providers | None | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: This award-winning panel is back again with new topics to discuss and insights to share. This year, the panel will feature some familiar faces and some new ones—all gathered to discuss things important to a CAD manager. Topics will range from technology and data to the even more challenging human aspects of teams and workflows. Learn from this panel of diverse CAD managers who are widely respected as leaders in their field. Hear their unique perspectives and discover solutions to challenges faced by CAD managers from organizations of all sizes and backgrounds. You won’t want to miss this chance to hear the important lessons they’ve learned from decades of experience.

title: From Design to Reality: How Avnet's AI Tools Are Making Better Engineering Decisions Earlier
speakers: Christopher Jackson, Vice President, Global Engineering, Avnet | Rogelio Gonzalez, GCET Apps Engineering Manager, Avnet
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Engineering service providers | EAGLE | Fusion | Fusion Design Extension | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | AECO
abstract: Product development is evolving beyond traditional CAD workflows. Join Avnet and Autodesk to see how AI-powered engineering experiences are helping engineers move from concept to manufacturable products faster while making smarter decisions earlier in the design process. Learn how Avnet's component intelligence—including real-time pricing, availability, lifecycle data, alternate part recommendations, and engineering content—integrates directly into Autodesk Fusion. Discover how AI-assisted design workflows combined with supply chain insights enable teams to evaluate feasibility, manufacturability, and sourcing tradeoffs from the start. By connecting AI-driven design with real-world component and procurement intelligence, engineering teams can reduce redesigns, improve collaboration between engineering and sourcing, and accelerate the path from idea to production-ready products.

title: Connecting AECO Workflows End-to-End with the Autodesk Forma Industry Cloud
speakers: Alejandra Beaujon, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk | Joey Matla, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Build | Docs | Forma | Model Coordination | Quantity Takeoff | AECO | Architecture
abstract: See how architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) teams connect planning, design, coordination, and construction workflows in a single AI and data-driven environment using the Autodesk Forma industry cloud. This technical and practical deep dive will walk through real workflows—from site planning in Autodesk Forma to design in Revit software, coordination in Forma Design Collaboration, and execution in Forma Build. Learn how data flows through Autodesk Data Management as a common data environment, preserving decisions across phases with practical examples. Explore practical AI-powered use cases such as rapid design iteration, automated analysis, and model-based coordination. And discover how to reduce manual work, improve collaboration, and implement connected workflows across the AECO lifecycle.

title: AI Agents Meet Autodesk Platform Services: From Autodesk Forma Building Design to Operational Digital Twin
speakers: Frank Otto, Product Owner - Platform, N+P Informationssysteme GmbH | Hendrik Schön, Enterprise Architect, N+P Informationssysteme GmbH | Poyraz Yildirim, Developer Advocate Manager, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Autodesk Viewer | Docs | Forma | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Most digital twin projects stall at the same point: There’s no 3D model. Point cloud scanning takes weeks—too heavy for operational use cases like workplace booking or shop-floor monitoring. But we’ve found a faster path: Design buildings in Autodesk Forma Building Design, process them server-side via the Autodesk Platform Services Automation API for Revit, then use agentic AI workflows via Model Context Protocol (MCP) to enrich the model with workplaces and connected production data. It takes hours instead of months. Through video walk-throughs and live demos, we’ll show two use cases we’re deploying this year—replacing our own third-party desk-sharing tool, and building a manufacturing digital twin. You’ll leave with a replicable pattern for AI-enabled design-to-operate workflows.

title: The Adoption Flywheel: Lessons from the Bain and Co. Deployment of Autodesk Forma at a Leading Indian Developer
speakers: Shubika Sardana, Associate Partner, Bain and Company | Shradha Vaid, Partner, Bain & Company | Yashaswi Sharma, Management Consultant, Bain and Company
topics: Data and Document Management | Buildings | Build | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Most digital transformation efforts share one struggle: The platform is live, but users stick to legacy systems. Working with a leading Indian real estate developer, Bain embedded Autodesk Forma as the operating backbone for its preconstruction workflows. The adoption flywheel included the following: Bain focused on strategy before deployment, co-creating more than 40 workflows and 150 decision rights. Then role-specific dashboards were customized for individuals and management. Following that, the focus shifted to change management, considering management mandates, weekly leaderboards (project and user), and focused communication. Contextualized knowledge materials and hands-on training (in-house and external) completed the picture. This session is designed for executives and implementation agencies who want a replicable approach to closing the deployment-adoption gap.

title: Get the Water to the Pond: Use Drainage Design and Analysis in Civil 3D
speakers: John Sayre, Sr. Technical Marketing Manager, Infrastructure Products, Autodesk | Charlie Ogden, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk | Prince Trinidad-Rhodius, Technical Marketing Manager, Water, Autodesk
topics: Water Infrastructure | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: In this session, we’ll walk through what you need to perform a pipe-to-pond drainage study in Civil 3D software, beginning to end. If you have to pipe the stormwater to the proposed detention pond or get it there by overland channel, you’ll see what it takes to create the study. This session will be fast and furious, but you’ll leave with the step-by-step process to perform the design. Hope to see you there!

title: Winning the Enterprise: How Brown and Caldwell Replaced ProjectWise with Autodesk Forma and Egnyte
speakers: Nick Decker, Director of Engineering Segment, AEC, Egnyte | Jeremiah Dunn, National Specialty Leader - BIM/VDC, Brown and Caldwell | Michael Rybacki, Project Owner, Brown and Caldwell
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | ACC Connect | Civil 3D | Data Management API | Forma Construction Connect | Forma Data Management | AECO
abstract: Discover how Brown and Caldwell (BC) transformed its design delivery by moving away from the rigid constraints of Bentley ProjectWise. In this real-world case study, BC will share how the firm unified its design and business ecosystems using Egnyte and Autodesk Forma, keeping systems natively in sync without friction. We’ll explore how BC achieved true platform freedom, allowing every user type to work exactly where they’re most comfortable, while ensuring central governance and auditability. Whether an engineer is modeling in Autodesk Forma or a project partner is collaborating directly in Egnyte, files stay completely mirror-matched across all formats—from DGN and DWG™ to XLSX—with absolutely no compromises. Designed for BIM/VDC and IT leaders, this session will provide the real-world reference architecture and checklist that BC used to maximize engineering speed and data integrity.

title: Concept-to-Consumer in 60 Minutes: Rapid Conceptual Design for Consumer Products with Autodesk Fusion and Vizcom
speakers: Jared Teiger, Community Manager, Vizcom | Kaelan Richards, CTO, Vizcom | Nicolas De Peyer, Product Expert Team lead, Vizcom
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Design Extension | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Fusion and Vizcom radically shorten conceptual design cycles for consumer products by pairing the Fusion parametric engineering and lifecycle controls with Vizcom’s real-time photoreal visualization and AI-driven variant generation. Learn how rapid ideation, material/finish sweeps, and perceptual testing produce validated visual states that automatically feed CAM snapshots, BOM and version updates, and manufacturability acceptance gates, preserving traceability and minimizing rework. The talk will include demos, concrete integration patterns, and data-contract best practices for the Fusion-Vizcom workflow. We’ll also cover a one-click pilot activation that turns validated concepts into prioritized production pilots with measurable POC outcomes.

title: Bridging the Gap: Custom Autodesk Forma Construction Connect Workflows for ERP and Owner Integration
speakers: Christopher Baze, Director of Construction Technology, Hawaiian Dredging Construction Company | Varun Bhartiya, CEO and Co-founder, nCircle
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Many firms struggle with "data silos" where project information is trapped between Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) and specialized enterprise resource planning (ERP) or owner systems. While off-the-shelf solutions exist, they often fall short of specific operational needs. In this session, Hawaiian Dredging Construction Company will share its journey of building custom integrations in Forma Construction Connect, with nCircle Tech as a consultant. We’ll dive into the technical architecture used to sync data between Forma and CMiC, and show how we automated reporting to owner portals. You’ll leave with a road map for evaluating custom versus out-of-the-box integrations as well as best practices for making Forma the central one-stop shop for field operations.

title: From Budget to Final Fee: Cost Forecasting Without the Guesswork
speakers: Heather Soderquist, VP, Construction Innovation, Jacobsen Construction
topics: Trust | Project Financials | Construction Operations | Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Unlock cost forecasting by exploring the range of tools in Cost Management in Autodesk Forma Build. In this interactive lab, you’ll immerse yourself in a real-world project, learning to create accurate cash-flow forecasts, manage revenue projections, and link budgets and schedules in one seamless workflow. Guided step by step, you’ll apply the new 3-Point Fee Enhancement to compare plans, forecasts, and fee goals. You’ll walk away with practical skills to identify fee risks early and forecast contract value with confidence.

title: Connected Preconstruction: BuildingConnected Workflows in Autodesk Forma
speakers: Ariel Castillo, Subject Matter Expert, Preconstruction, Autodesk | Cory Kintz, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Samira Tily, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, PreCon Products, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Build | Forma | TradeTapp | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: BuildingConnected has long been the backbone for bid management and subcontractor qualification at Miller Davis. As early beta users, Miller Davis has worked closely with Autodesk to test workflows that bring BuildingConnected into Autodesk Forma alongside Autodesk Forma Takeoff and Autodesk Forma Estimate. The Miller Davis team will share how Forma Bid helps reduce tool fragmentation and keeps preconstruction work connected within a single environment. We’ll discuss lessons learned from early adoption, and we’ll walk through familiar workflows reimagined in Forma—including RFP management, multiple proposals per project, bidder recommendations, qualification insights, bid leveling, and flexible reporting. The Autodesk product team will join to support the discussion.
