title: The Scan-to-Build Playbook: The Walsh Group’s Success with Autodesk Reality Capture
speakers: Emmanuel Graves, Technical Specialist, Construction, Autodesk | Rhett Rutherford, Construction Technology Manager, The Walsh Group
topics: Reality Capture | Construction services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Cloud Worksharing | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Join us for an insightful session on how The Walsh Group is transforming construction processes using Autodesk Forma and ReCap Pro reality capture. This session will explore the full journey from initial scanning to the final build phase, showcasing how advanced capture technologies improve accuracy, efficiency, and collaboration. Speakers will demonstrate real-world applications of reality capture within a connected platform, highlighting benefits like enhanced visualization, streamlined workflows, and reduced rework. You’ll gain practical information about integrating capture data into Forma to support better decision making and project delivery.

title: Design Like a Rocket Scientist: Generative Design Versus Topology Optimization in Autodesk Fusion
speakers: Roman Stoma, Student Structural Engineer, Elara Aerospace
topics: Aerospace and defense equipment | Fusion | Fusion Generative Design Extension | D&M | Product Development
abstract: What’s the difference between topology optimization and generative design—and why does it matter when you're building components with strict safety factors and manufacturing requirements? In this session for both CAD beginners and pros, we’ll explore the tools and workflows that helped Elara Aerospace design a launch-ready, record-breaking rocket capable of surviving the extreme forces of space. You’ll work through guided exercises in Autodesk Fusion software, learning how to apply both generative design and topology optimization to reduce mass, increase strength, and improve overall performance under tight constraints. By the end of the session, you’ll have built and optimized a component ready for spaceflight-level performance.

title: Informed Design API from Autodesk in Action: Real Workflows with Gaylor Electric
speakers: Jack Atkinson, Engineering Manager, Gaylor Electric, Inc | James Cotter, Production Innovation Center Manager, Gaylor Electric, Inc
topics: Building products and fabrication | Docs | Forma Data Management Essentials | Informed Design | Inventor | Revit | D&M | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: In this session, Gaylor Electric, a leading US electrical contractor, will share how it’s using the Informed Design API as part of its prefabrication and project delivery workflow. The team uses Informed Design to rapidly configure and generate design outputs early in the project lifecycle, enabling estimation, coordination, and planning before full project setup. You’ll see how these workflows work in practice and how configurable design approaches can support more-scalable project delivery.

title: Design and Manufacturing Tech Admin Meetup: Connect, Share, and Learn with CAD, PDM, and PLM Manager Peers
speakers: Paul Munford, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect - D&M, Autodesk | Ron Hyman, Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Industrial machinery | Factory Design Utilities | Fusion | Fusion Manage | Inventor | Vault Professional | D&M | Meetup
abstract: Are you a CAD manager, PDM/PLM admin, technology leader, or CAD geek supporting design and engineering teams? If you manage Autodesk software, data, standards, and/or users, you know the role can feel isolated. Meetups at AU are casual networking opportunities designed to help you find like-minded people and make meaningful connections. Join your technology manager peers across CAD, PDM, and PLM to connect, share experiences, and consider common challenges together. Discuss what’s working and what’s not, and get a fresh perspective on how others are managing their technology environments to meet business objectives. Leave with new ideas, practical insights, and a support network you can rely on long after AU.

title: Link It Up: Using the Electromechanical Link Between AutoCAD Electrical and Inventor
speakers: Bryan Fields, Subject Matter Expert, IMAGINiT
topics: Industrial machinery | AutoCAD Electrical | Inventor | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Curious about how to link your schematics in AutoCAD Electrical software to your models in Inventor software? Get an understanding of the functionality that links these two programs together. This session will cover the key elements you’ll need to know to bridge your design between AutoCAD Electrical and Inventor.

title: AutoCAD Electrical Works—Once You Tell It How
speakers: Melissa Vrobel, Engineering Team Lead, FTI | Luke Van Hecke, CAD Technician II, Faith Technologies
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD Electrical | Inventor | Vault Professional | D&M | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: AutoCAD Electrical software ships with powerful tools, but many teams struggle to move beyond the out‑of‑the‑box configuration into a setup that truly supports their design standards, workflows, and project scale. This class will focus on how to configure AutoCAD Electrical so it becomes a reliable production tool instead of a constant source of rework and work-arounds. Rather than focusing on schematic drafting basics, this class will emphasize configuration strategy, governance, and best practices that scale across teams and projects. You’ll leave with a clear understanding of what to configure, why it matters, and how to maintain a healthy AutoCAD Electrical environment over time.

title: Rivian’s Digital Twin Strategy: Turning Asset Data into a Product, Not a Byproduct
speakers: Derek Milz, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk | Alex Barilov, Lead, Production Facilities VDC, Rivian Automotive LLC
topics: Automotive and other transportation | Forma | Revit | AUTO | D&M | Preconstruction | AECO
abstract: Rivian is bridging the gap from Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to a full-scale digital twin by treating asset data as a product—not a byproduct. In this session, we’ll show you how assets are structured in Autodesk Forma, live-linked to model elements in Autodesk Tandem using Tandem Connect, and integrated with enterprise resource planning (ERP) and computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) systems to form a single, reliable asset backbone. We’ll break down the data standards, ID strategy, and integration patterns that connect design, construction, and operations. Using real examples unique to Rivian manufacturing plants, we’ll share lessons learned from early pilots, and we’ll describe how we manage change so teams across design, field ops, maintenance, and finance can all trust and use the same digital twin.

title: Innovators Stage | From Reality Capture to BIM: Preserving Fallingwater with Autodesk—Panel Discussion
speakers: Mark Dietrick, Director of Services, Case Technologies | Justin Gunther, Director of Fallingwater, Fallingwater | Touf Hassoun, President/CEO, Case Technologies | Dan Lohmeyer, VP, AutoCAD, Building, and Infrastructure (ABI) Solutions, Autodesk
topics: Reality Capture | Architecture services | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Explore how one of the world’s most iconic buildings—Fallingwater—is being preserved for the next century using Autodesk technology. This session will walk through an end-to-end digital preservation workflow—from reality capture using LiDAR, drones, and photogrammetry to BIM development in Revit and collaboration in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Learn how integrated data enables deeper insight, supports conservation decisions, and lays the foundation for digital twins. Discover how teams are transforming heritage stewardship through connected workflows, innovation, and scalable digital strategies.

title: From Sustainability Intent to Spatial Decisions: Integrating Environmental Performance into Autodesk Forma
speakers: Marta Bouchard, Dir., Sustainability Solutions, Autodesk | Armelle Langlois, Head of Sustainable Performance, VINCI Construction
topics: Architecture services | Forma | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: The future of sustainable design isn't about creating more data - it's about transforming fragmented information into connected intelligence that helps teams make better decisions, earlier. In this panel discussion, leaders from VINCI Construction and Autodesk will explore how AI, digital platforms, and connected workflows are helping project teams access the right data, in the right context, at the right time. Drawing on major infrastructure and building projects, biodiversity research, and digital transformation initiatives, the panel will examine how project requirements, environmental intelligence, and organizational knowledge can be brought together into one layered system to inform design decisions from the earliest stages of a project.

title: The Superb Guide to Easy Revit Rides On!
speakers: Rina Sahay, BIM Lead, Wade Trim | Nauman Mysorewala, Design and Engineering Technology Manager, GFT Infrastructure
topics: Architecture services | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Docs | Inventor | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: The award-winning Superb Team continues with enhanced insights into the ever-expanding world of Revit software and its friends. Our lively conversation spiced with weird, wild, witty, and wonderful war stories will energize you with the latest and greatest developments in Revit 2027 and Autodesk Forma industry cloud. Discover wild and wonderful things to do with Revit using native tools or third-party software for reality capture, visualization, and AR/XR. Use interoperability with add-ins and other authoring and visualization software. Get a glimpse of the future with innovative use cases using AI. Discover more ways and means to enhance productivity. Join us for wise and fun pointers on how to be a fearlessly productive Revit Warrior.

title: Reality Capture Now and Next: The Power of Point Clouds and Mesh Modeling
speakers: Olivia Morgan, BIM Specialist, SmithGroup | Mike Deacon, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
topics: Reality Capture | Data and Document Management | Architecture services | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Laser scanning has become indispensable for capturing existing conditions, yet getting that data into Revit efficiently remains a challenge for many firms. This class will show a proven real-world workflow—from registering point clouds in ReCap software to structuring and linking RCS files into Revit across a cloud-connected team in Autodesk Forma. Beyond today's best practices, we'll explore how the ReCap 2026 scan-to-segmented mesh capabilities and classification features can fundamentally transform the scan-to-BIM pipeline. As meshes increasingly replace raw point clouds as the geometry reference standard, you’ll leave with both a time-tested workflow you can implement immediately and a clear-eyed view of where this technology is headed.

title: Unlocking Enterprise Content: Real-World Content Catalog Strategies That Work
speakers: Paula Rama, BIM Consultant, slantis | Mahzad Fasih, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Cloud Worksharing | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: As organizations scale, managing digital content becomes increasingly complex. Fragmented assets, inconsistent metadata, and inefficient search workflows slow teams down and limit reuse. This session—co-presented with the Content Catalog product manager—will introduce the software’s latest capabilities, which are designed to bring structure, discoverability, and intelligence to content at scale. You’ll learn how new features enable better organization, faster search, and improved collaboration. Through a real-world implementation, slantis will show how Content Catalog is applied, from initial setup and governance decisions to daily workflows and measurable outcomes. We’ll also share lessons learned and strategies for driving adoption.

title: “Works on My Machine” Isn’t a Strategy: Controlling AutoCAD Xrefs, Standards, and Sheet Set Manager in Forma Data Management
speakers: Satheesh Kumar, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Dhananjai Gopika, Manager, Technical Support, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | AutoCAD | Desktop Connector | Docs | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Managing AutoCAD projects in shared environments often leads to broken references, inconsistent templates, and file conflicts. This session will focus on workflows using AutoCAD and Autodesk Forma Data Management (formerly Autodesk Docs) to bring control and consistency to multi-user projects. You’ll learn how to structure projects, manage permissions, maintain reference integrity using Connected References, and manage multi-user editing using checkout workflows. This session will also demonstrate how to deploy project-aware standards using Connected Support Files, coordinate deliverables using the new Connected Sheet Set Manager, and apply repeatable workflows to improve consistency and reduce errors across teams.

title: Collaborative Multi-Agents for AEC: A New Way to Navigate Design Decisions
speakers: Lorenzo Villaggi, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk | Nikita Klimenko, Senior AI Research Scientist, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Future Industry Innovations | Cross Industry
abstract: Achieving net-zero carbon in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) at scale can be complex, often requiring trade-offs between cost and carbon reduction goals, as well as new design approaches and workflows. Collaborative multi-agent systems (MAS) can unlock new opportunities for these kinds of multi-objective problems. At Autodesk Research, we’re developing and testing agentic-based capabilities for design decision making, including defining design representations for automated design exploration, navigating metrics trade-offs, and sharing design tasks. This talk will present our findings and demonstrate how they can be applied to real-world projects, as demonstrated through our partnership with LA28.

speakers: Nikita Klimenko, Senior AI Research Scientist, Autodesk | Lorenzo Villaggi, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk

title: From Dirt to Data: Automating Site Design with Dynamo as a Service and Autodesk Forma
speakers: Aaron Coffman, Senior Architect, SSOE | Daniel Drennen, VDC Technical Leader, SSOE Group
topics: Architecture services | Civil 3D | Dynamo | Forma | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: This technical deep dive will present an automated site-development workflow linking Civil 3D, Revit, Autodesk Forma Site Design, and Dynamo as a Service (DaaS). First, Civil 3D extracts the contextual data from a Forma project, analyzes grading limits, and generates back in Forma hatched “buildable pad” areas (max flat footprint without major walls/earthwork). Next, a Dynamo graph reads building program data from a spreadsheet. Then, the user selects the site boundary and pad outline in DaaS. And a Python node places buildings based on editable criteria (daylight, sun angle, wind, noise, orientation) to rapidly generate and compare options.

title: Design, Make, and Move: Real‑World Workflows on Slim Mobile Workstations Powered by Intel
speakers: David Butts, Virtual Design and Construction Manager, Kimley-Horn | Lindsay M Benjamin, ISV Partner Marketing Manager, INTEL CORPORATION
topics: MEP Engineering  | Structural Engineering  | Construction Operations | Building products and fabrication | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Fusion | Revit | D&M | Architecture
abstract: Design and Make teams are under pressure to deliver more-complex projects, faster, from anywhere. In this session, a frontline “super user” from industry joins Intel to show how Autodesk Fusion, AutoCAD, and Revit come together on slim mobile workstations powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 and Intel Arc B390 graphics to meet that challenge. You’ll see how the speaker’s organization moved from traditional, desk‑bound workflows to a flexible, AI‑enabled setup that keeps designers, engineers, and BIM teams productive—whether they’re in the office, on the shop floor, or on the jobsite. Revit drives rich intelligent models and documentation. AutoCAD handles detailed 2D and 3D work that still anchors many projects. Autodesk Fusion connects design, generative exploration, and manufacturing in a single environment. All of it runs on slim, professional mobile workstations—with integrated Intel Arc graphics and on‑device AI acceleration—without sacrificing performance or reliability.

title: Beyond the Foundation: Scaling 10 Years of Legacy Code for the Next Generation
speakers: Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc. | R.K. McSwain, IT Customer Service Manager / CAD Manager, LJA, Inc.
topics: AutoCAD | Civil 3D | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Opening a decade-old LISP file is like entering an ancient tomb: You half-expect a curse if you move a parenthesis—but, instead, you find how more than 1,300 people get work done. This "staple" launch sequence has been our firm's silent engine for more than 10 years, staying rock solid, even as we grew sixfold in size. In this case study, the original architect and a new innovator will share how we collaborated to honor this foundation while using AI to drive productivity. We’ll dive into modernizing legacy AutoCAD and Civil 3D code and providing IT with AI-enhanced detailed reporting and problem-solving. Join us to learn how to balance stable history with the future innovation required for the next decade.

speakers: Eric DeLeon, Founder & Principal Consultant, DeLeon Consulting & Coaching | Deborah Lilley, Sr Mgr, Community Strategy & Advocacy, Autodesk | Sam Karas, Program Manager - Community, Autodesk

title: AECO Roadmap: Data Solutions
speakers: Eddy Krygiel, Sr. Manager, AEC Data Model Strategy, Autodesk | Shilpa Ghanmode, Group Product Manager, AEC Data, Autodesk | Paul Markovits, Senior Group Product Manager, AEC Data, Autodesk
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma | Model Analytics | Model Derivative API | AECO
abstract: The AEC Data Model is becoming the shared language that connects design, construction, and operations as AECO shifts from file-centric BIM to data-centric delivery. In this roadmap session, learn how Autodesk is unifying files, models, and granular data through Forma Data Management and the AEC Data Model, unlocking governance, automation, analytics, and data reuse. We’ll highlight what’s next across Content Catalog, Extended Properties, Model Analytics, Parameters Service, Forma Assets, Datum, and emerging capabilities such as Information Requirements, Asset Information Connector, and Asset Registry. The result? Teams can access, trust and connect data across the full asset lifecycle.

title: AECO Roadmap: Data Solutions
speakers: Eddy Krygiel, Sr. Manager, AEC Data Model Strategy, Autodesk | Shilpa Ghanmode, Group Product Manager, AEC Data, Autodesk | Paul Markovits, Senior Group Product Manager, AEC Data, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma | Model Analytics | Model Derivative API | AECO
abstract: The AEC Data Model is becoming the shared language that connects design, construction, and operations as AECO shifts from file-centric BIM to data-centric delivery. In this roadmap session, learn how Autodesk is unifying files, models, and granular data through Forma Data Management and the AEC Data Model, unlocking governance, automation, analytics, and data reuse. We’ll highlight what’s next across Content Catalog, Extended Properties, Model Analytics, Parameters Service, Forma Assets, Datum, and emerging capabilities such as Information Requirements, Asset Information Connector, and Asset Registry. The result? Teams can access, trust and connect data across the full asset lifecycle.

title: Beyond Digital Twins: How AI and Engineering Models Are Transforming the Built World
speakers: mark king, Senior Product Manager - Reality Capture, Hexagon Multivista | Valerie Ashe, Sr. Account Executive, Hexagon Multivista | Mariano Franchini, Director of RC & Scan to Services, Hexagon Multivista
topics: Reality Capture | Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Engineering service providers | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | ReCap | Revit | Tandem | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: For years, digital twins have been presented as the ultimate goal of digital transformation. But today the conversation has evolved. The real value lies in creating a digital representation of an asset and enabling it to analyze, predict, and support better decisions via artificial intelligence. This session will explore how engineering models, BIM, reality capture, operational data, and AI combine to create intelligent digital ecosystems. We'll examine the evolution from traditional to AI-enabled digital twins. We’ll discuss the role of foundation and domain-specific engineering models. And we’ll explore how organizations can leverage existing digital assets to unlock new operational insights and automation. This session will provide a practical road map for those seeking to transform engineering and construction data into actionable intelligence. You’ll leave with a clear understanding of how AI complements digital twins and how technologies can drive measurable business value throughout the asset lifecycle.

title: Preparing LAX for the 2028 Olympics: AI-Powered Digital Twins with Autodesk Tandem MCP
speakers: Mingxun Zou, BIM Administrator, Los Angeles World Airports | James Awe, Sr Distinguished Architect, Head of Tandem Connect, Autodesk | Michael Beale, SWE, AWS
topics: Geospatial and GIS | Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Autodesk Viewer | Forma | Tandem Connect | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: With the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics approaching, Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) is modernizing to handle millions of visitors. Managing billions in capital assets across disconnected BIM, CMMS, and GIS systems is no longer viable. In this session, Mingxun Zou, James Awe and Michael Beale will reveal how Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA) built an AI-powered digital twin platform. We'll demonstrate the following: An Autodesk Tandem MCP server enabling natural language queries, a Python/Grasshopper automation extracting asset attributes to GeoJSON, and a real-time MapLibre visualization. Building on an Esri Dev Summit 2026 presentation, we'll show the evolution from manual CAD exports to AI-driven facility intelligence. Through live coding, you'll build the same integrations—preparing LAX for its Olympic moment.

title: From Model to Trust: Making BIM Reliable for Construction
speakers: Debora Machado, BIM Manager, Walter P Moore | Edward Leonard, Senior Technical Modeler II, Walter P. Moore | Jesse Young, BIM Integration Manager, Walter P Moore
topics: Buildings | BIM Collaborate | Build | Docs | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Digital delivery only works when models are reliable enough to build from. Yet many teams still struggle with trust, alignment, and inconsistency expectations. This session will share lessons from a large-scale structural project where model reliance became critical during the transition from design to construction. We’ll walk through what worked, what didn't, and how expectations shifted across architects and contractors. You’ll leave with a practical framework to improve model reliability and reduce coordination risk.

title: What Airport Restrooms taught us about Smarter Asset Data.
speakers: Liliana Martinez, Senior Manager, Design Technology, Port of Seattle | Mark Mergenschroer, Technical Success Manager (NAMER Adoption), Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Buildings | Build | Docs | Revit | Tandem Connect | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: At Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, restroom operations presented a familiar challenge: plenty of activity, plenty of data, but not enough trusted visibility into what was happening across the spaces, assets, supplies, and vendor work.  Not a new problem. An invisible one. This session will break down how Sea-Tac cut through the “smart restroom” hype by fixing the foundation first—structured asset and space data. Space IDs and Asset IDs were defined in Revit, carried through Build Assets, verified in the field, and connected through Autodesk Tandem and IBM Maximo. That’s when everything changed. Restrooms became measurable. Vendor work became verifiable. Operations became controllable. Because smart doesn’t start with sensors. It starts with data you can trust.

title: Turning BIM into AI-Powered Digital Twins: Real-Time Predictive Maintenance with IoT
speakers: Beril Oytun Çetinkaya, Architect, Metro İstanbul | Tolga Bozkurt, AI Digital Twin & IoT Specialist, Metro Istanbul
topics: Civil infrastructure | Autodesk Platform Services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Docs | InfraWorks | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Intelligent models are often underused after design, remaining static and disconnected from real-world operations. This session will present a real-world deployment in a metropolitan rail system, where BIM is transformed into a live, AI-powered predictive maintenance platform. Using IFC-based workflows derived from Revit software, models are converted into lightweight, web-ready formats and integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data at the asset level. An AI layer enables anomaly detection and failure prediction, reducing unplanned downtime and improving maintenance efficiency. You will gain a practical understanding of how to extend BIM into an operational digital twin and implement scalable, data-driven maintenance strategies.

title: Digital Twin Meetup (Volume 2): Digital Twins Meet AI
speakers: Steven Bloomer, BIM & Information Management Lead, GHD | Viv Devadas, AI Solutions Manager, Mott MacDonald | Mostafa Elashmawy, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Civil infrastructure | Forma | Tandem Connect | AECO | Meetup
abstract: Following last year’s digital twin meetup, this second edition will explore how digital twins are evolving with AI and reality capture across infrastructure and construction. Discover how BIM, geographic information system (GIS), and reality capture enable connected, data-driven environments that support simulation, prediction, and informed decision making. This interactive meetup will focus on real-world challenges, lessons learned, and practical strategies for scaling digital twins. Join an open discussion to exchange ideas, explore what’s working today, and understand how to move from static models to dynamic digital twin solutions.

title: Connecting a Nation: How MOEI Unified Infrastructure Delivery Across the UAE Using Autodesk Forma
speakers: Moza Neimi, CEO for AI MOEI, ministry of energy and infrastructure | abdulrahman alkholy, Digital transformation lead & AI, Ministry of energy and infrastructure
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Civil infrastructure | Forma | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: When the United Arab Emirates set its Net Zero 2050 target, the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MOEI) faced a critical challenge: Project data was spread across disconnected systems in seven emirates, creating delays, inconsistency, and poor visibility. This session will share how the MOEI moved to a connected delivery model using Autodesk Forma, scaled ISO 19650-aligned BIM standards nationally, created a single source of truth, and used AI-powered environmental analysis to support better design decisions. We’ll also share what failed, how we handled resistance, and the lessons learned. You’ll leave with a practical road map you can apply to government and institutional projects immediately.

title: A Year in Review: What You Might Have Missed in Autodesk Fusion
speakers: Kyle Williams, Senior Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk | Bankim Charegaonkar, Director, Product Management, Autodesk | Richard Hammerl, Senior Customer Advocacy Manager - Electronics, Autodesk | Sualp Ozel, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Peter Champneys, Principal Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Design Extension | Fusion Manage Extension | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | D&M | Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: Over the past year, Autodesk Fusion software has continued to evolve across design, manufacturing, electronics, and data—delivering new capabilities that help teams move faster from concept to production. In this session, we’ll take a look at the most impactful updates introduced since last AU. You’ll see how recent enhancements connect design and manufacturing more seamlessly, expand electronics capabilities, and improve data management and collaboration. We’ll also highlight the strategic areas of investment shaping the Fusion future and what they mean for the way you work. Whether you’re a designer, machinist, engineer, or product developer, this session will help you understand where Autodesk Fusion is headed—and how to take advantage of what’s new.

title: Naya AI and Autodesk Fusion for Physical Product Development: Estimation, Workflow, and Sustainability
speakers: David Gerber, VP of Business Development and Partnerships, Naya Studio | Saad Rajan, CEO & Co-founder, Naya Studio | Vivek Haligeri Veerana, CTO & Chief of AI, Naya Studio
topics: Project Financials | Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | Consumer products | Autodesk Viewer | Fusion | D&M
abstract:
Naya is an AI Product Development Platform for physical goods, from footwear to furniture, working with MillerKnoll, Adidas, Google, and hundreds of other brands. Naya connects to Autodesk Fusion.
Attendees will learn how Naya Estimation AI helps teams determine manufacturing cost within minutes instead of weeks from a Fusion model, Sketch, BOM, drawing, or CAD, move quicker through product development, negotiate better, and get more products to market at target price. With features for value engineering and scenario planning, teams can make more informed design decisions.
Attendees will also see how, from the same Sketch, BOM, drawing, or CAD, Sustainability AI generates a full environmental footprint in minutes: carbon, water, energy, and plastics, so teams can weigh trade-offs before committing to production.
Workflow AI brings briefs, BOMs, CAD, drawings, and more into one place so teams move faster, maintain accountability, and unlock greater creative potential.

title: Using Autodesk Forma Build and Autodesk Forma Assets for Heritage Rehabilitation
speakers: Andrew Macdonald, Senior VDC Manager, EllisDon | Arturo Baselli Gutierrez, VDC Manager, EllisDon
topics: Construction services | Build | Forma Data Management Essentials | ReCap | Revit | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: The Centre Block Rehabilitation is the restoration and renovation of Canada's seat of Parliament, including the removal, repair, and reconditioning of the building’s heritage assets. Using point cloud data, Autodesk Forma Build, Revit, and Dynamo software, the construction manager's virtual design and construction (VDC) team modeled every heritage asset requiring tracking and repair. Through Forma Build, the heritage team efficiently tracks and manages stonework for approximately 1,000,000 assets. This approach reduced costs by 40% while meeting schedule requirements. Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) centralizes issue tracking, scope changes, shop drawings, and asset management, streamlining the entire process using connected data and integrated workflows.

title: Agentic AI for AEC: Orchestrating Autonomous Project Delivery with Autodesk
speakers: Irene Won, Customer Success, Anthropic | Adam Sheather, Sr Principal, Solution Architect – APAC Lead Technical Advisory, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Forma | Revit | AECO | Software Development | Cross Industry
abstract: Agentic AI is rapidly changing how work gets done, moving beyond prompts into systems that can plan, act, and automate tasks across tools. This session will explore how to apply agent-based approaches using tools like Claude Code and Claude Cowork, Dispatch, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Autodesk Platform Services. In this session, you’ll learn how to connect agents to Autodesk data, manage authentication and permissions, and orchestrate workflows that automate design and project delivery tasks. Through practical examples, we’ll show how to combine agents, Claude skills, and APIs to move from isolated automations to scalable, end-to-end processes.

title: Breaking Data Silos: Connecting Design and Construction Insights with Power BI
speakers: Trupti Deshpande, Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk | Juan Diego Aranda Yaulimango, LIDER BIM, V&V BRAVO | Vishwa Shah, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Project data often lives in silos across design and construction, limiting visibility to real-time insights and slowing decision making. With the latest Power BI integrations, Autodesk is bringing together Data Exchange and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to enable unified, end-to-end project insights. In this session, you’ll learn how to combine granular model data from Data Exchange with project, issue, and asset data from Forma into Power BI to build actionable dashboards. Discover practical workflows, customer examples, and best practices that help teams connect data across phases, reduce risk, and drive better project outcomes.

title: An Agentic Future-State of Embedded Certainty Through Autodesk Forma, Informed Design, and KOPE
speakers: David Flynn, Co-Founder, KOPE | Mark Thorley, Co-Founder & CEO, KOPE
topics: Construction services | Informed Design | Revit | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: Discover the future of productization in Autodesk Forma. Learn how connecting Forma to KOPE and Informed Design begins to deliver on the convergence of construction and manufacturing. This session will show you how to use AI agents to translate generic design intent in Forma into constructible building systems, like detailed partition wall assemblies in KOPE, while adding full manufacturing components from connections to fasteners in Informed Design. By instantly transitioning to high-fidelity models, you use fluid workflows in Forma with instant, quantifiable insights that drive certainty around design risk and cost drivers in preconstruction.

title: Megaproject Scheduling Reimagined: How Boldt Aligns Field and Office with Outbuild and Autodesk Forma
speakers: Mike Wong, VP of Customer Success, Outbuild | Klas Berghede, VP Production & Innovation, Boldt
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | None | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Megaprojects don't just require more resources. They require a fundamentally different approach to planning, communication, and accountability. When hundreds of trades converge on a single site over years of construction, the gap between the schedule on paper and the field can compound into costly delays. Klas Berghede (VP of production and innovation at Boldt) and Michael Wong (head of customer success at Outbuild) share how Boldt integrated Outbuild with Autodesk Forma to bring structure, real-time visibility, and field alignment to Boldt’s most complex projects, connecting master schedules with weekly lookaheads and field data with the office to drive faster, more confident decisions at scale.

title: AI-Assisted CAM for Prototype Shops: Accelerating Autodesk Fusion Workflows with CloudNC
speakers: Ryan Walker, Machine Shop Manager, Avalanche Energy
topics: Aerospace and defense equipment | Fusion | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | D&M | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: Avalanche Energy operates a high-mix prototype shop where parts must move from design to machining in hours, not days. This session will show how the team uses the Autodesk Fusion Manufacture workspace with CloudNC’s CAM Assist to automate toolpath generation and accelerate CAD-to-CAM workflows. See how standardizing tooling, fixturing, and machining strategies enables consistent, repeatable programming across evolving designs. Learn how automation reduces programming time from hours to minutes, allowing programmers to focus on setup planning and process optimization. You’ll leave with practical workflows to identify high-impact automation opportunities, structure CAM setups, and scale fast, reliable part production.

title: Orchestrating Industrialized Construction with AI Agents: Connecting Product and Project Workflows
speakers: Andy Akenson, Distinguished Architect, Autodesk
topics: Building products and fabrication | Forma | Fusion | Fusion Manage | Inventor | Revit | D&M | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: Industrialized construction requires coordination across design and manufacturing workflows, but today these processes remain fragmented. This session will explore how AI agents can help connect product and project workflows, enabling earlier decision making and improved constructability. You’ll see how validation and specification workflows can be applied today within Autodesk tools, along with a phased view toward configuration, productization, and continuous improvement. A real workflow example will demonstrate how teams can move from disconnected automation to coordinated execution.

title: Autodesk Fusion Manage for Digital Factory ... What?
speakers: Harshit Gole, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Dave Graves, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Matt Zielke, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | Docs | Fusion Manage | Vault Professional | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: In this session, we’ll explore the complete factory asset lifecycle—from the initial procurement and commissioning of equipment to maintenance, optimization, and eventual decommissioning. You’ll learn how to use cloud-based PLM to gain real-time visibility into production readiness, track the health of your physical assets, and eliminate silos between engineering and the shop floor.

title: iLogic in Practice: A Panel of Experts on Rule Management and Automation Excellence
speakers: Jerry Berns, Design Technology Specialist, Newell Machinery Co. | Brandon Bibelhauser, Mechanical Engineer/Software Developer, FORTNA | Tiffany Hayden, Application Developer, KETIV Technologies Inc. | Paul Munford, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect - D&M, Autodesk | Curtis Waguespack, Design Automation Solutions Architect, Topper Industries
topics: Manufacturing Other | Inventor | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Join experienced contributors from the Autodesk Community Inventor Customization forum as they compare their real-world approaches to organizing and managing iLogic rules. This panel is designed for intermediate-to-advanced Inventor users and CAD managers who want to take their iLogic implementations to the next level. Panelists will share their real-world insights on internal versus external rules, the advantages of maintaining a centralized iLogic rule library, and proven approaches for structuring rule logic across parts and assemblies. The discussion will also tackle the pros and cons of event triggers and practical techniques for controlling rule execution more effectively.

title: Why GIS Is Essential to Design, Construction, and Operations in AEC
topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Michael Davidson, Senior Product Manager at Esri, joins the Digital Builder podcast to explore how geographic information systems (GIS) are reshaping the built environment. The conversation examines how location intelligence connects design, construction, and operations workflows, why GIS is becoming foundational for digital twins, and how emerging technologies including AI and open standards are changing the way organizations make decisions about the assets they build and manage.

title: From Preparation to Production in Autodesk Fusion: Serial Additive Manufacturing for Automotive and Aerospace
speakers: Vasyl Tymoshchuk, Project Manager, Yamaha Motors Europe | Dmytro Mukhin
topics: Automotive and other transportation | Fusion | Inventor | Netfabb | AUTO | D&M | Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: This session will focus on serial additive manufacturing using Autodesk Fusion software, with practical insights into designing and producing functional parts. We’ll cover real-world use of FDM and SLA technologies, including workflows with UltiMaker and Formlabs printers, and working with high-performance, flame-retardant, and rigid materials. Key topics will include defining proper tolerances and clearances, optimizing designs for repeatable production, and preparing parts for testing and certification requirements. Special attention will be given to early-stage design decisions—including integration of assembly fixtures and quality control features—considering material behavior and process limitations.

title: Beyond 4D: Resource-Based Construction Simulation with FlexSim
speakers: Anitha c, Junior project Associate, Desapex | AkshayKumar Pawar, Project Associate L2, Desapex Engineering Consultants LLP
topics: Automotive and other transportation | Fusion Operations | Inventor | Inventor Professional | Manufacturing Data Exchange Utility | AUTO | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: Traditional 4D workflows show sequence—but they rarely quantify how labor, equipment, and logistics decisions affect project performance. This technical deep dive will show how FlexSim extends construction simulation beyond schedule playback into resource-based decision support. Using a practical case study, you’ll learn how to connect schedule logic with crews, equipment, productivity assumptions, and site logistics. You’ll also see how to model the difference between resource-driven and time-bound activities. And you’ll understand how to compare workforce, equipment, and delivery scenarios before execution to identify bottlenecks and improve planning accuracy.

title: A Tale of (Digital) Twin Cities. A Tale You'll Actually Want to Hear.
speakers: Allen Weed, BIM Analysist / GIS Tech III, City of Portland BES
topics: Utilities and telecom | BIM Collaborate Pro | Build | Docs | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: In this session, we’re going to take you through the entire process of creating a digital twin for a wastewater treatment plant that’s more than 80 years old. This will cover everything from laser scans of existing conditions to creating assets that show live data and allow scheduled maintenance and access to drawings—and loop diagrams it. Let's explore how to set up Revit, Civil 3D, GIS, Autodesk Forma Data Management, Autodesk Forma Build, and Autodesk Tandem software to be used in far more ways than you may have considered. Learn with us how we create a management system that our future workforce wants to use.

title: From Pilot to Practice: How Lake Flato Evaluates and Scales New Tools
speakers: Daniel Stine, Director of Design Technology, Lake Flato | Ross Wagner, Head of Strategy, Pirros
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | None | AECO
abstract: Many firm leaders can name the software tools they bought last year. Fewer can say which ones are still in use. Dan Stine, Director of Design Technology at Lake Flato, walks through how his team decides what tools are worth evaluating, what they measure during a pilot to know whether a new tool is achieving its objectives, and what it takes to roll out a tool firmwide, including the parts that did not go as planned. He is joined by Ross Wagner, a former architect and Head of Product Strategy at Pirros, on the patterns that separate the rollouts that take hold from the ones that fall out of use after a few months. Attendees will learn how industry-leading firms evaluate the ROI of new software and incorporate new technology into existing workflows.

title: Forma CS Summit l The Forma AI & APIs Roundtable: Connected Data, AI, and Business Transformation
speakers: Jordan McKeown, Director of Operations, Pankow Builders | Matt Racher, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk | Edmundo Herrera, Principal Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
abstract: AI is everywhere—but where is it delivering real business value? Join this interactive Forma AI & APIs Roundtable, hosted by Autodesk Customer Success, for platform owners, administrators, innovation leaders, and digital transformation teams. Through facilitated peer discussion and engagement with Autodesk Product, SMEs, and industry peers, explore how connected data, AI, APIs, Autodesk Assistant, and intelligent automation are transforming workflows and business outcomes. Exchange ideas, learn from real-world experiences, explore Autodesk's vision for AI, and help inform the future opportunities and priorities shaping innovation across the Forma platform.

title: A Dynamic Lab on AutoCAD Dynamic Blocks
speakers: Tracy Chadwick, Computer Drafting Professor/Coordinator, Hutchinson Community College
topics: Architecture services | AutoCAD | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Why should you be using dynamic blocks? Quite simply, dynamic blocks can greatly reduce the number of blocks in your library, improving your efficiency. While it does take a little more time up front to create a dynamic block, the time saved on the back end makes it well worth the effort. Even better news: If you’re a proficient AutoCAD user, you should have no problem converting those boring static blocks into shiny, new dynamic blocks.

title: Learn How to Use Autodesk Forma Building Design by Recreating a Modernist Classic Design
speakers: Jesper Staahl, Senior Technical Marketing Manager, Forma, Autodesk | Arne Bjelland, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: This hands-on lab will teach a repeatable early-stage design workflow using Autodesk Forma Building Design through a controlled case study of a famous, modernist, residential icon. Using a shared reference model reduces project complexity and allows participants to focus on workflow, not design invention. Participants move from site context and massing to environmental analysis and iteration—then to facade and plan design options evaluated on daylight and solar performance, orientation, and layout design. The workflow supports continuity into Revit software, reducing rework and improving coordination.

title: AEC Roadmap: MEP
speakers: Ian Molloy, Director, Product Management, MEP, Autodesk | Martin Schmid, Prod./Prod. Line Mgr., Autodesk
topics: MEP Engineering  | Engineering service providers | Revit | Revit LT | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: For MEP teams, reliability depends on how well analysis, system logic, and detailing stay aligned. In this session, Autodesk product leaders will showcase the latest updates and share what’s ahead for MEP engineers, detailers, and fabricators across Revit, the AEC Collection, and Autodesk’s cloud collaboration tools. You’ll get a first look at improvements to modeling workflows, new sustainability-driven capabilities, and emerging AI-powered design assistance. This roadmap session highlights how Autodesk is advancing its solutions to better support multi-disciplinary coordination and drive greater project efficiency. We’ll also open the conversation—sharing what’s coming while inviting your feedback on what should come next.

title: From Quantity to Cost: Streamline Takeoff-to-Estimate Workflows with Autodesk Preconstruction
speakers: Dhruvesh Shah, Principal Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk | Ovais Mattoo, Principal Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Build | Quantity Takeoff | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Preconstruction teams often lose time when takeoff, pricing, and estimate updates are managed across disconnected processes. Manual quantity transfers, revision checks, and pricing adjustments can create inefficiencies, rework, and risk. In this hands-on lab, you’ll work through a connected Autodesk preconstruction workflow from 2D and 3D takeoff to estimate generation and cost refinement. You’ll learn how to capture quantities, apply formulas, push results into Estimate, manage updates, and use libraries, templates, and cost markups to standardize your process. By the end of the class, you’ll be able to create a more consistent, scalable process for turning quantities into cost insights with greater speed and confidence.

title: From Bid to Build: Unified Cost Management with Autodesk Forma and the Tech Ecosystem
speakers: Tyler Patton, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Project Financials | Construction services | Build | Forma | TradeTapp | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Cost management doesn’t happen in one phase—it spans preconstruction, risk, contracting, and field execution. In this hands-on lab, experience how Cost Management in Autodesk Forma Build directly integrates with BuildingConnected Pro, TradeTapp, DocuSign, and Rhumbix to break down silos, accelerate workflows, and increase transparency for stronger cost control. You’ll explore how teams can reduce risk, accelerate buyout, and streamline contract execution through integrated workflows. You’ll also explore how field data flows back into cost management, delivering real-time visibility and enabling more-informed decisions. Walk away with practical, repeatable skills you can apply immediately to implement cost workflows across your projects.

title: From 2D Layout to 3D Simulation: A Digital Factory Hands-On Lab
speakers: Dave Graves, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Mike jolicoeur, Sr Sales Specialist, Flexim, Autodesk | Harshit Gole, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD Mechanical | Factory Design Utilities | FlexSim | Vault Professional | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: In this hands-on lab, you’ll experience a connected digital factory workflow by executing it in real time. Starting with a 2D factory layout in AutoCAD using Factory Design Utilities, you’ll convert it into a 3D model in Inventor with a single click and bring it into FlexSim for simulation. The lab will also demonstrate how design changes are synchronized across AutoCAD, Inventor, and FlexSim, ensuring a connected workflow and reducing manual rework. You’ll gain practical skills to move from layout to simulation in minutes.

title: Unlocking GIS Data for Early-Stage Planning with Esri ArcGIS and Forma Site Design
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Discover how to enhance your early-stage planning workflows by unlocking GIS data from Esri within Autodesk Forma Site Design. See how the ArcGIS for Autodesk Forma extension brings real-world spatial context directly into your projects, helping you assess site conditions, streamline workflows, and make more accurate decisions from day one.

title: Lunch
abstract: Midday is made for good food and good company. Join fellow attendees for lunch and enjoy a relaxed break before the afternoon sessions begin.

title: Every Project Builds the Next: How Agentic AI Turns Design Projects into Software
speakers: Brian Lee, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk | Ray Wang, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | None | AECO | Future Industry Innovations | Cross Industry
abstract: Every design project starts almost from scratch — zoning analysis redone, energy models rebuilt, hard-won design logic left behind in last year's project folder. What if each previous project made the next one better? This session will present Autodesk Research's prototype system for agentic Design and Make. As you work through the different phases of a project, from conceptual design with physical models to collaborative design reviews with clients and engineers, the system captures your workflows and design knowledge as reusable software that compounds over time. When a new commission arrives with different requirements, that software comes with you, automatically adapting. Your firm doesn't just deliver results — it builds bespoke software that makes every project smarter than the last.

title: Every Project Builds the Next: How Agentic AI Turns Design Projects into Software
speakers: Brian Lee, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk | Ray Wang, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Future Industry Innovations

title: MCP on the Autodesk Platform: Three Production Servers Across the Full Stack
speakers: Enrique Galicia Tovar, Director of Innovations and AI, AvantLeap | Jose Baquero, Senior Consultant MGF - AI Solutions, Avant Leap
topics: Architecture services | Autodesk Platform Services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Software Development | Cross Industry
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the layer that lets AI agents access Autodesk tools, data, and APIs through a standardized interface. The firms building this infrastructure today will define the standard—not just use it. This session will go deep on three production MCP servers: revitDeploymentMCP (CI/CD pipeline as four AI-callable tools), a Dynamo MCP server (exposing Dynamo scripts for AI orchestration), and an Autodesk Platform Services Data Pipeline server (chaining the Model Derivative API, the Data Management API, and the Design Automation API without auth failures or silent webhook drops). Each server is examined at the architecture, implementation, and deployment levels. You’ll receive complete implementation patterns for all three.

title: Revit Cloud Worksharing Migration Has Arrived—But Linked Models Still Need a Control Plane
speakers: Moses Scott, Director of Platform Architecture & Data Insights, Woolpert | Zhong Wu, Principal Developer Advocate Engineer, Autodesk | João Martins, Principal Systems Integration Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | Autodesk Platform Services | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Many customers are struggling to migrate high volumes of existing Revit Cloud Worksharing models from BIM 360 to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). The process is often manual, slow, and difficult to scale. Autodesk Platform Services now offers developers a batch workflow that can automate this migration using Autodesk APIs. In this session, Zhong Wu, Autodesk developer advocate, will show what the new Autodesk Platform Services migration capability makes possible, while Moses Scott, platform architect at Woolpert, will show why linked-model scenarios still require preflight diagnostics, user-visible link-state guidance, and control-plane thinking before migration proceeds.

title: Innovators Stage | Whose Model Is It Anyway? (Comedy Show)
speakers: Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc. | Donnie Gladfelter, Design Technologist, The CAD Geek | Steven Bloomer, BIM & Information Management Lead, GHD | Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+ | Alex Eckhart, Principal Marketing Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Architecture | BIM Collaborate Pro | Civil 3D | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Step into the hilarious side of CAD and BIM in this 30-minute comedy show! Hear stories of mysterious warnings, impossible client requests, chaotic models, and the kinds of design mishaps that make you laugh, wince, and nod in recognition. Packed with jokes, relatable chaos, and surprise twists, this show will celebrate the absurd, unpredictable, and sometimes ridiculous moments that happen behind every model. Whether you’re a designer, engineer, or project manager, you’ll leave entertained—and maybe even inspired to look at your own files a little differently.

title: Innovators Stage | Whose Model Is It Anyway? (Comedy Show)
speakers: Dzan Ta, Autodesk Technical Specialist, Symetri | Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc. | Donnie Gladfelter, Design Technologist, The CAD Geek | Steven Bloomer, BIM & Information Management Lead, GHD | Alex Eckhart, Principal Marketing Specialist, Autodesk | Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Architecture

Whether you’re a designer, engineer, or project manager, you’ll leave entertained—and maybe even inspired to look at your own files a little differently.

title: Visualization as Design Practice: How CannonDesign Is Thoughtfully Incorporating AI to Rethink Design Workflows
speakers: Andrew Petty, Director - Design Technology, CannonDesign | Jeff Espinoza, Director of Customer Success and Services, D5
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Architecture services | None | AECO | Architecture
abstract: The relationship between design and visualization is undergoing a fundamental shift. For years, the rendering pipeline demanded a separate skill set—one that pulled architects away from design and toward modeling, tracing, and asset hunting. By integrating AI-enabled functionalities across workflows, CannonDesign stopped treating visualization as a downstream step and rebuilt it as part of the design process. This session will explore how real-time rendering and AI-enabled workflows are collapsing the distance between design intent and finished imagery, eliminating the 3D model-to-visualization handoff, and allowing architects to work directly on content rather than a representation of it. It's a new approach to design where clients engage with designs early, deliverables are experiences rather than static files, and architects invest more time developing strong design concepts. To illustrate the modern workflows outlined, the session will conclude with a D5 demo by Jeff Espinoza.

title: Content Creators Community Meetup
speakers: Neil Cross, Autodesk Software Consultant, Tech3D | Chris Benner, Community Manager, Autodesk
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Meetup
abstract: Join us for an enriching Content Creator Community Meetup. This event is designed for those keen on enhancing their craft, networking with fellow content creators, and discussing effective strategies for building engaging content and growing their impact. Whether you're a seasoned creator or just starting your journey, this meetup is your chance to connect, share insights, and learn from a supportive community of Autodesk experts and enthusiasts.

title: International Perspectives on Open Standards and Adoption
speakers: ERIC BUGEJA, Chair / Director, buildingSMART Australasia/International | Calvin Kam, CEO / Chapter President, SBI / buildingSMART USA | Claudia Cozzitorto, Director of Digital Practice, KPMB Architects | Jugal Makwana, Senior Business Development Executive, Autodesk | Najib Najib, Director, Head of Digital Delivery / Vice Chair, JESA /  buildingSMART Morocco
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | None | Architecture | AECO
abstract: This session explores the critical role of open standards in accelerating digital transformation across the global AECOO industry. As the demand for interoperability grows, the collaboration between buildingSMART International and Autodesk becomes a cornerstone for seamless data exchange and sustainable project delivery. Featuring a panel of buildingSMART Chapter leaders and Autodesk executives, we will dive into regional adoption trends, the evolution of open standards, and real-world strategies for implementing openBIM. Attendees will gain insights into how open standards drive efficiency, support regulatory compliance, and empower stakeholders to own their data.

title: Do You Trust Me? Building Trustworthy AI for Design and Engineering Workflows.
speakers: Ousama Lakhdar-Ghazal, Director, Trusted AI & Privacy, Autodesk | Nicolas Bonnet, Head of AI Trust, Autodesk
topics: Trust | None | Future Industry Innovations | Cross Industry
abstract: As AI becomes embedded in design and engineering tools, the question isn’t just what it can do—it’s whether you can trust it. This session will cover practical ways to make AI more reliable, including handling proprietary versus common design data—and validating outputs. You'll learn practical tactics for increasing the trustworthiness of AI models, with a focus on real-world challenges like distinguishing proprietary intellectual property from common design elements and validating the accuracy of AI-generated outputs. We’ll explore assessing inputs, adding safeguards, and creating feedback loops to improve performance over time—so you can adopt and build AI responsibly without sacrificing quality or compliance.

title: Customer Case: Explore Autodesk Workshop XR implementation in Wartsila
speakers: Johann Ackermann | Thomas Mård, IT Manager, Wärtsilä Finland Oy | Fredrik Rasmus, Senior Project Engineer, Wärtsilä Finland Oy
topics: XR & Immersive Tech | Engineering service providers | Docs | Navisworks Manage | Revit | Workshop XR | AECO | XR | Cross Industry
abstract: This session demonstrates how implementing Autodesk XR has delivered direct business value through faster issue detection and improved collaboration. By bringing project teams into a shared XR environment, design errors and conflicts are identified earlier, reducing rework, cost, and decision lead times. We will outline the workflow from Autodesk Construction Cloud (Forma) to XR ready VR models and show how XR is used in live new build projects to support joint reviews, stakeholder alignment, and informed decision making. The session also highlights future plans to further enhance value through GAMMA AR for extending the experience to construction site.

title: Fragmentation to Flow: How Vanderlande Connects Design, Delivery, and Operations with Autodesk Forma
speakers: Matthew Rowland, Engineering Senior Manager, Vanderlande
topics: Data and Document Management | Engineering service providers | Forma | Revit | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: Fragmented data, disconnected tools, and inconsistent workflows continue to limit visibility and slow decision making across complex projects. Vanderlande’s projects span design, construction, and operations, and maintaining reliable and aligned information is increasingly challenging. In this session, discover how Vanderlande is transforming project delivery across both airport and parcel logistics projects using Autodesk Forma as a unified platform. While airport projects require tailored approaches for each customer, parcel programs demand scalable, repeatable workflows across multiple sites. Explore how this approach replaces fragmented systems, improves collaboration, and enables consistent delivery across diverse project types.

title: Autodesk Platform Services GraphQL in Production: AEC, MFG, and Data Exchange Patterns from Analytics to AI Agents
speakers: Kevin Vandecar, Sr Mgr, Technology Consulting, Autodesk | Mayank Mridul, Senior Software Engineer, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Engineering service providers | Docs | Forma | Fusion | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract:
Autodesk's Data Model APIs for AEC and MFG, along with Data Exchange GraphQL APIs, use GraphQL—unlocking richer integrations, workflow automation, and AI-powered workflows. But GraphQL differs from REST in ways that quietly break production systems.

Our team has shipped analytics dashboards, workflow automation, Data Exchange workflows, and MCP servers letting AI agents query live design data. We've hit the pitfalls so you don't have to.

This session delivers production-proven patterns: query design for AEC/MFG Data Models and Data Exchanges, partial-success error handling, enterprise authentication, mutation patterns, and AI agent enablement via MCP. We also highlight the underutilized GraphQL capabilities in the User Profile API.

Real examples. Real lessons. Patterns that work from day one.

title: From Superpowers to Payoff: Turning MCPs into Real Business Value in Construction
speakers: Dustin Bolte, Senior Consultant Informationmanagement, Heijmans | Piotr Kruczkowski, Principal Solution Architect, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Viewer | Build | Model Derivative API | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: In this session, we share how Heijmans and Autodesk moved MCPs from innovation pilots to real business value in the construction industry. After 1.5 years of working with Autodesk Model Context Protocol (MCP), Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC), and custom MCP clients, we focus on what it takes to scale MCPs in daily workflows. Attendees will learn how we combined custom-built and off‑the‑shelf MCP servers to reduce administrative tasks, connect data across systems, and support engineers and site teams with a personal assistant (JARVIS). We’ll discuss architectural decisions, key challenges, lessons learned, and show live examples of MCPs delivering measurable value on real projects.

title: MEP Early, Not Late: Using Autodesk Forma, Revit Systems, and AI to Influence Design Before It’s Locked
speakers: Dagmara Romaniak, Architect Design Automation & BIM Specialist, Jacobs | Dawid Szczerba, BIM & Design Automation Specialist, Jacobs
topics: MEP Engineering  | Buildings | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Autodesk Forma Site Design isn’t just for architects. This session will show how MEP engineers can use Forma Site Design analytics to influence early-stage design, and carry design intent into Revit MEP through structured data and AI-assisted evaluation. Instead of reacting to fixed architectural geometry, MEP teams use Forma Site Design to inform early massing, orientation, and program decisions. We’ll use real project examples to demonstrate how early metrics such as area, volume, and orientation are interpreted from an MEP perspective and translated into system assumptions that feed Revit MEP workflows. AI-driven analysis supports option comparison, capacity estimation, and risk identification, resulting in fewer late redesigns and earlier MEP ownership of decisions.

title: Integrated Real-Time MIDP Using Reviews in Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Platform Services
speakers: Mateusz Lukasiewicz, Associate Director - Digital Technology, KEO International Consultants
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Keeping a Master Information Delivery Plan (MIDP) accurate on live projects is one of the biggest challenges for BIM managers and project managers. Issuing incomplete or unreviewed deliverables puts contracts at risk. In this class, we’ll show how Autodesk Platform Services Webhooks and the Reviews tool in Autodesk Forma transform the MIDP into a live system that validates deliverable metadata against information requirements and confirms review status before submission. Using real project examples and proven metrics, we’ll show how this ensures 100% compliance with contractual deliverables, eliminates manual tracking, and mitigates the risk of noncompliant submissions. Join us to learn how to build a QA/QC system that keeps your MIDP accurate, connected, and audit ready.

title: Turning Site Design into Quantifiable Flood Resilience with InfoDrainage and Civil 3D
speakers: Juan Aguirrebengoa, Principal Civil Engineer CEng MICE, Mott MacDonald
topics: Water Infrastructure | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Dynamo | InfoDrainage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Early‑stage flood resilience design relies on simplified assumptions, limiting understanding of how site-design decisions influence flood performance. This session will present an InfoDrainage‑led workflow to quantify flood resilience at site scale through coordinated parametric design and hydraulic modeling. The session will show how InfoDrainage, Autodesk Civil 3D, Subassembly Composer, and Dynamo software are used together to drive parametric site design and generate inputs for 1D‑2D flood simulation. Rule‑based design logic enables rapid, repeatable generation of site grading and flood mitigation solutions using Dynamo Player. The resulting BIM‑ready terrain and surface models support scenario testing across exceedance and climate change scenarios.

title: Integrating Company Policies in Autodesk Assistant: AI-Driven Governance and Automation in Autodesk Forma
speakers: Rodney Dsilva, Principal Solution Architect, Autodesk | Mark Kroezen, Senior Consultant (BIM Manager), Arcadis Nederland B.V. | Freek Matheij, Global AI Platform Director, Arcadis
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | Autodesk Platform Services | Docs | Forma | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: Explore how Arcadis and Autodesk embedded Arcadis policies and standards into Autodesk Assistant as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). This integration delivers tailored, policy-driven responses for cross-project maturity checks, quality control, and workload distribution. Learn how Autodesk Assistant proactively triggers issue creation and review workflows aligned with Arcadis governance, while seamlessly interacting with external systems to generate support desk tickets and schedule Microsoft Outlook meetings. Discover the architecture, AI insights, and automation patterns enabling smarter, policy-compliant project delivery at scale—improving compliance, reducing manual oversight by 40%, and doubling cross-region worksharing efficiency.

title: IFC’d Around and Found Out: Model-Based Quantity Takeoffs for Linear Civil Projects
speakers: Kyle Field, Construction Technology Lead, ISL Engineering and Land Services | Joshua Boardman, CAD Management Specialist, ISL Engineering
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Dynamo | Quantity Takeoff | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Model-based takeoff for linear civil projects sounds great, until Civil 3D-to-IFC exports leave out the quantities and metadata needed to actually price the work. In this session, Kyle Field and Josh Boardman from ISL Engineering will show how they used Civil 3D, Dynamo, and Autodesk Forma Takeoff software to bridge that gap. You will see how custom Civil 3D property sets can turn 3D solids into takeoff-ready bid items by embedding missing length and area data, carrying standardized bid item information, and making model objects easier to isolate and quantify. The result is a more scalable workflow with less retracing, stronger QA/QC, and cleaner estimating outputs for linear civil projects.

title: Building the Intelligent Catchment: Using InfoWorks ICM and AI to Create Cleaner, More Resilient Water Environments
speakers: Tony Smithson, Storm Overflow Director UK, Mott MacDonald | Samer Muhandes, Senior Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
topics: Water Infrastructure | Civil infrastructure | InfoWorks ICM | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Building intelligent catchments requires a combination of high-quality data, hydraulic modelling and emergency AI capabilities to support better decisions and cleaner, more resilient water environments. This joint presentation between the project director and the InfoWorks ICM product manager will explain how InfoWorks ICM was used to produce site-specific analytics and potential solutions to inform intervention planning. We’ll present the project timeline, key modeling and data pipelines, methods used, and how these outputs were embedded into decision support tools for key decision makers. You’ll see a short technical demonstration of InfoWorks ICM workflows, and get a peek into the future of using AI prediction capabilities. A discussion of practical outcomes for the water sector will follow.

title: Building the Intelligent Catchment: Using InfoWorks ICM and AI to Create Cleaner, More Resilient Water Environments
speakers: Samer Muhandes, Senior Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk | Tony Smithson, Storm Overflow Director UK, Mott MacDonald
topics: Civil infrastructure | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: The Only Rainwater into Windermere project represents a system-level approach aiming to stop sewage and highway runoff from entering England’s largest lake. This joint presentation between the project director and the InfoWorks ICM product manager will explain how InfoWorks ICM was used to produce site-specific analytics and potential solutions to inform intervention planning. We’ll present the project timeline, key modeling and data pipelines, methods used, and how these outputs were embedded into decision support tools for key decision makers. You’ll see a short technical demonstration of InfoWorks ICM workflows, and get a peek into the future of using AI prediction capabilities. A discussion of practical outcomes for the water sector will follow.

title: From Innovyze to Autodesk Tandem: Digital Twins and AI for Climate‑Resilient Water Infrastructure
speakers: Priyanka Talkal, Associate-Water, WSP | Parthasarathi Mishra, Associate, WSP Global
topics: Water Infrastructure | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfoWater Pro | InfoWorks ICM | Tandem Connect | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Water infrastructure is entering a decisive decade. In 2026, utilities face climate volatility, aging assets, regulatory pressure, and rising expectations for resilient, transparent service. Traditional approaches based on static hydraulic models and reactive operations are no longer sufficient. This keynote will explore how connected digital twins and AI are reshaping water infrastructure across the full lifecycle—from planning and design to operations and maintenance. It will present a practical workflow showing how Innovyze modeling outputs evolve into a live operational digital twin in Autodesk Tandem software, enabling continuity from design to asset maintenance, and supporting predictive, risk‑based decision making.

title: From Source to Farm: Digital Twins for End-to-End Irrigation with Autodesk Water Infrastructure
speakers: Rajeshwari Mynepalli, Technical Specialist, Water, Autodesk | Ayyer Sadal, Assistant Manager, Product Sales, CSTech AI
topics: Water Infrastructure | Civil infrastructure | Info360 Asset | Info360 Insight | InfoAsset Manager | InfoWorks ICM | InfoWorks WS Pro | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: Irrigation systems are often managed in silos: Reservoirs, canals, and farm distribution lack integrated visibility, leading to inefficiencies and water losses. This session will demonstrate how Autodesk water infrastructure solutions can create a connected, data-driven irrigation system. InfoWorks ICM is used to model river basins and canal hydraulics, while InfoWorks WS Pro simulates pressurized distribution networks. InfoAsset Manager structures irrigation assets for seamless integration, and Info360 Insight enables real-time monitoring and operational decisions. In this session, you will learn practical workflows to improve water allocation, reduce losses, and enable demand-based irrigation using simulation, asset intelligence, and analytics.

title: Bridging CAD and GIS: A Streamlined Workflow for Faster, Smarter Proposal Development
speakers: Joan Rickard, GIS Manager, Areli Corp
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Use Autodesk for fast drafting, quick design changes, and concept development. Then bring that DWG™ proposal data into your geodatabase to streamline integration with your existing geographic information system (GIS). Autodesk excels at rapid design, while GIS provides spatial context and publishing power. By designing in AutoCAD software and delivering through ArcGIS Pro or ArcGIS Online, you get both speed and accuracy for customer‑ready proposals.

title: Unlocking the Power of Reality Capture: The Leica CloudWorx Seamless Integration with Autodesk Software
speakers: Michael Harvey, Sr. Product Manager – Reality Capture, Leica Geosystems
topics: Reality Capture | Construction Operations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Geospatial and GIS | Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Navisworks Manage | Revit Live | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Reality capture has been in the industry since the late 1990s, evolving from its tripod-based roots to encompass many different forms of modern data capture. One could easily make an argument that reality capture has also grown from a handful of sensors to a wide variety of processes today. Regardless of where the data comes from, there has been one consistent and constant challenge that professionals still face: what to do with the volumes of data reality capture creates and how to make meaningful deliverables. This session will provide insight on how Leica CloudWorx continues to provide powerful tools for converting massive point cloud data into meaningful 3D models, 2D CAD drawings, and topographic deliverables. Furthermore, many tools in Leica CloudWorx serve as enhancements to the standard CAD tools that are in the Autodesk suite of software packages.

title: Design Without Disruption: Solving Electronics Obsolescence at the Source
speakers: Rogelio Gonzalez, GCET Apps Engineering Manager, Avnet
topics: Consumer products | EAGLE | Fusion | Fusion Team | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: At Avnet, our mission is to accelerate the adoption and seamless supply of new technologies. We understand the challenges engineers face when bringing innovative designs to life, and we’re here to help. Our latest app is designed to empower engineers by providing direct access to critical resources, streamlining the design process, and optimizing the supply chain. This session will be an engaged demonstration of Autodesk Fusion Electronics and Avnet’s App to solve for the most-challenging obsolescence problems within your electronics supply chain

title: Fusion + Naya: End-to-End Workflow for Physical Products
speakers: Vivek Haligeri Veerana, CTO & Chief of AI, Naya Studio | David Gerber, VP of Business Development and Partnerships, Naya Studio | Saad Rajan, CEO & Co-founder, Naya Studio
topics: Consumer products | AutoCAD | Docs | Fusion | Fusion Manage | Maya | D&M | Product Development
abstract: The next decade of physical product design will be defined by what teams choose to automate. Modern design tools should not just make things happen faster. They should free teams to focus on taste-making, creation, and human intuition, while quietly handling the repetitive work no one wants to do.
