This session explores how end-to-end product workflows, powered by AI and human collaboration, are enabling teams to design faster, more efficiently, and better for the world. See how Autodesk Fusion and Naya complement each other across the full design process, from first concept to manufacturing, and walk away with a strategic view of how Fusion and Naya enable a better design process, and where the next year of AI and workflow is heading.

title: Integration Workflows in a Stadium—Autodesk Forma As a Communication Bridge
speakers: Oscar Uriel Hernandez, BIM Specialist, GIA
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | BIM Collaborate Pro | Build | Navisworks Manage | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: GIA successfully delivered the new Oaxaca Warriors baseball stadium, covering 40,934 square meters, in just 12 months using BIM methodology and the integration of Autodesk Forma into office and field workflows. Faced with a tight 12-month deadline, complex coordination, and a large volume of project data, the team adopted a common data environment (CDE) to centralize information and optimize collaboration between the office and the field. This digital approach allowed for process automation, improved traceability, and optimized real-time decision making. The result was a high-quality project delivered on time, demonstrating how cloud platforms are transforming efficiency and collaboration in Mexico’s construction industry.

title: The Preconstruction Meetup: Ideas, Insights, and What’s Working
speakers: Kellie Herring, Customer Success Manager, ACS, Autodesk | Aaron Jech, Technical Success Manager, Preconstruction (NAMER Adoption), Autodesk | Samira Tily, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, PreCon Products, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | BuildingConnected | Forma Estimate | Forma Takeoff | TradeTapp | AECO
abstract: Preconstruction is evolving fast—and the way teams bid, qualify, and estimate work is changing with it. This meetup will bring together preconstruction professionals to connect with peers, exchange real-world strategies, and explore how leading teams are using data to make smarter, faster decisions. From improving bid accuracy to strengthening go/no-go decisions, join the conversation to hear what’s working, what’s not, and where the industry is headed. Whether you’re refining your current approach or looking for fresh ideas, this session is your chance to learn from others facing the same challenges—and winning.

title: A New Era for Stadium Design and Construction: Huntington Bank Field
speakers: Phil Dangerfield, SVP, Operations, Haslam Sports Group | Sidharth Haksar, VP,  Construction Strategy and Industry Partnerships, Autodesk | Patrick Wipperman, AECOM
topics: Data and Document Management | Construction services | Build | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Modern stadiums are no longer just places to watch a game. They are year-round destinations that serve as community hubs, host diverse events, and deliver exceptional fan experiences. As expectations for performance, sustainability, and operational efficiency continue to rise, the complexity of designing, constructing, and operating these facilities has never been greater. Get an inside look at the Cleveland Browns' new stadium, a landmark project across North East Ohio that is redefining how modern sports and entertainment venues are planned, delivered, and operated. Learn how the team is using Forma to create a fully digital project from design through handover.

title: Modular Data Center: Innovation and Performance with a Connected Workflow Powered by Autodesk
speakers: Carlos Silva, Mechanical Engineer, Modular Data Centers | Paulo Santos, Head of Design and Manufacturing, NTI Brazil
topics: Building products and fabrication | Forma Data Management Essentials | Fusion Manage | Inventor Professional | Vault PLM | D&M | Industrialized Construction | Product Development
abstract: In this session, we’ll explore the challenges and strategic solutions involved in the transition of the Modular Data Center from Dassault SolidWorks to Inventor software, along with the implementation of Vault PLM software and integration with Revit and Autodesk Forma. This change required us to overcome technical and operational obstacles, including compatibility with legacy data, migration of custom properties, and user adoption. We’ll demonstrate how we addressed these challenges and present the gains in performance and efficiency, highlighting the advantages of a connected workflow in delivering complex projects.

title: From Design to MAKE at ITT Flow Technologies: Building a Connected Digital Manufacturing Strategy
speakers: Trevor Mallaber, Designer, ITT Flow Technologies | Daniel Mills, Engineering Applications Manager, ITT Flow Technologies
topics: Industrial machinery | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | Fusion Nesting and Fabrication Extension | Fusion Team | Inventor | Vault Professional | D&M | Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: ITT Flow Technologies designs highly configurable equipment. But as with many manufacturers, the digital thread breaks as data moves from engineering to programming, production, and the shop floor. Disconnected CAD, CAM, and manufacturing systems reduce traceability and drive manual work-arounds, delays, and rework. This session will show how ITT Flow Technologies is reconnecting design and manufacturing using Inventor, Vault, and Autodesk Fusion software. We’ll review a real-world approach to creating a connected data flow across the product lifecycle. And we’ll assess digital maturity, identify high-impact opportunities, and build a phased road map that delivers early value while improving collaboration, productivity, quality, and efficiency.

title: "Level 4" Live "What-If" Digital Twins for Manufacturing Using FlexSim
speakers: Gergely Popovics, Simulation Engineering Manager, Flex Ltd. | Diana Ceballos, Simulation Engineering Manager, Flex
topics: Manufacturing Other | FlexSim | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: Flex has more than 100 facilities in more than 30 countries worldwide, manufacturing a wide range of products across seven different categories. To extend our forecasting capabilities, Flex GISE (global industrial and system engineering) simulation teams developed a web-based comprehensive (Level 4) digital twin application that users can adapt to support different types of manufacturing. The tool combines the FlexSim web server and advanced data-acquisition capabilities to deliver accurate, real-time forecasting and scenario-based decision support. It combines live production data with simulation, enabling users—even those with limited simulation expertise—to perform “what-if” analyses through an intuitive interface.

title: AEC Roadmap: Structures
speakers: Dan Peticila, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Pawel Piechnik, Director, Product Management, Structures Product Line, Autodesk | Piotr Pysz, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Structural Engineering  | Civil infrastructure | Revit | Revit LT | AECO | Civil Engineering | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Structural teams across design engineering, fabrication and construction face increasing pressure to deliver safe, sustainable, and highly coordinated outcomes on tighter schedules. Designers must produce accurate, analysis-driven models that inform decision-making, while fabrication and construction teams need detailed, buildable information for efficient execution. Discover how Autodesk is advancing model accuracy, enhancing analysis capabilities, and strengthening multi-disciplinary collaboration across the structural workflow, persona and project phases. You’ll also get an early look at features in development and get the opportunity to share your feedback directly with the team shaping the roadmap.

title: How Digital Preservation Is Securing Fallingwater's Future
topics: Construction services | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract: Justin Gunther, Vice President and Director of Fallingwater, Touf Hassoun, President & CEO of CASE Technologies, and Mark Dietrick, Director of Services at CASE Technologies, join the Digital Builder podcast to discuss how one of the world's most iconic buildings is being digitally documented and preserved. The conversation explores the intersection of historic stewardship and emerging technology, and what the Fallingwater project reveals about the future of managing, understanding, and protecting important built assets.

title: From Data to Decisions: Putting AI to Work in Construction
speakers: Ralph Schoch, Technology Manager, Victaulic
topics: MEP Engineering  | Construction Operations | Construction services | Revit | AECO
abstract:
The AEC industry has invested heavily in BIM, cloud collaboration, fabrication technology, and connected project platforms. Yet many teams still face the same challenge: turning all that project data into clear, actionable insight.

This session explores how AI can close the gap, connecting existing project data to surface insights faster, identifying risks earlier, tracking progress more effectively, and supporting better decisions across design, fabrication, and field operations.

Beyond the technology, attendees will learn what it takes to put AI to work in real construction environments, including implementation, governance, and lessons learned. Participants will leave with a practical framework for improving project visibility, streamlining reporting, and getting more value from the data they already have.

title: Small Business Roundtable - Media & Entertainment
speakers: Nikola Todorovic, VP, Emerging Technology, Autodesk
topics: Advertising, publishing, and graphic design | M&E | Media & Entertainment
abstract:
Hosted by Nikola Todorovic, Autodesk's VP of Emerging Technology and Co-Founder of Autodesk Flow Studio, this session will bring together fellow entrepreneurs, builders, and creators for an intimate, conversation-driven roundtable designed exclusively for small business customers. Limited to under 50 attendees, this session creates space for honest, two-way dialogue—no slides, no pitches, just real talk.

 Share what's working well in your Autodesk experience, discuss the challenges you're navigating, and tell us what you'd love to see next. Autodesk leaders will be on hand not just to answer questions, but to genuinely listen and learn from the businesses that use our products every day.

title: Autodesk Platform Services Viewer Reborn: A Developer’s Deep Dive
speakers: Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk | Alex Berner-Gandras, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Sebastian Dunkel, Sr. Principal Software Engineer, Graphics, Autodesk
topics: Autodesk Platform Services | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: This session will explore the next-generation Autodesk Platform Services Viewer, redesigned for performance and extensibility. We’ll break down its WebGPU-first rendering pipeline, large model experience, and the new API for programmatic control over loaded content. Through code-level examples, you’ll see how to optimize rendering, stream data efficiently, and build advanced interactions directly in the viewer. This session is ideal for developers looking to push Autodesk Platform Services Viewer beyond out-of-the-box capabilities.

title: Autodesk Tandem: What Early Digital Twin Deployments Taught Us About Real Value
speakers: Robert Eckdahl Ii, VDDS Solutions Leader, Black & Veatch
topics: Engineering service providers | Tandem Connect | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: What does it really take to make Autodesk Tandem software valuable beyond a demo? This session will share candid lessons learned from early Autodesk Tandem and digital twin planning efforts, including challenges around asset data, model readiness, contractor engagement, and owner expectations. You’ll gain insight into what should (and should not) be included in record models, how to align Autodesk Tandem with CMMS and operational data, and how to avoid common missteps that limit long-term adoption.

title: Miami Dade InfoWorks ICM Model and Master Plan
speakers: Ethan Hypes, Senior Principal Engineer, Hazen and Sawyer | Dimitry Lebedev, Senior Associate, Hazen and Sawyer
topics: Engineering service providers | InfoWorks ICM | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: As part of the Miami-Dade County Water and Sewer Department (WASD) Integrated Master Plan, Hazen calibrated one of the largest and most hydraulically complex wastewater models developed in InfoWorks ICM. It represented 1,038 pump stations, 3,200 miles of gravity sewer, and 980 miles of force main conveying approximately 310 MGD to three regional wastewater treatment plants that serve more than 2.3 million residents. The effort included long-term simulation and calibration using the InfoWorks ICM Ground Infiltration Model (GIM) to represent groundwater influence, detailed pump station simulation and verification, Ruby-script-based QA/QC and RDII calculations, and the use of the InfoWorks ICM model to simulate wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) hydraulics as part of an integrated system evaluation.

title: From Office Data to Smarter Decisions: Digital Twins for Workplace Optimization
speakers: Elliott Crossley, Director Digital Delivery, BDP | Siva Koppula, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
topics: Data Analytics and Visualization | Buildings | Revit | Tandem Connect | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: Office relocations are often driven by assumptions rather than data, leading to inefficient space use, unnecessary asset procurement, and missed energy optimization opportunities. This session will present a real-world case study from BDP showing how digital twins created with Autodesk Tandem software connect occupancy, energy, and asset data to drive smarter workplace decisions. By making existing data visible and usable, the team avoided £600,000 in furniture spend, enabled reuse of 71% of assets, and reduced required floor area by 27%. Learn how to integrate sensor data, structure asset information, and apply digital twin insights to reduce cost, improve sustainability, and optimize real estate decisions.

title: Bridge Design Automation: From Alignment to BIM‑Ready Deliverables
speakers: Tatjana Somova, Senior Digital Designer, Mott MacDonald
topics: Civil infrastructure | Forma | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Bridge teams face pressure to deliver faster, consistent, and low‑carbon outcomes. Yet, many bridge BIM workflows remain manual and hard to scale. This technical deep dive will demonstrate a workflow used on real projects to generate and compare bridge design options from a single alignment input. It will take you from option generation to coordinated models, carbon results, and a final decision point. The session will show how scalable, model‑based delivery enables faster optioneering and earlier sustainability decisions for engineers and project managers to drive better outcomes. In practice, this approach has delivered time savings on bridge projects, including the production of 20 bridge models within days.

title: Scaling Rail Data at MRS Logística: From Fragmented Workflows to Real-Time Intelligence
speakers: Camila Kfouri, Technical Specialist, Construction, Autodesk | Paulo Renato, Digital Engineering Leader, MRS Logística
topics: Civil infrastructure | Build | Docs | Forma | Insight | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: In a reality of more than 200 railway infrastructure projects running simultaneously, data fragmentation is not a risk—it’s inevitable. This technical deep dive will show you how MRS Logística tackles this challenge by refining BIM requirements and building a standardized common data environment (CDE) in Autodesk Forma. From issues and daily reports to audits, model coordination, cost, and schedule, workflows are structured and connected at scale. Discover how Autodesk Assistant enables structured analysis and how the Insight Builder tool turns connected data into real-time intelligence—driving consistency, reliability, and faster decision making across projects.

title: From Vague to Precise: Write AI Prompts That Actually Work in AutoCAD and Civil 3D
speakers: Stella Zhou, Senior Experience Designer, Autodesk | James(Jinan) Xue, Principal Software Tester, QA, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | AutoCAD | AutoCAD LT | Civil 3D | AECO | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Discover how better prompts can transform the way you work with Autodesk Assistant in AutoCAD and Civil 3D software. The feature just landed as a tech preview, but users who get value from it share one thing: They know how to ask. Most people type something vague, get a poor result, and move on. As the product team behind this experience, we’ve seen where the gaps are—ambiguous scope, missing context, overly broad requests. This session will use live before/after demos to show you how prompts with clear tasks, contexts, and constraints turn frustrating results into reliable outcomes for workflows like standards checks, counts, queries, and style changes. Whether you’re a drafter or CAD manager, you’ll leave with a prompt template library your team can adopt right away.

title: Developing Reinforcement Shop Drawings for Viaducts and Station Buildings Using Revit: A Case Study
speakers: Matias Mantilla, Sr Technical Account Manager, Autodesk | Lovneet MAHAJAN, Head of Department, SYSTRA MVA Consulting India Pvt. Ltd.
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Dynamo | Forma | Navisworks Manage | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: This session will look at a case study on delivering reinforcement shop drawings for viaducts and station buildings using Revit software at metro scale. SYSTRA India adapted building-centered workflows to infrastructure precast through a template-to-transmittal strategy which included: standardized content and shared parameters; parametric rebar families aligned to fabricator shape codes; and automation for numbering, scheduling, and batch sheet creation. Rule‑based QA checks, strict revision control, and ERP‑ready exports ensured traceability from model to yard. Results included 30% to 40% faster turnarounds.

title: Your Bottlenecks Are Showing: 10 Lessons from Thousands of Product Design and Development Companies
speakers: Jason Lichtman, Principal Technical Specialist,  Fusion, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Design Extension | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | Fusion Simulation Extension | Inventor Professional | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Designing great products is difficult. Successfully taking those products to market on time and under budget is even harder. After working with thousands of product design and engineering businesses, clear patterns have emerged between teams that struggle and those that consistently deliver. In this fast-paced 30-minute session, we’ll break down 10 key lessons that separate successful teams from the rest. We’ll dive into what worked for them as well as what didn’t. You’ll leave with practical strategies to reduce delays, improve alignment, and move from concept to production with greater speed and increased confidence. If you’re a business owner or business leader who wants to fast-track your company’s success, this session is for you.

title: Digital Twins and the Missing Middle: Strategies for Filling the Lifecycle Data Gap in Large Projects
speakers: Benjamin Wills, Senior Digital Delivery Program Manager, VEC | Bryan Blas, Digital Delivery Program Manager, VEC | Tadeh Hakopian, Program Manager, Digital Delivery, VEC
topics: Construction services | Dynamo | Forma | Navisworks Manage | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) teams excel at BIM for construction, but a "missing middle" exists between handover and operations where high-fidelity data often rots. For owners of 200MW+ mission-critical assets, this data gap creates massive operational risk. How do we bridge this divide to ensure a living digital twin? This session will deconstruct the missing middle using a data-first framework. We’ll explore how to use Owner Data Delivery Requirements (ODDR) and ISO 19650 to align design with operations from inception. Learn the technical workflows to migrate and validate data from Revit software and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll also preview how AI agents can automate QA/QC, transforming static models into actionable digital currency for the entire building lifecycle.

title: 30 Autodesk Forma Features You Should Be Using—But Probably Aren’t
speakers: Shir Rustici, BIM Program Manager, Turner & Townsend | Jonathan Hand, Technical Marketing Manager, Construction, UK, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Forma | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Are you getting the full value from Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), or just scratching the surface? In this session, we’ll go through 30 features across the Autodesk Forma platform that can improve how you design, analyze, and manage your projects. Some of these are well known but underused, and others are hidden in plain sight. The goal is simple: show you what’s available today and how to start using it right away. We’ll cover a mix of well-known capabilities that are often underused, along with lesser-known tools that are easy to miss but highly impactful. Examples are grouped across design exploration, data-driven analysis, and project coordination, so you can see how they connect into a more efficient, end-to-end workflow.

title: Industrialized Construction at Scale: Data-Driven Sustainability for Modular Systems
speakers: Mergim Hoti, BIM Specialist, Max Bögl Nederland B.V.
topics: Construction services | Revit | AECO | Impact & Sustainability | Industrialized Construction
abstract: How can industrialized construction, intelligent data, and integrated workflows turn sustainability from a reporting burden into a scalable design strategy? In this session for architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) leaders and delivery teams, Max Bögl Group will share how one company manages the value chain—from raw material sourcing and design to off-site production, delivery, assembly, and maintenance—to deliver modular buildings and bridge systems with measurable sustainability outcomes. As we use projects from Germany and the Netherlands, you’ll see how standardized, parametric products, connected models, and automated assessments help teams compare options faster, respond to strict European requirements, and build the data foundation for future AI-supported design decisions.

title: Data Exchange in the Real World: Customer Stories, Lessons Learned, and What's Next
speakers: Lejla Secerbegovic, Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk | Gaurav Bhamre, Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk | Anna Baranova, Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Civil 3D | Forma | Inventor | Navisworks Manage | Revit | AECO | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: What does Data Exchange look like when it’s solving real problems on real projects? In this session, you’ll first hear directly from teams using Data Exchange today and learn how they’ve connected disparate tools, reduced manual handoffs, and built more-reliable cross-discipline workflows. These are live production use cases demonstrating interoperability with measurable impact on delivery. Then, the Data Exchange product management team will connect these stories to what’s next, sharing road map priorities, upcoming capabilities, and the ways that customer feedback is shaping the platform. Leave with practical ideas to apply in your own workflows and a clear view of where Data Exchange is headed.

title: Connected Carbon Data for Construction: API-Powered Decisions at Scale
speakers: Dick van Ginkel, Technical Innovation Manager, TBI_WOONlab | Marta Bouchard, Dir., Sustainability Solutions, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Construction services | Forma | Quantity Takeoff | Revit | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Construction teams face growing pressure to make early, data-driven carbon decisions. Yet fragmented regional data sets limit consistency and scalability across tools. This session will explore how TBI, a leading construction firm, is advancing end-to-end carbon assessment by connecting data across planning, design, and preconstruction workflows. Using Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights (Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Forma Takeoff) and the Sustainability Data API, TBI will demonstrate how API-powered strategies enable early-stage carbon comparisons across multiple regions, reduce manual data handling, and scale assessments across projects. You’ll gain a strategic framework for driving better, data-informed decisions through connected, scalable carbon workflows.

title: Builders in the AI Loop: How We Accelerate Construction and Preserve Judgement
speakers: Richard Antczak, Senior Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: AI is increasing output across construction teams, but many leaders are seeing a quieter problem: more-polished work, less ownership. With more options come harder decisions. This strategy talk will use one concrete story and a practical framework to show how to adopt AI without eroding the judgment that experienced builders, designers, and owners have earned the hard way. You’ll learn how to separate AI-assisted production from the human decision making that takes decades to develop. We’ll discuss how leaders in the industry add thinking checkpoints within workflows that make teams faster while preserving their precious (and playful) cognition.

title: Automate the Last Manual Step: Scheduling MEP Fabrication Publishes with Stratus and Revit
speakers: Jake Olsen, CEO, Stratus
topics: Building products and fabrication | AutoCAD Plant 3D | Construction Cloud | Forma | D&M | MEP Engineering & Fabrication | AECO
abstract: Industrial contractors using AutoCAD Plant 3D already know how to publish DWG files to the Autodesk Construction Cloud/Forma. Now, the cloud-hosted model becomes the source of truth for Stratus as well, so VDC teams can access the full Stratus fabrication processing pipeline. You'll learn how this enables consistent model throughput from design to shop floor to field install, and avoids risk of spool fabrication teams working from stale PDFs, Isos, or 2D instructions.

title: From AutoCAD Toolsets to Inventor: Enabling Connected Workflows with Desktop Connector and Autodesk Forma
speakers: Sagar G S, Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk | Chaitanya Belsare, Sr Associate, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | AutoCAD Electrical | AutoCAD Mechanical | Forma Data Management Essentials | Inventor | D&M | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: This session will demonstrate how to connect AutoCAD Electrical electromechanical workflows, AutoCAD Mechanical linked with Inventor software, and factory design workflows for seamless data exchange. Learn how to integrate layouts and models across tools, enabling accurate coordination from schematics to 3D design. Discover how cloud-based solutions like Desktop Connector and Autodesk Forma improve collaboration, maintain data continuity, and reduce rework. Through practical examples, see how connected workflows enhance efficiency and accelerate project delivery.

title: From Reality to Production: ReCap Mesh Workflows and Model Coordination at Porsche
speakers: Anastasia Thoma, Sr Solution Architect, Autodesk
topics: Reality Capture | Automotive and other transportation | Docs | Model Coordination | Navisworks Simulate | ReCap | Revit | AUTO | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: Learn how Porsche uses ReCap software, mesh extraction, and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to create accurate “last stand” models of production factories before retooling. In high-cost environments where production downtime must be minimized, existing Revit models of assembly lines are compared with current as-built conditions using lightweight, segmented meshes. This enables precise adjustments or extensions of production lines with reduced risk. This session will cover mesh generation, semantic segmentation, and integration into Model Coordination, with real project insights and best practices for large-scale manufacturing environments.

title: The Re‑Emergence of the CPU for Your Workloads: From Traditional CAD/BIM to Agentic AI
speakers: Jamie Gwilliam, WW User & Industries Lead, Workstations, Intel
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Buildings | AutoCAD | Fusion | Revit | AECO
abstract: This session will answer a simple question for AU attendees: “In a world obsessed with GPUs, where should I actually spend my money across CPU, GPU, and NPU for my design, make, and emerging AI workloads?” For years, workstation buying has been “GPU‑first.” Agentic AI and modern Autodesk workflows are pushing CPU back to center stage as the orchestrator for both traditional and AI workloads. Traditional workloads (Revit model updates, AutoCAD drafting, Autodesk Fusion modeling, simulation, office, and collaboration) are still heavily CPU‑bound. Piling on GPU does not fix a starved CPU. Agentic AI and AI assistants add a new control layer that is CPU‑intensive orchestration: planning, tool calls, APS integration, retrieval, evaluation, and logging. The right answer is a balanced portfolio of CPU, GPU, and NPU—mapped to how AU customers actually work, not just to spec sheets.

title: Prefab Promised a Lot. Here's Why It Underdelivered.
speakers: Josh Lewis, Chief Operations Officer, FrameTec | Kaushal Diwan, WND Ventures Leader, DPR Innovation and R&D Sponsor, WND Ventures by DPR Construction | Scott Nyborg, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, Dusty Robotics
topics: Trust | Project Financials | Reality Capture | Construction Operations | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Buildings | AutoCAD | Point Layout | AECO
abstract: Prefabrication promises better quality, safer jobsites, reduced costs, and compressed schedules. But those gains only materialize when what you build in the shop connects precisely to what happens in the field. For many firms, accurate field layout is the hidden bottleneck between prefab strategy and prefab results, no matter what you build. In this session, hear from two firms that used automated layout to fully realize their prefab strategies across very different sectors. One brings experience from hyperscale data center construction, where prefab modules must meet tight tolerances across massive floorplates. The other operates in high-volume residential construction, where speed, repeatability, and cost drive everything—and where a misstep in framing snowballs into delays for every trade that follows. What unites them is how automated layout changed the relationship between the shop and the site. What they've learned will challenge how you think about your own prefab potential.

title: From Asset Data to Digital Twin: How Rivian Builds a Trusted Asset Backbone
topics: Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract: What does it take to turn project data into a digital twin teams can actually trust? Rivian shares how it treats asset data as a product, connecting Autodesk Forma, Autodesk Tandem, ERP, and CMMS systems into a reliable asset backbone. Hear how data standards, ID strategies, integrations, and lessons from manufacturing pilots are helping connect design, construction, operations, maintenance, and finance.

title: Forma CS Summit l The Forma Data & Insights Roundtable: Turning Data into Strategic Impact
speakers: LaShawn Hodge, Principal Account Services Rep, Autodesk | Brad Buckles, VP, Technology and Innovation, Charles Perry Partners, Inc. | John Prior, Sr Technical Specialist, Construction, Autodesk
abstract: What separates organizations that collect data from those that use it to drive meaningful impact? Join this interactive Forma Data & Insights Roundtable, hosted by Autodesk Customer Success, for leaders focused on reporting, analytics, digital transformation, and operational excellence. Through facilitated peer discussion, engage with Autodesk Data & Insights leaders, Product experts, and industry peers to explore how connected, standardized data within Forma is enabling elevated reporting, dashboard-driven visibility, and more informed decision-making. Share experiences, gain practical insights, and help shape future reporting and analytics priorities while building stronger connections across the Forma community.

title: Building What the Industry Won't: Running Your Digital Practice Like a Tech Start-Up
speakers: Alfonso Monedero, Digital Practice, Heatherwick Studio
topics: Architecture services | Forma | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Architecture
abstract: What happens when off-the-shelf software limits your vision? At Heatherwick Studio, Revit and Rhino software are our core engines. But true innovation requires breaking out of closed files. This session will reveal how to run your digital practice like a tech start-up by building cloud ecosystems that democratize data. Instead of waiting for vendors, we build tangible tools to expand our impact. Take “Nessie”: We bypassed the Revit UI so nonusers can access and modify data across multiple files at once, straight from the cloud. We’ll explore how to use machine learning (ML) and AI for automated QA/QC, how to deploy AutoDocs, and how to use DIGIPIN for collaborative review. Learn to architect an open, data-rich future that empowers your entire studio.

title: Don’t Wait, Non-Revit Developers! Create Your Own Revit Add-Ins Using AI and the Revit API.
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Many Revit users have workflow wish list items that could automate repetitive tasks or add missing functionality. This class will show how to create Revit add-ins. Aimed at non-developers, we will cover add-in basics. We’ll also show how AI can help generate and refine code while users stay in control. You’ll learn enough to review results, test behavior, and improve tools step by step. No programming experience is required. By the end, you’ll understand how Revit add-ins work and how AI can help turn everyday workflow problems into useful custom tools.

title: Don’t Wait, Non-Revit Developers! Create Your Own Revit Add-Ins Using AI and the Revit API.
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Many Revit users have workflow wish list items that could automate repetitive tasks or add missing functionality. This class will show how to create Revit add-ins. Aimed at non-developers, we will cover add-in basics. We’ll also show how AI can help generate and refine code while users stay in control. You’ll learn enough to review results, test behavior, and improve tools step by step. No programming experience is required. By the end, you’ll understand how Revit add-ins work and how AI can help turn everyday workflow problems into useful custom tools.

title: Industrialized Revit: How We Turned Tilt-Up and Precast into a Productized Delivery System
speakers: Josue Balderrama, Core Innovation Lead, Grupo Hermosillo | Pedro Alejandro Bermea Leynes, CORE Innovation Specialist, Grupo Hermosillo
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | Industrialized Construction | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Industrialized construction relies on repeatable systems, not hero modeling. In this session, we’ll show how Hermosillo applied that mindset to productize Revit delivery for tilt-up and precast projects. By combining standards, clearly defined deliverables, and end-user involvement, a core innovation team of designers (with no prior programming experience) used AI-assisted workflows, Dynamo, and the Revit API to build production-ready automation. The result: a system capable of generating hundreds of views, sheets, facades, and renders in under 50 minutes, reducing documentation time by over 90% and compressing weeks of work into hours. You’ll leave with a blueprint to replicate this approach and scale automation across your projects.

title: AutoCAD Support Clinic
speakers: Volker Cocco, Sr Technical Enablement Specialist - AutoCAD, Autodesk
topics: AutoCAD | AutoCAD LT | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Join a panel of Autodesk product support experts as they share practical tips and proven techniques to boost your AutoCAD productivity. This interactive session will include a brief overview of Autodesk’s support organization, key resources available to customers, and introductions to the panelists. You’re encouraged to bring real-world challenges—our experts from Technical Support, QA, and Licensing will be available to provide live guidance and solutions. A workstation with AutoCAD will be set up for in-session problem demonstrations, making this a hands-on opportunity to get answers to your most-pressing issues.

title: From Ideas to Outcomes with Autodesk Platform Services
speakers: Rami Kuret, Product Manager, Autodesk | Vasini Govindarajan, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Dwanill Mehta, Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: None | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract:
AI is changing how people build with Autodesk Platform Services (APS). Instead of learning APIs, stitching together integrations, and manually orchestrating workflows, you'll now be able to describe the outcome you want and let APS find, connect, and execute the capabilities needed to achieve it.
See how new AI-powered experiences are making APS more approachable for everyone - from experienced developers to Design and Make professionals who have never built with APS before. Learn how APS works with the AI interface of your choice, helping turn natural language into governed, repeatable workflows built on trusted Design and Make data and Autodesk capabilities. Whether you're new to APS or already building with it, you'll leave with a clear understanding of how AI is transforming the APS experience and how you can use it to deliver business outcomes faster, with greater consistency and at scale.

title: Measuring Perceptions of Trust: How to Turn Trust into Tangible Results
speakers: Kate Adam, Director, Customer Trust & Engagement, Autodesk | Mariluz Blandon, Director, Global Belonging Strategy​, Autodesk
topics: Trust | Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Inclusive Innovation, Culture, & Belonging | Cross Industry
abstract: In this interactive session, you’ll learn how to apply to your organization some frameworks for measuring and building trust. You’ll learn strategies for assessing trust across customer and employee experiences, and you’ll learn how to identify gaps and prioritize high-impact opportunities. Through guided exercises and real-world scenarios, you’ll map trust drivers—capability, reliability, transparency, and humanity—to key workflows, products, and culture. The session will conclude with a practical action plan to build trust, improve outcomes, and drive measurable business results.

title: From Single Client to Multi-Tenant: Forma Data Management Architecture for APS App Store Success
speakers: Matt Mason, Director, Software Development, IMAGINiT Technologies | Michael Beale, SWE, AWS
topics: Autodesk Platform Services | BIM 360 Build | BIM 360 Docs | Forma | Autodesk Platform Services (APS) | Cross Industry
abstract: When an independent software vendor (ISV) submits an app to the Autodesk App Store with a single Client ID, all customers share identical credentials—creating data leakage risks. This session will introduce the "robot-per-tenant" pattern: provisioning unique robot email addresses per customer (for example, acme-mep-robot@clientid.com), which ensures token scope isolation at the identity level. We'll cover onboarding flows, three-legged OAuth (3LO) token management scoped per tenant, Hub/Project membership automation, and audit trail design. Even application logic errors cannot breach tenant boundaries. Drawing from production deployments with Forma Data Management and Forma Admin APIs, learn how to scale from 10 to 1,000 tenants.

title: Prompting for Fusion: AI basics for Autodesk Assistant in Fusion
speakers: Sualp Ozel, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Luke Mihelcic, Senior Manager,  Product & Technical Marketing - Design, Autodesk
topics: Trust | Product Development | D&M
abstract: Learn how to use effective prompting techniques to accelerate script execution and add-in creation in Autodesk Fusion. This introductory session will cover prompt engineering fundamentals, practical workflows for generating and refining code with AI, and best practices for working with Fusion APIs and automation tools.

title: Next-Gen Rebar in Revit 2027: Bridges and Buildings
speakers: Ovidiu PAUNESCU, Senior Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
topics: Engineering service providers | Revit | AECO | Structural Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: This hands-on lab will introduce the next-generation rebar workflows in Revit 2027 software, focusing on placement, editing, and validating reinforcement in 2D and 3D views. The class will use practical exercises to address real-world situations, including bridge components and standard building structures. It will show how to model reinforcement with uniform geometry distributed within complex structural elements; manage changes to the bars and models; and extract fabrication information using tags, bending details, and rebar schedules.

title: Empower Your Designs: Combine Third-Party Models with Inventor Automation
speakers: Coy Pannell, Senior Designer, Subsea 7 | Anthony Muzzillo, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Engineering service providers | Inventor | AECO | Design & Engineering | D&M
abstract: Are you overwhelmed by the variety of 3D models from vendors, suppliers, or OEMs? Formats like STP, SAT, IGS, CGR, and OBJ may showcase product shapes, but they often lack features needed for effective use in complex CAD environments. In this session, you’ll learn how to use advanced templates and techniques combined with iLogic automation to create useful models in Inventor software. These templates will define connection points, establish constraint frameworks, set BoM descriptions, and even create accurate CoG work geometry on models that lack material properties. Join us for an engaging exploration of tips, tricks, and modeling strategies that will empower you to achieve your automation goals and elevate your design process.

title: BIM and VDC Professionals Meetup
speakers: Antia Rodriguez, BIM Transformation Manager, Hitachi Energy | Mariangela Toscano, BIM Lead (Europe & Middle East), Grimshaw | David Gonzalez, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Buildings | BIM Collaborate Pro | Forma Data Management Essentials | Navisworks Manage | Revit | AECO | Meetup
abstract: Join this interactive meetup for BIM and virtual design and construction (VDC) professionals to exchange ideas and experiences in an open, peer-driven discussion. Together, we’ll explore how AI and automation are being applied in BIM workflows, the realities of scaling BIM across organizations, and the lessons learned along the way—both successes and challenges. This is a collaborative space for participants to share insights, ask questions, and learn from each other’s real-world experiences. Whether you're testing new technologies or leading BIM implementation, come ready to contribute to the conversation.

title: Built on Trust: How Autodesk and Multiconsult Accelerated Revit Performance at Scale
speakers: Casandra Armeanu, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk | Thea Marie Danielsen, Head of BIM for Buildings and Properties, Multiconsult Norge AS | Stian Ingvaldsen, VP Digital Engineering Solutions, Multiconsult Norge AS
topics: Buildings | BIM Collaborate Pro | Desktop Connector | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: What happens when mega projects push Revit beyond its limits? For Multiconsult, 30+ minute open and sync times became a critical barrier across multidisciplinary teams working on highly detailed healthcare projects. In this session, we’ll show how Autodesk and Multiconsult partnered to expose performance bottlenecks by analyzing journal data, model structures, and sync patterns. Together, we optimized linking strategies, streamlined sync workflows, and strengthened model health practices, turning insights into targeted Revit hotfixes addressing scalability challenges in loading and regeneration. This collaboration built trust and delivered shared value. Discover how this work is driving scalable, cloud-centric workflows and how to apply it.

title: Digital Twins: Hot Takes and Cold Truths
speakers: Iria Carreira, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Karina Cardenas, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Tandem Connect | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: The audience for this session will be polled beforehand on digital twin hot takes and cold truths. Based on the results, former virtual design and construction (VDC) professionals working in the digital twin technology space will share a hot take and cold truth from their experiences. For example, a hot take is: "You can build a digital twin with poor data quality, set goals with an emphasis on 3D visualization over operational outcomes, and do many pilot projects without scaling into broader operations." We’ll identify opportunities and share anecdotes on empowering owners, operators, and their design and construction partners to connect capital delivery and facilities operations through digital twins.

title: Digital Twins: Hot Takes and Cold Truths
speakers: Iria Carreira, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Karina Cardenas, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract: The audience for this session will be polled beforehand on digital twin hot takes and cold truths. Based on the results, former virtual design and construction (VDC) professionals working in the digital twin technology space will share a hot take and cold truth from their experiences. For example, a hot take is: "You can build a digital twin with poor data quality, set goals with an emphasis on 3D visualization over operational outcomes, and do many pilot projects without scaling into broader operations." We’ll identify opportunities and share anecdotes on empowering owners, operators, and their design and construction partners to connect capital delivery and facilities operations through digital twins.

title: AI Agents for Electrical Design: Driving Revit with Model Context Protocol (MCP)
speakers: David Robison, Founder and President, Design Master Software
topics: MEP Engineering  | Buildings | Revit | AECO
abstract:
At the top of this session, I'll give an AI agent a real electrical design task: review the electrical system in a Revit model, determine what's circuited, identify what needs power, and circuit those loads. Along the way it will hit the questions an engineer actually has to answer. Do we add another panel, or work with what's there? How do we split the loads across panels?

While the agent works in the background, we'll look at how MCP connects AI to Revit, what tools an electrical engineer might give an agent, and where the engineer needs to stay in control.

You'll leave knowing what AI agents can and can't reliably do in Revit today, and how to start experimenting yourself. Whether the agent succeeds, stalls, or takes a wrong turn, you'll see exactly where the line falls.

title: Autodesk Forma at the Center: Designing a Real-World CDE for Multidiscipline Engineering
speakers: Rafael Lucero, Head of Digital Engineering EMEA, Parsons | Ian McGovern, VP Operations & Innovation, Parsons
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | BIM Collaborate Pro | Docs | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Many organizations adopt Autodesk Forma industry cloud as their common data environment (CDE) for BIM collaboration. But complex infrastructure projects rely on far more than BIM tools alone. Traffic modeling, hydraulic analysis, geotechnical simulations, and geographic information system (GIS) workflows often depend on specialized software that cannot operate effectively within cloud collaboration platforms. This session will show how Parsons implemented a practical CDE architecture with Autodesk Forma at the center of coordination while supporting discipline-specific production environments. You’ll learn how clear governance, ISO 19650 alignment, and defined workflows can unify multidisciplinary collaboration without constraining engineering delivery.

title: Building Tomorrow: Mastering Project Delivery in the Age of Technology
speakers: Kelly Barber, Chief Engineer, PennDOT
topics: Civil infrastructure | Build | Docs | Forma | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: As Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) continues to navigate its digital transformation, the team is using Autodesk Forma as the digital backbone for their Project Delivery Collaboration Center (PDCC). Capitalizing on the flexibility and interoperability of the Forma environment, PennDOT is able to connect legacy system data. Learn how PennDOT uses Forma to manage design and construction projects, as well as for its connectivity to other off-the-shelf solutions. Learn how processes are being streamlined, time’s being saved, and project transparency is all accomplished through the rollout of PDCC. To showcase its benefits, PennDOT will be sharing the current use of PDCC on its projects and the road map to the future.

title: Civil 3D Corridor Chaos Meets Control: A Hands-On Lab
speakers: Kristen Liggett, Senior Project Engineer, VHB
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Corridor modeling in Civil 3D can be a beautiful, efficient thing—or a nightmarish mire. If you’ve ever lost a late night trying to change one tiny end condition in a sea of them, this hands-on lab is for you. You’ll build and compare corridor models in Civil 3D software using a single-baseline, single-region approach with spiderweb-like conditionals. Then you’ll use a multiple-baseline, multiple-region approach with limited conditionals. You’ll test switching end conditions in corridor parameters; you’ll test how the workflows respond to design changes; and you’ll learn how a better-structured model reduces friction and rework, improves flexibility and design review, and supports faster, more informed project decision making at concept or final design.

title: From Handover Chaos to Operational Certainty: What Changes When Data Becomes Usable
speakers: Cristina Ispas, BIM Lead, Beheersmaatschappij Antwerpen Mobiel | Siva Koppula, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Revit | Tandem Connect | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: Infrastructure owners often face a gap between project delivery and operations, where asset data exists but is fragmented, inaccessible, and effectively invisible to operations teams. This leads to uncertainty, rework, and delayed readiness. While many approaches focus on how digital twins are built, this session will focus on what changes for operations once data becomes visible and usable. Through a real-world case from Lantis, learn how Autodesk Tandem software enables operational certainty from day one, reducing handover rework by roughly 30% and accelerating maintenance readiness by up to six months.

title: Information Management Strategies at the World’s Busiest Airport
speakers: Chris Harman, BIM Program Lead, WSP / ATLNext
topics: Data and Document Management | Civil infrastructure | Forma | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: Let’s talk about implementing a comprehensive information management strategy as it relates to BIM, digital twins, and asset data. In this session, you’ll hear about the new information management strategy created for the Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) Planning and Development department.

title: Autodesk Product Lifecycle Management Hands-On Test Drive
speakers: Giancarlo Caldarella, Account Executive, Autodesk | Bas Claassen, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk | Ashley Hooper, Technical Specialist, Fusion PLM, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Consumer products | Fusion Manage | Fusion Manage Extension | Vault PLM | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Get a greater understanding of how businesses can unlock the full potential of Autodesk Fusion data management and PLM in this hands-on workshop. Learn how to connect design data, streamline workflows, and standardize processes across the product lifecycle. You’ll explore key capabilities of Autodesk Fusion Manage, helping you manage product data, improve collaboration, and reduce errors from design through production. This session will provide a clear introduction and practical insights for anyone looking to get more value from integrated data management and PLM within the Fusion platform.

title: AI-Powered Digital Thread: Connecting Requirements, ALM, and PLM Across a Product's Lifecycle
speakers: Fernando Valera, CTO, Visure Solutions, Inc.
topics: Consumer products | Fusion Manage | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Discover how Visure Solutions and Autodesk unite ALM and PLM to enable a seamless digital thread across software lifecycles and physical designs. This session will explore how integrating Visure’s strengths in requirements and traceability with the Autodesk Fusion Manage capabilities delivers end-to-end visibility—from concept to validation. Learn how AI enhances impact analysis, automates traceability, and supports smarter decision making. Through practical use cases, we’ll show how teams can reduce risk, accelerate development, and ensure alignment across engineering disciplines, while meeting the evolving expectations of modern product development.

title: Ahead of the Curve: A VDC Leader's AI Playbook for When Your Organization Isn't Ready
speakers: Blake Titus, VDC Manager-Planning, Miron Construction
topics: Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: AI isn't just changing how construction work gets done. It's changing how the best leaders plan, communicate, and develop their teams. Most organizations aren't keeping pace, leaving forward thinking VDC leaders navigating the gap alone. This session delivers a practical playbook for managers already ahead of their organization with AI. Planning decisions get sharper, team communication gets stronger, and coaching conversations improve. AI tools get matched to your department's real capability and fit, including what's already built into Autodesk Forma. Credibility for leading adoption gets built even when policy or access hasn't caught up. You will leave this session with high-value entry points you can use this week with zero approval required from your organization.

title: AEC Roadmap: Autodesk Forma—Admin, Standards, and Insight
speakers: Sheryl Yang, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Ash Gupta, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Ross Collinson, Dir., Product Management, Autodesk | Jonathan Hand, Technical Marketing Manager, Construction, UK, Autodesk | Avani Saxena, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Construction services | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Insight | AECO
abstract: Operational efficiency isn’t just about speed—it’s about consistency, control, and clarity. In this session, we’ll explore how the latest updates in Autodesk Forma are helping teams standardize processes, streamline administration, and turn project data into meaningful insights. We’ll cover recent enhancements and what’s coming next across Project and Hub Admin, Bridge, Templates, Library, Reports, Data Connector, Dashboards, and more. Learn how we’re reducing setup time, increasing governance, and unlocking insights across projects and portfolios. If you want to scale smarter and operate with confidence, this session will deliver a clear path forward.

title: Innovators Stage | I'll Take "Clash Detected" for 400: An AECO Jeopardy Challenge
speakers: Tanmay Bhalerao, Sr Account Technical Lead, Autodesk | Fabiane Amorim, Sr Field Marketing Manager, AMER AECO, Autodesk | Erica Bowman, Account Based Marketing Manager, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Think you know architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) workflows? Prove it. In this Jeopardy-style session, architects, engineers, contractors, and BIM managers will go head to head across categories like "Clash Detected," "Connect the Platforms," "Coordination Gone Wrong," and "Who Owns the Data?" Audience members will compete live for a prize. And everyone will walk away with sharper cross-discipline instincts and a better understanding of where handoffs break down—and how integrated workflows fix them. Equal parts fun and educational, this session will turn real workflow pain points into a room full of engaged, competitive learners.
