title: Unlock Smarter Construction: AI Workflows in Autodesk Forma
speakers: Snow - Snezhina Shukina, Principal Customer Success Manager, Construction, Autodesk | Sarah O' Sullivan, Senior Customer Success Manager, Construction, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: AI is transforming how work gets done across the industry. In this hands-on lab, you’ll discover how Autodesk Forma Build enables AI-powered, intelligent data and integrated workflows to power transformation in construction outcomes. You’ll explore practical use cases on Construction Intelligence and AI Automated Workflows. Learn how AI in action can streamline coordination, reduce manual effort, and support more-connected, informed decision making across the project lifecycle.

title: Designing the Future Workforce Together: Connecting Education Outcomes with Industry Expectations
speakers: Michael Brackney, Senior AEC Customer Success Manager, US, Autodesk | Jason Roth, Principal Account Manager, US, Autodesk
topics: Education | Forma | Fusion | EDU | Meetup
abstract: Education and industry must work together to prepare the next generation of designers and makers, but how do we get there? What’s one skill students are missing today, and how do we help prepare them to design and make for tomorrow? This interactive session invites you to move beyond casual mingling into purpose-driven connection-building between educators and industry professionals. Engage in guided discussions, share challenges and insights, and uncover opportunities to better align curriculum with real-world needs. Walk away with meaningful connections, fresh perspectives, and actionable ideas. Join us and help shape the future workforce together.

title: Turning Curtain Walls into Configurable Products with Revit, Dynamo, and Informed Design
speakers: Daniel Noviello, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Building products and fabrication | Dynamo | Informed Design | Inventor | Revit | D&M | Industrialized Construction | Cross Industry
abstract: Coordinating Revit curtain wall layouts with configurable manufactured panel units is often manual, slow, and difficult to validate at scale. In this hands-on lab, you will use custom Dynamo nodes backed by the Informed Design API to connect a Revit curtain wall layout to a configurable unitized panel. Starting from a prepared model and scaffolded graph, participants will extract panel dimensions, send geometric data to the Informed Design API, and generate a complete manufacturing data set with shop drawings and parts lists. We’ll generate a report highlighting supported, unsupported, and changed panel conditions in Revit. And we’ll unpack the API concepts behind the nodes so you can adapt the workflow to your own products.

title: Ask the Vault Team
speakers: Senthil Kumar, Sr. Manager, Software Development, Autodesk | Jason Dai, Principal Engineer, Autodesk | Santhosh Palaniappan, Principal Software Development Engineer, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Industrial machinery | Vault Mobile | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: If you have any queries regarding the functionality and operation of Vault software, or if you would like to learn more about a specific feature, this session will offer an excellent opportunity to engage with the Vault team. The team comprises both the engineering and the product management teams, and they will provide candid and insightful responses to any inquiries you may have about Vault.

title: Unlocking Autodesk Assistant: Secrets of World-Class Data Management with Vault, Common Data, and PLM
speakers: Tyson Copa, Platform Specialist, IMAGINiT Technologies | Allen Gager, Applications Expert - MSD, Rand
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Industrial machinery | Docs | Fusion Manage | Vault PLM | Vault Professional | D&M | Product Development
abstract: World-class implementations don’t happen by accident—they’re built on deep knowledge of how to make Autodesk tools work together intelligently. In this no-fluff session, Allen Gager will reveal the secrets every expert knows for maximizing Autodesk Assistant across the Autodesk platform while building a robust common data environment (CDE) powered by Vault and Vault PLM software. Discover how to use Autodesk Assistant (now integrated in Vault 2027, Autodesk Fusion, AutoCAD, Autodesk Forma, and beyond) as your always-on, context-aware AI partner. Learn natural language techniques to find files faster, automate routine tasks, get in-context guidance, query project data, and even drive simple automations—without ever leaving your workflow.

title: Real-Time Digital Twin with iWG/iCG and InfoWorks WS Pro and InfoWorks ICM: An Italian Water Utility Case Study
speakers: Luca Serena, Principal, Sales Specialist, Water, Autodesk | Raffaele Marciano, Engineering Head Officer, Piave Servizi S.p.A. | Davide Russo, CEO & Technical Director, Idrostudi s.r.l.
topics: Utilities and telecom | InfoWorks ICM | InfoWorks WS Pro | InfoWorks Workgroup Server | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: In this session, we will look at 3,300 kilometers of water supply networks serving 344,000 inhabitants, 155 district metered areas (DMAs), and more than 400 monitoring stations—with one digital twin keeping it all together. Piave Servizi used Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP) to enhance water supply operational efficiency by adopting iWG, a web platform by Idrostudi. Integrating InfoWorks WS PRO advanced modeling engine, iWG digital twin creates precise virtual replicas of water supply networks (WSNs), enabling simulations, what-if scenarios, and pressure analyses—accessible to all operators, no modeling expertise required. By providing instant, data-driven insights, the iWG digital twin empowers water utilities to cope with daily challenges. And the journey continues: the iCG digital twin with InfoWorks ICM is bringing the same power to sewerage management.

title: From Plan to Pour: Aurigo Primus Plan and Autodesk Forma for Asset Owners
speakers: Johann Potgieter,  Director of Product, Aurigo Software Technology
topics: Project Financials | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Utilities and telecom | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Bridge the gap between capital planning and project execution. Led by Aurigo's director of product, this technical deep dive will explore Primus Plan and its powerful integration with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll showcase our AI-powered what-if scenario planning, demonstrating how to optimize multi-year capital portfolios before pushing them to downstream construction management. Walk through the technical architecture and data flows that move infrastructure projects from early-stage planning straight into execution within Autodesk Forma. Learn how to eliminate data silos, maximize funding, and maintain total visibility across the entire project lifecycle.

title: Reimagining Stadium Delivery Through a Digital-First Approach
topics: Construction services | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators
abstract: Phil Dangerfield, SVP of Operations at Haslam Sports Group, joins the Digital Builder podcast to discuss the Cleveland Browns' new Huntington Bank Field and the decision to make BIM a contractual deliverable for a major sports venue project. The episode explores digital delivery, owner priorities, long-term operations, fan experience, and lessons that could influence the future of major venue development.

title: What Structural Engineering Taught Two Start-Up Founders About Building Software
speakers: Ari Baranian, CEO and Co-Founder at Pirros, Pirros | Peter Johann, Co-Founder & COO at Pirros, Pirros
topics: Trust | Data and Document Management | Architecture services | Revit | AECO
abstract: Architects and engineers are often asked to adopt tools that fundamentally change how they work, without having had a voice in how those tools were designed. That disconnect can turn new technology into another process teams have to work around. Before founding Pirros, Peter Johann and Ari Baranian worked as structural engineers and experienced that disconnect firsthand. Using the development of a new QA/QC product as a case study, they will describe how their engineering experience helped them identify problems with traditional QA/QC processes, and how they partnered directly with Pirros clients to design, test, and refine the new product. Attendees will learn how architecture and engineering firms can provide feedback that shapes product decisions and how software teams can involve clients more effectively throughout development. Both sides will leave with practical ways to build stronger working relationships, and create tools that better reflect real project workflows.

title: Don't Just Imagine the Future—Build It: How Information Became the Infrastructure of Interior Construction
speakers: Diane Turnwall, Architectural Solutions  Director, Haworth
topics: Construction Operations | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | XR & Immersive Tech | Buildings | None | AECO
abstract:
The future of construction is often discussed in terms of new materials, technologies or products. Yet the industry's biggest challenges stem from an older problem: disconnected information. Every day, project teams recreate data, translate intent and manage friction when design, specification, manufacturing and construction operate separately. As expectations for speed, flexibility and sustainability increase, this fragmented approach is difficult to sustain.
In this session, Diane will draw from real-world examples, including the development of 4SPACE Rooms and a partnership with Autodesk. You will explore how connected data,manufacturable intelligence, AI and integrated workflows are changing not only how spaces are designed, but how ideas move from concept to reality.
Learn why information is a foundational layer of the built environment, how digital workflows reduce friction across a project lifecycle and what organizations must do to bridge gaps between innovation and adoption.

title: Residential by Design: Building the People, Templates, and Tools That Make Area Data Work
speakers: Rachel (Se Won) Min, Senior BIM Specialist, Kohn Pedersen Fox (KPF)
topics: Architecture services | Dynamo | Revit | Revit Cloud Worksharing | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Residential area data seems straightforward until multiple definitions come into play. Sellable, zoning, gross, usable, net leasable, supply, and target—they each serve different stakeholders and follow different rules. This session will present KPF's approach, starting with a cross-disciplinary committee that established shared standards and templates. At its core is an expanded area framework that extends Revit capabilities through Dynamo automation and parameter-based logic to produce reliable outputs directly from the model. Custom tools and dashboards streamline presentation plans, while light and air analysis tools support local compliance. Project examples from the United States, Korea, and Singapore show how these workflows scale across markets.

title: AECO Community Meetup
speakers: Nicola Ianeselli, Senior Director of Technology, Chenmoore | Briani Carey, Construction Community Program Manager, Autodesk | Alex Eckhart, Principal Marketing Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Architecture services | Civil 3D | Forma | Revit | AECO
abstract: Connect with Autodesk’s AECO community, including members of The Big Room, Autodesk’s online AECO Community Hub. Join us for a special in-person meetup designed to bring industry peers, community connections, and online conversations to life.Enjoy an interactive icebreaker, win some swag, and connect with your peers IRL. Meet the people behind the ideas, posts, and conversations happening across the online AECO community!Whether you’re already part of The Big Room or simply looking to meet more AECO colleagues, you’re welcome here. Stop by to say hello, share ideas for future community activities, and help shape what’s next together.

title: Automating Minimum Plumbing Fixture Calcs in Revit Using Schedules, Formulas, and Spatial Data
speakers: Gracey Carol, Practice Technology Project Leader, HED | Amanda Gioia, Practice Technology Computational Leader, HED
topics: Data and Document Management | Architecture services | Dynamo | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Minimum plumbing fixture (MPF) calculations are often inconsistent, time-consuming, and dependent on Microsoft Excel (and the users' capabilities within it). This session will demonstrate how to integrate MPF calculations directly within Revit software using repurposed area data, project parameters, key schedules, and formulas. You’ll learn how to implement piecewise functions to reflect code requirements, apply consistent rounding methods, and incorporate strategic overrides. This course will also introduce color scheme visualization to communicate fixture demand clearly to project teams and Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs). By the end, you’ll produce standardized, accurate, and code-compliant plumbing fixture calculations entirely within Revit, with a little help from Dynamo.

title: Stuck? Unlock Solutions with Autodesk Expert Elites.
speakers: Deepak Maini, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk | Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc. | Todd Rogers, Civil Administration, Walter P Moore | Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+ | Cary Mandell, Principal Customer Advocate, Autodesk
topics: 3ds Max 2 | AutoCAD | Fusion | Inventor | Revit | Community & Expert Elites
abstract: Got a challenge you just can’t crack? Bring it with you! In this interactive “Ask an Expert” session, you’ll engage in group conversations led by Autodesk Expert Elites to troubleshoot real-world issues together with your peers. Whether you’re dealing with a stubborn assembly, broken references, animation problems, or unclear workflows, this is your chance to get unstuck. There’s no formal presentation—just collaborative problem-solving, shared insights, and practical guidance tailored to the questions in the room. Come with your toughest issues, learn from others, and leave with actionable solutions.

title: Beyond AEC: Designing a Climate-Resilient Agroforestry System with Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Platform Services
speakers: Juan David Hurtado Henao, Owner - General Manager, Blue Bird Coffee
topics: Autodesk Platform Services | Build | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: What if the tools we use to design buildings could also save coffee farming? This session will present a real pilot from Colombia where Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Platform Services are used to design Climate-Resilient Agroforestry Systems. See a live Autodesk Forma Site Design demo of digital twin shade and microclimate simulations. Discover how to use Autodesk Forma Data Management to capture geolocated pest data, Brix readings, and reforestation tasks. And learn how Autodesk Platform Services connects it all into actionable farm intelligence. Outcomes include a 67% reduction in coffee berry borer infestation, and layout decisions that once required years now being validated in days. You’ll leave this session with a new mental model for where Autodesk platforms can drive sustainability impact beyond construction.

title: Autodesk Young Professionals & Veterans Network Meetup
speakers: Shashwat Bhardwaj, Sr Account Technical Lead, Autodesk | Kimberly Fuhrman-Jones, Community Manager, Autodesk | Kristina Poluyanova, Sales Specialist, Construction, Autodesk | Booth Staff, test
topics: Inclusive Innovation, Culture, and Belonging | None | Meetup
abstract: This meetup is sponsored by Autodesk Employee Belonging Groups (EBGs) to support connection and shared growth across communities. We bring employees and customers together through interactive, networking-focused experiences. Participants will engage in small-group conversations designed to encourage meaningful dialogue, knowledge sharing, and relationship building across teams, roles, and communities.

title: AI-Connected Workflows: Fusion, Claude, and MCP 101
speakers: Brian Frank, Sr. Director, Product Management, Autodesk | Patrick Rainsberry, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Luke Mihelcic, Senior Manager,  Product & Technical Marketing - Design, Autodesk
topics: Trust | Product Development | D&M
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Fusion, Claude, and MCP (Model Context Protocol) can work together to create smarter, more connected engineering workflows. This introductory session will explore how conversational AI can assist with design, automation, scripting, documentation, and workflow generation inside Fusion environments, while MCP enables secure connections between AI, tools, and data sources. Attendees will learn foundational concepts, practical integration examples, and real-world use cases that demonstrate how AI-driven workflows can improve productivity, collaboration, and decision-making across product development and manufacturing.

title: One Platform, Global Ambitions: Bridging the Gap Between CDE Vision and Reality
speakers: Maxence BOUTIN, Project manager - Collaborative Platform, Bouygues Construction IT | Aurélien DESCHAMPS, Head of BIM / Interior Design / XR, Bouygues Batiment International
topics: Data and Document Management | Buildings | BIM Collaborate Pro | Build | Docs | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Common data environments (CDEs) promise a single platform to manage construction workflows—but how do they perform on real international projects? At Bouygues Construction, we deployed Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) from tender to construction across multiple autonomous projects. This session will share what worked, what didn’t, and why. Learn how field teams actually used the platform, where gaps required complementary tools (for example, progress tracking and document control), and why centralized governance models fell short. Discover how a shift toward an enablement-driven approach improved adoption, and gain a practical framework to assess CDE platforms, design realistic governance, and support digital adoption in decentralized environments.

title: openBIM and Interoperability Workflows at Autodesk: 2026 Edition
speakers: Angel Velez, Distinguished Engineer, Autodesk | Lejla Secerbegovic, Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk | Janina Sánchez, Senior Product Manager - Revit Data Workflows, Autodesk
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Buildings | Civil 3D | Forma | Model Coordination | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Workflows based in openBIM enable interoperability and collaboration among different software applications and stakeholders in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry using neutral, industry-standard formats. These workflows center around Industry Foundation Classes (IFC), an open and neutral data format for BIM. In a continuing series, you'll learn about the Autodesk strategy around IFC and openBIM, the newest and future capabilities of Revit, and other AEC products supporting openBIM workflows. And you’ll learn how these standards are being used in defining the AEC Data Model API and granular cloud data workflows. As a bonus, we'll also offer some insights for Revit users to optimize their IFC usage.

title: Powering Paperless Contractor Submissions and Tracking Across 50 Million Square Feet with Autodesk Forma and Data Analytics
speakers: Ritesh Mittal, General Manager, DLF Limited | Japneesh Singh, Deputy Manager, DLF
topics: Construction Operations | Buildings | BIM 360 Build | Build | Forma | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Disconnected contractor submissions and manual tracking reduce visibility, slow approvals, and limit scalability. In this session, you’ll learn how a paperless submission framework was deployed across a 50-million-square-foot portfolio using Autodesk Forma. Integrated workflows were established using Submittals, RFIs, and Forms to standardize contractor interactions, enable consistent data capture, and ensure full traceability. Through APIs, disparate data sources were unified and transformed into intelligent data models that power advanced dashboards. Discover how this approach delivers real-time submission tracking, improved transparency, and faster data-driven decisions—providing a scalable blueprint for digital transformation at an enterprise level.

title: Streamlined Stormwater Design with InfoDrainage
speakers: John Neff, Civil Engineer, Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc | Mike Pizzino, Technical Account Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | InfoDrainage | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Many stormwater design teams rely on workflows that bounce between multiple programs, require repeated file transfers, and depend on clunky spreadsheets. This approach is inefficient, prone to error, and difficult to scale across an organization. InfoDrainage, on the other hand, allows for robust stormwater design all in one place, and easily round-trips with Civil 3D software. In this class, we’ll show where Kimley-Horn teams saw meaningful efficiency gains in generating RCNs and round-tripping storm drain networks. Drawing on Kimley-Horn’s collaboration with Autodesk, we’ll discuss how real-world needs shaped InfoDrainage to benefit both project teams and the industry more broadly. Mike Pizzino, InfoDrainage expert at Autodesk, will co-present.

title: Civil BIM Runway Digital Twin
speakers: Clint Davis, Sr. Civil BIM Project Manager, Denver International Airport
topics: Reality Capture | Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Inventor | ReCap | AECO | Infrastructure Owners
abstract: See how more than a decade of standardized design projects have been aggregated into a digital twin runway for one of the world’s busiest airports. How can owners use verified utility designs to drive maintenance and regulatory compliance? In Denver, we’re tracking sanitary sewer, storm sewer, aircraft de-icing fluid delivery and recovery, jet fuel, water, electrical duct banks, airfield lighting and signs, and pavement models to inform future design and current operations. As the puzzle comes together, see how we can visualize a clear picture of our infrastructure.

title: Overcoming the Seven Deadly Sins of Civil 3D Project Performance
speakers: Donnie Gladfelter, Design Technologist, The CAD Geek
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: All you did was click “Open.” Now your fans are spinning at Mach 3D, and if your laptop were slightly more aerodynamic, it would likely defenestrate itself. Your Civil 3D project didn't slow down on its own. It was sinned against. None of it felt wrong at the time. Seven structural decisions are buried in your data management, file setup, and modeling workflows that Civil 3D punishes quietly and without warning until your 13-minute regen hits 42 minutes and sincity.dwg is due tomorrow. Donnie Gladfelter, Autodesk Expert Elite and AU Top Speaker, names the sins, earns each one its absolution—and sends you home with a project built the way Civil 3D actually wants to work. From first alignment to final handoff. Your laptop will thank you.

title: From Prompt to Production: Designing Furniture at the Speed of AI with Autodesk Fusion
speakers: Melike Ozdemir, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Consumer products | Fusion | Fusion Manage | Fusion Nesting and Fabrication Extension | Fusion Operations | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Designing and manufacturing furniture often relies on disconnected tools and repetitive work. This session will explain how to create a connected, end-to-end workflow using the Autodesk Fusion platform. Starting from simple prompts, Autodesk Assistant accelerates design and enables fast creation of parametric furniture models. This workflow will show how models are refined for engineering, prepared for manufacturing with integrated CAM tools, and transferred to production using Autodesk Fusion Operations software—while Autodesk Fusion Manage ensures process and data continuity from request to delivery. It will also highlight how design intent is preserved and how a single data environment reduces errors.

title: AEC Roadmap: Autodesk Forma for Preconstruction
speakers: Chico Membreno, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Samira Tily, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, PreCon Products, Autodesk | Joel Feldman, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk | Cory Kintz, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk | Liam Murray, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Bid Board Pro | BuildingConnected | Forma Estimate | Forma Takeoff | ProEst | Quantity Takeoff | TradeTapp | AECO | Preconstruction
abstract: Investing in preconstruction is one of the most effective ways to reduce risk and set projects up for long‑term success. Join this dynamic session with the Autodesk preconstruction product team to explore what’s new and what’s coming next for Autodesk Forma Takeoff, Autodesk Forma Estimate, Autodesk Forma Bid, BuildingConnected Pro, Bid Board Pro, and TradeTapp. You’ll get an exclusive behind-the-scenes look at our product strategy, major initiatives on the horizon, and the customer feedback that’s shaping our future. Bring your voice to the table and help influence the evolution of our preconstruction offerings. Whether you're a power user or just getting started, you won’t want to miss this session!

title: Catching Procurement Risk Before It's a Delay: Closing the Supply Chain Gap
speakers: Klas Berghede, VP Production & Innovation, Boldt | Eshan Don, CEO & Founder, Krane | Jared Christman, Vice President of Innovation and Technology, Hays Electrical Service
topics: Construction Operations | Data and Document Management | Construction services | Forma | Forma Build | AECO
abstract: Procurement risk rarely shows up early enough to act on. Most GCs find out about a lead-time problem when a submittal comes back rejected or a delivery date slips — by then, the schedule has already absorbed the hit. This session reframes the procurement log from a record of what happened into a signal for what's about to go wrong. We'll unpack what "proactive" actually means in practice: knowing critical lead items before design is finished, prioritizing submittals by schedule impact rather than spec order, and catching a delivery shift the same day it happens — not weeks later at the next OAC meeting. With switchgear lead times now stretching past a year and tariff-driven cost escalation, procurement has stopped being a construction activity and become a development-phase decision. We'll discuss what it takes to move that decision upstream — and why the construction "data leaders" already doing this see meaningfully higher profit growth as a result.

title: MEP Content Editor: Product Updates and Live Demos
speakers: Louie Mdanat, Solutions Consultant II, ARKANCE | Craig Farish, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
topics: Building products and fabrication | Fabrication CADmep | Fabrication CAMduct | Fabrication Data Manager | Fabrication ESTmep | Revit | D&M | MEP Engineering & Fabrication | AECO
abstract: Join this session to explore the latest updates to the MEP Content Editor and see how they can enhance your fabrication workflows. We’ll walk through new features, improvements, and real-world applications, followed by live demonstrations that showcase how to efficiently create, modify, and manage fabrication content. In addition, we’ll cover how fabrication content connects with Revit models through cloud-based workflows, including syncing between centralized cloud environments and desktop fabrication databases. Whether you're maintaining a database or building content from scratch, this session will provide practical insights to help you work smarter and more effectively.

title: From AI Concept to Product Development: Partner Innovation in Autodesk Fusion
speakers: Grace Chang, D&M Strategic Partnerships Ecosystem Manager, Autodesk | Christopher Jackson, Vice President, Global Engineering, Avnet | Casey Morgan, Strategic Business Developer Dir., Autodesk | Kaelan Richards, CTO, Vizcom | Vivek Haligeri Veerana, CTO & Chief of AI, Naya Studio
topics: Manufacturing Other | Fusion | Fusion Design Extension | Fusion Manufacturing Extension | Fusion Simulation Extension | Fusion Team | D&M | Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: AI is changing how products are imagined, explored, and developed from the earliest stages. In this partner panel, Vizcom, Avnet, and Naya Studio will show how their Autodesk Fusion integrations bring AI and intelligent automation into conceptual design and the early stages of product development. Attendees will learn how Vizcom connects AI-powered concept visualization with Fusion design workflows; how Avnet supports electronics decisions, BOM insight, and early supply-chain awareness; and how Naya Studio connects Fusion models with the briefs, sketches, feedback, and approvals around them while turning Fusion geometry into early cost and sustainability insight. Together, these partners help product design teams turn early ideas into informed concepts and make smarter decisions before downstream development begins.

title: Autodesk Fusion Manage Beyond Engineering: From Ideation to Realization
speakers: Michelle Stone, Sr Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | Fusion Manage | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Autodesk Fusion Manage software is often positioned for engineering change and data management—but its real value emerges when extended across the broader product lifecycle. This session will show how manufacturing organizations use Fusion Manage to connect quality processes, supplier collaboration, ideation, and requirements management in a single system. Learn how to structure workflows for nonengineering teams, improve cross-functional visibility, and reduce delays caused by disconnected systems. You’ll leave with a practical framework to expand Fusion Manage beyond engineering and drive more-coordinated, traceable product development.

title: From Outsourced to In-House: How Product Teams Are Rebuilding Manufacturing with Autodesk Fusion
speakers: Christopher Gill, Technical Sales Specialist, Fusion, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | Fusion | Fusion Manage | Fusion Manage Extension | Fusion Operations | Inventor | D&M | Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: Offshore manufacturing used to be the cheapest option … until it wasn’t. As shipping costs rose by more than 200%, offshore rework rates soared three to five times higher, and lead times stretched by up to 30%, many manufacturers started to rethink offshoring and consider bringing production closer to home. This class will show how Autodesk Fusion software helps teams address the often-overlooked costs of offshoring by connecting design and manufacturing workflows in one platform. Through practical examples, you’ll see how Fusion reduces rework, improves process control, speeds iteration, and streamlines computer numerical control (CNC) programming to support more-agile and efficient in-house production.

title: Save Time and Improve Quality: Dynamic Factory Design with Factory Design Utilities, Revit, and FlexSim Integrations
speakers: Tyler Morrison, Industrial Systems Global Principal, Jacobs | Justin Freeman, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Process manufacturing | AutoCAD | Factory Design Utilities | FlexSim | Inventor | Revit | D&M | Digital Factory
abstract: Discover how combining Factory Design Utilities, Revit, and FlexSim software transforms facility design through seamless integration of 2D layouts, 3D models, and process simulation. This case study will demonstrate significant time savings by eliminating redundant updates across platforms and enabling engineering teams to make objective, data-driven decisions with less rework. This class will present the end-to-end Factory Design Utilities workflow, showing how AutoCAD, Inventor, Revit, and FlexSim software work together to enable rapid, realistic simulations and models. Engineers from Jacobs will share real project examples demonstrating ROI, cost savings, and how simulations validate designs, communicate decisions, and extend value into production planning and continuous improvement.

title: Meet Rhumbix: Connecting your Field-to-Finance Workflows
topics: Construction services | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Join the Rhumbix team to discover how connected field and finance workflows can help construction teams turn jobsite activity into actionable insights. In this session, we’ll demo how Rhumbix streamlines the capture of labor, time, and production data from the field and connects it to downstream cost and financial workflows. And, share how better connections between the field and office can reduce manual processes and improve visibility into project performance.

title: Ford Racing Generative Design for Suspension Components
speakers: Jeff Smith, Fusion Sr. Sales Specialist,  Enterprise, Autodesk | Dave Friske, Ford Performance Engineer, Ford Motor Company
topics: Automotive and other transportation | Alias AutoStudio | Fusion | Fusion Generative Design Extension | Fusion Simulation Extension | AUTO | D&M | Product Development
abstract: Join us for a conversation and presentation on the application of Autodesk Fusion Generative Design at Ford Racing. Learn about the how, the why, and the results. We’ll showcase process, testing, and a workflow of collaboration between Ford and Autodesk. In addition, come find out how engineering and design can work better together.

title: From 1893 to the Digital Twin: Revolutionizing Bilbao’s Century-Old Sewer Network with ICMLive
speakers: Frank Zamora, C.I.O. AGUA, Acciona | Paloma Akerman, Principal, Sales Specialist, Water, Autodesk
topics: Water Infrastructure | Utilities and telecom | ICMLive | InfoAsset Manager | InfoAsset Mobile | InfoWorks ICM | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: How do you transform Bilbao’s 130-year-old, 740-kilometer sewer network into a proactive, data-driven utility? By integrating InfoWorks ICM and ICMLive into Acciona’s "NETWIN" ecosystem, the city has moved from reactive maintenance to real-time predictive management. We’ll dive into the technical journey of creating an operational digital twin capable of simulating tidal influences and intense Atlantic rainfall (+20% projected) to mitigate combined sewer overflows (CSOs). You’ll learn how this integration provides a scalable road map for aging urban infrastructure, ensuring compliance with the new European Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (2024/3019) while delivering long-term value beyond temporary subsidies.

title: PM Break
abstract: Recharge, refuel, and reconnect during our afternoon break. Enjoy light refreshments designed to give you an energy boost, spark fresh conversations, and help you return to the next session ready to dive back in.

title: Ditching the Bloat: Re-Engineering MEP High-Density Modeling with Revit DirectShapes to Save Model Health
speakers: Michael Schinn, Director of BIM for DEWALT, DEWALT / MSUITE
topics: MEP Engineering  | Construction Operations | Data Exchange and System Integrations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Building products and fabrication | Revit Cloud Worksharing | D&M
abstract: A major crisis facing the VDC industry is model bloat. On large scale projects, placing thousands of dynamic, deeply nested native Revit hangers or small components triggers endless CPU parametric calculations that cripple model health, max out workstation RAM, and freeze synchronization times. To break this bottleneck, our product team chose a disruptive approach: pivoting away from standard Revit Families (.rfa) entirely and adopting Revit DirectShape technology. In this session, we will deep dive into the strategic evaluation behind moving the parametric engine outside of Revit to process calculations externally. We will demonstrate how injecting raw geometry directly into the project environment bypasses the family constraint solver, turning slow CPU-bound processing into fluid, GPU-driven visualization. Finally, learn how we map standard Shared Parameters to these elements to retain 100% of required BIM scheduling and tagging data.

title: Forma CS Summit l The Autodesk Forma Ecosystem Roundtable: Building Successful Projects Through Connected Teams and Data
speakers: Tawnya Reitz, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk | Mark Mergenschroer, Technical Success Manager (NAMER Adoption), Autodesk
abstract: The most successful projects are built on aligned stakeholders, shared visibility, and strong partnerships. Join this interactive Autodesk Forma Ecosystem Roundtable, hosted by Autodesk Customer Success, for owners, GCs, subcontractors, architects, and engineers looking to maximize the value of Autodesk Forma throughout project delivery. Through facilitated peer discussion with Autodesk Product, SMEs, and industry peers, explore how others are leveraging Autodesk Forma to connect teams, workflows, and project data to strengthen stakeholder engagement and project experiences. Bring your perspectives, learn from the Autodesk Forma community, expand your network, and leave with new ideas for driving long-term, collaborative project success.

title: Beyond the Tool: Aligning People, Process, and Technology in Cost Management
speakers: Randi Schieber, Sr. VDC Manager, Fortis Construction
topics: Project Financials | Construction Operations | Construction services | Build | AECO | Construction Management
abstract: Inconsistent cost practices, unclear ownership, and fragmented financial workflows are common challenges for general contractors of all sizes. Fortis Construction will share how its cost management operating model was redefined through the implementation of Autodesk Cost Management, aligning roles, processes, and technology along the way. Rather than focusing on system functionality, this session will offer a deep dive into the strategic decisions, trade-offs, and lessons learned. You will leave with a practical framework for evaluating and structuring your own cost processes toward scalable, consistent, and risk-aware cost management in partnership with Autodesk Cost Management.

title: Beyond CAD: Where AutoCAD and Forma Connect
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Join us for a fireside chat exploring the future of AutoCAD-to-Forma workflows. Learn how bringing the richness of AutoCAD data into Forma can unlock new design possibilities, extend familiar workflows, and help you deliver more value to your clients.

title: Build Your Firm's AI Adoption Plan in 90 Minutes
speakers: KENTON GRANT, Fractional CTO & Technology Advisor, Kenton Grant Consulting | Evan Troxel, Director, TRXL
topics: Architecture services | None | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Most architecture firms know they need an AI strategy, but few have one written down. In this hands-on lab, you will build a clear 30-day AI adoption plan during the session, including owners, simple guardrails, and one measurable pilot. Participants will complete a quick readiness check, audit where knowledge gets stuck on a recent project, and draft a one-page AI policy plus a 30-day action plan they can start using Monday morning.

title: HKS Is Making Autodesk Data Exchanges Real at Stadium Scale
speakers: Brian Nickel, Firmwide Practice Technology Specialist II, HKS Inc. | Bear Pope, Digital Practice Leader, HKS | Melvin Williams, Digital Practice Leader - Venues, HKS, Inc.
topics: Data Exchange and System Integrations | Architecture services | Cloud Worksharing | Forma | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | AECO | Architecture
abstract: Autodesk data exchanges only create value when exchange structure, naming, versioning, and downstream use are governed as part of delivery. In this technical deep dive, HKS will show how selective exchange logic, federated model handling, metadata preservation, validation, and stadium-scale export optimization support world-class facade delivery. You’ll leave with a production-minded framework for moving from oversized handoffs to controlled, traceable, downstream-ready exchange workflows.

title: Backstage Pass: System Variables Management
speakers: Peter Jamtgaard, Principal Structural Engineer, Jamtgaard Structural Engineering, LLC
topics: AutoCAD | AutoCAD Architecture | AutoCAD MEP | AutoCAD Mechanical | AutoCAD P&ID | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: With more than 700 system and environment variables inside AutoCAD software, it’s difficult for anyone to know them all. This class will walk through the standard AutoCAD options for learning the system variables, and also provide a free LISP application to browse and change the variables in a dialog. By the time the class is finished, you will be able to find and change any of these variables easily.

title: Connect AutoCAD to the Cloud: Reduce File Chaos for Small Teams with Autodesk Forma Data Management Essentials
speakers: Volker Cocco, Sr Technical Enablement Specialist - AutoCAD, Autodesk
topics: AutoCAD | Civil 3D | Docs | Forma Data Management Essentials | AutoCAD & General Design | Cross Industry
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Forma Data Management Essentials enhances AutoCAD workflows for small teams through a live demonstration of a centralized, cloud-connected project workspace. Included with AutoCAD, Revit, and Civil 3D subscriptions, Forma Data Management Essentials enables teams to organize, view, and share project data directly from the desktop. See how to reduce version confusion, improve collaboration, and connect design workflows without disruption. This session will also demonstrate how to get started, how to compare Forma Data Management Essentials to common file-sharing tools, and how to share project standards across teams.

title: Trust Enthusiasts Unite
speakers: Sebastian Goodwin, SVP, Chief Trust Officer, Autodesk | Mary Wing, Dir., Chief of Staff Trust, Autodesk
topics: Trust | None | Meetup
abstract: Join us for a meetup focused on cybersecurity, privacy, risk management, and responsible AI. Open to all experience levels, from students to professionals, this event will bring together a diverse community, including Autodesk Trust Org members. Connect with peers, share knowledge, and explore current trends and challenges shaping the digital landscape. Whether you’re new or experienced, you’ll gain practical insights, exchange ideas, and build meaningful connections. Join us for an evening of discussion, learning, and networking while contributing to a more secure and responsible digital world.

title: From Design to Decision: Automating Multimodal Corridors with Civil 3D and Dynamo
speakers: Jacob Marquez, CAD Manager / Project Engineer, ICON Engineering Inc | Sean Fahey, Senior Project Engineer, Shrewsberry & Associates | Elijah Shoulders, Project Engineer, ICON Engineering Inc
topics: Engineering service providers | Civil 3D | Dynamo | InfoDrainage | InfraWorks | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: Delivering a multimodal corridor requires more than geometry alone; it demands coordination across design, drainage, automation, and visualization. This session will show how ICON Engineering applied a connected approach on the 124th Avenue corridor in Thornton, Colorado. Civil 3D software served as the backbone of the design, while Dynamo, InfoDrainage, and InfraWorks software systems were integrated into a single pipeline. Dynamo automated alignments, profiles, and utility coordination tasks; stormwater design was developed and validated in InfoDrainage; and the design was brought into InfraWorks for visualization and stakeholder communication.

title: One Standard, Many Offices: Managing Electrical Revit at Scale
speakers: Matt McCarthy, East Coast Regional BIM Manager, Syska Henessy Group
topics: MEP Engineering  | Engineering service providers | AutoCAD | BIM Collaborate Pro | Docs | Revit | AECO | MEP Engineering & Fabrication
abstract: Managing electrical BIM standards across multiple offices can be one of the most challenging aspects of scaling Revit workflows. Differences in regional practices, project types, and team experience often lead to inconsistencies, inefficiencies, and rework. This class will explore a proven framework for developing, implementing, and maintaining electrical Revit standards across geographically distributed teams. You’ll learn how to balance standardization with flexibility, how to structure shared parameters and templates, and how to create governance models that drive consistency without slowing production.

title: From Pilot to Portfolio: Scaling Digital Twins Across a University Campus
speakers: Leejo Johney, Head of Digital Estate, University of Exeter | Siva Koppula, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
topics: Buildings | Autodesk Platform Services | Forma Data Management Essentials | Revit | Tandem Connect | AECO | Capital Project Owners & Operators | Cross Industry
abstract: Many digital twin initiatives succeed at the pilot stage but fail to scale across portfolios. This session will present a real-world case from the University of Exeter, showing how a structured facility template enabled digital twins to scale across four buildings—covering both new build and retrofit projects. By standardizing asset data and workflows, the team reduced handover activation effort by 60% to 70%, enabled CAFM-ready asset activation within two to three days, and improved access to operational data by 40%. Learn how to create reusable templates and governance models to scale digital twins across campuses and capital programs.

title: Ultimate Convergence Throwdown: Revit Versus Civil 3D Project Alignment with Model Coordination
speakers: Louisa Holland, Principal Business Consultant- Infrastructure, Autodesk | Misha Shanley, Principal Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Civil infrastructure | Civil 3D | Forma | Model Coordination | Revit | AECO | Civil Engineering
abstract: There are multiple workflows that result in Revit and Civil 3D projects aligning correctly in the Autodesk Forma Model Coordination tool—but which is best? This session will end the ambiguity around best practices for spatially aligning Civil 3D site information with Revit. We'll cover what’s changed in Revit in recent releases that makes site coordination easier. For anyone who’s encountered surprise units, survey feet translation problems, or Revit footprints in far-off coordinates, this session will clear up the confusion. You'll find out if the Shared Reference Point tool is needed and when to Acquire Coordinates.

title: AI in Construction Meetup
speakers: Kellie Herring, Customer Success Manager, ACS, Autodesk | Mark King, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk | Ramya Palani, Senior Customer Success Manager - Team Lead, Autodesk
topics: Construction Operations | Data Analytics and Visualization | Construction services | Build | AECO | Meetup
abstract: Join us as we connect owners, general contractors, and specialty contractors around the United States to exchange best practices, wins, and lessons learned that enhance the construction customer experience with AI. This will be a place to network with like-minded contractors and owners and share ideas and dive deeper into workflows you wouldn’t normally find on an Autodesk webinar. We want to connect you with your peers to elevate the way you manage your facilities, helping Autodesk create the most valuable tool for your needs—based on your feedback, presented by your peers.

title: AEC Roadmap: Informed Design
speakers: Az Jasat, Dir., Strategic Planning/Analytics, Autodesk | Ryan McMahon, Sr. Dir. & GM, Manufacturing Informed Design, Autodesk | Andy Akenson, Distinguished Architect, Autodesk
topics: Construction services | Informed Design | AECO | Industrialized Construction
abstract: Join the Autodesk Informed Design product team for a forward-looking session on how Autodesk is advancing industrialized construction. This session will showcase the latest developments and future roadmap for Informed Design—Autodesk’s platform tool that connects design intent to manufacturing execution. Learn how we’re helping architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) and manufacturing teams accelerate delivery, reduce rework, and unlock new levels of collaboration and efficiency.

title: Engineering Out Resonance: Practical Modal and Frequency Response Workflows in Inventor Nastran
speakers: Diego Ramirez, Director, D.R. Engineering Solutions Pty Ltd
topics: Industrial machinery | Inventor Nastran | Inventor Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Unwanted vibration can lead to equipment failure, structural fatigue, and costly downtime. In this technical deep dive, we’ll walk through a practical modal and frequency-response workflow in Inventor Nastran software using a fully generic vibrating‑machine model. You’ll learn how to identify natural frequencies, interpret resonance behavior, tune stiffness, shift critical modes, and validate safe operating ranges. This session will deliver a repeatable, production-ready simulation workflow for engineers working with vibrating systems across mining, manufacturing, and machinery design.

title: Scaling iLogic Architecture Without Chaos
speakers: Brandon Bibelhauser, Mechanical Engineer/Software Developer, FORTNA
topics: Industrial machinery | Inventor | Inventor Engineer-to-Order | Inventor Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Large Inventor iLogic environments often suffer from duplicated code, fragile “Call External Rule” workflows, and rules that become difficult to maintain as teams grow. This session will share a production-tested approach for building a centralized iLogic function library that behaves like native Inventor functionality. You will learn how to structure reusable VB-based subroutines, enable IntelliSense across internal and external rules, and apply versioning and governance patterns that allow automation to scale safely. You’ll see real-world examples that show how this approach reduced duplication, improved consistency, and accelerated engineer-to-order development in Inventor.

title: AI Data Ready: From Design to Construction to Operations
speakers: Gilbert Kwan, BIM Business Process Owner, Amgen | Stacy Goins, Senior Manager, Engineering Projects, Amgen
topics: Data and Document Management | Data Analytics and Visualization | Life sciences manufacturing | Assemble Products | BIM 360 Build | Revit Cloud Worksharing | D&M | Construction Management | AECO
abstract: Design and construction projects involve diverse tools and stakeholders across phases, creating fragmented, inconsistent data and documentation. This session will show how we establish an AI-ready data foundation from day one using the Autodesk Forma Assets module, enabling a continuous digital thread from design through construction to operations. We’ll demonstrate how standardized data from Revit models and equipment lists—aligned with CSI MasterFormat and UniFormat—connects design, procurement, project controls, commissioning, and operations. By treating models and metadata as lifecycle deliverables, we reuse and enrich data instead of recreating it—with Forma serving as the central platform for integrated, reliable, AI-ready project data.

title: From Sketch to Toolpath: Reducing Design-to-Manufacturing Time Using Connected Autodesk Workflows
speakers: Sagar G S, Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk | Chaitanya Belsare, Sr Associate, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
topics: Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | Desktop Connector | Fusion | Inventor | D&M | Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: Disconnected workflows between 2D design, 3D modeling, and manufacturing often lead to delays and reduced productivity. This session will demonstrate how to connect AutoCAD, Inventor, and Autodesk Fusion software into a seamless design-to-manufacturing workflow, supported by cloud platforms like Autodesk Desktop Connector for data management and collaboration. Learn how to transform 2D drawings into parametric models and generate computer numerical control (CNC) toolpaths while maintaining data continuity. Through real-world examples, discover how connected workflows reduce errors, minimize rework, and accelerate delivery from design to production.

title: Vault on Autopilot: AI-Driven PDM Automation Across Lifecycle, Revisions, and ERP
speakers: Jose Baquero, Senior Consultant MGF - AI Solutions, Avant Leap | Enrique Galicia Tovar, Director of Innovations and AI, AvantLeap
topics: Data and Document Management | Manufacturing Other | AutoCAD | Inventor | Revit | Vault Professional | D&M | Design & Engineering
abstract: Vault Professional software manages thousands of engineering workflows—but property assignment, lifecycle transitions, revision management, approval routing, and enterprise resource planning (ERP) synchronization remain manual. Every operation is predictable and rule-governed. This session will deliver AU 2026's Intelligent Data theme in practice: an AI agent connected to the Vault API monitoring product data management (PDM) events and executing the right action autonomously via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) agent loop. The large language model (LLM) interprets PDM state against business rules, and the API executes without manual intervention. In controlled workflows, this has reduced administrative overhead by up to 70%. You’ll leave with an ROI-prioritized implementation road map.

title: Agentic Design Exploration: How LA28 and Autodesk
speakers: Arthur Harsuvanakit, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk
topics: Architecture services | AECO | Impact & Sustainability
abstract: Agentic design exploration marks a new frontier in sustainable architecture, shaped through partnerships like Autodesk and LA28. In this real-world case study, you’ll see how the approach aligned design, cost, and climate goals. By combining domain expertise with AI workflows, the team addressed ambitious targets using agent-based tools across the project's site, building, and assembly scales—integrating codes, performance, and program needs. These workflows enabled rapid generation and refinement of design options, helping identify high-performing, buildable solutions earlier, reducing carbon and costs. You’ll compare where AI-driven workflows succeed, where they fall short, and how to apply them at scale.
